europe's cultural diversity is our common wealth. we have it only as long as the european nations share the vision of a european community and strive to fulfil it. we are still learning how to use this wealth, and i must say that i see the benefit of the report presented, which maps in detail both the potential and the shortcomings in managing the spiritual wealth that is our common heritage. i think that many of the proposals in this report are correct. however, i am opposed in principle to the idea of linking gender ideology and the gender perspective to common european values such as solidarity, subsidiarity or the dignity of the human person. neither the treaties nor the charter of fundamental rights recognize the term gender or the gender perspective, only equality between women and men. of course, these dates undoubtedly enrich european diversity today. but at most they can be the subject of intercultural dialogue. they are in no way its assumptions or its objectives. unfortunately, the report presented in paragraphs 20 and 27 states the exact opposite, and i consider that very unfortunate. i'll support the report, though.
tax policy has a significant impact on the environment for job creation and i believe that preserving tax sovereignty and tax competition within the union is the right solution. but we can do much more with standardization. i am referring in particular to the introduction of a uniform vat registration. such an arrangement would help not only the development of e-commerce but also, and especially, small businesses, which employ the most people. we have a duty to help them at european level too. the best way forward is through simplification of administration, the same rules and the consistent use of the european single market. i believe that the uniform registration of value added tax, as well as the facilitation of setting up a new company for one euro online across the european market, will help those who need it most, namely small entrepreneurs, those who start new companies and, consequently, the citizens for whom they create the most jobs.
i would like to express my solidarity with the women who have been subjected to violence, threats and harassment in cologne and other german cities. we will not tolerate this kind of behaviour in europe. we have a duty to protect the dignity of every woman. so it doesn't matter whether those who attacked the women in cologne were immigrants or citizens of the european union. what matters is the act that is inexcusable. in judging such acts, we must use the same yardstick for everyone. the events in cologne have shown that the challenges ahead are not easy. let us treat them with all seriousness, but let us not be drawn into superficial judgments that are often based on prejudice.
‒ meps enjoy the immunity accorded to members of their national parliament in their own country. under the laws of the republic of poland, criminal proceedings cannot be brought against a member of parliament without the prior consent of the parliament. in order to properly investigate and assess the traffic offence allegedly committed by the member, the ep agreed to waive the member's parliamentary immunity.
‒ the european parliament has received two requests for waiver of the immunity of mr czesław adam siekierski, which were forwarded to the european parliament by the prosecutor general of the republic of poland. the requests were made in connection with criminal proceedings brought by the polish inspectorate general for road traffic. both requests were unanimously accepted by the committee on legal affairs (juri). moreover, mr siekierski himself expressed his understanding that his immunity should be waived in order to allow further legal proceedings to be carried out in this case. that is why i voted to accept this motion to waive immunity.
in writing ‒ i supported the request for waiver of the parliamentary immunity of the ep member for the republic of poland, mr czeslaw adam siekierski. the request was submitted by the prosecutor general of the republic of poland to the president of the ep to open proceedings against the mep for speeding offences. the polish chief inspectorate of transport claims that on 10 january 2015 mr siekierski did not observe the maximum speed allowed in the parking area while driving. the chief inspectorate further stated that in response to the summons, the member sent copies of his membership card, his certificate of election to the european parliament and a statement in which he admitted to having driven the vehicle in question at the relevant time. the acts of which mr siekierski is accused constitute an offence under the polish administrative offences laws. although mr siekierski pleaded guilty, he failed to indicate on the relevant form whether he accepted or rejected the fine, and it was therefore necessary to waive the member's immunity in order to allow the competent authorities of the republic of poland to bring the offence in question to an end.

in writing ‒ the prosecutor general of the republic of poland has submitted a request for waiver of the parliamentary immunity of mr czeslaw adam siekierski, member of the european parliament, in connection with a speeding offence. the polish chief inspectorate of transport claims that on 19 april 2015 at 11.19 h in the town of stopnica, mr siekierski was recorded by a speed camera driving at 79 km/h in a zone where the speed limit is 50 km/h. the chief inspectorate further states that in response to the summons sent to him on 29 april 2015, mr siekierski sent copies of his membership card, his certificate of election to the european parliament and a statement in which he admitted to having driven the vehicle in question at the relevant time. the acts of which mr siekierski is accused constitute an offence under article 92a of the polish code of administrative offences in conjunction with article 20 (1) of the polish road traffic act of 20 june 1997. in order to close the proceedings, it was necessary to waive the member's immunity, which i also voted for, because i believe that members of the european parliament must also comply with the laws and regulations and must face the consequences of breaking them.
in writing ‒ the bluefin tuna recovery plan is proving to be very successful and effective and it is therefore realistic to consider moving the total allowable catch from 2017 to 2016 already. in order to ensure a uniform and effective application throughout the european union of all measures of the recovery plan adopted in the years 2012 to 2014, this proposal aims at their incorporation into the regulation. however, the problem of the european parliament's lack of involvement in international negotiations still persists. the european commission proposes to transpose future amendments to this recovery plan by means of delegated acts. the removal of this already very limited power which parliament has at the final stage of the approval of international agreements would in practice mean that parliament would have no say in iccat and no say in future in any other international forums.
in writing ‒ the proposed regulation harmonises the application of all measures of the bluefin tuna recovery plan in force from 2006 to 2022. in view of the positive evolution of the stock, the catch quotas for the years 2015 to 2017 and the technical measures for monitoring their status are adjusted. the commission shall be empowered to adopt acts to incorporate international commitments into union law.
the iccat commission adopted a recovery plan for bluefin tuna in 2006. since the plan was adopted, european fishermen have done a great deal of work, by taking a responsible approach to the rules adopted and by using a conservative approach to fishing, to bring the bluefin tuna stock back to healthy levels. it is essential that non-eu fishermen also comply with these rules, to avoid fluctuations in the growth of the bluefin tuna stock. i also think it is important to highlight the importance of promoting traditional trapping methods, which have been used in the past and protect fish stocks and the ecosystem. the use of these traditional methods will avoid unnecessary over-fishing.
in writing. ‒ as i have stressed on many occasions, sustainable development must be the eu's top priority when it comes to economic issues! in this context, it is also of paramount importance to manage our natural resources responsibly. the multiannual recovery plan adopted by iccat in 2006 was established to halt further declines in bluefin tuna in our seas and to maintain its stocks at sustainable levels. i support measures that are necessary to achieve these objectives, such as territorial and seasonal fishing restrictions and reductions in the total allowable catch.
in writing ‒ the european union's actions have also helped to restore the endangered bluefin tuna stock in the mediterranean and atlantic. however, despite the positive trend in bluefin tuna biomass since 2008, i believe that it is essential to continue to regulate and control the tuna fishery if we are to maintain the current satisfactory situation. on the other hand, i am pleased that, on the basis of sound scientific data, the regional organisation decided in 2014 to increase the total catch for the following three years (from 2015 to 2017) by 20%. i supported the rapporteur's proposal to refer the report back to committee so that further negotiations could take place between the commission, the council and the ep. i am confident that the multiannual plan for the recovery of bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean will also help us to achieve all the objectives we have set for this area by 2022. however, i call on all stakeholders to apply all measures of the recovery plan in a uniform and effective manner and to ensure a level playing field for all operators involved in the tuna fishery, including operators from non-eu countries.
in writing ‒ this annual report enables the european parliament to make policy statements on the state of competition in the european union. although the european commission closely monitors the econ committee's position, the european parliament has very limited powers in this area. it is therefore appropriate to ask the european commission to be more active in combating social dumping in the labour market, to seek to exclude services of general economic interest from competition rules, to punish fragmentation and anti-trust behaviour in the digital market, but also to tackle many other outstanding issues. competition policy should promote a level playing field for all companies and encourage their participation in competition in the internal market.
in writing ‒ a well-implemented competition policy is a tool for ensuring a fair and level playing field for business in order to achieve economic prosperity and growth in the common internal market. in order to increase transparency and the effectiveness of competition control, it is essential to strengthen the european parliament's legislative position vis-à-vis the commission as soon as possible and to ensure a strict separation of legislative powers from executive and supervisory powers.
in writing small and medium-sized enterprises form the basic structure of the economy of every country. although large enterprises provide many jobs and produce more goods, it is smes that keep the economy of a country afloat. it is well known that these enterprises have more difficulty coping with the strain of administration, changes in legislation and the normal business life, as they are often family-run, often without the possibility of employing additional qualified reinforcements. it is common practice in member states to favour large companies in the field of taxation, further complicating the situation of small businesses that do not benefit from tax relief. with regard to these undertakings and the economies of the member states, it is essential that the european parliament should also be involved in resolving this situation by means of codecision.
in writing. ‒ i support the adoption of the report, knowing that in a well-functioning market economy, market competition is the key to long-term development. since the start of the economic crisis, the european commission has taken a number of measures that have gone against the principle of free competition by taking into account the social needs of citizens, including the large-scale support to the banking sector during the crisis. i do not wish to question the legality of these steps, but i urge that in the current growing economic environment we allow the greatest possible scope for market competition, thereby ensuring the sustainable development of the eu in all market segments.
‒ i supported the resolution because i consider eu competition policy to be a key instrument of the union and one of the fundamental pillars of the social market economy in europe. although the fundamental objective of competition rules in the union is to protect competition from distortions, we still see serious distortions of competition in many member states. it is important that the commission undertake an in-depth review of existing competition instruments and, in the light of new challenges, create conditions that will continue to provide an environment that supports entrepreneurship and the development of smes, which are the engines of growth and employment. i also believe that competition policy must play an even greater role in ensuring that financial markets are safer and more transparent for consumers. i also consider it extremely important to implement eu competition rules more quickly and effectively, which can prevent the current fragmentation and help to remove many barriers to market access.
in writing ‒ competition policy is one of the most important instruments of the european union's common market. the evaluation of the annual report shows that eu competition policy also needs to adapt to the new conditions and challenges in the internal market. it is essential that eu competition policy takes account of the specificities of certain sectors and focuses on creating conditions in the digital single market. the current competition policy should also aim at the development of e-government and the adoption of new public procurement rules for the development of e-government. it is also necessary to review the rules on state aid assessment, merger control and to streamline the antitrust procedures.
‒ i did not support the report, which is the european parliament's response to the european commission's report on competition policy for 2014. although there is no problem with this type of report in most cases, i was not convinced by the content of mr langen's report, and in particular by some of the elements with which i disagree. one of the most salient issues for me was the common consolidated tax base. i am of the opinion that taxation matters should remain the responsibility of the member states and therefore i do not support tax harmonisation. also because of my disagreement with too much harmonisation, references to the banking union and its completion were problematic for me in this report. on the question of individual cases of harmful tax practices and their investigation, i do not agree with the proposal in the report that a parliamentary committee should be set up for this purpose. i think the competence to investigate individual cases is already given to the taxe 2 committee and should be left to it. for all these reasons, i voted against.
in writing. ‒ intercultural dialogue, cultural diversity and education can play a significant role in promoting the eu's core values, says the report of the committee on culture, which i voted in favour of. the fundamental values of the union as laid down in the treaties are human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights, including the rights of persons belonging to minorities. and there are opportunities to reinforce these values through education, dialogue, sports. the report also places particular emphasis on the role of volunteering, sport and the arts in strengthening the socialisation process. the text does not specifically address national minorities, but focuses on the socialisation process of marginalised communities, migrants and refugees. nevertheless, i consider its message to be important in order to overcome the problems of coexistence between different groups of people living in the regions of europe.
‒ the report focuses on the role of intercultural and interreligious dialogue with all stakeholders and the role of education at all levels in the light of all recent events as a prerequisite for peace and a tool for managing conflicts. it is essential to embrace intercultural dialogue as a strong and clearly stated objective of the european union in the field of interactive communication within and between cultures and to train and prepare future generations to be courageous in tackling the problems and challenges they will face as future european citizens by investing more in effective and innovative and easily accessible and quality education at all levels. we must strive to offer young generations access to education and citizenship and the opportunity to acquire civic, social and intercultural skills and competences that will help them develop ethical and civic values and be active, responsible and open-minded members of society, respecting diversity and combating social phenomena such as discrimination, violence, radicalism, racism and xenophobia.
‒ the report covers events in recent months in the union where groups of people who do not accept the european core values, intercultural and interreligious dialogue, have increased tensions among the population. it is not just in europe that they have interfered with life in an illegal, violent, punishable and inhumane way. it is the responsibility of all politicians to ensure in advance that measures are taken to exclude such conduct in europe and to ensure adequate and preventive protection against such conduct. otherwise, it is only natural that mistrust, hostility and violence will grow in europe and among europeans themselves, ultimately leading to an increase in extremism, intolerance and tension.
the european union is facing truly historic events of late. the arrival of large numbers of foreigners and their integration into european life is constantly reopening the problem of integration not only of adults but also of children. children and young people are the easiest to integrate into a new society, as they learn quickly and naturally and accept the values that are instilled in them by their upbringing. it is of the utmost importance that the member states of the european union in general approach children sensitively, including by introducing them to other cultures in an attractive and non-violent way, which can contribute to mutual understanding between members of different nationalities and eliminate the growing extremism and disagreements with other cultures or religions in europe.
in writing. ‒ over the years, the european union has not only grown with the addition of new member states, but also with the arrival of many new nationalities, cultures, religions, customs and traditions. this is why values such as democracy, human rights, equality or non-discrimination are of particular importance. the report, which i supported, was designed to reinforce the role of intercultural dialogue, cultural diversity and education. to achieve this, it calls for the use of tools such as the mobility of young teachers and students, cooperation between schools, and intercultural dialogue on social media. i believe that the report has a major role to play in building a strong, cohesive and resilient european community.
in writing. ‒ this report on fundamental rights and european values contained some encouraging points; emphasising the importance of defending freedom of religion and conscience and recognising the family as the first place children are introduced to the ‘culture, values and norms of their society’. however i voted against this report because it ignored the principle of subsidiarity, seeking to dictate what those values were to sovereign member states. it also focused on gender ideology and lgbti rights, rather than rights and responsibilities for all european citizens.
‒ i supported the current resolution because i believe that, within the context of considerable cultural diversity, we can achieve a deepening of mutual respect and thus a prevention of radicalisation and extremism through the proposed measures and meaningful intercultural dialogue with all stakeholders. we can certainly agree that traditional cultural diversity is now becoming more and more profound, and that europe is becoming an area of increasing cultural diversity. i am glad that the enlargement of the european union, the deregulation of employment and the free movement of labour, as well as globalisation, have brought many positive things to europe. unfortunately, i am increasingly concerned that in recent times we have seen some of the negatives more and more frequently. the specificity of the last two decades is mainly the migration of representatives of more distant and hitherto only mediated cultures and subcultures. it regrets that the violent and dramatic events facing europe in recent months and years have caused european citizens to have a certain fear for their lives and existence. i hope that, on the basis of the concrete recommendations and actions of this report, we will build on the achievements of the european year of intercultural dialogue (2008) and thus lay the foundations for a stronger and more functional european union.
in writing ‒ i abstained in the final vote on the report on intercultural dialogue. in the light of last year's attacks in paris, the report seeks to address the prevention of radicalisation and extremism through enhanced dialogue between different cultures and religions. it also seeks to introduce tolerance and diversity into schools and to strengthen the role of intercultural exchanges, for example through the erasmus programme, already for school-age children and to make study exchanges available, for example, to disadvantaged groups, marginalised children or children with disabilities. the report also encourages better and more targeted pedagogical preparation of teachers for situations that will naturally arise in today's society, including in view of the high mobility within the eu, but also migration from third countries. this should enable teachers to travel, for example through exchange visits, or to acquire new knowledge of different cultures in lifelong learning programmes. on the other hand, it must be borne in mind that, in view of its subject, namely the inclusion of intercultural dialogue in teaching, the report could interfere with the sovereignty of the member states and thus violate the principle of subsidiarity, which is why i decided to abstain in the final vote.
in writing ‒ the economic and financial crisis of 2007-2008 called for a number of measures by european legislators, who had to adopt a number of measures in the area of financial services in the european union. this report, which is submitted to the european parliament, aims to assess the legislative work in question. the current legislation deserves full implementation and strong enforcement in the member states. financial stability and customer protection must become important priorities for policymakers, with greater emphasis on applying a consistent risk-based approach.
in writing ‒ financial services regulation should now focus more on rigorously monitoring and dealing with the consequences of financial services, while disclosing penalties and impacts in a way that fulfils preventive tasks. the uniform and effective implementation of existing legislation will also increase trust in the union institutions and member states, as well as in the legislation itself, with a positive impact on a global scale. the results of the checks and findings should also be reflected in any necessary legislative adaptation. the expansion of legislation and the adoption of additional new standards may not be effective. on the contrary, it will lead to a deterioration in transparency and thus to a more complicated interpretation of the standards.
in writing the financial crisis, whose origins date back to 2007, shook the world economy, including europe. the european union's member states are still feeling the effects of it, even though the situation worsened almost a decade ago. today we are witnessing a so-called legislative shrinkage which, while seeking to reverse the negative impact of the financial crisis, can also be a risk factor for the lack of uniformity in legislation, which is signed off on the weakening of legal certainty, which is one of the fundamental pillars of the rule of law. with particular regard to smes, it is crucial that checks on the coherence and proportionality of legislation are carried out and that they are complied with in all member states.
in writing. ‒ there is a great need for positive change in the wide-ranging field of financial regulation at eu level. the development of a pan-european financial regulatory framework has been accelerated amid the difficulties caused by the economic crisis and the results achieved on each issue are welcome. however, the main problem at the moment is that the existing regulation is not uniform and the resulting legal gaps distort competition and reduce budget revenues. it is in the clear interest of small member states such as slovakia to introduce uniform rules as soon as possible, which is why i support the adoption of the report.
‒ the financial crisis that europe faced in 2008 was a major impetus for the union to start seriously addressing the impact of financial services on the real economy. since the crisis, the commission has taken a number of measures to restore financial stability and strengthen consumer protection. i supported this report as it seeks to assess the legislative changes that have been adopted and to point out shortcomings or gaps that still need to be addressed. as financial regulation legislation has been adopted in response to crisis events, many pieces of legislation may be potentially inconsistent. the report therefore proposes that the commission examine the impact of these regulations on financial markets. we also ask it to advocate for the protection of efficient and effective financing of the real economy and smes. harmonisation of financial services legislation should go hand in hand with the creation of a capital markets union. it would be beneficial for the real economy if businesses also had access to alternative financing methods such as traditional banking products. however, there is no possibility of deregulation of the financial market, which we expressly draw the commission's attention to. in addition, it is crucial that member states start applying the current rules and avoid creating excessive regulation. this would promote the functioning of the internal market and competition.
in writing ‒ an effective and efficient financial services framework ensuring financial stability is a prerequisite for increasing (long-term) investment and fostering growth in a competitive european economy. however, in addition to the proposed cmu measures, it is also necessary to adopt instruments for the complementary non-bank financing of companies. the principle of building a capital markets union should be to focus in particular on the end-users of capital markets, i.e. companies and investors as well as consumers. financial services regulation in the eu should be coherent, consistent, proportionate, unambiguous and free from undue complexity, and should avoid legal uncertainty and high costs for potential financial market participants. the potential for innovative market-based financing, in particular the possibilities of financial technologies, including crowdfunding and peer-to-peer lending, in particular the harmonisation of relevant regulatory requirements and administrative simplification, should be highlighted.
in writing ‒ i supported mr balz's report on the regulation of financial services in the eu. the report itself assesses the regulation of financial services and identifies challenges in this area. in particular, she says that we should seek to apply existing rules in this area better and more effectively than to create new ones, which i, as a member of the european parliament, have always agreed with in relation to european legislation as a whole. i also welcomed the fact that the report deals with consumer and sme protection, calls for less red tape and a level playing field for all within the european union, and criticises the lack of diverse and beneficial products for consumers. these are the facts which convinced me to vote in favour of the adoption of this report.
i want to congratulate the epp rapporteur on the report she has adopted, which mentions the obstacles women face in becoming entrepreneurs. i believe that girls and women deserve encouragement and support in their work. but i'm more careful about how we're supposed to work in this field with the prejudice that persists against women. unfortunately, parliament cannot determine how household chores should be divided up among families, and it cannot decide to simply boost women's self-confidence through support programs. but what we can do in the member states and what we can appeal to is to offer women opportunities, flexibility and more time to achieve their own goals. for example, access to childcare facilities and quality training in schools. because the kind of students we don't think about as much in business today - future nurses, caregivers, beauticians, cooks - also need good entrepreneurship training. many of these students may one day become successful entrepreneurs.
in writing. ‒ differences between women and men are evident in the entrepreneurial career. data from 2012 show that only 31% of all self-employed citizens in the eu-28 were women. women are more likely than men to prefer working as employees. there are also differences in the way women and men finance their own companies. women start their businesses with less capital and credit, use family financing more often than men and rely less on debt financing. women may be less informed about available financing options and more cautious about taking economic and financial risks, or they may have less financial management experience than their male counterparts. the promotion of women's entrepreneurship is one of the main objectives of the european people's party. to give new impetus to the european economy and create new jobs, the union needs more businesses. women's enterprises need to be given more attention, partly because they are a major source of women's economic independence. the report we voted on today identifies the factors that negatively affect women's entrepreneurship, thus reinforcing indirect discrimination against women from the moment of their creation, and proposes solutions.
in writing ‒ despite the european union's efforts over the past 20 years to improve the position of women in terms of their entrepreneurial careers, it is still evident that the proportion of women among all self-employed citizens is only around 30%, an alarming figure. women have considerable difficulties in obtaining financing for their businesses, despite strong evidence of direct discrimination in member states equally, the failure to provide funding to women entrepreneurs may also be the result of economic logic that investors seek a higher return on investment in larger companies from more profitable sectors dominated by men, despite directive 2004/113/ec explicitly prohibiting direct or indirect discrimination in financial services, including bank loans.
in writing ‒ business sectors such as education, social services, health, hairdressing and cosmetics are dominated by women. on the other hand, there is a need for women to be more involved in other areas, such as finance, construction, trade, etc., where women can contribute to economic growth and employment through their skills. to increase women's interest in entrepreneurship, conditions need to be created that take into account women's maternal role and their care for children and family and that will motivate women more to start professions and companies. municipalities and cities must provide sufficient places in kindergartens, quality after-school care for children in the form of voluntary activities under appropriate conditions. available financing of business plans and reduction of bureaucratic burden in business are important.
in writing i see the promotion of women's entrepreneurship in europe as key to tackling a number of poverty-related issues. compared to the us, women in europe do not do business at such a rate, although some regions of europe suffer from high unemployment, which is accompanied by an increase in poverty. women who are entrepreneurs are often mothers, as entrepreneurship allows them to better manage their time and to devote it to their children. naturally, they are more cautious in their approach to equity financing in an effort not to increase business risk. i support and welcome the facilitation of access by women entrepreneurs to grants and other forms of aid, which would ultimately lead to an improvement in the economic situation of the member states, in particular their poorer regions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of a report on the external factors that hinder women's entrepreneurship, as i believe that europe needs more entrepreneurial citizens. such activities play an important role in boosting the economy and entrepreneurs often contribute to the development of other sectors with their innovative ideas. our task is to create the right conditions and to motivate ambitious europeans who want to be entrepreneurs. this report is important because it highlights the need to support women to take their place in the world of entrepreneurship without discrimination or prejudice.
in writing ‒ i believe it is important to support women entrepreneurs because entrepreneurship is a good way of reconciling women's private and professional lives. women entrepreneurs also make an important contribution to the eu's economic growth. entrepreneurship also allows them to increase their economic independence. however, i cannot agree with the support for women's entrepreneurship that is linked to the imposition of compulsory paternity leave by the eu or the introduction of gender quotas in all forms of targeted support for women to ensure progress towards equality in entrepreneurship. such a decision should remain the responsibility of the member states. i therefore had to vote against this motion for a resolution on the external factors that constitute an obstacle to women's entrepreneurship in europe.

written ‒ the world health organisation defines gender roles as 'socially constructed roles, behaviours, activities and attributes that a society considers appropriate for men and women'. but motherhood is not a gender stereotype. it is this that has the greatest impact on women's economic activity, whether in business or employment. a society that wants to be sustainable must promote and appropriately reward responsible motherhood, not punish it with income cuts and lower pensions. the key to empowering women entrepreneurs is to accept the fact that any of them can become a mother, not to repeat the mantra of gender and stereotypes. i would therefore welcome it if, in future, we spoke more about women in similar resolutions instead of gender.

in writing. ‒ youth unemployment is one of the eu's most significant problems. there are 5 million young people out of work, and there are 2 million jobs that are vacant. because young people tend to have less experience, youth unemployment is more sensitive to economic conditions than general unemployment. the report adopted by parliament today, which i voted in favour of, contains proposals to tackle youth unemployment. among other things, changes in the labour market require a more flexible education system. implementing effective education, training and skills development policies with the support of employers, employment agencies and other relevant stakeholders can make a significant contribution to reducing youth unemployment. furthermore, there is a need to link higher education institutions with the economic sector and to provide adequate training for recruiters, human resource managers, employment services, employers and those working in the education sector. the report also points out that the solution is to increase the entrepreneurial spirit of young people, but this requires the promotion of entrepreneurial skills, which is the responsibility of public bodies, the education system, business and civil society. finally, given the differences in labour markets in the member states, it is necessary to determine which level of government has the most effective means of identifying and describing the skills needed.
in writing ‒ tackling youth unemployment remains a top priority if europe does not want to risk losing an entire generation of young people. the first step must be to further strengthen and properly implement the youth employment guarantee. the positive long-term impact of the opportunities offered to young people needs to be enhanced, in particular through meaningful training that will improve their employability and help create stable jobs. europe will be a better place if equal opportunities become a reality for all young people in europe.
in writing ‒ the youth unemployment rate stood at 21,4% at the end of 2014, with seven million young people aged 15-24 not in employment, education or training. these figures are alarming and may have dire implications for the future of the union. they demonstrate that both government and social mechanisms are failing in the process of educating young people. we're not managing to educate and motivate the younger generation, despite the amount of money that's poured into these policies. the vast potential of young people in terms of their abilities is often not exploited. the need to reassess the system and quality of education in the light of the development of the digital society and the impact of globalisation, as well as the provision of social and economic security in relation to compulsory education, training and employment of young people, is therefore becoming more urgent.
in writing the high rate of youth unemployment is one of the most alarming signs of our times. the negative impact of unemployment is seen not only in the declining ability of young people to pay but also in their social or moral decline. young people must not lose their work habits, as it will be increasingly difficult for them to fit into a normal way of life. it is necessary to change the approach to education, to support apprenticeship and industrial schools and their cooperation with employers, to improve their image in society and to draw attention to them by young people who choose to go to school or who have not found a job in their field and can thus expand their application. graduates from these schools are woefully underrepresented in europe, although their entry into working life is quick and financially attractive. such an approach could lead to a greater reduction in youth unemployment and, consequently, to an improvement in their living situation.

in writing. ‒ in 2013, the commission presented the package on procedural rights, which includes three proposals for directives. the proposal for a directive on the strengthening of certain aspects of the presumption of innocence in criminal proceedings and the right to be present at one's own trial is one of them. the directive, which points out that the presumption of innocence is a fundamental right and an essential principle to avoid arbitrariness and abuse in criminal proceedings, was finalised during the luxembourg presidency. the presumption of innocence is a fundamental principle in the protection of the right to a fair trial, which states that any accused or suspected person is to be treated as innocent until proven guilty. the burden of proof is on the prosecution. the proposal focuses on the principle of presumption of innocence, the burden of proof, the prohibition of the obligation to incriminate oneself, the right to refuse to cooperate, the right to remain silent, the right to be present at one's own trial and the right to a retrial. today's vote formally confirmed the joint text reached by the council and parliament in the interinstitutional negotiations, thus ensuring that suspects or accused persons enjoy a sufficiently high level of protection throughout the union.
in writing ‒ effective procedural safeguards in criminal proceedings at the level of the european union continue to play a unique role, striking a balance in the european union between repressive measures and the right of individuals to a fair trial. the adoption of rules governing the presumption of innocence is an important step towards achieving that balance. i therefore welcome the proposal for a directive submitted by the european commission to strengthen certain aspects of the presumption of innocence and the right to be present at the trial in criminal proceedings. the presumption of innocence is one of the fundamental rights and guiding principles in the effort to prevent arbitrariness and any abuse in criminal proceedings, and this principle is translated into the protection of the right to a fair trial.
in writing ‒ the presumption of innocence is a natural part of any democratic legal order and the rule of law. the reinforcement of the presumption of innocence and the right to be present at the trial in criminal matters increases the responsibility of the state to thoroughly investigate every act. they are essential to the exercise of the right to a fair trial. the absence of the president shall be limited to the extent necessary and shall be clearly and legally justified. the restriction of personal liberty must always be justified by law. at the same time, however, it is important to create the material, personnel and legislative conditions for swift and timely action so that the facts are investigated as quickly as possible and that the passage of time does not spoil evidence and investigations.
in writing the presumption of innocence and the rights of the accused in criminal proceedings have been among the most fundamental rights of the european legal system since the earliest times. without their unconditional observance, we cannot speak of the rule of law and fair trial. the need to respect procedural rules and to improve them continuously is based on the fact that each of us can be brought before a court. life brings situations that often are beyond our control. one small error of carelessness or human error exposes a person to the action of law enforcement authorities. the lawful procedure of the authorities involved in criminal proceedings and, in particular, the possibility of participating in the proceedings in person, enable the accused to protect his procedural rights to an adequate extent. let us not forget that the dignity of the human person must also be paramount in criminal proceedings. i welcome any new legislation that more protects the dignity of the accused person.
in writing. ‒ i support the report on the presumption of innocence and the right to be present at trial, as the fundamental rights of the accused are still frequently violated in many member states of the european union. the report will enable us to introduce a minimum level of protection of the principle of innocence, which could contribute, inter alia, to the mutual acceptance of decisions taken in individual member states and to the strengthening of mutual trust.
in writing ‒ i supported the resolution because i consider the presumption of innocence and the right of accused persons to be present at trial to be one of the fundamental principles of any democratic society and should be guaranteed throughout the union. i am glad that such a proposal is coming, because we have recently seen the limitation of the rights of suspects and accused persons in several eu member states and also the violation of the principle of presumption of innocence. i believe that the proposed directive will strengthen the right to a fair trial in criminal proceedings and strengthen member states' confidence in the criminal justice systems of other member states. although some member states already follow the concept of criminal liability of legal persons under their national legislation, i am convinced that these rules on certain aspects of the presumption of innocence and the right to be present at the trial in person can help those member states which do not have a developed concept. i believe that by adopting this directive we will guarantee a minimum level of protection of the presumption of innocence in all member states and thereby strengthen the right of the accused person to be present at the trial in his own case.
in writing. ‒ i abstained on the vote on the directive on the presumption of innocence. this directive aims to lay down minimum rules on the presumption of innocence and thus to guarantee that everyone within the european union enjoys at least a minimum level of protection. the rules themselves concern in particular the right to be present at the hearing of one's case, the right not to be declared guilty until the final decision on the case, the standard of proof required, the burden of proof and other procedural rights. it is of course very important that the principle of presumption of innocence be strictly observed in criminal proceedings until the person is proved beyond a reasonable doubt to be guilty and is found guilty. on the other hand, i do not agree with some of the elements contained in the draft directive. for example, the directive proposed too broad a range of remedies for infringements of the right to be present at trial, which, given their excessive benevolence, may ultimately end up being abused. that is why, although i believe that the presumption of innocence is one of the fundamental principles that must be respected, i abstained from this vote.

in writing. ‒ the gas equipment regulation approved today aims to replace directive 2009/142/ec. this directive is an example of union harmonisation legislation ensuring the free movement of gas-fired equipment. the directive has made a significant contribution to the establishment and functioning of the single market and has harmonised the conditions for the marketing and/or putting into service of the gas-fired equipment covered by it, taking into account the safety risks associated with gas and the rational use of energy. directive 2009/142/ec lays down the essential requirements that gas-fired equipment must meet in order to be placed on the union market. despite the successful functioning of the directive, there is a broad consensus that it needs to be improved. the directive was changed into a regulation because, in accordance with the principle of full harmonisation, member states' national laws cannot impose stricter or additional requirements on the placing on the market of gas-fired equipment. the essential requirements to be complied with and the conformity assessment procedures to be followed by manufacturers should therefore be the same in all member states. the instrument of the regulation saves member states the cost of transposing the directive. in addition, the regulation avoids the risk of divergent transposition, which could lead to different levels of protection and distort the internal market. the common text of the regulation, which parliament approved today, was a welcome outcome of the interinstitutional negotiations.

in writing. ‒ the proposal for a regulation on cableway installations is an example of eu harmonisation legislation. the proposal aims at harmonising the conditions for placing on the market of sub-assemblies and safety components to be incorporated into cableway installations and at ensuring the free movement of those products within the union. all safety components and sub-assemblies shall be designed and manufactured in accordance with the essential requirements laid down in this regulation. it also provides for the full harmonisation of the essential requirements to be met by cableway installations. it also repeals and replaces directive 2000/20/ec on passenger rolling stock. the directive was changed into a regulation because the regulation provides for full harmonisation, member states cannot impose stricter or additional requirements in their national law. the regulation avoids the risk of divergent transposition, which could lead to different levels of protection and distort the internal market. the common text of the regulation, which parliament approved today, was a welcome outcome of the interinstitutional negotiations.
