the european union has for many years supported developing countries by granting trade preferences through a system of generalised tariff preferences. this support is not automatic but conditional on the fulfilment of certain conditions and therefore a country applying for gsp beneficiary status is required to fulfil certain conditions by its actions. if a country does not fulfil these conditions, it cannot be included in the list of beneficiary countries. the ilo committee on the implementation of ilo standards, the committee against torture, the committee on the elimination of racial discrimination and the committee on the rights of the child have confirmed serious violations of the standards and conditions set by the european union by the kyrgyz republic. i therefore agree that the resolution be referred to the commission and that it be informed that the delegated regulation cannot enter into force.
in writing ‒ by the european parliament resolution of 25 november 2015 on the commission delegated regulation of 25 november 2015 amending annex iii to the regulation of the european parliament and of the council applying a scheme of generalised tariff preferences, we empowered the commission to adopt delegated acts to establish or amend annex iii, thereby granting a requesting country specific incentives for sustainable development and good governance by including it in the list of beneficiary countries under the scheme of generalised tariff preferences. the ep requested that the commission issue an objection to the delegated act of 25 november 2015 amending annex iii to regulation (eu) no 978/2012 applying the scheme of generalised tariff preferences, given that the authorities monitoring the relevant conventions have identified significant deficiencies in kyrgyzstan in relation to a number of conventions on generalised tariff preferences and that those deficiencies constitute serious failures.
in writing ‒ the gsp system favours certain countries in accessing the european union market. the status of a country is not granted automatically, but after the fulfilment of certain conditions. since the kyrgyz republic has not been found to fulfil the conditions and serious deficiencies have been identified in the area of restrictions on human rights, the rule of law, discrimination against minorities, child abuse and other serious issues, it was necessary to object to commission delegated regulation (eu) no c(2015) 08213 of 25 november 2015 amending annex iii to regulation (eu) no 978/2012 applying a scheme of generalised tariff preferences.
in writing as a doctor and a father, i was concerned to learn that the delegated regulation in question allows 30% of the energy in baby food to come from sugar. today we face an increase in obesity not only among adults but also in the alarming rate of childhood obesity. obesity is one of the causes of various serious, often incurable, diseases. if we continue to increase sugar intake in children from infancy, we will not be able to eliminate obesity and the many other diseases of civilization that are directly related to it. it is our duty to take all measures to ensure that the food intended for children is balanced and made from quality raw materials. i agree that such a regulation should not enter into force.
in writing ‒ i supported the ep resolution on the implementation of the commission regulation of 25 september 2015 supplementing the regulation of the european parliament and of the council as regards specific compositional and information requirements for processed cereal-based foods and baby foods. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the protection of the european union's financial interests against counterfeiting is based on the principle of proportionality. the measures provided for in the delegated regulation are not sufficient to protect infants and young children from obesity and the maximum level of sugar should be significantly reduced in accordance with the who recommendations. also, due to the particular sensitivity of the endocrine system of infants and young children, the principle of zero tolerance should apply to pesticides. by the adopted resolution, we called on the commission to postpone the adoption of the delegated act until it publishes its report on nutrition for young children.
in writing as a doctor, i have always stressed the importance of breast-feeding, a balanced diet, and a healthy lifestyle. eu food safety legislation is already very detailed and sets very high standards and clear requirements for food labelling, all to the benefit of the consumer. to enable consumers to make informed choices, european legislation sets out rules on information on product labels, forcing food manufacturers to indicate in particular the date of use, safety warnings, nutritional properties and details on recycling. scientists and doctors agree that breast milk is the best diet for all healthy infants, providing a sufficient supply of all the nutrients needed to support their growth and development. the composition of breast milk is continuously changing, whereas the composition of infant formula remains stable over time, and therefore infant formula cannot in fact replace breast milk. each baby food product must be nutritionally balanced and take into account the gradually diversifying diet. the general scientific opinion is that nutrients and food supplements should be added to infant formulae only if they are nutritionally or developmentally necessary.
in writing ‒ the objection we voted on concerned the composition of processed cereal-based foods and baby foods and was directed against a delegated act of the european commission, in particular against the allowed sugar content in baby foods. this was several times the amount of sugar recommended by the world health organization. i think that in the current trend of increasing childhood obesity, there is no need to increase the energy intake of children in such a needless way, and therefore to go against the health of the next generation. i also agreed to the addition of an article on the precautionary principle with regard to new technologies, such as genetically modified organisms and nanotechnology. as there is not yet sufficient evidence of their effects on human health in all these cases, i think that they should be banned at least in foods intended for young children.
‒ the peace process in colombia cannot go unnoticed by the european union, as it is a historic moment that deserves full recognition by the european union and its representatives. we must use all available means to support the peace talks that will bring an end to 50 years of armed conflict. after more than a year and a half of negotiations, the colombian government and the revolutionary armed forces of colombia have reached a landmark agreement on transitional justice, marking a huge step forward in the effort to bring peace and an end to the long-running armed conflict in latin america. the two parties to the conflict have committed themselves to conclude a final peace agreement by 23 march 2016 at the latest. this resolution therefore clearly declares the political support of the european parliament for the peace process, particularly at the initial implementation stage.
‒ colombia is currently the country with the second highest number of refugees, a consequence of a long-standing internal conflict between the government and leftist movements. this situation also affects neighboring countries, especially venezuela, where most of the refugees have left. in order to eliminate and resolve this conflict, it is necessary that the union, through all its diplomatic components, assist the peace process and supervise the investigation of facts, judicial proceedings and the enforcement of decisions in a manner consistent with international treaties and conventions on fundamental human rights.
the conflict in colombia has been going on since 1964, which means that generations of colombians are affected. the world was relieved to learn that the warring camps were able to negotiate an end to the unrest and to reach an agreement that included a pledge by both sides to work to prevent a recurrence of violence. today, the most important thing is no longer to deal with who caused more damage. it is important to look ahead with a view to achieving peace and justice. i fully support the efforts of both sides to achieve peace and i highly value this initiative. i also welcomed the agreement between the government and the farc to compensate the victims, whose number has increased immensely in the 50 years of conflict. i call on the parties to continue their efforts to achieve the peace that colombia so desperately needs.
in writing. ‒ after many years of fighting between the colombian government and the farc there is finally a chance for peace. this resolution supports the parties to negotiate further and stop the violence. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing ‒ the internal armed conflict in colombia has lasted for more than 50 years, causing great suffering to the population, whether as a result of terrorist attacks or the activities of paramilitary groups, and resulting in, inter alia, murder, enforced disappearances, kidnappings, sexual violence, the abuse of minors, internal and external displacement of the population and landmine attacks. the eu, international organisations and the current colombian government therefore prioritise ending the internal conflict and achieving a stable and lasting peace. cuba and norway have an important role in this peace process as guarantor countries and chile and venezuela as assisting countries in the peace process, and a great deal of thanks goes to pope francis for his cooperation in this role. the eu also welcomes the announcement by the colombian military units that they intend to revise the colombian military doctrine in order to prepare the army to respond more effectively and promptly to new tasks in the post-conflict period and to serve as a guarantor of peace agreements.
‒ ending the internal conflict in colombia, which has claimed millions of victims for more than 50 years, and achieving a stable and lasting peace in colombia are top priorities for the country, but also for the european union and the international community. tools and measures for peacebuilding are needed.
‒ i supported the joint motion for a resolution on the peace process in colombia. i think it is important to send a signal that the european parliament supports the peace process, which will hopefully bring an end to the 50 years of internal armed conflict, during which the population has suffered greatly as a result of terrorist activities or attacks by paramilitary groups. during this period, there were many murders, kidnappings, disappearances, sexual violence, and the abuse of minors. it is therefore positive that the peace talks that started in havana in 2012 will finally bring peace, but above all rules for compensating victims, the establishment of a special commission to search for missing people and the exclusion of any amnesty or pardon for crimes against humanity, genocide and serious war crimes. i therefore hope that the signing of the peace agreement will be achieved as planned by march this year and i have voted in favour of ending this terrible period for the people of colombia.
madam president, association agreements (aa) and the deep and comprehensive free trade areas (dcfta) are one of the most advanced tools we have at our disposal to promote closer cooperation with our neighbours. in the case of georgia, moldova and ukraine, we made an important political choice to strengthen our ties and bring them closer to the eu. these agreements were partly a response to the aspirations of those countries and their citizens to put their relations with the eu on a higher level. in the situation in which the countries are juggling different internal reforms and external pressures, the aas and dcftas should stimulate reform processes and economic growth. we have to be supportive of the reforms, but also demanding, especially when it comes to consolidating democracy, eradicating corruption and strengthening the rule of law. these are the values which are associated with the eu. delivering on them is a crucial test for our partners but also for the eu’s image and credibility in the neighbourhood.
madam president, first of all i would like to congratulate kosovo’s government and parliament on finalising and adopting this agreement – it is a milestone in our relations with kosovo. establishing contractual relations will open new opportunities on the road to closer integration between kosovo and the eu. the agreement provides an incentive for the implementation of reforms in kosovo. as one of the poorest countries in the region, kosovo should take this agreement as an opportunity for economic and social growth, but also as a chance to make substantial political and institutional reforms. the eu shares responsibility for development in this region. we therefore have to tighten our relations with these countries and their citizens. the saa with kosovo is a step in this direction. the next step should lead to visa-free travel for kosovars. this will be crucial to enable kosovo businesses and people to fully benefit from the saa. in other words, with the saa we have taken an important step, dismantling barriers in our relations with kosovo. we should be ready to take the next step, dismantling the barriers in our relations with the kosovan people.
mr president, today we are focusing again on the systematic mass murder of religious minorities by isis. why do we not call it what it is: a genocide? this is the same question as my colleagues have asked. christians in syria are killed or displaced because of their faith. only half of the 1.25 million christians remain, and in other regions 80% or more have been eradicated. without action, no christians will remain there, and situation of yazidis is very similar. many churches are destroyed or turned into mosques. this happens in syria and iraq, but also in turkey. i call upon you, madam high representative, to present concrete steps that the commission will implement to stop this. moreover, this threat is here in the eu as well. we have seen christians in the refugee camps in europe being attacked by other refugees because of their faith. what action will the commission take? if we want to stop this systematic mass murder and give these religious groups hope, we must recognise them as genocide and help the democratic self—administration in northeastern syria, in the rojava canton, with both weapons and aid.
what daesh is doing must be officially called by this parliament and the european commission the real name of genocide. at the same time, we must urge the un security council to adopt a resolution calling for the violent acts of the so-called islamic state terrorists to be dealt with by the international criminal court. the killings and violence targeting christians and other religious minorities that are taking place in iraq and syria are comparable to the killings in srebrenica and rwanda. the christians who live here are waiting for international recognition of their suffering, they are waiting for solidarity and justice from us. if we truly call these horrific acts genocide, we will also be better able to protect syrian and iraqi christians from the violence perpetrated by radical salafists right in europe's refugee camps.
our resolution rightly calls for equal security guarantees for all citizens of the european union and equally rightly calls for the european union's seat on the un security council. but both these requirements, and the one france is asking for under article 42 of the lisbon treaty, cannot be met at the bilateral level. both these requirements - security guarantees for citizens and the eu's place on the un security council - can only be made possible by the existence of a european command and a common european army. small, operational, but available to the european union as a whole. and that's not all, we also need a european intelligence service. without these two bodies of joint command and a european intelligence service, the tasks required by the lisbon treaty to protect our citizens cannot be fulfilled.
this year we have many challenges closely linked to the human rights agenda. europe itself is facing unprecedented challenges in this regard - such as waves of migration, terrorism, or the increasing instability in our immediate neighbourhood. for these reasons too, human rights issues will become increasingly pressing. so we need to set our priorities right this year at the un human rights council. human rights are the foundation of modern europe. we should therefore be the leader in promoting this agenda at the un. we should therefore also look more closely at the human rights agenda in relation to migration. the primary task should therefore be to strengthen humanitarian and development assistance and contribute to poverty reduction in critical regions of the world. however, there is also a need to face the consequences and to strengthen international cooperation and further steps leading to the fight against international trafficking networks, but also to the agenda of strengthening the protection of women's and children's rights.
it is very important to guarantee the right to petition, as this is a means of communication for eu citizens. the petition is seen by citizens as a gateway to the european union, and as a tool for us meps and the other eu institutions to do our job. however, the report shows that the number of petitions received is modest compared with the total population of the union. i can attest to that from personal experience. as a hungarian-speaking citizen and representative of southern slovakia, i receive many requests. i'm not saying that every single issue can be petitioned, but i'm saying that a lot of issues are likely to be petitioned. the commission's 2014 activity report highlights problems and breaches of eu citizenship rights in the areas of fundamental rights, discrimination, free movement and the environment, which the committee on petitions should investigate. i would therefore like to continue to focus on information. the vast majority of citizens either do not know or know very little about the right to petition. in the statistics for the previous year, the number of petitions in hungarian or even slovak is negligible. as vice-president of peti, i therefore see my role as mainly about bringing our work and the right to petition closer to the people of central europe. petitions are also a means for eu citizens to exercise control over the development and application of eu law. however, the report does not contain the guarantees laid down in the previous report, which could have advanced the work of the committee on petitions. i regret that the commission parts of the administrative reform introduced by the secretary-general of parliament in 2014 were not included in the report. all of this would be in the interests of eu citizens with the right to petition and would increase their trust in our institution.
in writing. ‒ a stabilisation and association agreement between the eu and kosovo was negotiated between october 2013 and may 2014. the agreement was signed in july 2014. the parliament of the republic of kosovo confirmed it on 2 november 2015. the stabilisation and association agreement may enter into force upon completion of the current consensus procedure before the european parliament. the agreement will establish a contractual relationship that will provide for increased political dialogue, closer trade integration and new forms of cooperation. it will cover a number of areas, including respect for and strengthening of democratic principles and human rights, and the establishment of various sectoral cooperation frameworks, such as education, energy, environment, justice and home affairs. the stabilisation and association agreement also contains provisions aimed at promoting european standards in areas such as competition, public procurement, intellectual property and consumer protection. it will create opportunities for investment, growth and business development, while at the same time strengthening good governance through approximation to european standards and union law. in today's vote, parliament gave its consent to the council adopting a decision on the signing and conclusion of the framework agreement on the participation of kosovo in eu programmes.
in writing ‒ the eu-kosovo agreement is a key document in the process of stabilisation and association of kosovo with the european union. in addition to clearly defining rights and obligations, we are also providing kosovo with a significant stimulus to implement and institutionalise the necessary reforms. with this agreement, we are creating opportunities to intensify contacts not only between professionals in the fields of education, crime and smuggling, or culture, but also between people. we also envisage further strengthening relations and cooperation with neighbouring countries, which can contribute to stability in the region. last but not least, i would like to point out that kosovo has not yet been recognised by some member states of the european union.
in writing one of the basic principles of roman law, which we still consider to be almost perfect, is the principle: pacta sunt servanda - agreements must be observed. this principle applies without exception in both private and international law and, if it is not respected, stable relations cannot be achieved. in 1975, a declaration was adopted at the conference on security and cooperation in europe in helsinki, which included the principle of the inviolability of borders. the inviolability of borders means that borders cannot be changed even by the creation of a new state. in 2008, kosovo unilaterally declared independence, in violation of international law and the territorial integrity of serbia. for these legal reasons, slovakia and four other eu member states have not recognised kosovo's independence, and i wholeheartedly support this position. for this reason, i also oppose the conclusion of the association agreement between the european union and kosovo.
in writing. ‒ agreements with neighbouring countries are an excellent way of maintaining good relations with them, which in some cases can also mean new alliances. i believe that such agreements are in the interests of the european union and provide a good basis for cooperation in various fields. for this reason, i also support the conclusion of a stabilisation and association agreement with the republic of kosovo. this treaty will help to promote increased political dialogue, trade integration and democratic principles, and will provide opportunities for cooperation in areas such as education, energy or environmental protection.
in writing. ‒ the stabilisation and association agreement with kosovo is the last of the agreements to be concluded with the western balkan countries. kosovo has benefited from preferential trade arrangements with the eu since 2000 with duty-free and quota-free access to the european market except for certain agricultural and fishery products. those measures are currently laid down in a council regulation which expired on 31 december 2015. the proposed agreement provides for essentially the same regime guarantees unrestricted access for industrial products and most agricultural products (except live bovine animals and their meat, sugar products, certain wine products, products of young bovine animals and certain fishery products). the eu-kosovo stabilisation and association agreement is the first formal step towards the process of accession of the republic of kosovo to the eu and its european integration. since slovakia is one of the five eu countries that have not recognised the republic of kosovo, i did not vote in favour of the agreement.
‒ the stabilisation and association agreement is a very important first formal step towards the process of accession of the republic of kosovo to the eu and its european integration. relations between the republic of kosovo and the eu are expected to be further strengthened. in order to normalize relations between belgrade and pristina, recognition by all (including the remaining five eu member states) is required. all eu member states should make every effort to promote economic and people-to-people contacts and social and political relations between their citizens and the citizens of the republic of kosovo.
in writing parliament's approval of the eu-kosovo stabilisation and association agreement (saa) will allow the council of ministers to formally conclude the procedure and bring it into force. the agreement introduces a strengthening of the eu-kosovo political dialogue, closer integration of trade and new forms of cooperation through contractual relations. the agreement covers a wide range of areas, including the strengthening of democratic principles and respect for human rights, the fight against crime and trafficking in human beings, and provides a framework for cooperation in the fields of justice, education and home affairs, and contributes to stability in the region. there is broad agreement that the agreement will be decisive in the process of stabilisation and association of kosovo, in that it requires the introduction and institutionalisation of reforms. the gsp also includes provisions to promote european standards in areas such as competition, markets, intellectual property, consumer protection, energy and the environment. it also creates a free trade area, creating opportunities for investment, growth and business development through the application of european standards and the approximation of eu legislation.
in writing ‒ i supported the recommendation on the conclusion of a stabilisation and association agreement between the european union and kosovo. these agreements are part of the stabilisation and association process with the western balkan countries, and kosovo is the last country in this geographical area with which an agreement has not yet been signed, and the first agreement ever concluded between the european union and kosovo. the agreement includes, inter alia, a call for kosovo to be recognised by the remaining five member states that have not recognised kosovo. although the slovak republic is one of the five countries and does not yet intend to recognise kosovo, it is not opposed to maintaining relations and cooperation with kosovo and therefore supports this agreement. i hope that the agreement will go a long way in consolidating democracy and act as a new stimulus for reform and an opportunity for new investment, growth and prosperity. i also regard it as an important step in kosovo's integration into the european union.
in writing ‒ the european institutions' examination of the emissions-forgery scandal by a major multinational company such as volkswagen is a necessary step towards restoring consumer confidence. the european union has decided to set up a commission to measure emissions in the automotive industry, the results of which will be very important for our citizens who are concerned about environmental protection. i therefore consider it important to select the persons who will be part of this committee, because their credibility will play a significant role.
in writing in september of last year, information about emissions violations by volkswagen, europe's largest car manufacturer, came to light. violation of emission limits means that cars produce more nitrogen oxide or carbon dioxide than is allowed by standards, which can cause various health problems for the population. such conduct must be strongly condemned. given that the serious infringement comes from the largest car manufacturer in europe, and that it is likely that the volkswagen group was not the only one, and that other car manufacturers have also committed such activity, it is necessary to tighten up the emission measurement in the automotive industry. i therefore welcome the establishment of an inquiry committee on emissions measurements, which will contribute to better monitoring of compliance and thus to protecting the health of the general public.
in writing ‒ as regards the european parliament's legislative resolution on the proposal for the appointment of members of the committee of inquiry into emission measurements in the automotive industry, i voted in favour of the resolution. i welcome the appointment of independent members of the inquiry committee. i believe they will help to refine laws and standards in such a way that they are based on the latest technological research and ecology. the final price to consumers must also be taken into account in order to avoid unnecessary price inflation.
in writing ‒ in accordance with rule 198 of the rules of procedure, a draft decision on the establishment, powers, number of members and duration of the committee of inquiry into emission measurements in the automotive industry was submitted to the ep. i support this motion and i also signed the motion in support of putting it to the vote in the ep plenary. it is important that we properly investigate the co2 emissions scandal and, above all, that measures are taken in the future to prevent car companies from cheating. just a few days ago, the very difficult climate change negotiations in paris ended, and a climate agreement was born that has yet to be ratified by individual states. the eu 2020 strategy also sets the objective of reducing co2 emissions, and i therefore welcomed the european parliament's interest in ensuring that large companies in the automotive industry comply with declared emission values, so that consumers are not misled when buying a car and, ultimately, so that we protect the environment.
‒ the european parliament today appointed me, as the only slovak, to the committee of inquiry into emission measurements in the automotive industry. my aim is not to impose unreasonable fines and to introduce new regulations. the automobile industry and its subcontractors employ thousands of people in the slovak republic. but the rules must apply to everyone and we cannot tolerate the deception of the consumer. even large companies have to follow the rules they've agreed upon. environmental standards in the european union are among the highest in the world. if there is a demand for their change, the european union is open to negotiations. together, we will seek solutions to prevent such acts in the future.
‒ we have established the european neighbourhood policy and the eastern partnership to ensure peace, stability and prosperity in europe. to this end, instruments promoting democracy, the rule of law and sustainable economic development should be used. the association agreements have been in force for one year and the creation of a deep and comprehensive free trade area between the european union and georgia, moldova and ukraine represents a significant benefit of the association agreements, as they have a significant impact on growth of economies or job creation. the associated countries are making considerable progress in a number of areas, but democratic institutions are still weak in all three countries. the conclusion of association agreements should not be the ultimate goal but rather part of the process of achieving deeper cooperation between the european union and the countries concerned.
in writing. the eastern partnership was established in 2009 as a joint effort by the european union and its eastern european partners to link political and economic integration on the basis of common interests. the eastern partnership states have committed themselves to the rule of law and democracy, and to respect for fundamental human rights and market economy principles. georgia, moldova and ukraine have concluded association agreements with the european union, including a deep and comprehensive free trade area. i am of the opinion that these agreements, which can help these countries to achieve their objectives, should be respected and that their rejection should not create further unnecessary conflicts.
in writing ‒ in the case of the votes on the association agreements and the comprehensive free trade agreements with georgia, moldova and ukraine, i voted in favour of adopting this resolution. despite the visible problems we have in the eu, it is clear that the accession process and slovakia's membership in the eu itself has brought us the opportunity for more significant economic growth. i am therefore happy to support this process in countries that are struggling not only with economic uncertainty but also with russia's desire for greater influence.
‒ i supported the joint motion for a resolution on the association agreements/deep and comprehensive free trade areas with georgia, moldova and ukraine. the eu recognises the european ambitions of these three countries and highlights the added value of the association agreements in their reform processes. the recent political unrest and dissatisfaction in moldova is worrying as the political impasse has reached a critical point that risks destabilising the country and threatening the economy, with a significant impact on the inflow of foreign direct investment. in this resolution, we therefore called on the political forces in moldova to stabilise the political situation in the country and to move forward with reforms for the benefit of all moldovan citizens. we also called on the georgian government to continue the reform of the judiciary, including strengthening its independence and de-politicizing the prosecution service. on ukraine, we emphasised greater efforts to promote a peace process in eastern ukraine, to fight corruption and to reform the decentralised areas of state power and the judiciary.
‒ the association agreement and deep and comprehensive free trade areas with georgia, ukraine and moldova bring economic growth and political stability to these countries. relations with the eu have led to the development of democratic legislation, the free movement of goods and business as a whole. these countries need to be supported economically as well as politically in order to develop their relations with the eu.
in writing this resolution on the reform process in georgia, moldova and ukraine, adopted one year after the ratification of the three association and free trade agreements with the eu, highlights the democratic reservations and reforms still to be adopted in these three countries. the resolution stresses the need for russia to end its direct or indirect involvement in the conflicts in these territories, in particular the occupation of crimea. as regards georgia, it is necessary to eliminate the threat to the independence of the judiciary and the plurality of the media. as regards moldova, parliament welcomed the formation of a new government, approved after more than a year of unsuccessful negotiations, and looked forward to its reform plan. in respect of ukraine, it insists on the implementation of commitments to fight against corruption. the european parliament also condemned russia for suspending the free trade agreement with ukraine at the time when the eu-ukraine free trade agreement entered into force. it deplores the 'harsh trade restrictions' on ukrainian exports to russia and is concerned about the economic and financial paralysis of ukraine. it also recalls the need for further union financial assistance to that country and the possibility of adopting a legislative proposal to include ukraine in the list of visa-free countries.
‒ i supported the association agreements with the three eastern partnership countries. this type of agreement between the european union and third countries involves major political and economic reforms in exchange for very good trade relations and cooperation. although all three countries have experienced problems related to either judicial deficiencies, media freedom or, in the case of ukraine, the loss of crimea, i believe that it is the conclusion of such agreements that motivates and stimulates countries to continue the reforms already initiated in all three cases, and it is better conditions for trade relations with the european union that will help them stabilise the situation and achieve growth and prosperity.
‒ at their informal meeting on the fight against terrorism, the eu's interior ministers agreed almost a year ago to strengthen cooperation between police and security services, including the exchange of information on dangerous persons and joint action to combat the proliferation of illegal firearms and the financing of terrorism. the european union has adopted a counter-terrorism strategy, which proposes that action be focused on four basic objectives: prevention, protection, prosecution and response. it is therefore essential that the council and the member states adopt swiftly a policy framework to assist the implementation of article 42 (7) teu, including a timetable and a clause on review and monitoring mechanisms.
in writing for a mutual defence clause to be meaningful, its content must be implemented in a sufficiently timely and flexible manner. member states' authorities are required to inform in good time of the lack of capacity of their own forces. the refugee crisis coupled with terrorist attacks clearly show that this is no time for statements and politics. the security of europe and its people requires decisive and decisive action. the indecision and ignorance of integrated assessment reports has already taken its toll in the form of terrorist attacks in paris and other violence in several parts of europe. the mutual defence clause guarantees mutual assistance between member states in the event of terrorist attacks, but at the same time urgent measures are needed with a priority for preventive effects.
in writing the attacks that took place in paris last november shook the world. the situation had escalated dramatically, as was felt in several major european cities, and we began to ask questions about common security. we have seen reports emerge in the media about the lack of exchange of information on criminals between the intelligence services of the various member states of the european union. this area deserves increased attention, as the exchange of correct information can greatly contribute to crime reduction. i also consider it essential for the security of europe that the details of the mutual defence clause be precisely defined. i welcome paragraph 6 of the motion for a resolution, which gives priority to a political solution to the crisis in the middle east and north africa. armed conflict always has two sides: it rarely produces satisfactory results, but it is inherently accompanied by unnecessary loss of life. for the reasons set out above, i agree with the content of the motion for a resolution.
in writing ‒ the attacks in paris last november were a horrific crime committed against european citizens. the way in which defenseless people lost their lives is most cowardly and reprehensible. therefore, i believe that the declaration of war on the terrorist organization daesh was a justified reaction of the french government. but it must also be admitted that these events have exposed the weaknesses of european security in full. mutual assistance is also one of the eu's founding principles. for the first time since the attacks, a member state had requested assistance by invoking the mutual defence clause. under this article, other member states are obliged to provide the means and assistance within their means if one of their countries is the target of an armed attack. all countries have shown a willingness to support france wherever possible. on the other hand, these are still bilateral agreements between france and other countries. since this clause was used for the first time, there are no precise procedures for its application yet. the lack of common rules resulting from mutual defence thus led to targeted measures and uncoordinated cooperation. the council must be informed of the activities carried out by the countries in cooperation with france in order to be able to consider in the future the prerequisites for a common european defence. in a time of constant conflict in our immediate neighbourhood, a european defence system is also in our interest, which is why i supported the resolution.
in writing ‒ this resolution follows the paris attacks, after which france began to invoke article 42.7 of the treaty on european union. this is an unprecedented application of this article instead of article 222 of the same treaty, which could also be applied to this situation, and perhaps in a more appropriate way. while it is of course essential to express solidarity with france and to show that member states are united in the face of the threat of terrorism, the activation of this article should not be seen as a call for the harmonisation of security and defence policy at european level. in this respect, i am clear that defence and security policy must remain a matter of national sovereignty and that, instead of greater harmonisation at european level, the states should focus on nato as the basis for collective defence. for these reasons, i did not support the resolution.
in writing ‒ the promotion of respect for human rights is the duty of all states. human rights are indivisible and interrelated and the withdrawal of any such rights has a direct impact on other rights. all states are obliged to respect the fundamental rights of their citizens and to take steps and measures to facilitate the enforcement of these rights at the national level, as well as to cooperate in removing obstacles to their enforcement at the international level. respect for and protection of the universal value of human rights are part of the european union's ethical and legal acquis and also a cornerstone of european unity. respect for human rights must therefore be part of all policy areas. the year 2016 is, like 2015, a year of significant anniversaries in the field of human rights, peace and security. in particular, i would like to recall the important un security council resolution 2242 on women, peace and security, which has placed women at the centre of all efforts to address global problems, including the rise of violent extremism.
in writing respect for human rights is an inherent part of the law of the member states and of the union itself and must also be reflected in all eu external policies, including trade, investment, public services, development cooperation and the common security and defence policy. the promotion of human rights in third countries must also be promoted through political dialogue and diplomatic channels. the european union must strengthen its position and influence in international forums (especially the un and unhcr) in this regard. all efforts must be focused on eliminating problems in non-member countries in europe and africa and on preventative conflict management.
the draft resolution lists the different areas that will be the european union's priorities for the un human rights council in 2016. europe and the world are facing unprecedented social change and the most serious humanitarian crisis since the second world war. the migrant ratio is extremely bad. all these issues have a serious impact on the situation in europe, and i appreciate that the refugee problem is one of the topics that have become a priority for the european union. but we should not forget the other areas where we have seen violations of fundamental rights even before the refugee crisis. i include in particular women's rights and children's rights. these are two groups that always require a special approach at all times. at a time of escalating violence in the middle east, the situation of women and children in the region is truly appalling. the european union must take a strong stand for the protection of human rights in the middle east and condemn the current situation which does not respect fundamental freedoms and rights. i welcome the provisions that deal with the situation.
in writing. ‒ the importance of the un human rights council's relationship with the european union is unquestionable, as the organisation's day-to-day work is focused on monitoring and protecting human rights. our task was to adopt a motion for a resolution that would convey the european union's priorities to the etuc in an appropriate way. the proposal presented by the european parliament covers key areas such as the effective fight against terrorism, human rights and migration, the fight against discrimination and the exercise of economic, social and cultural rights. i think we have a well-thought-out and well-formulated proposal, which i voted in favour of.
in writing. ‒ this resolution seeks to set the un agenda at the human rights council by speaking as one eu voice on migration, climate change, lgbti rights, russian aggression and the middle east peace process (amongst many others). the resolution had such a strong liberal agenda i was unable to support it, as this would have meant voting for sexual and reproductive health and rights. sovereign member states should all have their voice at the un and not be diluted into one eu position.
in writing ‒ promoting respect for human rights and protecting the universality of human rights is part of the eu's ethical and legal framework. in addition, the un human rights council aims to monitor the progress of individual countries in the world in implementing them. i therefore support the independence and integrity of the office of the un high commissioner for human rights, as it is absolutely crucial to its ability to fulfil its mandate effectively and impartially. i also welcome the initiative of the un high commissioner for human rights, who has advocated for change and supported the creation of eight regional centres for direct cooperation with partner countries. the current migration crisis in particular shows that the humanitarian situation of refugees is often not in line with their fundamental rights, and cooperation with third countries is the way to change this. the seriousness of the humanitarian crisis faced by refugees requires effective and coordinated international action to address current and future migration challenges. it is important to remember that migration must also be approached from a human rights perspective precisely because women and children are among the marginalised and disadvantaged groups of migrants. the strategy for dealing with migration must be linked to humanitarian and development policies, and when we talk about the return of migrants, we need to think about respecting their rights and providing them with adequate protection in their country.
, in writing this resolution underlines the priorities needed to improve the protection of human rights, including: reaffirming the eu's zero tolerance for the death penalty and its long-standing opposition to such punishment and torture; recalling that freedom of thought, conscience, religion and belief is a fundamental right recognised by the universal declaration of human rights and calling for concrete action to protect religious minorities; addressing the challenges of the greatest humanitarian crisis since the second world war. we are witnessing a growing number of people at risk of persecution, armed conflict, general violence, forced to leave their homes and risk their lives in search of safety and a better life; calls for effective and coordinated international action to address the root causes of migration flows; incentives for all states to combat gender-based violence against women and girls and the importance of developing gender-sensitive migration policies. however, i could not support the resolution as a whole, as it emphasises universal access to sexual and reproductive health services, family planning, including abortion, contraception and artificial insemination, and emphasises gender ideology.
‒ i did not support the draft joint resolution on the priorities of the european union for the 2016 unhrc. the proposal covered a very wide and diverse area of the european union's human rights interests and touched not only on general human rights issues but also on situations in specific countries. the proposal also addressed, inter alia, current problems and challenges related to migration, but also issues related to technological progress, such as the use of unmanned aircraft. although i agree with most of the issues raised in the report, i could not support it, especially given a number of sensitive issues, such as access for lgbti people to all legal institutions or the issue of universal access to sexual and reproductive health services.
in writing. ‒ the annual report of the committee on petitions aims, among other things, to examine how procedures and relations with other institutions can be improved. i supported the amendments to the report which refer to the procedural guarantees on petition handling laid down in the previous report and which take forward the work of the committee on petitions. this concerns elements of the administrative reform introduced by the secretary-general of parliament in 2014 concerning the committee on petitions, such as responding to citizens within a reasonable time limit of 9 months. all this is in the interests of eu citizens with the right to petition and increases their trust in our institution. in addition to these guarantees, the report also gives an annual breakdown of the number of petitions received by the member states, which shows that citizens do not use the right to petition in the same way in all regions. central european eu citizens still need more information on eu rights and related opportunities. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing ‒ the right of petition in the european union is one of the fundamental pillars of european citizenship and a fundamental right which provides that every citizen or person residing or having its registered office in the european union has the right, individually or jointly with other citizens or persons, to petition the european parliament on a matter which falls within the european union's field of competence or which directly concerns it. most citizens ask the european parliament for help in areas such as justice, the environment, the internal market and fundamental rights. as the committee on petitions' report for 2014 shows, 2714 petitions were received by the european parliament, a decrease of 6% year on year.
the right to petition is one of the fundamental political rights and a form of direct democracy. it emphasises the sovereignty of citizens and is also a good communication tool between citizens, the eu institutions and bodies. if it works properly, it can help to solve many of the citizens' problems and can also act as a stimulus for legislative initiative. however, in some countries there is a need to increase awareness and education about this right of citizens and about the possibilities and ways of exercising it.
in writing i find the work of the committee on petitions very useful. the importance of his work is also seen in the report presented, which allows us to look more deeply into the problems of ordinary citizens of the european union. by submitting a petition, citizens express their disagreement with the state of affairs or the activities of the authorities in a particular area and draw attention to the violation of their rights. most of the petitions submitted concern the areas of justice, the environment, the internal market and fundamental rights. so we can view these petitions as a mirror reflecting what people are really concerned about. at the same time, this report must be approached responsibly and we must also reflect on the fact that many of the petitions had to be declared inadmissible because they called for the assistance of the european parliament, even though it was unable to help them in this area. this shows a lack of awareness among citizens. for this reason, i fully agree with the rapporteur that citizens should have a single point of contact at european union level to guide them in finding a solution to an alleged violation of their rights.
in writing. ‒ i do not support the adoption of the 2014 report, as i consider the work in the committee on petitions to be unsatisfactory. from the very beginning, i could sense that the socialist rapporteur was trying to minimise dialogue and cooperation with the members of the people's party committee and was looking for the possibility of cooperation with the greens, gue and efdd members. this was evident in the only shadow reporter meeting held two days before the committee vote. i also do not support the report because the recent politicization in the committee on petitions is not focused on achieving the stated objectives, but rather on meeting the national electoral campaign objectives of individual members.
in writing ‒ the report of the committee on petitions contained very stimulating comments and suggestions for solutions that would ensure, on the one hand, citizens' access to law and justice within reasonable time limits and, on the other hand, the effectiveness of the committee. however, the resolution adopted calls for a broader interpretation of article 51 of the charter of fundamental rights, which would result in the eu's powers being extended to the detriment of the member states. this approach is totally unacceptable and i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ i consider the right to petition the european parliament to be one of the fundamental pillars of european citizenship and the fundamental right of any citizen or person residing or established in the union to petition the european parliament on a matter which falls within one of the union's fields of competence or directly concerns it. i would like to take this opportunity to thank the rapporteur for her report, which, on the basis of a detailed analysis, not only evaluates the activities of the committee on petitions in 2014, but also comes up with a number of proposals and measures of initiative that offer possibilities to address existing problems in the field. although there was a slight decrease in the number of petitions submitted in 2014 compared to 2013, it is pleased that the majority of petitions (80%) are closed in the year following their processing and admissibility and only a small number of petitions remain unresolved for more than four years. given the total number of petitions received and the number of inadmissible petitions received (39%), i consider it extremely important to inform european citizens more intensively about the existence of the right to petition and its possibilities, as the european institutions and the member states can draw attention to problems that concern them and that are of concern to them.
these days, the european parliament is making full use of its role in co-creating the european union's trade policy. we endorse the recommendations for the negotiation of the trade in services agreement, tisa. i would be delighted if we, as representatives of the citizens, could help to ensure that there are no unnecessary, false myths surrounding the negotiations, but that we negotiate constructively an agreement which has the potential to bring about improved services for the more than two dozen countries involved. tisa is a chance for our consumers to get cheaper services abroad, and it will give them more options when they travel or shop online. tisa is an opportunity for our entrepreneurs to create jobs and to penetrate markets in third countries more easily. the services offered by eu citizens today are of high quality. our task is to help bring them to third countries and to modernise international trade rules to match the modern world and to exploit the potential that today's digital sector and financial and professional services offer, for example.
in writing the recommendations for the agreement on trade in services should cover an important segment that currently employs tens of millions of people in europe. the further expansion of this sector is also linked to the repeatedly stressed need to support the digital economy. we hear a lot about the importance of technological and market innovation for sustainable economic growth. europe is maintaining its leading position in this area. this position cannot be compromised under any circumstances. the possible conclusion of a new trade agreement should therefore be conditional on the european union's position as the most important global exporter of services being clearly consolidated. in addition to the european union, more than 20 countries are involved in the negotiations on tisa. their markets account for more than two-thirds of current global trade in services. the european union already has established mutual links with several of them in this area. the agreement must therefore contain concrete potential for further progress. otherwise, it's meaningless to us. it must bring more jobs, more rights and lower prices for european consumers. at the same time, it is necessary to define clear boundaries within which it can no longer intervene under any circumstances. this is particularly the case for public services, cultural services, data protection rights and fair working conditions.
written steel companies in europe, including u.s. steel košice, have been paying a heavy price in recent months for excess capacity in the world's steel production, especially in china. the commission also found that the chinese exporting producers were not able to compete with the union producers. the commission has not established that the chinese exporting producers are in a position to export the product concerned to the union market. it distorts the market and threatens production in countries that respect and abide by international trade rules. in the 15 years since its accession to the wto in 2001, china has failed to take legislative and structural steps to become a standard market economy. in the event of granting market economy status to china, the european union will lose any form of control and the possibility to protect itself against the excessive increase in imports of various types of chinese goods into the european market. the european union should choose a common approach with other wto member states and reach a compromise with china in the form of partial or sectoral recognition of market economy status. but along with this must come pressure to end unfair practices and improve environmental and social standards in chinese industrial production.

the european union is facing a historic event today, with more refugees arriving on its territory than at any time in its history. the difficult situation in the middle east and africa is forcing many people to flee their homes and seek safety in other countries. many of them are seeking refuge in the countries of the european union. the schengen area, which is a great asset for making life easier for ordinary people and businesses in europe, must be sufficiently protected by precise rules and their observance, with regard to the safety of citizens and refugees crossing its borders. for the reasons set out above, i welcome all the amendments introduced by the draft legislative resolution which regulate the legislation in this area in a positive way.
in writing ‒ in the current crisis, concrete action is needed. big bailouts and quotas don't work in practice. i therefore support the concrete definition of the practical modalities of external border controls. however, the rules of this system should be defined in a clearer and more understandable way, respecting the sovereignty of the member states. i therefore abstained from voting on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a codified version of the schengen borders code.
‒ the schengen borders have been under enormous pressure in recent months. on the one hand, it is the external borders that require stronger protection. but it is also necessary to ensure that in crisis situations it is possible to carry out effective protection of the internal borders of the member states. to this end, the commission has proposed the codification of the schengen code directive. i welcome and support the commission's efforts to clarify and rationalise the rules governing the conditions for introducing border checks, although it should be noted that this is mainly a matter of harmonising the existing rules. i believe that checks at the external borders of the member states should only be introduced in extreme cases in order not to impede free movement in the schengen area in the long term. but the authorities of each country must be able to ensure their own internal security. in addition to checks at border crossing points, the schengen code also includes risk analysis, border patrols and the use of the schengen information system. third-country nationals must move within the eu in such a way that it is clear from the visa information system and from their travel documents when they entered the eu and which borders they crossed. if border controls for eu citizens are to be introduced in some places, they should be carried out in a manner that respects human dignity and minimises waiting times for border crossings.
‒ the code fully respects the right to move and reside freely within the territory of the eu member states. the issues of asylum, the movement of aliens, border control, the protection of the rights of third-country nationals and of union citizens and their family members are among the primary tasks of a democratic society founded on the principles of freedom, security and justice.
in writing ‒ i abstained on this report. the report on the draft regulation establishing the schengen borders code was intended to be a mere codification of existing texts without altering their substance. despite this reassurance, however, in my view the report is moving towards a greater transfer of powers from the member states to the european union at one point, which goes beyond the definition of codification without changing the substance. the report states that, since the objective of the regulation cannot be satisfactorily achieved at the level of the member states and could be better achieved at the level of the union, the european union should be able to adopt measures which, prior to this codification, were within the competence of the member states. and although this particular article may not mean any substantial change in the long run, i think it should not be inserted into the regulation without due consideration.
in writing. ‒ the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution aims to protect the human environment from air pollution. since air pollutants do not respect borders and travel thousands of kilometres before they settle, the problems caused by air pollution must be addressed at international level. the convention, which entered into force in 1983 and was subsequently supplemented by eight protocols, was the first international instrument in this field to have binding legal force. the accession of the community to the protocol was approved on behalf of the community by council decision 2001/379/ec of 4 april 2001. the protocol entered into force in december 2003 and has been transposed into union law by a number of different acts. the protocol was amended in december 2012 by decisions 2012/5, 2012/6 and 2012/7. decision 2012/5 is subject to ratification by the parties. the ratification of the amendment will be a significant step towards a higher level of protection of human health and the environment from transboundary air pollution. parliament gave its consent to this today.
in writing ‒ the problems caused by air pollution must be tackled globally at international level, as several studies show that air pollutants can travel thousands of kilometres before they settle. the 1979 convention on long-range transboundary air pollution was the first instrument in this field. to date, eight protocols have been annexed to the convention, the most important of which is the 1998 aarhus protocol, which deals in particular with emissions of lead and mercury into the air. the proposal for a council decision is an important step towards a higher level of protection of human health and the environment.
in writing. ‒ economic development has a negative impact on air quality. it is an international problem, and its effective solution requires the active involvement of all countries of the world. the decision to adopt amendments to the 1998 heavy metals protocol, which has been transposed into eu law by several acts, strengthens the limits for dust emissions from large stationary sources, which is in line with already adopted eu legislation. i believe that ratification of the decision and its implementation will contribute to effective protection of the atmosphere.
in writing air pollution is an unpleasant and dangerous phenomenon because it is not visible to the naked eye and its extent cannot be determined immediately after the pollution has occurred. at the same time, pollution can travel hundreds or even thousands of kilometres through the air, with potentially negative effects on human health. for these reasons, it is important and appropriate that environmental legislation on air pollution be continuously improved. in the proposal i have tabled, i welcome the linking of the revised aarhus protocol to a new directive setting updated emission ceilings for specific substances that threaten the cleanliness of the air. i also see the preference for the best technologies that have been developed so far from an economic and technical point of view, the so-called bat, as an essential condition for any new legislation on environmental protection. for these reasons too, i support the motion for a resolution.
‒ the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution is intended to ensure the protection of the human environment from air pollution. i support the development and maintenance of emission inventories for pb, cd and hg and the reduction of hg concentration levels in alkaline batteries. it was also necessary to introduce measures for the handling of other hg-containing products, including measuring instruments. that's why i voted yes.
in writing ‒ the 1998 aarhus protocol on heavy metals aims to reduce and control anthropogenic emissions such as lead, cadmium and mercury into the air. it requires the parties to reduce their total annual emissions of these three metals below their 1990 levels or below the levels of either 1985 or 1995. the protocol aims at reducing emissions from industrial sources, combustion processes and waste incineration. it sets emission limit values for certain large stationary sources and requires the use of best available techniques. the parties shall also develop and maintain emission inventories for lead, cadmium and mercury, phase out leaded petrol and reduce lead concentration levels in alkaline batteries. the protocol proposes the introduction of measures for the handling of other products containing lead, including measuring instruments.
in writing ‒ given the nature of this topic, there is a need to strengthen the consistency and certainty stemming from the convention and to set stricter emission ceilings for certain air pollutants as well as annual national emission inventories.
in writing ‒ in this legislative resolution, the european parliament gave its consent to the amendment of the 1979 protocol on heavy metals to the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution. the objective of this protocol is to reduce and control emissions of heavy metals such as lead and mercury, in particular from industrial sources, combustion processes and waste incineration. the parties also undertake to phase out leaded petrol and reduce the level of mercury in alkaline batteries and measuring instruments. of course, all these changes and restrictions will require the introduction of appropriate measures at the level of the parties, which may not be too far from slovakia, but i think that in view of the negative impacts of heavy metal emissions on health and the environment, as well as the impossibility of controlling emissions at national level, which is caused by the rapid and uncontrolled spread across national borders, such international regulation is very important. i therefore supported this proposal, as well as mr la via's second proposal for a protocol on persistent organic pollutants.
in writing. the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution aims to protect the human environment from air pollution. air pollutants travel thousands of kilometres before they settle, so the problems caused by air pollution must be addressed at international level. the convention, which entered into force in 1983, is the first international legally binding instrument to establish a framework for monitoring and reducing the adverse effects of transboundary air pollution. the convention has been supplemented by eight protocols. the purpose of the 1998 aarhus protocol is to control, reduce or eliminate discharges, emissions and losses of persistent organic pollutants. the accession of the community to the protocol was approved by council decision 2004/259/ec of 19 february 2004. decision 2009/1 is subject to ratification by the parties. the amended protocol includes seven new substances, updates the implementation requirements, limits and expands the range of substances subject to annual emission limits and reporting obligations. the amendments to the protocol are governed by union law and will be further implemented by a new directive. the ratification of the amendments will be a significant step towards achieving a higher level of protection of human health and the environment from transboundary air pollution. i voted in favour of obtaining the necessary parliamentary consent for the draft council decision.
‒ the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution aims to ensure the protection of human health and the environment from air pollution. this convention established a cooperation programme for the monitoring and measurement of large-scale airborne pollutant transmissions. the convention was subsequently joined by eight protocols identifying specific measures to reduce emissions of air pollutants. the draft council decision includes amendments to the protocol which are an important step towards a higher level of protection of human health and the environment and concern persistent organic pollutants.
in writing persistent organic pollutants are not normally found in nature but are introduced into the atmosphere through human activity, mainly as by-products of industry. they are able to persist in the environment for long periods of time and are transported over long distances. thus, they can also enter areas whose air is not adversely affected by industrial production and thus worsen it unnoticed. better and newer legislation is therefore needed. the amendments introduced by the new version of the protocol will contribute to the protection of the environment by better regulating dangerous emissions. i strongly welcome and support the motion for a legislative resolution and agree with the rapporteur that the european parliament should approve it, thus contributing to the protection of the environment, the protection of the air and the health of millions of people.

in writing ‒ eurojust was set up 14 years ago as a division of the european council to support national investigating authorities in serious crime. initially, it was only the initiative of a few countries, but the deterioration of the global situation linked to the terrorist attacks in the usa in 2001 led the member states to consolidate the position of eurojust, which was gradually transferred to the hague. eurojust's current objective is to coordinate the cooperation of investigators and prosecutors in cases of transnational crime. the framework of its activities includes in particular terrorism, drug and human smuggling, money laundering, corruption, fraud and cybercrime. in addition to the eu member states, the agency also seeks to cooperate with other countries in europe. i therefore support ukraine's accession to the cooperation agreement with eurojust. this will strengthen judicial cooperation in the fight against serious crime, in particular organised crime and terrorism. the cooperation shall also include an agreement to send a liaison prosecutor from ukraine to eurojust to participate in the mutual exchange of information. not only the eu but also ukraine must have a special interest in investigating serious crime. particularly in the current situation of destabilised ukraine, corruption is a problem that the country will have to contend with for a long time. strengthening the fight against transnational crime and strengthening judicial cooperation across europe is one of the tools to build mutual trust.

‒ eurojust was set up 14 years ago as a division of the european council to support national investigating authorities in serious crime. initially, it was only the initiative of a few countries, but the deterioration of the global situation linked to the terrorist attacks in the usa in 2001 led the member states to consolidate the position of eurojust, which was gradually transferred to the hague. eurojust's current objective is to coordinate the cooperation of investigators and prosecutors in cases of transnational crime. the framework of its activities includes in particular terrorism, drug and human smuggling, money laundering, corruption, fraud and cybercrime. in addition to the eu member states, the agency also seeks to cooperate with other countries in europe. i therefore agree to montenegro's accession to the cooperation agreement with eurojust. this will strengthen judicial cooperation in the fight against serious crime, in particular organised crime and terrorism. the cooperation shall also include an agreement for montenegro to send a liaison prosecutor to eurojust to participate in the mutual exchange of information. in order to be able to join the eu fully in the future, it is essential that montenegro participate in strengthening the fight against transnational crime. strengthening judicial cooperation across europe is one of the tools for building mutual trust between countries.
