in writing ‒ the request for waiver of immunity concerns a traffic offence committed on the territory of the republic of poland. in accordance with eu legislation and the law of the republic of poland, the waiver of immunity is necessary to establish criminal liability. i respect the law and i trust in a fair investigation and a fair resolution of the matter, so i agree to waive the parliamentary immunity.
in writing ‒ i supported the request for waiver of the parliamentary immunity of robert jarosław iwaszkiewicz, as it is important that in the republic of poland, where the member-designate committed an offence, his offence be investigated by the imposition of appropriate penalties. the request for waiver of immunity was lodged by the prosecutor general of the republic of poland in connection with criminal proceedings to be initiated by the general inspectorate of transport. the polish chief inspectorate of transport claims that back in september 2014 the mep violated the traffic rules by exceeding the speed limit of 50 km/h in a closed area by 29 km. in order to investigate the whole matter with the possibility of a subsequent penalty under the road traffic laws in force in the republic of poland, it was necessary to waive the parliamentary immunity of mr robert jarosław iwaszkiewicz.
☐ the polish chief inspectorate of transport has registered a traffic offence against mep robert jarosław iwaszkiewicz when he was recorded travelling at 94 km/h in the 60 km/h speed limit zone in august 2014. since a member of the european parliament is subject to the polish law on the immunity of members, no criminal liability can be invoked against members of parliament and senators without the consent of the sejm or the senate. in this case, the waiver of immunity is a matter for the ep, and the request of the prosecutor general of the republic of poland was therefore submitted to the president of the ep. after discussion in the committee responsible, the request was put to the ep for a vote. in the interests of justice, we have voted to strip the parliamentary immunity of fellow member of parliament robert jarosław iwaszkiewicz, so that he can be held accountable for the offence he committed in his own country, even though he was protected by parliamentary immunity.
in writing ‒ in the motion for a european parliament decision on the request for waiver of the immunity of mr florian philippot, member of the european parliament, i voted in accordance with the position of my group in the european democratic group for the adoption of this resolution, by which the european parliament decided not to waive the immunity of mr philippot. member of parliament philippot has been accused by the government of qatar of defaming the state by suggesting on television that qatar is funding terrorism. i agree with the position of the committee on legal affairs of the european parliament, which considered that the french judicial authorities' request for waiver of immunity in relation to criminal proceedings initiated in a third country was unfounded, since in the case of a member of the european parliament, immunity concerns not only the views expressed by a member at official meetings of the parliament but also his views expressed elsewhere, for example in the media, where there is a link between the opinion expressed and his parliamentary functions. the aim of immunity is generally to enable the legislative bodies to carry out their constitutional function without any undesirable external interference and the principle also applies to legal proceedings initiated by a third country.
‒ the ministry of justice of the french republic has submitted a request for the waiver of the immunity of mr florian philippot, member of the european parliament, in connection with the defamation proceedings pending before the court of first instance of nanterre, since article 8 of the protocol on the privileges and immunities of the european union provides that members of the european parliament enjoy in the territory of their own state the immunities accorded to members of the national parliament. member of parliament philippot has been accused by the government of a third country, namely qatar, of defaming that state during a radio broadcast on 9 january 2015 and a television broadcast on 19 january 2015 when he implied that qatar finances terrorism. since expressing views on eu and third countries' foreign policy in public is part of the performance of the duties of an mep, we have decided not to waive the parliamentary immunity of florian philippot.
in writing. ‒ at the very beginning of its mandate, the 8th european parliament was given a mandate to take up the fight against undeclared work. the complexity of the challenge stems from the nature of the problem, namely that paid activities are legal in nature but are hidden from the relevant public authorities or, in the case of disguised self-employment, are misreported. the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council establishing the european platform sets out the challenge that the platform should be a forum for collecting and sharing reliable information on best practices and existing problems, and for cooperation in the development and application of effective enforcement and incentive measures. the objective is to establish, inter alia, a work programme that fully takes into account the need for targeted action to reverse the current trend in the spread of undeclared work and to increase the number of regularised jobs that provide decent livelihoods and useful services to clients, while contributing to fair competition in the market and sustainable financial stability. the outcome of the interinstitutional negotiations was acceptable to the european people's party, and i therefore voted in favour of the report.

in writing. the loss of biodiversity has a negative impact on nature and humans, undermining the earth's natural resilience. the main causes of decline are habitat change, pollution, over-exploitation of resources, invasive alien species and climate change. efforts to halt the loss of biodiversity failed in 2010. in 2011, the eu developed a new strategy. in 2020, the eu will again fail to meet its targets. the ecological footprint of the eu-28 is twice the size of europe's biological capacity. i agree with the report that more political will and a political priority for biodiversity conservation would be needed to achieve concrete results. this is an issue that affects all of us and future generations even more, which is why it is important to involve as many stakeholders as possible, including regional and local actors. full implementation of the existing nature directives, the birds and habitats directives is essential for the implementation of the whole biodiversity strategy. the eu has a unique network like natura 2000 thanks to the directives. the amendment of the directive to the extent that it would endanger biodiversity is to be avoided and further innovative solutions are needed. a growing number of aware european citizens see and value the steps taken to preserve diversity. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing ‒ according to the eurobarometer survey on biodiversity, at least 80% of european union citizens consider the impact of biodiversity loss to be serious. however, the european effort to halt the decline in biodiversity ended in failure in 2010, and a new strategy was set in 2011 with six objectives to help halt the global level of biodiversity loss. last year, however, according to the official report, alarming findings were confirmed, suggesting that without additional efforts by the european union, the targets proposed by the council will not be met by 2020. however, biodiversity conservation and investment in nature are not only socially but also economically necessary, and biodiversity and its great intrinsic value must be protected in order to preserve the planet in the best possible condition for future generations.
in writing ‒ preserving biodiversity for future generations is a complex and sensitive process. its decline is and always will be affected by human activity, both direct and indirect. the loss of biodiversity will negatively affect all future life on earth, affecting entire generations of humanity. it is therefore necessary to take effective measures on an ongoing basis to keep nature in balance with human economic activity as far as possible. i will support all proposals that seek to preserve biodiversity, integrate nature and landscape protection into all policies and reconcile economic development with biodiversity protection.

in writing. ‒ a regulation of the european parliament and of the council is needed to introduce the instrument for the application of the bilateral safeguard clause and the anti-circumvention mechanism into eu internal law. the association agreement with moldova contains a bilateral safeguard clause. this instrument allows for the temporary suspension of trade preferences in cases where their application would result in an unexpected and significant increase of imports, causing significant economic damage to the domestic industry of the importing party. furthermore, that agreement contains a so-called anti-circumvention mechanism which provides for the possibility of reinstating the mfn in case imports of certain agricultural products originating in moldova exceed a certain threshold and do not provide adequate justification for their precise origin. in other words, the proposed regulation is necessary to protect union producers where appropriate. i therefore voted in favour of the commission's proposal.
in writing ‒ this report concerns the integration of the safeguard clause and the anti-circumvention clause as provided for in the association agreement between the european union and moldova. this means that no new substantive conditions may be introduced in the course of the legislative process that have not been approved during the negotiation of the association agreement with moldova. a safeguard measure may be imposed where, as a result of the reduction or elimination of customs duties, a product originating in moldova is imported into the european union in such increased quantities that it could cause substantial injury to the manufacturing sector. the association agreement also includes a so-called anti-circumvention clause, which provides for the possibility to introduce customs duties if imports of certain agricultural products from moldova exceed a certain permissible limit, without duly justifying their precise origin.
in writing ‒ i agree to the introduction of safeguard elements in the bilateral agreement with moldova, which aims to protect the union agricultural market against excessive or illegal imports of agricultural products from moldova. the measures in the form of a safeguard clause and an anti-circumvention mechanism should prevent the interests of the agricultural market in the union from being harmed.
the republic of moldova and the european union agreed on the safeguard measures referred to in article 9 of the resolution during joint negotiations, and the adoption of their legislative text was therefore the logical step. the adoption of the amendments to the resolution in question is also important because they bring the regulation into line with the wording of the association agreement with moldova. moreover, it also contributes to the clarification and unification of terminology, which is an essential prerequisite in legal acts for the possibility of complying with agreements in the way originally intended. the anti-circumvention mechanism included in the agreement serves to protect the european economy. i consider all the measures mentioned above to be logical and appropriate and therefore support the draft legislative resolution.
in writing ‒ i supported the mutual protection clause, which will be able to be applied within the limits of free trade with the republic of moldova. the eu is already moldova's largest trading partner, with agricultural products accounting for a significant share of total imports. in order to protect the internal market of the union, it is necessary to maintain the possibility of restricting imports of a certain product if, as a result of the reduction or elimination of duties, its importation could cause serious injury to production in eu countries. such a measure could be applied for two years. the agreement also includes a so-called anti-circumvention mechanism, which allows the reintroduction of a customs duty if the volume of imports of certain products from moldova exceeds a certain threshold without justifying their precise origin. in this way, the union aims to prevent non-moldovan products from being imported into the eu from moldova. for these reasons, i agree with the view that these provisional safeguard measures are necessary to prevent economic injury to the union market in the event of increased imports.
‒ the agreement has significantly deepened moldova's political association with economic integration in the european union, which i support. however, the clause is necessary to protect eu producers.
in writing. the eu is now georgia's main trading partner, accounting for 27.2% of its trade with the eu, while the eu's trade with georgia accounts for 0.1% of its trade. the main agricultural products exported from georgia to the eu are fresh and dried nuts, mineral water and wine. the regulation proposed by the european commission implements the provisions of the eu-georgia association agreement approved by parliament in december 2015. the adoption of the regulation is necessary in order to enforce georgia's obligations under the agreement on the anti-circumvention mechanism. the anti-circumvention mechanism allows the reintroduction of the mfn if imports of agricultural products originating in georgia exceed a certain threshold without precise determination of origin. the 'anti-circumvention clause' is necessary in particular to prevent products not originating in georgia from entering the european union through georgia 'with the benefits of the agreement'. the clause also serves as a protection mechanism for georgian producers against possible abuses. the average annual import volume of the products listed in annex ii-c to the agreement has been established. the agreement establishes a preferential trade regime. the commission also includes in the proposal a reporting obligation to submit an annual report to the co-legislators on the application and implementation of the regulation. this will increase parliamentary scrutiny and transparency of the common commercial policy. i supported the report.

in writing ‒ as the world health organisation's specialized agency for research on cancer classified genetically modified soybean mon 87708 × mon 89788 as a substance with probable carcinogenicity for humans in march 2015, i support the proposal to withdraw the commission implementing decision authorising the placing on the market of products containing, consisting of, or produced from this genetically modified soybean.
the european parliament rejected the commission's proposal to allow a national ban on the sale and use of gmos, as it indirectly leads to the closure of borders between the member states of the european union. such a proposal is contrary to union law because it does not respect the principle of protecting human health while ensuring the functioning of the internal market. i repeatedly call on the commission to submit proposals in accordance with union law, taking into account the requirements of the member states.

in writing ‒ it is estimated that around 430 000 europeans die prematurely due to poor air quality, largely due to nitrogen oxides and particulate matter emissions. at the same time, 17 member states are subject to infringement proceedings for failure to comply with the ambient air quality directive. the findings showed that in the automotive sector there is a significant difference between the level of emissions when measured under laboratory conditions and when measured in real driving conditions. so we need to get to a point as soon as possible where today's laboratory limits are the limits in real life. without the compromise negotiated by the commission and agreed by the council, there was a risk of solutions being blocked, of wasting time on the way to real-world emission measurements and, therefore, of putting the brakes on emission reductions in the automotive industry. in slovakia, up to 44% of gdp is accounted for by the automotive industry, with more than 200 000 jobs dependent on this sector. on the way to our goals, we must take all measures to protect the environment, but we must also take into account the social aspect and employment in this sector.
in writing in the european union, more than 400 000 people die each year as a result of air pollution. the union is obliged to reduce these figures radically. however, the commission proposal does not sufficiently protect human health. that number is really ridiculously high, so it is necessary to eliminate harmful influences early on. i think it is important that the type-approval checks for vehicles which are to be put on the market are tightened up, and i think it is equally important that the checks for cars which are already in use are made. the controls must be designed to produce concrete results and thus reduce air pollution.
in writing, i consider the automotive industry to be key to the slovak economy. but we also need to protect the environment. i therefore approve the rde proposal, which has been prepared for a long time and which is also supported by the representatives of the slovak automotive industry. i therefore consider it useless to create another document that would introduce absurd standards that even the latest technologies cannot meet. in practice, these new standards could even lead to the cessation of diesel car production. for this reason, when voting on the article 106 objection concerning emissions from light passenger and commercial vehicles, i voted against this resolution.
in writing ‒ last year, fraud was revealed by some car manufacturers in their emissions reports, and it is therefore very important that you properly investigate this co2 emissions scandal and above all that you take measures to prevent car manufacturers from cheating and to protect consumers and the environment. the eu 2020 strategy has one of its measurable targets to reduce co2 emissions, so i welcome the commission's compromise proposal on measuring emissions from motor vehicles in real use. in slovakia, the automotive industry currently accounts for 44% of gdp and more than 200 000 jobs depend on car manufacturing, so i did not support the envi objection, as its approval could seriously damage the european automotive industry with an impact on the slovak economy as well. i think the commission's proposal is sufficient to reduce co2 emissions in the car industry and to protect the environment.
in writing - protecting the environment is very important to me. as the sole representative of slovakia on the european parliament's committee of inquiry, i will advocate for manufacturers to strictly comply with the legislation and to communicate their comments openly. the first priority must be to ensure that the consumer receives the product with the declared characteristics for his money.
written ‒ i did not support the objection of the envi committee, which called for a new, stricter proposal for a commission implementing decision on the introduction of real driving emission testing. the introduction of real driving emission testing is a significant step both in reducing environmental pollution and as a preventive measure against a repeat of the volkswagen scandal. i think that the introduction of an additional test to the original laboratory tests, by which emissions are measured under real conditions, is an ideal and ambitious means of doing so. on the other hand, i think that these measures should not be too ambitious. unrealistic requirements would only lead to a situation where the automotive industry, which also considers the introduction of the test to be beneficial, would not be able to adapt to the new strict requirements in time and develop new technologies, which would ultimately be counterproductive. i also believe that the requirement to withdraw a proposal and submit a new one, as contained in this objection, could ultimately lead to the introduction of the test being unduly delayed, since it cannot be assumed that a new proposal would be submitted in a short time.
in writing. article 218 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union provides that parliament has a decisive role not only in the adoption of trade agreements but also in the prompt and full information of parliament at all stages of the procedure for negotiating trade agreements. the report concludes that tisa negotiations should ensure increased reciprocity in market access, a level playing field at global level, and tangible benefits for consumers. furthermore, interested parties should be given access to the negotiations. public and cultural services, fundamental rights to data protection and fair working conditions and the right to regulation should not be the subject of negotiations and should be clearly excluded from the scope of the agreement. an important element is the libe proposal that the agreement guarantees full respect for the fundamental eu legal norms by introducing a human rights clause with a legally binding and deferred effect, which is a permanent part of eu agreements with third countries. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing ‒ the further expansion of this sector is also linked to the repeatedly stressed need to support the digital economy. we hear a lot about the importance of technological and market innovation for sustainable economic growth. europe is maintaining its leading position in this area. this position cannot be compromised under any circumstances. the possible conclusion of a new trade agreement should be conditional on the european union's position as the most important global exporter of services being clearly consolidated. in addition to the eu, more than 20 other countries are involved in the negotiations on tisa. their markets account for more than two-thirds of current global trade in services. the european union already has established mutual links with several of them in this area. the agreement must therefore contain concrete potential for further progress. otherwise it is of no significance to the european union. it must bring more jobs, more rights and lower prices for european consumers. at the same time, it is necessary to define clear boundaries within which it can no longer intervene under any circumstances. this is particularly the case for public services, cultural services, data protection rights and fair working conditions.
in writing ‒ i support the conclusion of a trade in services agreement that sets transparent terms for all partners. the commission should aim to strengthen europe's current position as a leader in trade in services and ensure reciprocity in market access. the agreement can be a pathway to further liberalisation and greater dynamism in trade in services, which can help european firms, workers and consumers, in particular in the areas of market digitalisation, financial services and logistics.
europe is at the top of the ranking in trade in services. the european union has huge potential in this area and tisa is an opportunity for it to gain greater access to foreign markets. on the other hand, it is still very important that culture, labour law, consumer protection and data protection in particular, simply our whole european way of life, remain intact. i support the motion which calls for the highest level of transparency and information. national parliaments and other local authorities must also be involved in the debate in order to make the negotiations and their results transparent to the general public. in concluding agreements of such importance as tisa, i consider consistency to be the most important element, because its final wording will have an impact not only on today's europe but also on future generations.
in writing ‒ the aim of the trade in services agreement (tisa) is to liberalise the services sector. but the deal will have an impact on our institutions, which we've been used to for years. these include consumer protection, health, education, social affairs, waste management and the protection of personal data. there is a need to make greater use of the transparency of the negotiation of the final version of the document and to further assess the possible negative effects of this agreement. i therefore abstained in the vote on the european parliament's recommendations to the commission for the negotiation of this agreement.
in writing ‒ the trade in services agreement (tisa) is a trade agreement currently being negotiated by 52 members of the world trade organisation (wto), including the eu, as of the beginning of 2013. i supported the resolution because i believe that the trade in services agreement (tisa) will remove barriers for service providers and ensure a level playing field through reciprocal market access and fair competition. it is pleased to note that services already employ some 70% of the eu's workforce and account for 40% of the value of goods exported from europe. i believe that tisa is an opportunity for the eu not only to consolidate its position as the world's largest exporter of services, but under certain conditions it can also be a suitable trigger for inclusive growth, sustainable development, reducing poverty and inequality and creating new jobs. i believe that the trade in services agreement will provide more robust protection for small and medium-sized eu service providers against unfair practices by non-eu service providers.
‒ tisa is a significant opportunity for european companies to provide their services in third countries and thus protect european companies beyond the eu's borders and public services within it. i support this instrument, which is to result in the liberalisation of trade in services in areas such as finance, e-commerce, transport services, licensing, telecommunications, shipping and temporary labour mobility, and is to cover some 70% of world trade in services.
‒ i have supported the report containing the recommendations to the european commission on the tisa agreement. i think that the rules governing trade in services need to be updated, as the original gats agreement dates back to 1995 and fails to cope with the advent of digital technologies in many respects. i think tisa presents great opportunities for our companies to penetrate third country markets and thus not only present their quality services to the world but also help create new jobs and economic growth. in addition to the positive effects on employment, the benefits of this agreement will also affect consumers, who will enjoy protection, but also easier and cheaper access to services abroad. but as the administrative report notes, in order for the negotiations to succeed, it will be necessary not only to define sufficient rules on the protection of personal data, but also to define further exceptions, for example concerning services of general interest. last but not least, public confidence must be won, which can only be achieved through transparent negotiations on this agreement and by maintaining a constructive dialogue.
in writing ‒ the it is essential that we adopt a new strategy on gender equality and women's rights for the period after 2015, as the previous strategy expired last year. the new strategy should cover important areas such as the need to combat violence against women effectively or to improve their position in the labour market. we have set ourselves certain objectives in this area, but we are only slowly approaching them. without a clear, shared commitment to achieve them in the coming years, which the new strategy should bring, this will be very difficult to achieve. a few years ago, a promise was made to draw up a new binding legislative act specifically addressing, for example, gender-based violence. when that failed to happen, the european commission came up with a strategy, but it still does not see the reality of the daily lives of the citizens of the member states. instead, the european commission has presented a document entitled 'a strategic commitment to equality between women and men 2016-2020' which, paradoxically, commits no one to anything. this shows that the european commission absolutely refuses to reflect a reality which clearly says the exact opposite.
in writing ‒ the right to equal treatment, equal access to employment opportunities, education and healthcare, and the development of a strategy for equality between men and women, taking into account the unique and specific role of women as mothers, are all part and parcel of any european union policy. i believe it is necessary for the commission to present as soon as possible a strategy for gender equality and women's rights, which will define the conditions for the natural and self-evident equal treatment of women in all areas of life.
in writing although not only the european union, but european society as a whole, prides itself on the equal status of men and women, we know that true equality between men and women is not yet achieved. personally, i do not consider the strategy presented to be a tool to eliminate these inequalities. instead, it reminded me of a picture that's been circulating on social media. it's a nice contrast between justice and equality. three children, from highest to lowest, want to look over the fence, but neither one of them reaches it. thus, each child is given an equal rank, but one that is appropriate only for the eldest child; the second must stand on tiptoes; and the third, the smallest child, despite or because of having received "just" help, still cannot see through the fence. the problem i see is the constant twisting of the word equality. women still do not receive the same value at work as men, and those who give birth and raise multiple children have almost no concessions. social assistance for mothers with children is still insufficient, parental allowances are minimal. i see these and other areas as real problems of contemporary women, and therefore of society as a whole, and solving them would contribute to real equality between men and women. i consider the documents and strategies that circumvent them to be a conscious ignorance and i have no interest in dealing with them.
in writing. ‒ it is clear that men and women should be treated equally in terms of pay, human rights and many other areas. the joint motion did recognise that equality is a matter for member states to act on, respecting the principle of subsidiarity, which i always point out. however it went too far in proposing that a quota be applied as to how many women should be on company boards. instead of focusing on the successful implementation of existing legislation it called for additional legislation and unjustified investment in new strategies. for these reasons i voted against this resolution, and note that it was adopted by just a small majority.
in writing ‒ gender equality is a core value of the eu. the right to equal treatment is an important right, recognised in the eu treaties, and it is essential for the further development of society that it is applied in legislation, practice, case law and everyday life. in this regard, the ep resolution called on the commission to take action following the results of the public consultation and the positions of parliament and the council by adopting immediately a communication on a new strategy for gender equality and women's rights for 2016-2020, addressing gender equality in the areas of violence against women, working time, decision-making, health, education, media and external relations, and in line with the international agenda, namely the 2015 beijing+20 outcome document and the new framework on gender equality and women's empowerment: how eu external relations 2016-2020 can transform the lives of girls and women. on this basis, the commission should propose legislative initiatives in its work programme to address persistent inequalities between women and men in the eu.
in writing ‒ i propose to increase the participation of women in the labour market, but not through the introduction of quotas for employers, which could interfere with the freedom of enterprise. i also support the elimination of the wage and pension gap and the promotion of equality between men and women in decision-making.

one of the european union's fundamental values is human dignity. respecting and protecting the dignity of every human being, woman, man or child, is not only a matter of cultural tradition in europe, but also an imperative of law. actions that violate the human dignity of another person are reprehensible and must be punished uncompromisingly, especially when the victims are women. it does not matter whether the perpetrator is a citizen of a country, a tourist, a migrant or a refugee. the geneva convention allows for the expulsion of a refugee if he or she is a threat to the security of the state or if he or she has been legally convicted of a particularly serious crime. i personally believe that both violent and verbal attacks on the dignity of women should be classified as serious, regardless of the origin and status of the perpetrator. but in a situation where tensions are rising in europe as a result of the great wave of migration, any such action by migrants must also be seen as a security threat. i therefore call on the member states to amend their laws in order to protect effectively and decisively the human dignity of all who live here.

serbia, as an independent country, is one of the youngest countries in europe. it was created in 2006 after the secession of montenegro. serbia is seeking eu membership, with formal negotiations starting in 2014. serbia's position was complicated by the situation connected with the declaration of the former province of kosovo as an independent state, which serbia did not recognise. however, relations are gradually normalising, with bilateral agreements between these entities finalised in 2015. as a candidate country for the european union, serbia must fulfil all the conditions laid down for european integration, for which we will provide the necessary assistance from the union.
serbia has a turbulent history which has greatly influenced the development of the country. since serbia has set itself the goal of joining the european union, not only the government but also the population, each generation, must make efforts to achieve the set criteria as a state. this is not an easy path, as any country that has gone through the process of joining the eu knows. however, serbia has recently made great progress towards european integration in several areas. i particularly welcome the progress made in the area of entrepreneurship, including through appropriate legislation. improving the business environment would help to reduce the regional disparities that are a reality in serbia. economic reforms will remain essential for serbia in the future, but further steps are also needed, particularly in the area of the rule of law and democracy.
‒ the european council decided on 28 june 2013 to open negotiations with serbia on eu accession, the monitoring process for this country was completed in march 2015 and the commission has now submitted to the european parliament a progress report on serbia for 2015. it notes that serbia has taken a significant step towards normalising relations with kosovo, and has made significant progress in the areas of the business environment, the reduction of the budget deficit and the labour market, including labour law and employment policy. the rule of law, an independent judiciary, is of key importance for serbia. in this regard, despite some progress in adopting provisions on the evaluation of judges and prosecutors, the level of influence remains high, which is why serbia needs to implement a national strategy of judicial reform to ensure that judges and prosecutors are not influenced by politicians and the government. the concern is that corruption and organised crime are an obstacle to serbia's democratic, social and economic development. the report commends the constructive approach of the serbian government to relations with neighbouring countries, which has enabled significant progress to be made in deepening regional cooperation and in strengthening relations with the eu.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament resolution adopted today welcomes the un-backed libyan political agreement of 17 december 2015, which is a key step in the implementation of the libyan political agreement. a secure and politically stable libya is essential not only for the security of libyan citizens, but also for the security of the entire region and the european union. the motion condemns the destabilising terrorist attacks by daesh against the libyan people, including attacks on minorities and on the oil facilities in al-sidra and ras lanuf, and all attempts to disrupt the stabilisation process. it considers that the union should use its diplomatic and foreign policy instruments within the framework of the common security and defence policy and should seek to stabilise the region. since the anarchy in libya, the country has become an even more transit zone for people smuggled to europe's southern borders. it therefore calls on the office of the un high commissioner for refugees to be more closely involved in coordinating un efforts and calls on the eu and the member states to effectively address the problem of the sudden surge in migration and refugees from north africa, especially from libya.
in writing ‒ the islamic state-affiliated militias have used the civil war and power vacuum to expand their presence in the country, increasingly committing acts of terrorism and brutally abusing the local population. in early january 2016, these groups launched an offensive against major oil facilities on the middle east coast and simultaneously carried out the most tragic terrorist attack in libya since 2011, killing dozens of newly recruited members of the zalite police. i welcome the signing of the libyan political agreement to establish a government of national accord as the only legitimate government, because the most effective response to the presence of radical militants in libya is ultimately the creation of inclusive domestic institutions capable of ensuring the rule of law, providing public services and ensuring local security, and effectively combating groups that threaten the stability of the country and the wider region. this government must pursue reforms in the country to be able to face the challenges posed by terrorists and militias.
the absence of a stable government contributes to the opaque situation in libya, allowing terrorist groups and organisations to operate in its territory. the ep has clearly stated that it recognises and supports the government of national unity, established by consensus among the libyan parties, as the only legitimate government of libya. the commission, the european external action service, which coordinates the action of the member states in libya in cooperation with the un and regional partners, must focus its assistance and support to libya on state and institution building so that the legitimate government gains control of the territory and the situation in the country gradually normalises.
libya, this great and rich country in north africa, has been in a state of misery for five years. the quality infrastructure that libya could have been proud of is destroyed. attacks by islamists, various terrorist organizations, and other groups that commit violence against the general population are a daily reality here. after a long period of turmoil, the country and its diverse population need stability to breathe and start anew. we must not forget the number of migrants that libya has to deal with, and it is desirable for the security of europe that libya does so at a high level. the european union can help libya in this regard by providing a financial package as well as by peacekeeping missions. nevertheless, i am of the opinion that interference with the functioning of the state should be kept to a minimum. i agree with the rapporteur's assessment of the situation and views on providing assistance to libya.
in writing ‒ the situation in libya since 2011, when libyans took to the streets in the so-called arab spring, is still unstable, destabilizing, and the country is in a state of war, with terrorist attacks by the da'esh group on the population on a daily basis. the very presence of daesh in libya is destabilising the country and posing a threat not only to the sahel and sahara neighbours but also to the eu. the fate of libyan migrants, asylum seekers and refugees, whose already intolerable situation is worsening, is also a cause for concern. therefore, the engagement of the un refugee agency and the joint efforts of all eu member states in addressing the situation in libya must focus on the economic reconstruction of libya and on supporting the libyan authorities in the fight against terrorism in order to provide the libyan people with the necessary protection and key economic infrastructure. the eu has provided libya with eur 100 million and stands ready to offer immediate support in areas to be identified as priorities jointly with the newly established libyan government of national unity. i voted in favour of the motion.
‒ island regions have both common and specific characteristics and features which clearly distinguish them from continental regions and therefore require special attention. it is therefore important that the european commission clarifies how it intends to apply the wording of article 174 tfeu in relation to the permanent disadvantage of island regions which impedes their natural development and does not allow them to achieve economic, social and territorial cohesion. i therefore support the european parliament's call for the european commission to present a communication containing a programme for the islands of the european union and subsequently a white paper on monitoring the development of islands, based on best practice and involving local, regional and national authorities and other relevant actors, including the economic and social partners and representatives of civil society.
in writing the island countries belonging to the european union require a special approach because of their special features arising from their location. in order to address the problems of islands and the associated costs in a transparent manner, it is necessary for the commission to identify the permanent geographical, natural and demographic disadvantages of islands which prevent them from achieving economic, social and territorial cohesion. such a definition will be the basis for the elaboration of the eu strategy for the islands.
the island regions are an exceptional contribution to european culture. the historical heritage of europeans and the original way of life are preserved in a special way in these places, representing a kind of entry into european culture. however, these areas are exposed to many obstacles. they face harsh weather conditions and natural disasters, lack of employment opportunities, often live off tourism, which only flourishes in certain seasons, and are now, to a considerable extent, the first point of contact of migrants arriving from the middle east or africa by sea with european soil. the islands, lacking sufficient financial and human resources, have a very difficult time dealing with such serious issues. i agree with the rapporteur that the situation of the islands requires a solution at european level and the commission should adopt instruments to bring about positive change through the establishment of appropriate programmes and financial assistance.
in writing ‒ this particular situation of islands must be taken into account as a natural feature which has a negative impact, directly or indirectly, on the attractiveness of islands and consequently creates obstacles to their sustainable development. this does not offer the same opportunities for these areas as the rest of the european union. i nevertheless abstained from voting on this resolution. i believe that we should focus on all the eu regions where there are specific obstacles that impede their sustainable development.
in writing ‒ the main objectives of cohesion policy are to reduce economic, social and environmental disparities between regions and to achieve polycentric, harmonious development. the island regions are classified as nuts 2 and nuts 3 regions and have permanent and specific features that clearly distinguish them from the landlocked regions. islands face constraints, but also benefit from territorial potential, which should be used as an opportunity for development, growth and job creation. many mediterranean islands are currently experiencing and facing huge numbers of migrants, and a holistic eu approach is needed, including eu support and joint efforts by all member states. it is important for the development of islands to exploit all possible synergies between the european structural and investment funds and other union instruments in order to offset the disadvantage of islands and to improve their situation in terms of economic growth, job creation and sustainable development. i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution because i consider the development of islands and the creation of conditions for their development to be of great importance for regional development.
in writing ‒ the oral question on the conditions of isolation, such as islands and peripheries, affects many member states which feel a certain bias in relation to natural conditions which affect them negatively in relation to other member states. island regions have to contend not only with transport and water supply constraints, but also with lower education levels and the outflow of labour to other, less-favoured regions where there is more scope for employment. i therefore consider it useful to set out clearly the set of disadvantageous conditions, thereby clarifying the conditions which entitle these regions, for example, to receive funding from the european funds. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution.
‒ local and regional authorities play a very important role in the european structural and investment funds because they are closest to citizens and should therefore have the best understanding of their needs. on the other hand, they have limited possibilities and therefore rely on financial and budgetary support to co-finance projects. it is therefore crucial how the european commission intends to support local and regional authorities in the future, in order to strengthen their role and influence in the management and use of the structural funds, in order to maintain and increase economic growth and promote sustainable jobs.
in writing multi-level governance and partnership principles support the promotion of the eu's core policy objectives of economic growth and sustainable development through the involvement of local and regional authorities. local and regional authorities are best placed to know, identify and actively participate in the problems of their regions. in doing so, they are faced with solutions to problems that go beyond their regions. i therefore consider it important to create conditions for cooperation and to strengthen the role of local and regional authorities in the management and implementation of the esi funds.
in writing the importance of local and regional authorities in the use of the structural and investment funds is undeniable. local authorities are best placed to know the shortcomings as well as the prospective areas of a city or region and to know where help is needed. i would point out that the draft resolution mentions the need to strengthen administrative capacity. the lack of skilled workers causes delays and opacity in the procurement processes, which is often why people consider the use of these funds to be inefficient and too demanding. i believe that improving the functioning of local authorities in the area of structural and investment funds can help to reduce the regional disparities that plague many member states.
in writing ‒ in the new programming period 2014-2020, there have been several changes in the allocation of the structural funds. in addition to the creation of common rules for all five cohesion policy funds, more emphasis has been placed on the principle of partnership and multi-level governance. this means that in most cases the local and regional authorities were consulted when negotiating the form of operational programmes for this period. unfortunately, these bodies have not always been accepted as full partners in the debate. i believe that for regional policy to be truly successful, it is absolutely crucial that the views of the people living in the regions themselves are taken into account. i therefore supported the resolution calling for a strengthened role for local and regional authorities in achieving the objectives of cohesion policy. community-led local development initiatives, whose role has also been strengthened during this period, are also of considerable importance. the local community must be clearly involved in improving living conditions at the local level. national governments should therefore strive to increase the administrative capacity of cities and regions to be able to produce effective and long-term projects. local and regional authorities are currently facing a variety of challenges, from globalisation to energy security to increased urbanisation, which the structural and investment funds are designed to address.
‒ strengthening the influence and role of local and regional authorities in the management of the european structural and investment funds can strengthen the economic, social and territorial cohesion of the european union and, in particular, bridge the gap between regions and contribute to the objectives of sustainable and inclusive growth.
in writing. ‒ in its motion for a resolution adopted today, the european parliament expressed its grave concern at the worrisome deterioration of the humanitarian situation in yemen. the situation in yemen also poses a serious risk to the stability of the region, in particular the horn of africa, the red sea and the wider middle east. despite repeated calls for a cessation of hostilities, the previous internal conflict, the saudi-led coalition's airstrikes have intensified, the fighting and bombing have made food supplies insecure, indiscriminate attacks against the civilian population and health and humanitarian workers have been launched, and civilian and medical infrastructure has been destroyed. the report stresses the need for coordinated humanitarian action under the un leadership and urges all countries to participate in meeting humanitarian needs. it further urges all parties to participate as soon as possible, in good faith and without pre-conditions, in a new round of un-led peace negotiations, to resolve their differences through dialogue and consultation, to reject the use of force for political ends, and to refrain from provocation and from any unilateral action that could undermine the political solution.
in writing ‒ the humanitarian situation in yemen remains alarming as the saudi-led coalition has unilaterally withdrawn from the ceasefire agreement and has demonstrably bombed blind and deaf centers in yemen's capital sanaa, as well as chambers of commerce and a school. the rebel siege of taiz continues, with enormous humanitarian consequences for the local civilian population. in addition, the saudi-led coalition ordered the un high commissioner for human rights to leave the country. he must immediately resume peace talks and end coalition bombing and blockade as well as rebel siege of cities.
in writing the current yemen is another sad chapter in the history of the middle east. the civil war eventually grew into a conflict of even greater significance. we can say without any hesitation that the humanitarian situation in yemen is catastrophic. hospitals lack electricity and fuel to run ambulances, and there is a huge shortage of doctors and staff to help the injured. the poor condition of the sewers caused by the bombing can later cause the spread of dangerous diseases. this situation must be resolved unequivocally and without undue delay. first of all, i strongly condemn the fact that some european countries are supplying weapons to yemen. these deliveries must be stopped immediately. it is also necessary to ensure that humanitarian workers are allowed into the country. i agree with the rapporteurs that the only and best possible solution to the whole conflict is a political solution.
mr president, i am very happy that parliament today took the important step of calling the atrocities and mass murders carried out by isis or daesh on christians and other religious minorities genocide. obviously i wholeheartedly supported this. today we gave them a message of hope. it is a historic step. yesterday we not only officially recognised the many crimes carried out by isis or daesh, but we also named them as what they are: genocide. we showed that we see what is going on and that we accept the consequences as well. i would therefore like to draw your attention to very urgent situation in rojava canton, where humanitarian aid is much needed. the turkish and iraqi kurdish borders need to be opened immediately. the whole canton, comprising approximately 2 million people, is at the moment supplied through one border crossing. we do not have a solution yet for solving the whole syrian crisis, but we can at least save 2 million lives.
international law knows the exact criteria by which genocide is judged. it is an act intended to destroy a national, ethnic, racial, or religious group. it includes the deliberate killing of members, inflicting serious physical and psychological harm with intent to physically destroy them. recognising the suffering of christians and other minorities in iraq and syria as genocide is the first step towards the adoption of a security council resolution mandating the international criminal court to investigate and prosecute crimes in this area. given their seriousness, it is important that the european union establishes a special post, represented by a representative, to defend the rights and lives of christians and other religious minorities worldwide. i am very pleased that this proposal has been approved. the resolution adopted is a historic text for this parliament.
in writing. the european parliament's resolution was drafted and adopted in the light of the current situation in syria and iraq. the ep strongly condemns the so-called 'isis/daesh' and its human rights abuses. it urges the un security council to declare these crimes genocide. the ep is concerned that this terrorist group is deliberately targeting christian minorities and sunnis who do not agree with their interpretation of islam. parliament condemned the destruction of religious and cultural sites and objects by isil/daesh. the ep recognises and supports the inalienable right of all ethnic and religious minorities and other persons in iraq and syria to continue to live in dignity, equality and security in their homeland and to practice their religion and beliefs freely, and calls for this right to be respected by all. a declaration by the political and religious leaders of the region supporting their continued presence and rights is essential to prevent the suffering and mass exodus of christians, yazidis and other communities in the region. it calls on the international community to provide the necessary security conditions for those who have been forced to leave their homes. the report calls on the union to establish a permanent special representative on freedom of religion or belief. i supported the ideas in the text.
in writing ‒ since 2014, following the declaration of the caliphate in iraq and syria, isis has posed a threat to the entire world. isis continues to carry out ethnic cleansing and systematic attacks on secular, non-arab and non-sunni muslim communities, as well as sunnis who do not identify with the barbaric and fundamentalist understanding of their religion, in northern iraq, killing or abducting thousands of people and forcing more than one million people to flee the territories it occupies in iraq and syria. i unequivocally condemn all mass killings and other human rights violations committed by isis, regardless of the ethnicity or religious minority of the victims. we cannot turn a blind eye to the deterioration of the situation of women in iraq that has been occurring in parallel with the decline of their country over the past 30 years, with women being trapped between a lack of attention from iraqi society, which has been exacerbated by the presence of isis, and a vision of law enforcement by isis that condemns iraqi women to social exclusion.
in writing freedom of religion and belief is a human right that every democratic country must respect. sadly, in modern history, religious intolerance has led to inhuman acts that society has been unable to prevent. the complex and protracted difficult situation in africa is incomprehensible to many people and reduces confidence in the action and capacity of international organisations, communities and even governments of some member states. it is not possible to give aid on the one hand and to make the situation in these countries worse by promoting the interests of certain groups on the other. i believe it is necessary for all the security and diplomatic forces to come together and, using international law and agreements, to start working on concrete steps that will unite forces regardless of the interests of certain groups. we must prevent further suffering and human slaughter.
in writing we must call the actions of the islamic state in africa and the middle east by their true name: crimes against humanity and genocide. we in europe see the suffering of millions of people through the media, but they have to fight for their bare lives, protect their daughters from sexual violence, run away from home. they lost their possessions, their families, and their hope. the consequences will not be borne only by individuals or religious groups. the islamic state has succeeded in upsetting the character of areas where people of different nationalities or religions have lived in harmony and peace for hundreds of years. so these people who have become refugees today are not a homogeneous group that would be easy to help, but they are mixed christians, shiites, yazidis, and people of other religions, who also come from diverse ethnic backgrounds. i agree that the persons responsible for this situation should be punished in accordance with the un conventions and agreements. the situation needs to be addressed quickly and responsibly, and preparations need to be made for a period of time to help the affected areas after these events have ended.
in writing ‒ the situation of religious minorities living in areas occupied by the islamic state continues to deteriorate. the un, together with other international organisations, continues to report widespread and serious violations of international human rights and humanitarian law. the isil has targeted ethnic and religious minorities in syria and iraq with killings, forced conversions and kidnappings. anyone who disagrees with the radical vision of the is becomes an enemy of their ideology, which serves as a justification for their actions. i therefore agree with the call for the international community and the eu member states to work towards the recognition of the crimes of this terrorist organisation as genocide. there is no other way to describe the actions of a group that does not agree with anything other than a radical interpretation of islam. the group has been involved in the eradication of all religious minorities in the territories under its control. un member states must also comply with their obligations under security council resolutions and prohibit any kind of is aid, from arms supplies to oil trade to financial aid. if individual countries do not act, if they close their eyes to genocide, they will also be violating international law. the gulf states have a major responsibility to step up their efforts to confront is extremist ideology. minorities living in their historic homelands of syria and iraq have an inalienable right to life.
in writing ‒ minorities are the most vulnerable group in any conflict. the attacks on national minorities in syria and iraq are a manifestation of violence, especially against christians. to deny the christian roots of europe would be to deny the culture of europe. it is necessary to condemn this mass murder, not only in words but also in deeds, and in this way to send a signal to christian minorities that we have a responsibility for them in the form of a systemic solution to protect them.
in writing. since its entry, the uk has been a major member of the eu. the uk's continued membership of the eu will benefit not only the eu but also the uk itself. as it is economically closely linked to the eu, i believe that the preservation of the ability to shape european legislation and the other benefits of membership outweigh the counter-arguments. that the eu remains united and strong. in the context of the migration crisis, it is important that eu member states ensure the functioning of the schengen area, but at the same time that all actions are in line with international obligations in the field of refugee law. the stability of both syria and libya remains an eu security interest.
for the ecr group. let me thank the rapporteur, mr becker, for the very balanced proposal we have today, which has the ambition to improve the services provided by eures, while also giving member states the opportunity to retain unpublished posts, for example as part of an active labour market policy programme. but i must say at the outset that it is my wish - and i think it is the wish of many of us - that european union citizens find employment, especially in their own member states, as this is often a sign that the labour market is working, that the country is doing well, that they are not being forced to leave their families for long periods of time to work abroad. on the other hand, there will always be a section of citizens who live close to the border, for example, or simply people who want and need foreign experience for their work. such experience helps, improves language skills, helps skills transfer, but also personal development, and thus ultimately enriches us all. it is therefore desirable that we can support these workers, make it easier for them to find vacancies and help them to find their way around the labour market. it is also important to me personally that we have reached a broad consensus during the negotiations and that the proposal also respects the principles of non-discrimination and that the eures portal will also be accessible to people with disabilities. i believe that an improved eures will be a very concrete and practical tool of assistance for both jobseekers and employers, and that we will be able to bring it to the attention of the widest possible public. written an extraordinary session of the united nations general assembly on drugs (ungass) will be held in vienna from 19 to 21 april 2016. the objectives of the fight against drugs were already set out in the political declaration and action plan adopted in 2009. this action plan aims to significantly reduce or eliminate drug demand and supply. children and young people in general, but also women, pregnant women, ethnic minorities and persons suffering from a combination of mental and physical disorders, are particularly vulnerable and vulnerable to drug use and exploitation in the drug trade. problems related to drug use and trafficking are often defined in urban problem areas. it is therefore necessary to adopt appropriate reintegration measures that offer a viable alternative to young people who have already fallen into drug addiction or become so-called 'child soldiers' in the service of criminal organisations. however, we must recognize that if the fight against drugs is to be successful, we must start with prevention in the family. they are one of the few effective tools in the fight against not only drugs but also juvenile delinquency and other social ills that plague our society. the family, often underestimated, is fighting a successful fight where the state and its resources fail.
