in writing. the european ombudsman has a special role to play in protecting citizens and their fundamental rights. the main task of the independent office is to investigate complaints about maladministration in the work of the eu institutions, such as abuse of powers, discrimination or unjustified delay. in 2014, the european ombudsman dealt with a total of 2163 complaints, of which 325 were initiated. the complaints received are largely related to public access to the documents of the institutions. i think it is important that we pay attention to cases where the ombudsman has found maladministration and take the necessary steps to improve the situation.
in writing. i would like to begin by paying tribute to the ombudsman's work, not only in the year under review but throughout her tenure, in increasing fairness and transparency in the eu. anyone who has read the report will agree that the ombudsman's job is very responsible and not at all easy. it should also be said that it is the european institutions that do not make the ombudsman's job any easier. the report notes that, as in previous years, the majority of inquiries opened by the ombudsman concerned the commission (59,6%) and the number of inquiries concerning other eu institutions, including the ep, opened by the ombudsman in 2014 shows that we are not making her job easier. transparency, openness, access to information, respect for citizens' rights and high ethical standards are essential for the trust of citizens and institutions, especially european institutions, if we are to maintain the trust of the people. i therefore believe that the european institutions, also thanks to the open, innovative and transparent work of the ombudsman, will contribute to greater openness and transparency in their activities with the new edition of the european code of good administrative behaviour.
in writing. ‒ the hague convention of 15 november 1965 allows for service of official documents in another state party. the convention applies only to the cross-border service of official documents originating in or sent to third countries: regulation (ec) no 1393/2007 on the service of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters applies to the cross-border service of official documents within the european union. the hague convention is already applied by 26 of the 28 member states. the remaining two member states, austria and malta, also indicated their intention to join. the convention does not allow for the accession of international organisations. following the adoption of union legislation on the cross-border service of documents, the union has acquired exclusive external competence in this area under article 3 (2) tfeu. this approach has been confirmed by the court. accordingly, the union should authorise the member states concerned to act on its behalf with a view to acceding to the convention. it is in the common interest of the eu and the two member states concerned to have a uniform system for the service of documents in their cross-border relations with third countries. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the hague convention of 15 november 1965 governs the conditions for the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil and commercial matters in signatory states. the convention applies in 26 of the 28 member states. the ep gave its consent to the draft decision allowing austria and malta to accede to the convention. this will create a single system of crossborder delivery with third countries in the member states of the union.
‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament giving its consent to the proposal for a council decision authorising the republic of austria, in the interest of the european union, to sign and ratify the hague convention of 15 november 1965 on the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters and authorising the republic of malta, in the interest of the european union, to accede to that convention.
in writing. ‒ the 1965 hague convention allows for crossborder service of documents in individual signatory states. it concerns the service of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil and commercial matters to third countries outside the eu, as a specific regulation applies to this matter within the eu. the hague convention is now applied by 26 member states, with austria and malta remaining, which have now expressed their wish to accede to the convention. since the convention does not allow for the accession of international organisations, the eu has adopted specific legislation conferring on it exclusive competence by member states in matters of cross-border service of documents. i supported the european parliament's position because it would allow the republic of austria to sign and ratify the hague convention and the republic of malta to accede to the convention. both countries will thus participate in the exchange of letters with third countries under the current european framework.
in writing. ‒ the european union and the republic of san marino signed an agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information on 8 december 2015. the agreement aims to ensure that san marino applies measures equivalent to the union legal framework updated in december 2014. the aim of the agreement is to improve international tax cooperation and compliance with the rules relating to it. the agreement is an important element of the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion, which will allow for the automatic exchange of information between the eu and san marino on the financial accounts of residents of the two states as from 2017. cooperation is intended to resolve situations where taxable persons seek to conceal income or capital representing assets for which tax has not yet been paid. the agreement contributes to strengthening the fight against tax evasion. this type of tax evasion and avoidance adversely affects the income of the union's economies and therefore international cooperation on this matter is justified and important. i voted for the report.
in writing. ‒ the ep voted to approve the conclusion of an amending protocol to the agreement with san marino of 8 december 2015 on the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts. the aim of the agreement is to improve international cooperation and tax compliance and to reduce tax fraud and tax evasion in the signatory countries. the amended protocol will allow the eu and san marino to exchange information on financial accounts of their residents automatically from 2017. this contributes to reducing tax fraud and tax evasion in signatory countries.
in writing ‒ in the case of the vote on the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the conclusion of an amending protocol to the agreement between the european community and the republic of san marino adjusting the arrangements for the taxation of savings income in the form of interest payments, i voted in favour of this resolution. the signature of this amending protocol will allow the implementation of the agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information, which aims to improve international cooperation and compliance in the field of taxation, signed by the european union and san marino in december 2015. the aim is to address situations where the taxpayer attempts to conceal capital in the form of income or property for which tax has not been paid.
in writing. ‒ the events in recent years show that we still have problems with tax evasion in europe. i therefore welcome the agreement between the eu and san marino, which will allow for the exchange of information on financial accounts from 2017. this agreement will help to address situations where the taxpayer attempts to hide capital in the form of income or assets for which he has not paid tax. i supported the agreement because it will result in improved access for member states' tax administrations to data from san marino authorities. the competent authorities of the member states will be able to correctly and unambiguously identify the taxpayers concerned and to enforce the application of tax laws in cross-border situations. they will also be able to investigate the conduct of taxpayers in cases where tax evasion is suspected. and the agreement will also allow member states to avoid further unnecessary investigations. it should be noted that the agreement is fully in line with oecd standards. the information exchanged will thus concern not only income such as interest and dividends, but also the balance of accounts and the proceeds from the sale of financial assets. i believe that this agreement will also have a positive impact on taxing profits where they are generated.
‒ fair taxation and the fight against tax evasion is a topical issue not only in the member states but also at eu level. however, cooperation in this area with third countries is also essential, especially in the area of exchange of information between tax authorities.
in writing ‒ i supported the agreement between the european union and san marino. it will be used by the european union to exchange information on residents' financial accounts with san marino. the main purpose was not only to eliminate instances where people tried to hide their income and assets, but also to bring the automated exchange into line with oecd requirements. i think both goals are right. on the one hand, tax avoidance by abusing another country's system needs to be avoided, but on the other hand, aligning requirements with oecd standards avoids the potential problems of applying two different systems. this is not an isolated case, on the contrary, the european union has already concluded a similar agreement with switzerland or liechtenstein, for example, and others are in preparation. i supported all these agreements and i voted for this one.
in writing. ‒ the treaty of accession of the republic of croatia in 2011 introduced a simplified system for croatia's accession to conventions concluded by member states. annex i to the act of accession lists the conventions and protocols concerned. that list includes the convention of 26 july 1995 on the protection of the european communities' financial interests, the protocols of 27 september 1996 and 29 november 1996 and the second protocol of 19 june 1997 adopted for the purpose of establishing a common fund for the criminal law protection of the ec's financial interests under title vi of the ec treaty. however, in order for croatia to be able to accede to the convention, the parliament must approve the commission's proposal. the ep voted today to take up the commission's proposal.
in writing. ‒ the treaty of accession of the republic of croatia of 2011 provides in a simplified manner that croatia accedes to the conventions and protocols concluded by the member states on the basis of article 34 teu, the list of which is set out in the annex to the treaty of accession. the ep also welcomes the commission's recommendation that the council adopt a decision setting the date of entry into force of these conventions for croatia.
‒ i agree with the convention on the protection of the european communities' financial interests, which has already been signed, and which establishes a common legal basis for criminal law in the protection of financial interests. fraud in respect of revenue and expenditure must be effectively investigated. the investigation shall be carried out in accordance with the principles of proportionality, fairness and transparency. as croatia has joined the european union, i voted to accede to this convention as well.
in writing. ‒ i agreed to endorse the commission's recommendation that croatia accede to the convention on the protection of the financial interests of the union, as this is a standard procedure that every new member state has to go through. the convention on the protection of financial interests was adopted by the member states of the european communities as early as 1995 and is still valid for all countries that are members of the union. the individual protocols which have been subsequently amended are also part of the convention. member states undertake by this convention to ensure that their criminal laws protect the financial interests of the union, since fraudulent activities involving union revenue and expenditure may be organised by criminal networks operating across borders. it is therefore in the common interest of the member states to prevent fraud by adopting legislation which will discourage potential perpetrators from acting. those who exercise management functions in large corporations should also not be exempt from penalties for fraud, as they too bear criminal liability for their decisions. this is one of the reasons why i support croatia's accession to this basic european legal framework.
‒ the protection of the community's financial interests by combating fraud is an eu priority. the accession of the eu's youngest member state will strengthen the eu's capabilities in this area and further deepen european integration.
in writing. ‒ the free choice of employment within the union is an integral part of the right to free movement, one of the four fundamental freedoms of the european union, and thus an important element of eu citizenship. today, there are 23 million unemployed in the eu, and nearly one in five young people are out of work. some regions were hit harder, while others were less so. the solution to this would be to increase the mobility of workers within the union. this is low in relation to the size of the labour market and the active population in the eu, but even in relation to its larger competitors (usa, japan) the eu27 mobility rate is only 0.29%. it is therefore necessary to strengthen labour mobility within the union in order to improve the employment opportunities of workers and to help employers to fill vacancies better and faster. the regulation aims to make the eures network an effective tool for jobseekers and employers, while respecting the competences of the member states in respect of labour market regulation, which remained a national competence. all jobseekers should be provided with comprehensive information on the employment conditions and services at their place of work. the platform should be easily accessible and as user-friendly as possible. i consider it important that member states and the commission should ensure that priority is given to nationals of eu member states in filling vacant posts, in order to achieve eu preference.
in writing. ‒ i support the adoption of a regulation to facilitate labour mobility in the eu. the free movement of workers within the territory of any eu member state is one of the fundamental freedoms in the eu. the introduction of a single platform, the improvement and accessibility of information on job vacancies in all member states, together with job requirements and jobseeker profiles, can significantly help labour mobility and thus higher employment. such a platform can have a significant positive impact, in particular in cross-border regions.
in writing i come from slovakia, a country where we have a very high unemployment rate for a long time. this fact forces many of our people to go abroad. it's a tradition because our ancestors went to distant countries like the united states to find solutions to poverty and deprivation. today, the situation is simpler because there are no restrictions on movement within the european union. workers can move freely, seek work in another eu country and work in that country without a work permit. i consider the eures portal for labour mobility in the eu to be a unique opportunity for jobseekers, as it is free of charge and offers information on living and working conditions in all participating countries. the number of people who visit it every day is huge, which is why i support the reform of this network to increase the number of partners offering mobility services through it. it should be borne in mind, however, that labour policy is a competence of the member states. public administrations, especially ministries, need to improve cooperation with each other to help overcome the obstacles for those who want to find work abroad.
in writing ‒ the free movement of workers is one of the key elements for the development of a more integrated union labour market. every day, more than 1.1 million european citizens living in one of the european union countries cross the border to work in a neighbouring country. the proposed regulation on a european network of employment services, workers' access to mobility services and further integration of labour markets focuses on the reform of the eures network. this reform will make it possible to increase the number of partners offering mobility services through the eures network, as well as to consolidate cooperation between public and private organisations with a view to filling a higher percentage of the total vacancies. that is why i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution because the proposed regulation comes with new proposals that can significantly enhance not only labour mobility within the eu, but also improve job opportunities for workers and create better conditions for employers. i also agree with the proposed regulation because it incorporates new forms of employment that allow greater mobility of workers from areas of high unemployment to areas characterised by labour shortages. i welcome the proposed changes and expansions to the eures (european employment services) network, which is a very effective tool for jobseekers or employers interested in labour mobility within the eu. i agree that the eures network should be extended to include apprenticeships and traineeships, but i would welcome a more significant improvement in the quality of traineeships, particularly as regards the content of education and training and working conditions. i hope that the proposed regulation will also help us to overcome the legal obstacles that workers often face when they want to work in another country.
‒ the free movement of labour within the common market has always been and must remain a fundamental pillar of the eu. the eu and its member states must continue to support labour mobility through transnational partnerships and other instruments.
in writing ‒ one of the eu's four fundamental freedoms is the free movement of labour within the eu. due to high unemployment within some regions, there is a need to strengthen labour mobility. i therefore support this proposal, which transforms the eures network into an effective tool for jobseekers or employers interested in labour mobility within the eu. this will create the widest possible set of job vacancies and jobseeker profiles, including apprenticeships and traineeships. the integration of public and private employment services into the eures network is also an important aspect. by increasing the number of partners offering mobility services within the network, eures will become an effective tool for reducing unemployment across the eu. the remuneration system for these workers will be an important factor in integrating labour markets.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the reform of the eures portal. i was the shadow rapporteur on this report and we tried to find the broadest possible consensus during the negotiations so that the portal was a tool for practical and effective assistance and to link supply and demand across the european union. i think that now that there is free movement of workers in the european union, it is very important that employers and jobseekers have a common place where they can meet and which would make it easier for them to offer or find a job. in a situation where there are large differences in the number of job vacancies between member states, such a portal is a very desirable tool. however, we must not forget that while working abroad broadens horizons, offers new experiences and knowledge, among them particularly highly valued language skills, it should not be the only way people can apply themselves to the labour market. we should always bear in mind that a person who wants to live and work in his native country should have the opportunity to do so there and should not be forced to seek work elsewhere. but if he does, i hope that the improved eures portal will be a useful aid to him.
in writing. ‒ the terrorist attacks in tunisia on 18 march 2015 and in sousse on 26 june 2015 have dealt a severe blow to the already struggling tunisian economy. in this context, the european union wishes to emphasise that it will continue to actively support tunisia's economic development. accordingly, the commission proposes to open a temporary unilateral duty-free tariff quota of 35 000 tonnes per year in the form of autonomous trade measures for exports of olive oil from tunisia to the union without increasing the total import volume. the tariff quota in question will be available for a period of two years from 1 january 2016 to 31 december 2017 and will become available after the exhaustion of the duty-free tariff quota of 56 700 tonnes currently in force, as set out in the association agreement between the union and tunisia. if the new quota would harm the commercial interests of the member states or have a negative impact on the internal market, the union shall be entitled to take the necessary steps to eliminate it. i was in favor of the solution.
in writing. ‒ the deteriorating security situation in tunisia caused by terrorist attacks has had a negative impact on the country's economy. in order to stimulate the economy, the european union will provide tunisia with assistance in the form of a single zero-duty tariff for olive oil exports of 35 000 tonnes per year from tunisia to the eu in 2016/2017. the olive oil industry employs one million people, one fifth of the jobs in tunisian agriculture.
tunisia is a long-standing partner of the eu, with the first trade cooperation agreement between the two partners dating back to 1969. the eu-tunisia free trade negotiations, which started in 2015, are the culmination of this long-standing cooperation. agreements of this type not only contribute to the economic improvement of both contracting parties but also to the strengthening of other relations between them and are therefore always very welcome. i very much appreciate the political situation in tunisia, which is a model for all the surrounding countries. despite the positive political situation, tunisia faces many challenges, mainly stemming from regional disparities and conflicts in neighbouring countries. in this area too, an eu-tunisia agreement could contribute to stability and consolidate democracy. despite the positive aspects of the agreement, i would like to call again for european standards to be respected, particularly in regulating those areas that affect the food industry and human health.
in writing ‒ i voted in favour of the commission offering a temporary unilateral zero-rate tariff quota of 35 000 tonnes per year for the next two years for the export of olive oil from tunisia to the union. this concrete commitment to promote economic development in partnership with the tunisian people also supports the process of democratic change in tunisia.
in writing ‒ in the light of the terrorist attacks in tunisia on 18 march last year, which have seriously damaged the tunisian economy, i have decided to support the report on the proposal for a zero-rate unilateral tariff quota for the export of 70 000 tonnes of olive oil from tunisia to the european union over a period of two years. olive oil is tunisia's most exported agricultural product and this specific measure will therefore make a significant contribution to the recovery of the country's economic development. this is a positive boost for the economy of tunisia, where the olive oil sector employs more than one million people, representing 1/5 of the total number of jobs in the agricultural sector. at the same time, this provision is also of a political nature, which supports the process of democratic change in the country.
in writing ‒ i voted in favour of this temporary emergency trade measure with respect to tunisia. tunisia is the only country in the middle east and north africa region that has successfully managed the process of democratic and political transition. it therefore serves as an example for other countries. as the tourism sector in sousse has suffered greatly as a result of the terrorist attack in june 2015, assistance from the european union is needed. i think that the new temporary duty-free quotas for olive oil are the right instrument, as olive oil is tunisia's main export item to the eu. the european union has thus shown its appreciation for the political transition in tunisia and its willingness to provide rapid assistance to sustain the economy and employment, as the sector creates more than one million jobs. that's why i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade. this is the first application to be examined under the 2016 budget and concerns the mobilisation of a total of eur 1 095 544 from the egf for the benefit of belgium. the request concerns 412 dismissed workers and approximately 100 unemployed young people not in education or training. according to the belgian authorities, the redundancies were the result of developments in the european glass industry, and in particular in the belgian glass industry, which had a significant impact on the glass production in wallonia in recent years. the ep committee on budgets, having regard to the opinions of the committee on employment and social affairs and the committee on regional development, has concluded that the application meets the conditions for a financial contribution from the egf on the basis of the relevant provisions of the egf regulation and is therefore eligible.
in writing. ‒ the belgian company in question, which produces other non-metallic mineral products, applied for aid to reintegrate 412 redundant workers into the labour market. the applicant fulfilled the conditions for granting the aid. this is the first call for the mobilisation of the egf in 2016. the ep therefore approved the allocation of eur 1 095 544 to belgium, representing 60% of the total cost of measures to reintegrate redundant workers.
in writing ‒ in the case of the european parliament resolution on the application of the european globalisation adjustment fund to a request from the belgian company hainaut-namur glass, i voted against the resolution in line with the position of the committee of the regions. i believe it is important to design policies that help to increase employment and create jobs. at the same time, however, i share the view of the epp group that the european globalisation adjustment fund is not the right and adequate instrument for this purpose.
in writing. ‒ the release of funds from the globalisation adjustment fund will help 412 redundant workers in the glass industry in belgium. i agree that these financial resources should be used to train and retrain these workers, as they are in a situation that is a consequence of global economic pressures. the european glass industry has in recent years had to cope with strong competition from chinese and japanese products. excess production capacity in asia has been blamed for the price depression in europe, which led to a 32% decrease in employment in the glass industry in europe between 2000 and 2010. the commission also found that the union industry was not able to recover from the injury suffered by the union industry. the vast majority of redundant workers are men, and up to a quarter of them are over 55 years old. i therefore welcome the fact that the belgian government is also trying to contribute in this way to the future employment of these people. for these workers, the fund has allocated over eur 1 million for a variety of personalised services that should help them acquire skills that they can use outside the threatened glass industry.
‒ globalization is a phenomenon that has been going on for decades. we can all benefit from more open world trade and better use of comparative advantage. the eu should also focus on areas where it is comparatively best. at the same time, however, it is important that the eu continues to support sectors and workers in member states that have lost competitiveness as a result of globalisation.
in writing ‒ i voted against the report on the request for mobilisation of the globalisation adjustment fund by hainaut namur glass, a belgian company. while i support measures to create growth and jobs and measures to help people who have lost their jobs, the globalisation adjustment fund is not the right instrument in my view. although the fund itself provides funding for active measures to help the surplus workers to find employment, there are no thorough analyses of the impact of the fund's assistance that would give sufficient comparative results. i think that because it has not yet been demonstrated that the fund generates sufficient added value, and with the help of the funds currently being spent on the fund, we could find more effective solutions for the redundant workers.
in writing. ‒ since the crisis, the number of private and public investments has varied across member states. the examination of the semester files showed that investment continues to be hampered by both regulatory and non-regulatory challenges. i consider it important that identifying and addressing challenges to investment should be part of efforts to improve framework conditions, reduce administrative barriers and eliminate regulatory bottlenecks. it is positive that the european commission has started to re-explore the policy areas and tools that can provide an overview of the main challenges that are holding back investment at national level in this semester cycle. however, the analysis of the main challenges summarised in the country-specific briefings should be continued in the context of the european semester, in particular in the country reports. it is time to re-launch dialogue with member states - including in the form of thematic discussions within the council and its committees - in order to identify these challenges and possible steps and measures to overcome them, otherwise the european semester process will not be able to fulfil the role it was intended to play when it was set up. i supported the report.

‒ i supported the european semester report because i believe that in the current situation of economic recession we need to ask ourselves some fundamental questions about how to improve the coordination of the economic policies of the individual member states. in the near future, europe will face important decisions on fiscal, monetary and structural policies. we will have to decide how to better coordinate the policies of the euro area countries and how to make decisions on the future of the euro more democratic. if citizens expect a stronger economic recovery and the creation of quality jobs with equal opportunities, we need to address the structural challenges of our economies, especially at european level. europe is facing global economic pressures to which it could respond more flexibly if there were greater agreement among member states on the direction of the union. recovery remains uneven across countries, and is often affected by external factors such as low oil prices. and we also have a lack of investment in europe, even though the current account surplus is increasing. as the 2008 crisis has proven to be not only cyclical but also predominantly structural, major structural reforms will be needed, but this requires a greater willingness of member states to seek common solutions to economic challenges.
in writing ‒ despite the gradual recovery of economic growth in the eu, some member states continue to struggle with the impact of the recession. europe still faces a number of challenges, including lack of investment and unemployment. sustainable public finances and investment in science and research are the foundations of economic stability and create the conditions for further growth.
in writing ‒ this report is parliament's contribution to defining the priorities of economic policies, while at the same time encouraging the strengthening of the democratic character of european economic governance. the report also aims to stimulate debate at european level, involving national parliaments and civil society, on three main themes: the combination of fiscal, monetary and structural policies; policy coordination at euro area level; and ensuring better implementation of recommendations. as a result of the long-term economic crisis, citizens are demanding a stronger economic recovery, quality jobs and a return to equality of opportunity. however, to boost economic growth, domestic demand needs to be strengthened, which of course requires greater investment from both the private and public sectors. however, the promotion of potential growth must be achieved through the elimination of inequalities, the efficient use of public expenditure and more effective tax collection linked to the prevention of tax evasion. at national level, thorough parliamentary discussions with commissioners and national governments will be key, based on the euro area recommendation, the european council conclusions, the european commission's country reports and the country-specific recommendations. i supported this report because it emphasises the strengthening of democracy in the interests of greater accountability and the need for higher investment given their low interest rates, which is particularly important given the high level of public and private debt.
i regret to say that this report on the growth of the european union is pure schizophrenia, and that is why i voted against it. the report criticizes undeclared work while proposing measures that make it more difficult and costly to get legal employment. the report calls for a policy of real growth while proposing to increase the rate of redistribution. the report criticises the level of debt, while proposing many measures that increase it even more. and the report notes that unemployment is high in the european union, and at the same time proposes to raise the minimum wage. that's simply not how economic policy works. we can write a lot of different reports here for a long, long time, but the real economy works by getting more freedom, less redistribution and less low taxes.

in writing. ‒ the single market governance report is one of the three parliamentary reports on the 2016 european semester. the crisis has shown that europe needs to take steps to improve its economic model and restore its competitiveness. this requires both public funding and targeted investments. however, the potential of the single market is not being realised at present. the union should support member states to significantly increase cross-border trade and to act urgently to make better use of digital technologies. to be a driver of growth and jobs, the eu needs to strengthen its governance of the single market. this requires the reintroduction of the highest level of political oversight, the harmonisation of the transposition and implementation of eu rules, and the development of more effective means to ensure that the single market truly benefits citizens and businesses. the most important thing we need to do now is to review the functioning of the single market in the context of the europe 2020 strategy. it is necessary to look at where progress has been made and to map out the difficulties and, on this basis, to define policy priorities. i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ the european ombudsman was re-elected by parliament in december 2014. the ombudsman reports annually on his activities, and the parliamentary report welcomed the report. the ombudsman's work contributes to bringing the institutions closer to the citizen. parliament welcomed the fact that the ombudsman had placed transparency at the heart of his work as a guarantee of good administration. the ombudsman deals with complaints of maladministration in the eu institutions and with their redress. its activities cover the topics of transparency, fundamental rights, ethical issues, citizen participation in eu decision-making and eu programmes. i would stress that interfering in the eu legislative process is not within the ombudsman's remit. the number of complaints outside its remit received by its office was twice as high as the number of complaints actually concerning it, which shows the need to inform citizens about their rights in as many languages as possible. in 2014, the ombudsman launched a consultation and then made recommendations to the institutions concerned in order to make the european citizens' initiative work more simply and transparently. the ombudsman examined ex officio the respect for fundamental rights in the member states' implementation of cohesion policy. in 2014, the european commission was the subject of the most ombudsman inquiries (204). the majority of complaints received concerned access to information and documents. proposals to improve the union's administration were implemented by 80% of the institutions. i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ the european ombudsman's office is a means of protecting persons resident or established in the union from maladministration by eu institutions and bodies. in 2014, the current ombudsman identified maladministration in 39 closed cases and issued 12 draft recommendations. as a last resort, the ombudsman may draw up and submit to the ep a special report to remedy any failure by the eu institutions and bodies to respect previous recommendations. in 2014, the ombudsman did not submit any such special report to the ep.

in writing. ‒ parliament gave its consent today to the possible conclusion of comprehensive free trade agreements between the eu and australia and between the eu and new zealand. australia and new zealand are among the eu's oldest and closest partners. the parliament's report adopted today lists the issues on which the european commission believes it should focus during the negotiations. the report stresses that ambitious agreements between the three advanced economies in question should reasonably address investment, trade in goods and services, e-commerce, public procurement, energy, state-owned enterprises, competition, anti-corruption, regulatory issues such as sanitary and phytosanitary restrictions, technology research and, in particular, the needs of small and medium-sized enterprises. it further notes that agriculture is a highly sensitive sector and that, in order to achieve a balanced outcome in the final chapters on agriculture and fisheries, the interests of all european producers, namely meat, milk, sugar, cereals and textiles producers, as well as those of the outermost regions, should be duly taken into account, for example by introducing transitional periods and appropriate quotas or by not making any commitments in the most sensitive sectors in these chapters. i consider it important that the report calls for the inclusion of effective bilateral safeguards to prevent a sudden increase in imports which would seriously damage the interests of european producers in sensitive sectors.
in writing. ‒ the european union is australia and new zealand's third most important trading partner. these are countries characterised by strong rule of law, respect for human and social rights, and strong protection of nature and the environment. i support the opening of negotiations on free trade agreements with these countries, which will be based on mutual partnership, mutual benefit and reciprocity. the agreements will facilitate trade and market access, especially for small and medium-sized enterprises, and thus help to promote economic growth in eu member states.
in writing despite their great distance from europe, australia and new zealand are very close to the european union. we are united not only by our joint solutions to problems and cooperation in various fields, but above all by the values that make us partners and friends. european values are also reflected in the character of these countries. these are states where respect for law and freedom comes first. they are strong states of law with which i welcome the conclusion of agreements. agreements can bring the european union many benefits in terms of trade and economic regulation. of course, as with any free trade agreement, all the provisions agreed must be in line with our common values while respecting european standards and rules. i support these measures, but on the condition of strict transparency! there's an old truth, as thomas mann wrote: "be free to make deals, but only so that you can sleep well at night".

in writing. pets are now part of the lives of many eu citizens and families, and animal husbandry is also a responsibility to preserve the welfare and health of the animals that contribute positively to our lives. animal husbandry is linked to the controlled and safe movement of animals within the union, which can also act as a deterrent to illegal trade. it is regrettable that the pet transport system is increasingly being abused illegally for commercial purposes. the improvements to the pet animal travel regime introduced by regulation (eu) no 576/2013 have brought about positive changes which can be implemented after the adoption of the animal health regulation. the parliament's report calls on the commission to take effective action against illicit trafficking. it also calls on the commission to publish the conclusions of the study on the welfare of dogs and cats affected by the commercial practices, which could help to resolve the problems in a professional manner. a solution at union level is needed for systems on means and methods of identification and registration of pet animals. identification and registration requirements for dogs and cats would reduce document fraud and illegal trade, improve animal welfare, protect public and animal health, and allow for effective traceability within the union; in order to achieve the above objectives, i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ i support the introduction of uniform pan-european requirements for the registration of pet animals in the member states. the identification and registration of animals, together with the owners' data, while protecting personal data, will contribute to the eradication of illegal trade in animals, their protection and the protection of life and public health.
the schengen area is a great asset for europe's economy, but it also carries risks, as has been fully demonstrated in this case. schengen allows the movement of animals without controls. inadequately regulated rules lead to illegal trade in animals, which in turn results in concerns for the health and safety of animals and people who come into contact with them. the report that 70 percent of the new diseases that have appeared in humans in recent years are of animal origin is alarming. we must ensure that animals are vaccinated and kept in appropriate conditions. the requirements for the identification of cats and dogs should be clearly harmonised. i welcome this proposal, as the commission has sufficiently examined the living conditions of dogs and cats that are the subject of trade.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution because it is necessary to introduce compatible systems of pet registration in the member states. pet animals that are trafficked illegally are often kept in poor conditions, with insufficient socialisation and at increased risk of disease. up to 70% of new human diseases that have emerged in recent decades are of animal origin, and animals commonly kept as companion animals are carriers of many zoonoses, including rabies. many member states already have some level of requirements for the registration or identification of pet animals, but most of them are not compatible and there is no possibility of monitoring the free movement of animals in the eu. compatible identification and registration systems for dogs and cats would limit the scope for document forgery and illegal trade, thus also contributing to improving animal welfare and protecting public and animal health.
in writing ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on the introduction of compatible pet registration systems. in the european union, we have free movement of people without frontiers, and so there are many people who want to take their pets with them on holiday, for example. however, in view of the possible transmission of various diseases, but also of the growing crime curve associated with the illegal trade in animals, it is necessary that these movements of animals take place in a controlled and safe manner. the measures which the european parliament called for in this resolution are in the interests of the people of the european union, since statistically many human diseases are of animal origin and harmonised databases would help to prevent and protect public health more effectively. on the other hand, the new rules would also be in the interests of animal welfare. unfortunately, illegal trade is associated with a lack of knowledge of the condition of animals or a lack of care for them, which could be more easily traced and prevented if the movements were traceable.
in writing. ‒ in its motion for a resolution adopted today, the european parliament expressed its grave concern at the worrisome deterioration of the humanitarian situation in yemen. the situation in yemen also poses a serious risk to the stability of the region, in particular the horn of africa, the red sea and the wider middle east. despite repeated calls for a cessation of hostilities, the previous internal conflict, the saudi-led coalition's airstrikes have intensified, the fighting and bombing have made food supplies insecure, indiscriminate attacks against the civilian population and health and humanitarian workers have been launched, and civilian and medical infrastructure has been destroyed. the report stresses the need for coordinated humanitarian action under the un leadership and urges all countries to participate in meeting humanitarian needs. it further urges all parties to engage in a new round of un-led peace negotiations as soon as possible, in good faith and without pre-conditions, to resolve their differences through dialogue and consultation, to reject the use of force for political ends, and to refrain from provocation and any unilateral action that could undermine the political solution.
in writing. ‒ yemen is one of the poorest countries in the world with the fastest growing population, which has doubled in the last twenty years. lack of education with high unemployment, economic, social disparities, and religious intolerance coupled with poverty have been and are breeding grounds for internal unrest and violence. this facilitates the violent activities of terrorist groups and organisations. as a result of the protracted crisis, yemen has become one of the countries with the highest number of internally displaced persons. in addition to the difficult access to food, the population is particularly threatened by the lack of healthcare. this, combined with the harsh sanitary and climatic conditions, can hasten the emergence of epidemics. the european union cannot underestimate the situation in yemen. it must therefore, in relation to yemen, promote the necessary measures, in particular through diplomatic channels, so that a ceasefire is concluded and the refugee crisis in the eu is not further complicated.
in writing the civil war in yemen is another blow to the middle east. today, we can literally say that the middle east is burning in the flames of war and violence. hospitals lack electricity and fuel to run ambulances, and there is a huge shortage of doctors and staff to help the injured. the poor condition of the sewers caused by the bombing can later cause the spread of dangerous diseases. this situation must be resolved unequivocally and without undue delay. first of all, i strongly condemn the fact that some european countries are supplying weapons to yemen. these deliveries must be stopped immediately. it is also necessary to ensure that humanitarian workers are allowed into the country. i agree with the rapporteurs that the only and best possible solution to the whole conflict is a political solution. the situation calls for a swift solution. the world can no longer stand by and watch children, women and old people die.
in writing ‒ the security situation in yemen is deteriorating. the situation needs to be resolved primarily politically, with peace and the territorial integrity of yemen preserved. however, there are also concerns about continued human rights violations, including attacks on journalists and media institutions, disappearances, violations of the convention against torture, persecution and imprisonment of religious minorities, and the alleged use of children in armed conflict. these acts need to be thoroughly investigated and remedied.
in writing. ‒ the in yemen, up to 82% of the population, or 21.2 million people, are currently in need of humanitarian assistance. it is estimated that up to 2.1 million people are currently malnourished, including 1.3 million children who suffer from severe acute malnutrition. the situation in yemen also poses serious risks to stability in the region. the need for coordinated humanitarian action under un leadership involving all eu member states, but also developed countries of the world, must therefore be directed towards the immediate provision of food, medicine, fuel and other essential needs for the yemeni people, in accordance with the principles of neutrality, neutrality and independence. in order for this assistance to reach the yemeni people, it is essential that the attacks on civilian infrastructure, in particular on medical facilities and water systems, cease immediately. in parallel, it is necessary to involve all parties to the conflict in a new round of un-led peace negotiations without preconditions in order to resolve differences through dialogue and consultation, rejecting acts of violence in order to achieve the political objectives of establishing peace and stability in yemen and the region.
in writing ‒ despite an international ban on the use of cluster munitions, these weapons have been used in yemen under the leadership of saudi arabia, leading to a catastrophic deterioration of the humanitarian situation in the country. the main victims are the civilian population, who are still living in difficult conditions. food shortages and severe malnutrition are signals for immediate action to halt this worsening humanitarian situation. the situation in health care is particularly alarming, with dozens of hospitals and ambulances in 18 of yemen's 22 districts closed or severely restricted due to fighting or fuel shortages, according to save the children. it should therefore be recalled that hospitals and medical staff are protected under international humanitarian law and therefore their activities must not be disrupted. i would welcome coordinated humanitarian action under the auspices of the un and improved safety for all peacekeepers, humanitarian workers, doctors and journalists, and i therefore support the motion for a resolution.

in writing the first rules governing animal health in europe were laid down in the 1960s. the emergence of new problems and diseases therefore naturally requires updated legislation capable of meeting the challenges of the present. it is desirable that the eu has a comprehensive system for the prevention, detection and control of animal diseases, as well as a common strategy to address safety risks related to health, food and feed. the current legislation, which is made up of some 50 directives and regulations, is complex and requires simplification in the form of a single piece of legislation laying down clear rules governing animal health issues. it is also necessary to lay down uniform rules for veterinarians and farmers who play an important role in the field of animal health, as well as to specify obligations relating to notification and surveillance, the introduction of specific rules for vaccination and control measures, the import and export of animals, or resource efficiency. it is important that the union is united in this area as well and that member states follow the same procedures in the event of an emergency, when a rapid and coherent response is required. i therefore agree with the proposal as it stands.

in writing ‒ the new animal health regulation is to replace some 40 different regulations, thus not only bringing greater clarity to the legislation but also updating many currently outdated regulations and bringing them into line with the latest scientific knowledge. the new legislation is based on binding rules for animal owners as well as traders, based on the principle of animal welfare but also on the very important link between animal health and public health. this concerns two priority areas. not only are many diseases transmissible from animals to humans, but the thoughtless and irresponsible use of antibiotics in animals contributes significantly to the rise of antimicrobial resistance. the legislation therefore encourages the responsible use of veterinary medicines and introduces registration of professional keepers and dealers to control communicable diseases more effectively. although we did not vote in plenary to accept this new amendment as a whole, we did vote on the amendment proposed by the political group which had requested that it be rejected. however, as i believe that updating and replacing non-transparent legislation is the right move, i voted against the political group's proposal to reject this legislation.

in writing ‒ consumption of fresh fruit and vegetables is declining, especially among children. thus, the prevalence of obesity among children is increasing as a result of unhealthy eating habits, as foods high in sugar, fat and additives are preferred. therefore, it is necessary to provide assistance in the form of consumption promotion of selected products, thus contributing to the promotion of healthy eating habits in our children.
‒ i supported the report proposing to merge the two projects, school fruit and school milk. these projects have already been successfully implemented in the past in most member states and it was decided to combine them under one scheme in particular in order to increase efficiency and reduce the administrative burden. in addition to these benefits, the new proposal also extends the range of products to be offered to children in schools, in particular by allowing member states to include local, regional or national specialities such as honey or, in southern european countries, olives. another innovation in the joint scheme is lactose-free products, which were included in response to the growing percentage of children suffering from lactose intolerance. in addition to the distribution of milk, milk products and fruit, these projects also included so-called accompanying measures to help build a positive attitude towards healthy eating among children through various educational activities. and while i think that children should be taught proper eating habits primarily at home, i hope that the project will help to increase the rapidly declining consumption of fruit and milk among school-age children and reduce the growing problem of childhood obesity in europe.
in writing. ‒ the eu regulation/proposal establishing a framework for access to the market for port services and financial transparency in ports aims to contribute to a more efficient and sustainable operation of the ten-t by creating a framework that improves the functioning of ports and helps them to adapt to changed transport and logistics requirements. the objectives of the commission's proposal include modernising port services and operations and establishing a framework to attract port investment. in addition, the commission aimed to offset the low level of competition and possible market abuse. the proposal is in line with the white paper on transport, the european network financing facility and the blue zone initiative. the regulation will apply to all sea ports identified in the ten-t guidelines. the parliament's report supports the commission's proposal, in particular the aspects relating to financial transparency. the ep proposes that the regulation should only cover services offered directly to port users and also proposes an amendment to port charges to allow port operators to set charges autonomously in line with their business strategy. in the interests of modernisation, i voted in favour of the report.
‒ maritime ports are important centres of the trans-european transport network (ten-t), centres of services, trade and hence sources of employment and economic growth. however, the challenges of globalisation have also affected their activities and their status. i support the commission's proposal, which will help to increase the legal certainty of ports, help to improve their performance, make transport and logistics more efficient and at the same time contribute to the financial transparency of these entities.
in writing ports are essential gateways linking europe with the rest of the world. they play an important role in the exchange of goods between the mainland and the island parts, making them indispensable for the functioning of the eu internal market. european ports are generally known for their quality, supporting the development of international trade and generating employment by employing over one and a half million workers. in spite of this, ports often have to deal with problems such as a lack of infrastructure or a low level of service, which in turn imposes increased costs on both carriers and end-users. the ten-t guidelines, together with the cef financial instrument, which allocated €26 billion to improve infrastructure within the eu, aimed to kick-start growth and competitiveness within the union's single market. however, the current wording of the legislative proposal for a regulation does not, in my view, sufficiently address the risk of possible distortions of competition and the free market in the area of access to the market for services provided by ports, nor the rules governing the granting of state aid. i also believe that a regulation as drafted would potentially represent an additional administrative burden for ports that are not currently facing more serious problems. for the reasons stated, i vote against the motion.
in writing. ‒ the proposal, which i support, aims to enable safe and environmentally friendly port operations, which it seeks to achieve by establishing a well-functioning and transparent framework. the report calls for compliance with and monitoring of minimum requirements such as the professional qualifications of service providers and the technical equipment necessary to provide a quality service. i also agree with the autonomous but transparent setting of port charges, which also contributes to the creation of natural competitiveness in this sector.
‒ i support the report on the draft regulation on the functioning of ports and port services because i believe that the negotiators have managed to reach an agreement that does not put port workers at a disadvantage. the regulation will not directly affect social and labour standards for port workers, but will require that these workers are sufficiently trained in their working conditions. we also call for the creation of training manuals on how to prevent accidents and ensure the greatest possible safety and health of port workers. in addition, the report stresses the need to preserve the right to strike in all circumstances. overall, the proposal aims to improve the performance of all ports and help them cope with changing transport and logistics requirements. the proposal also aims to modernise port services and operations and to create a framework to attract investment to ports. the commission also seeks to counteract weak competitive pressure and possible market abuse by this proposal, thereby increasing the efficiency of port services. as each member state has its own specific practice in setting rules for ports and port services, i am pleased that the regulation leaves sufficient freedom to the national regulatory authorities. at the same time, i believe that the regulation will contribute to the creation of legal certainty for ports and will have a positive impact on the functioning of the trans-european transport networks.
‒ european ports have a great potential to create a competitive environment on the world market and to offer jobs to many people. however, a number of problems persist in the maritime transport sector in the longer term. in particular, a significant simplification of the customs regime will be key, which will ultimately bring a significant economic advantage over competition.
in writing. ‒ inflation is measured in a harmonised way in the member states by means of harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicps). the current regulation on the hicp dates from 1995: changes in consumer price statistics have necessitated a revision of the framework in order to ensure maximum comparability for the main users of the hicp. the commission proposal for a regulation establishes a uniform framework for the development, production and publication of harmonised indices of consumer prices and house prices (hicps and hpis respectively) at union, national and sub-national level. the hicp allows the measurement of inflation, which provides valuable information on, among other things, the deflation of economic values such as wages, pensions and interest rates, and thus forms the basis for economic and monetary policy decisions. it is therefore important that those statistics are objective and comparable across member states and product categories. quality statistics are a public good of fundamental importance for all union citizens, researchers and those responsible for union public policy. the draft report recommends that euro area member states submit hicp flash estimates on a monthly basis and that the breakdown of hicp, ooh and hpi flash estimates be adopted by means of implementing acts. in addition, the commission should prepare a report to the european parliament and the council every five years assessing the results of the pilot studies. i supported the report in the interests of a better functioning of the single market.
in writing ‒ the current regulation on harmonised indices of consumer prices has been in force since 1995 and therefore needs to be thoroughly revised, as we need to be able to ensure maximum comparability for the main users in view of the new developments in statistics and, not least, the change in the decision-making processes of the european union following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. i therefore support the european commission's proposal in question.
in writing ‒ the proposed regulation establishes a common framework for the development, production and publication of harmonised indices of consumer prices and of residential property prices at union, national and regional level. these single comparable indices, which are recorded statistically, will serve as a priority basis for the preparation of forecasts and concrete measures necessary for further development.
in writing the existence of a harmonised eu-wide consumer price index is essential, as consumer price indices are one of the main indicators of countries' overall price stability. the purpose of their harmonisation is to ensure comparability of indices within the member states of the union, comparability of price stability, inflation and the state of monetary policy in the euro area countries. the harmonised index of consumer prices is an important tool for the functioning of economic and monetary union, as the measurement of the rate of inflation subsequently affects the level of wages, interest rates or rents. by tracking the causes of inflation, indexes can predict the impact of future tax changes on inflation, which is an important aspect for european households. the legislative proposal aims to establish a single framework for the development, production and publication of data on harmonised consumer price indices and housing price indices, thereby providing a reliable information basis for economic and monetary policy decision-making at the level of the union, its member states and regions. i therefore support the proposal.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the report on harmonised indices of consumer prices, the primary aim of which is to establish a common european legal framework for the development, production and publication of harmonised indices of consumer and housing prices. this would not only be viable at union level, but also at national and sub-national level. the introduction of this system could also have an impact on important policy decisions, as it would make it possible to measure inflation in each member state in order to obtain objective, unbiased and, above all, comparable results.
in writing ‒ i agreed to the new adjustment to harmonised consumer prices because it is mainly an update of the statistical methodology. the current regulation on harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicps) dates from 1995 and was also revised to take account of changes in eu decision-making following the adoption of the treaty of lisbon. this regulation will establish a single legal framework for the development, production and publication of hicp data as well as for housing price indices. the hicp serves as a measure of inflation, used inter alia as an important input for deflationary economic values, which include wages, rents or interest rates. this means that this index forms the basis for the economic and monetary policy decisions of the union and it is therefore desirable that statistics are objective, impartial and comparable. in addition, this statistical index provides information on price stability and is therefore essential to address macroeconomic disparities across the eu. i believe that this measure will allow us to obtain more accurate, unbiased statistics in the future and thus avoid a financial crisis similar to that of 2008.
in writing ‒ the primary purpose of harmonised consumer prices is to measure inflation in all member states. however, their legislation, as laid down in regulation no 2494/95, does not respond adequately to technical progress and current needs. i therefore welcome the union's action in the form of a new regulation which will ensure that harmonisation is in line with the latest knowledge in the field.
‒ i supported the report on the proposal for a regulation on harmonised indices of consumer prices. harmonised indices of consumer prices are important for several reasons. first, they provide important information on price stability within the european union, monitor the effects of monetary policy and measure inflation with high accuracy. it is therefore important that these statistics are objective, impartial and comparable across the european union. given that the existing legislation on consumer price indices could be described as rather complex and, in a sense, as it did not reflect the changes introduced by the lisbon treaty also as outdated, this revision of the legislation in the interests of simplification and updating was widely supported.
‒ the 2014 annual report on the protection of the european union's financial interests in the fight against fraud reveals a number of failures. in the area of detection and reporting of irregularities, the total amount of irregularities reported corresponds to approximately eur 3,24 billion. the european commission must take full responsibility for recovering funds unduly paid from the european union budget and put more pressure on member states to collect data and information. the information on the loss of vat revenue and estimated losses in the collection of vat is also worrying. the european commission will have to find a way and create a mechanism to motivate businesses to pay taxes regularly and not to evade their obligations. i consider it very bad news that there are still breaches of public procurement rules. member states must urgently transpose into national law the directive on public procurement, which makes electronic procurement compulsory and introduces a monitoring and reporting obligation in order to reduce procurement fraud and other serious irregularities.
in writing ‒ the protection of financial interests and the effective fight against fraud are directly linked to the trust of the public in the eu and its institutions. corruption alone accounts for €120 billion a year in the eu. the financial expression of fraudulent and non-submarine irregularities notified to the commission in 2014 increased by 36% compared to 2013. the total number of irregularities notified to the commission in 2014 was 16473, of which 1 649 were fraudulent, corresponding to eur 538,2 million. these figures are too high to speak of an effective fight against corruption. i think it is necessary to adopt simplified rules on the management of resources. complicated rules lead to misinterpretations and unnecessary irregularities and damage. all rules intended to increase transparency in the management of public finances must be clear, understandable and not subject to speculative interpretation. it is also necessary to increase and make more effective controls, to strictly enforce accountability and to regularly inform the public of these findings and measures. this will also have a positive effect on prevention.
in writing the protection of the eu's financial interests is one of the main principles of the union's functioning. the efficient, transparent and orderly management of european finances is a prerequisite for eu citizens' trust in the european institutions and their identification with the idea of european integration. at a time when all member states must necessarily participate in the consolidation of public budgets in the interests of financial sustainability, it is particularly important to prevent any waste and fraudulent activities (illegal and illicit trade, smuggling, money laundering, corruption, non-transparent public procurement, etc.) with eu funds, and all necessary measures must be taken in this regard. the european anti-fraud office (olaf), europol, eurojust, customs authorities and market surveillance authorities have a key role to play in this area and better coordination of their activities must be ensured, as well as enhanced cooperation between member states and the commission in preventing, detecting and combating fraud. a clear distinction must be made between fraud and non-fraudulent irregularities in the handling of european finances, and harmonisation of the definition of irregularities at member state level and of the processes for their detection and reporting are therefore necessary. i therefore fully support the motion for a resolution on the annual report in this form.
in writing. ‒ fraud, corruption and other irregularities have serious consequences for the european union. for example, facilitating the financing of organised crime and terrorist networks, and financial losses of around eur 3,24 billion per year. the situation is deteriorating year by year, which is why i regard as particularly important the report on the 2014 report on the financial protection of the european union and the fight against fraud, which parliament adopted today by a large majority. we have been talking about the creation of a common european public prosecutor's office for years and i think it is high time that concrete steps were taken to this end. i also believe that it is essential to improve the exchange of information between member states, and for this we need common definitions and rules on key issues such as reporting corruption or protecting whistleblowers.
‒ whereas sound public spending and the protection of the eu's financial interests should be key elements of eu policies aimed at enhancing citizens' confidence by ensuring the sound, efficient and effective use of their money; whereas sound financial management should be combined with a 'make the most of every euro' approach; whereas i therefore voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing ‒ the despite the commission and member states coming up with new tools to fight corruption, the commission's report finds that corruption costs the eu in all member states up to €120 billion a year. the fight against fraud is one of the eu's greatest challenges, both to increase its competitiveness and, above all, to increase citizens' confidence. i supported the resolution on the commission's annual report on the financial interests of the union in 2014 as it contains warnings that have been ignored by the competent authorities for a long time. as this report is also the first report evaluating the use of structural funds for the period 2014-2020, we are receiving information on trends that should be a wake-up call for all links in the chain. the report also highlights the need to improve the quality of the information provided by the member states and to ensure that the information provided by the commission is used in a proper manner. cohesion policy, and thus regional development instruments, are thus under obvious pressure. however, it should not be forgotten that in cohesion policy irregularities are more often caused by administrative claims than by deliberate fraud. local and regional authorities should therefore put more pressure on increasing their administrative capacity and continuing training of staff. at the same time, the commission needs to continue its remedial action and suspend payments in fraudulent proceedings as it has already done in the case of 193 payments.
in writing ‒ it is in particular the diversity of the legal and administrative systems of the member states of the union that creates the space for fraud to arise. corruption remains a major problem affecting all member states and costing the union economy almost eur 120 billion a year. not only does corruption undermine citizens' trust in institutions, but it also facilitates the financing of organised crime and terrorism. i therefore support the adoption of a multiannual anti-fraud strategy.

in writing ‒ i take gender mainstreaming in all eu policies for granted. the eu formally respects the principle of gender equality as a fundamental right and value. in many areas, however, this principle is increasingly being left on paper rather than in practice. it requires the creation of realistic conditions that take into account and at the same time eliminate gender gaps and the implementation of practical steps to achieve this.
in writing gender equality is a frequently discussed topic in our society, including in the european parliament. it is one of the main principles of eu primary law and a prerequisite for achieving growth, employment or social cohesion. the union sees gender equality as the promotion of equal access to needs for both sexes and has long integrated this issue into the content of its policies. the european parliament has already adopted a number of concrete measures to combat discrimination on grounds of sex. however, the rapporteur's report deviates from the traditional gender equality approach and clearly has a different objective, namely to significantly increase the powers of the committee on women's rights and gender equality (femm) by including gender issues in all other aspects of eu work. in addition to changing the european parliament's procedural rules and increasing financial and human resources, the report submitted calls for the creation of a post of rapporteur for 'gender mainstreaming' at parliament level. however, such a function is not provided for in the treaties and would result in a substantial increase in the workload and complication of procedures for the european parliament and the various committees. from the point of view of european citizens, parliament's work will appear even less understandable, adding to the already high level of euroscepticism. this report uses gender ideology as a cover to achieve greater influence of femm on other eu policies, which is contrary to my belief and therefore i have decided not to support it.

in writing the investigation of criminal offences in criminal proceedings is a complex and psychologically demanding process, especially for children and young people. if done improperly, it can have a severe and lasting impact on their mental development and future life. i think that for all member states, minimum and uniform qualification requirements should be established for all the child-related services involved in this process, from the investigating authorities to the judiciary. to this end, it is necessary that member state governments provide the material, financial and formal conditions for the training and acquisition of skills of these components in working with children and young people. a callous approach that ignores the age and intellectual development of children without adequate psychological support is traumatic for children and can have the opposite effect as an education. this will affect the life of the child and the whole society in which he lives. it is inconceivable that in the 21st century, in an era of open markets, borders and free movement in europe, a minimum uniform level of protection and rights for children in criminal proceedings should not be guaranteed. these are not things for long discussions. they must be dealt with expeditiously and promptly.
