in writing ‒ the european union has a tradition of strong protection of children's rights. however, it is necessary and necessary that we work continuously to strengthen the safeguards for young people. such measures include the draft directive on procedural safeguards for children suspected or accused of a criminal offence. unfortunately, there are still large disparities in the treatment of children involved in criminal proceedings across the member states of the european union. we need to work together to improve the protection of children and young people facing crime in the future.
in writing ‒ currently, the legal systems of the member states differ in the status and treatment of children exposed to criminal proceedings. children have varying, often inadequate, levels of protection in this procedure in different countries. the european court of human rights has also issued a number of judgments against member states in this regard. i support the adoption of the proposed directive, which takes account of the special status of children and provides for uniform minimum requirements for the protection of children's rights in criminal proceedings (the inalienable right to counsel, the right to free legal aid, the right to individual assessment, the rules on the conduct of questioning, etc.). the directive will also apply to young people aged 18 to 21 if the offence was committed before they turned 18.
in writing current estimates put the number of children subject to criminal proceedings in the eu at around one million per year. in order to protect the rights of juveniles, law enforcement authorities and courts should take into account the specific needs of juvenile suspects/accused of criminal offences by providing minimum procedural safeguards. the investigation of juvenile crime is complex and requires a specific approach compared to the investigation of adult crime. the legal framework for criminal proceedings involving juvenile suspects/defendants in the member states remains inconsistent and contains shortcomings which are reflected in a lack of consideration for the specific nature of the trials conducted against juvenile offenders (e.g. the absence of specialised juvenile courts and prosecutors in some member states). i believe that this directive will also help to overcome some of the shortcomings, since it contains procedural safeguards such as the right to a lawyer and free legal aid, the right to individual assessment of the case, the rules governing the conduct of hearings (including the right to audio-visual recording), the guarantee of the child's participation in the proceedings, the right to a medical assessment, the right to special treatment in the event of deprivation of liberty, the provision of mandatory special training for judges and the clarification of key definitions such as 'child' and 'holder of parental rights and obligations'. the proposal as it stands will ensure that the rights of juveniles are protected at all stages of the criminal proceedings, and i therefore support it.
in writing. ‒ the protection of children's rights is of particular importance and requires special attention. that is why i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on procedural safeguards for children who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings. the different member states of the european union have different ways of dealing with criminal proceedings involving children. while in some countries, such as my own country, slovakia, juvenile cases are dealt with by special prosecutors, there are member states where even legal assistance is not guaranteed in such cases. as the report confirms, the introduction of minimum rules on criminal proceedings involving children is very important in several respects. it would ensure that all minors receive adequate legal protection and encourage member states to trust each other's criminal justice systems, which would also likely increase the number of mutually recognised judgments and decisions.

in writing ‒ i supported the report on the draft directive on procedural safeguards for children suspected or accused of a criminal offence. i think it is in the interests of children, that is to say persons under 18, that minimum standards in criminal proceedings be introduced throughout the european union, although of course the new regulation does not preclude the introduction of greater protection by the individual states. it is these uniform standards that ensure, in addition to a minimum level of protection, easier mutual recognition of judicial decisions. and most importantly, persons under 18 will always have the right to a defence, to be treated in accordance with the best interests of the child, to be individually assessed, or to be detained only in cases of genuine necessity. however, we should not forget about the protection of children who, for example, according to the slovak legal system are not yet criminally responsible, that is, children who have not yet reached the age of 14 (or in some cases 15). where such children commit a criminal offence, they are not prosecuted under the criminal justice system and therefore do not benefit from the minimum protection provided for in this directive. member states with similar legislation should therefore also think about the rights of these children and ensure that they are treated in a way that is always geared to protecting their interests, so that these children have a chance to integrate properly into life without unnecessary stigmatisation.

in writing ‒ the current agreement with philip morris international has been in force since 2004 and was originally due to expire in july of that year. its purpose is to combat and take joint action against the counterfeiting and illicit trafficking of tobacco products. illegal trade in tobacco products is a serious problem. it contributes to the financing of various types of organised crime, including trafficking in human beings, drugs, arms and, according to several experts, also to the financing of international terrorism. on average, one in 10 cigarettes in the european union has become the object of illicit trafficking. this results in a combined annual tax loss of more than €10 billion for the member states. counterfeit cigarettes using uncontrolled quality tobacco pose a much greater risk to human health than the original. moreover, the lower price makes them more accessible to adolescents, whose smoking statistics are sadly on the rise. the european commission's evaluation of the results of the agreement has shown that it has also led to a significant decrease in the occurrence of pmi-branded contraband on the so-called black tobacco market in the european union. the possible continuation of such agreements must be conditional on the improved enforceability of the obligations undertaken by the tobacco companies. there must be strict rules. the european commission must be able to monitor these agreements and to monitor the fulfilment of all the obligations arising from them.
in writing ‒ smuggling and counterfeiting of illicitly imported cigarettes cause economic damage to member states' budgets and the eu budget of more than eur 10 billion a year, while endangering the lives and health of citizens. this has further negative effects on public finances. the eu-philip morris international tobacco agreement, which has been regulating the fight against smuggling and counterfeiting of tobacco products since 2004 with the aim of reducing the prevalence of smuggled cigarettes on the eu black market, expires in july 2016. however, the market and regulatory environment have changed since its entry into force. it is necessary for member states to respect the deadline for transposition of directive 2014/40/eu of the european parliament and of the council of 3 april 2014 responding to new conditions in the field of tobacco products. i support the proposal that the commission adopt control measures to track and trace pmi's tobacco products and take the necessary legal action in the event of their unlawful detention. at the same time, it needs to submit new additional legislation to introduce the track and trace system and other tools to combat smuggling and counterfeiting of tobacco products.
in writing the proposal for the extension of the agreement between the eu, the member states and philip morris international (pmi) tobacco states that the purpose of this agreement is to combat cigarette smuggling and counterfeiting and thereby reduce the presence of pmi's smuggled cigarettes on the eu black market in tobacco. the main argument for extending the agreement is that the direct cooperation of investigators at national and european level with the tobacco company in the fight against cigarette smuggling and counterfeiting has led to many cases of arrest and indictment of suspects, as well as to the detection and dissolution of international organised groups. however, it should be noted that there is no evidence to show a link between the cooperation with the tobacco company and the resolution of these cases (for the detection of which the quality of olaf's work is to be sought in particular). by renegotiating such an agreement, the union risks sending a negative signal to third countries with which it cooperates in the fight against illicit trafficking, that it considers bilateral agreements with tobacco companies as a priority in cases of smuggling and counterfeiting, which may subsequently lead to jeopardising the ratification of the illicit trade protocol. but most importantly, i believe that the agreement with the tobacco company does not contribute in any way to the protection of public health, but has far-reaching negative consequences for it. as a physician, i cannot agree with the motion that has been tabled and i vote against it.
‒ smuggling of tobacco products undermines eu public health policies and means that illicit tobacco products are available in many places at significant illicit discounts. not only are counterfeit cigarettes illegally manufactured and imported, but they also contain unknown ingredients, posing a serious health threat. the commission has therefore committed to ratify the protocol to the who framework convention on tobacco control to eliminate illicit trade in tobacco products in order to combat illicit trade in tobacco products, which is an essential step to strengthen the legal framework to combat illicit trade in tobacco products. the protocol has been ratified by 15 countries, including five eu member states, and the eu is currently preparing to ratify it. at the same time, the commission should also invite other member states and third countries to ratify the protocol, so that agreements with tobacco companies with any exceptions are not possible. the public health of eu citizens must take priority over the interests of tobacco companies. the commission must therefore take immediate measures to ensure full transposition of the tobacco products directive in all member states.
‒ the illegal trade in tobacco products and cigarette smuggling is estimated to cost national budgets and the eu budget more than eur 10 billion in lost public revenues annually. the agreement with pmi expires on 9 july 2016 and the main objective of this agreement has been fulfilled. but the reduction in the volume of smuggled cigarettes has not led to an overall reduction in the amount of illicit products on the eu market. tobacco products are available in many places at significant illegal discounts, including to young people. in addition, as counterfeit cigarettes are not only illegally imported but also manufactured, there is a risk bordering on certainty that such products contain unknown and potentially health-threatening components. i therefore supported the commission's proposal to ratify the protocol to eliminate illicit trade in tobacco products to the who framework convention on tobacco control and to discontinue the policy of agreements with tobacco companies.
in writing the situation in eritrea, one of the world's youngest nations, is very complicated. eritrea is now an authoritarian state where human rights are suppressed. as a result of fear and oppression, eritreans are on the run in huge numbers, representing the third largest group of refugees heading to europe, with 5,000 arriving each month. a month ago, on my last flight from strasbourg to košice from vienna, i also flew with 57 eritrean refugees who are un refugees, and after a few months in slovakia, where they will learn english, they will fly to the united states. seeing the old people, women, and children dressed very modestly despite the cold weather made me feel very sad. there was an incredible sadness on their faces, a desperate people who had been forced to leave their homeland, their relatives, and set out on an uncertain journey in the hope of a better chance of life for their children. they were just a small group of refugees from eritrea's six million people, but from meeting them, i have a question: is it only the authoritarian state that forces them to leave their own country, or are it also the multinational corporations and the globalization policies of the rich countries that exploit the poorest? the answer is for each of us. development aid to poor africa is well-intentioned, but it is limited and often unaddressed.

the regulation responds to the terrorist attacks in tunisia in 2015, which also affected the economy and economic situation of that country. in order to stimulate the tunisian economy, this regulation provides for the eu to assist the tunisian economy by fixing a zero customs duty for the years 2016-2017 on imports of olive oil into the eu up to a maximum of 35 000 tonnes per year. olive oil is the most exported agricultural product of tunisia. its manufacturing industry employs a million people. this measure will help to maintain employment, prevent the development of poverty in this african country and thus contribute to the fact that people from this country do not have to flee to such an extent in search of a better life.
in writing despite a series of political and economic reforms that tunisia has undergone since the arab spring coup and the last elections in october 2014, the situation in the country is far from stable. the seriousness of the current situation was 'contributed' by the terrorist attacks of march and june last year, which hit the economy hard. tunisia is part of the european neighbourhood policy, which is central to the eu's foreign policy, and as such is part of programmes aimed at encouraging economic and political transformation, based on the principle of common interests and values such as democracy, the rule of law, respect for human rights and social cohesion. the security challenges that continue to plague the country are slowing down the process of economic development, coupled with poorly-targeted government policies, low levels of investor confidence and high unemployment. in this context, we can help the citizens of tunisia by means of an effective instrument to boost trade between them, in particular by promoting exports from the country. the proposal proposed as one of the possible solutions a temporary unilateral tariff quota of 35 000 tonnes per year at zero rate for the period from 1 january 2016 to 31 december 2017 for the export of olive oil (the most exported product of tunisia and a sector representing one fifth of the jobs in agriculture), which will be opened after the exhaustion of the existing tariff-free quota of 56 7000 tonnes set out in the association agreement. i support the motion.

in writing the new regulation would constitute a separate legal framework for veterinary medicinal products, separate from the framework governing medicinal products for human use. it is a response to changes in the veterinary and pharmaceutical sectors, which should naturally be taken into account in the current legislation. the regulation aims to regulate the authorisation process, manufacture, distribution, sale, pharmacovigilance and use of veterinary medicinal products during their shelf life. i think it is important that the regulation addresses the issues of how to improve access to veterinary medicinal products and ensure their wider availability, how to respond to the problems associated with the trend of increasing antibiotic resistance in animals, how to encourage innovation or how to protect the environment. the new regulation should take into account the proposals made in the report submitted, concerning a complete ban on the prescription of antibacterial substances for prophylactic purposes, the establishment of a data protection period of 14 years with the possibility of extension, the problems of recognition of medical prescriptions in individual member states, labelling requirements for veterinary medicinal products, improvements and simplifications in the authorisation and marketing of veterinary medicinal products, etc. i therefore vote in favour of the motion for a resolution.

in writing. ‒ database marketing is a key segment of modern market trading, where different marketing companies try to obtain as much information as possible about customers in a personalised way, thereby dividing them into different categories based on their income, purchasing habits and interests. they want to build on this data to a large extent and then use the information they get from the data to build their business campaigns to make a product more successful with consumers. the european parliament considers it essential that in today's world, where the rise of information technology and mass services is increasingly expected to increase the activity of 'data hunters', the rights of european citizens should be protected as much as possible so that their data does not fall into the wrong hands.
in writing ‒ differences in digitalisation, lack of investment, as well as the lack of technical standardisation and outdated data protection legislation could lead to europe lagging behind technologically and economically in the development of the data-based economy. the european union needs to simplify grant award procedures and increase funding for research and innovation on integrated data use, digital innovation and market development in areas that should bring added value to citizens, society and the economy, as well as effectively supporting the entry of innovative products and services into the market. the main technological barriers to the development of a data-driven economy include the lack of interoperability and a common interface framework to facilitate data communication between sensors and machines and between the virtual and real worlds, the lack of availability of open data and the lack of market conditions enabling businesses to innovate and grow. to achieve this, member states need to work towards greater integration of ict in their national education programmes.
in writing a data-driven economy at national and european level has undeniable benefits for our society and economic development. it is a cornerstone for the creation of a functioning digital union and is of great importance for the horizontal aspects of the economy such as research and development, the creation of a data market, the promotion of a knowledge society with relevant digital skills, the promotion of start-ups, investment, growth, employment, the development of smes, the enhancement of competitiveness, social cohesion, etc. in a society based on data and virtual information exchange, however, it is essential to find a middle ground between the 'big data' market and the protection of personal data. a sufficiently clear and strict definition of the authorities and persons entitled to access and handle personal data is a sensitive issue and forms the basis for transparent and trust-based relations between citizens and consumers on the one hand and public authorities and companies on the other. the digital economy undoubtedly has the potential to create many new jobs as well as to facilitate the cross-border exchange of information, but another aspect that needs to be guaranteed in this context is the protection of intellectual property rights and patent rights, which is a key prerequisite for a functioning governance system and democracy based on information and data technologies. this proposal takes account of the above and i therefore support it.

in writing ‒ according to the forecasts of big data and services companies, the growth rate of the big data market will be six times faster than that of the ict market by 2017 and the market should reach a total volume of up to eur 50 billion. today, the volume of data is growing at an unprecedented pace, and decisions based on big data also have a significant impact on productivity and competitiveness. it is therefore understandable that the development of big data is an integral part of the new digital market. on the other hand, it is an undeniable fact that big data can bring with it certain problems with regard to fundamental rights such as the protection of privacy. taking into account both risks and benefits, i supported the european parliament's resolution calling for the integration of the data-based economy into the foundation of the digital single market strategy. in the future, we can expect data to be a valuable resource for society and the ability to process it efficiently will be beneficial not only for the business environment but also for the functioning of public administration. the data-driven economy will also require specific skills, which should lead to the creation of a large number of jobs. therefore, there is a need to continue to increase confidence in these technologies, to encourage investment in network infrastructure and to facilitate access to research and innovation grants.

in writing ‒ i supported the resolution on the situation in eritrea. although the country gained independence in 1991, its constitution was never implemented and its only president since independence has established an autocratic form of government. citizens of eritrea, both men and women, are required to perform compulsory military service, which in reality exceeds the period of service by several times. if they want to travel abroad, there are very few legal options for obtaining travel documents. moreover, the judicial processes in that country could hardly be called fair, and the persecution of religions contributes to the overall intolerable situation. eritreans often see no other option but to flee the country. in the resolution, we therefore called on the eritrean government to fully ratify the constitution, to immediately adopt the un convention against torture and other inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment, and to abandon indefinite military service. i hope that the european parliament's dissent, as well as its calls for immediate improvement, will put moral pressure on the eritrean government to bring about a rapid improvement in the situation so that the more than 440 000 refugees currently in neighbouring countries can return home safely.

in writing the creation of the banking union is a response to the financial crisis. it is crucial for the european financial system. it brings new demands on those who cause debt. the aim is to make a thorough and correct assessment of the risks. i consider this to be the right move from the point of view of maintaining the financial stability of the member states and of the union. the single supervisory mechanism and the single resolution mechanism shall be interlinked and coordinated with each other in order to provide sufficient guarantees to prevent and avoid a recurrence of the 2007 situation. however, even these measures cannot and will not be effective without the active participation and action of the member states and the union in cooperation with the banks. it is necessary to adopt concrete measures to streamline and harmonise the resolution of banking crises throughout the union and to ensure a really high and realistic protection of bank deposits, which is a necessary prerequisite for financial security.
the banking union has played a significant role in addressing the financial crisis, particularly in the countries whose economies were most affected. the establishment of the ssm was a right step in terms of enhancing the quality of supervision and a success, especially given the short timeframe set for its creation. the future involvement of the national competent authorities of non-participating member states, and in particular the closer coordination of the activities of those authorities, will make a significant contribution to ensuring the effective regulation and supervision of significant union banks. the establishment of a single resolution mechanism or national resolution authorities in the member states also has a great potential to ensure the efficient functioning of the banking sector even in times of crisis. in this context, it is important that member states fully transpose the bank recovery and resolution directive. the above instruments should ensure the ability to provide a uniform and high level of protection for deposits regardless of their location, thus contributing to breaking the link between banks and sovereign debt, restoring depositors' confidence, creating a level playing field and ultimately strengthening financial stability. i support the motion.
in writing ‒ the banking union is an integral part of monetary union and a cornerstone of genuine economic and monetary union, and is open to participation by member states whose currency is not the euro. the banking union is an instrument for ensuring stability and restoring confidence in euro area banks, reducing risk in european banking and playing a key role in financing, and thus in boosting growth and job creation across the eu. the single supervisory mechanism in the banking union is the first pillar of the banking union and aims to ensure uniform and consistent supervision of the banks of the participating member states, to create a level playing field in the banking market and to contribute to the safety and financial soundness of credit institutions and the stability of the financial system, while respecting the diversity of banks and their business models. the single resolution mechanism is the second pillar of the banking union and aims to ensure uniform rules and procedures and a common decision-making process in order to smoothly resolve the problem of failing banks with minimal impact on the rest of the financial system, the real economy, ordinary citizens or public finances across europe.
‒ the banking union has an irreplaceable place in the financing of investment and job creation. this is all the more important as regards transparency and trust towards market participants and the public. in particular, financial stability needs to be strengthened and appropriate solutions for the management of future banking crises need to be found, through a thorough assessment of the options available, in particular under union legislation.

in writing. ‒ under the new fisheries partnership agreement with denmark and greenland, the total financial contribution will be eur 17 799 978 per year for the duration of the agreement. the protocol aims to strengthen cooperation between the european union and greenland. the protocol serves to maintain fishing opportunities for european union vessels in the greenland fishing zone and contributes to better management and protection of fisheries resources by supporting the sector, in particular with regard to the monitoring of domestic and foreign fleets and the fight against illegal fishing, while also helping to develop the local fishing industry, including the promotion of local employment, in line with the policy of the common fisheries policy.
in writing. greenland, with full self-government and self-government since 1978, is one of the eu's overseas territories, the arrangements for relations with which are generally contained in the partnership agreement approved by the council in 2006. greenland's natural wealth lies in its surrounding seas, and therefore the country concentrates almost all its economic activity on the fishing sector. in this context, relations with continental europe are key almost all exports go to eu member states, with imports from denmark accounting for more than 90% of the union. these relations are governed by the fisheries partnership agreement, which provides eu vessels with access to fish stocks in the greenland eez, for which the union pays an annual financial compensation of eur 15,1 million, as well as a specific amount of eur 2,74 million to support the greenland fisheries sector. as regards the proposal for a new protocol setting out fishing opportunities and the financial contribution, i see it as ensuring the continuity of the enhanced cooperation between the eu and greenland and as supporting the partnership in developing a fisheries policy and the acquisition of fish from greenland waters. i also see the positive aspects of this protocol in the inclusion of provisions for the protection of natural resources and the effective management of fisheries policy. i therefore vote in favour of the recommendation as it stands.

in writing. ‒ the fisheries partnership agreements are the way eu countries gain access to fishing rights in the partner country's exclusive zone. the initial fisheries agreement between the eu, on the one hand, and the government of denmark and the local government of greenland, on the other, was concluded as early as 1985. it has been updated on several occasions since then and last year the commission adopted a proposal to renew the protocol to the agreement. as it is a mixed agreement that gives eu vessels access to the large fish stocks in greenland waters, the eu provides financial and technical support to the partner country in exchange for fishing rights. in parallel, the eu is involved in supporting a number of activities that are important to greenland's efforts to manage and control its fisheries in a sustainable way. fishing is an important part of greenland's economy, accounting for almost 90% of exports. virtually all greenland's exports of fishery products are destined for the eu, with the vast majority going to denmark. for companies in eu countries, the agreement has significant benefits as it creates added value in other supply and customer sectors as well. i support the introduction of the new protocol and believe that it will continue to be beneficial for both countries. however, in the future, consideration should be given to the possibilities of sustainable exploitation of fish stocks, with greater emphasis on better compliance with scientific recommendations.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament hereby approves the council proposal for the conclusion of an agreement between the eu and the government of the macao special administrative region of the people's republic of china, which amends the air services agreements concluded so far. the agreement eliminates the previous discriminatory measures that allowed a third country to refuse, withdraw or suspend the authorisation or licence of an air carrier established in the territory of a member state but owned and controlled by nationals of other member states. the court ruled that such a practice was contrary to eu law.
in writing. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's policy on aviation security and will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's policy on civil aviation security. from a strategic perspective, it is essential for the eu to remain globally competitive and to continue to develop its aviation industry, as the most important aviation markets are located outside the union. in this context, investments in building and modernising infrastructure and relations with our foreign partners, which are governed by bilateral air transport agreements, are key. we currently have 15 such agreements with the macao special administrative region of the people's republic of china, but they contained discriminatory provisions as regards the right of destination. the proposed decision would delete these provisions and replace them with a right of establishment for all eu carriers, bringing the agreement in line with the 2002 ruling of the court of justice of the eu. i believe that the union must also ensure that the legislation and rights in force are respected in the area of external relations, which is important for the development of air transport, and i therefore vote in favour of the recommendation.

in writing. ‒ the i supported the conclusion of an agreement on certain aspects of air services between the eu and macao, as this agreement is intended to replace the provisions of the 15 existing bilateral air services agreements between the member states and macao. the commission has negotiated this agreement in response to a ruling by the court of justice of the eu that the usual designation provisions in member states' bilateral air services agreements are contrary to eu law. this would constitute discrimination against eu carriers established in the territory of a member state but owned and controlled by nationals of other member states. the agreement with macao is thus intended to regulate several aspects of air services, such as provisions on designation, safety, taxation and compatibility of competition rules. for example, in the field of safety, the provisions will apply to cases where regulatory control of an air carrier is exercised by a member state other than the member state whose designation it bears. the provisions also apply to the taxation of aviation fuel and also prohibit practices distorting competition. the agreement was signed in 2013 and requires the consent of the european parliament. i welcome its conclusion and hope that it will bring more legal certainty to the european aviation industry.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal as it will help to make air transport between the eu and macao more efficient.
in writing. ‒ the the report in question is a purely technical proposal to extend the period of the 15% minimum basic rate from 1 january 2016 to 31 december 2017. this directive modifies the transitional system of minimum rates and provides that the basic rate of vat may not be set at less than 15% in the member states of the european union. given that all member states charge a base rate higher than 15%, the current system of a minimum base rate of 15% also provides room for manoeuvre for member states, allowing for vat reforms that aim to reduce the single rate by extending the vat base and limiting the use of reduced rates.
in writing. ‒ this directive, in the interests of the functioning of the single market and competition, aims at the harmonisation of legislation in the field of value added tax. the minimum basic vat rate of at least 15% is confirmed retroactively until 31 december 2015 and at the same time this transitional vat rate mechanism is extended until 31 december 2018. the commission should propose in 2016 a new system for the final settlement of vat within the eu, based on the destination principle (currently the country of origin principle).
in writing. tax harmonisation at eu level is an important tool to achieve the proper functioning of the internal market. in 1992, the council adopted the commission's proposal which set a minimum basic vat rate of 15% in all the member states of the union. the purpose of the regulation of the minimum vat rate is to apply vat at the place of origin rather than at the place of destination to cross-border distance sales and purchases not exceeding a threshold. in general, tax harmonisation and coordination of member states' tax policies is considered to be a major economic and political issue that governments must address in order to maintain economic growth and stability. it is also a rather difficult and controversial process, as on the one hand member states are bound by binding eu legislation and policies, and on the other hand they seek to maintain a competitive advantage over other countries. tax harmonisation in the eu is therefore an ongoing process, the completion of which will require further legislation. the proposal for a directive proposed so far proposes to maintain the existing minimum vat rate, which i regard as an economically advantageous measure to promote crossborder trade in goods. i therefore vote in favour of the report as it stands.
in writing. ‒ the proposal calls for a further extension of a permanent vat system, which has been in operation since 1993 on a temporary basis and is being extended continuously until 31 december 2015. i believe that a harmonised vat is a valid and necessary instrument for the functioning of the internal market and for avoiding distortions of competition on the market, in particular by helping small and medium-sized enterprises. the extension is, in my view, crucial for legal certainty, but i think it is important to point out that a complex, long-term solution needs to be developed, which requires more in-depth measures, with a constant focus on the protection of smes, the reduction of administrative burdens and the stability of the system against fraud. i voted in favour of the proposal, but i will actively follow the development of the commission's action plan for 2016, which is an inevitable part of the new long-term vat strategy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it is, in practice, only an extension of the common system of standard vat rates already applied for the period from 1 january 2016 to 31 december 2017. this system provides that, under directive 92/77/eec, the standard rate of vat may not be less than 15%.
in writing. ‒ i supported the commission's proposal for a directive to extend the minimum vat rate until 2018, even though the proposal was published late, which would have made it necessary to apply the minimum vat rate retroactively. the directive establishing the vat system entered into force as early as 1993, when it provided that the basic vat rate would not be lower than 15% in any country. the objective of this measure is to achieve the harmonisation necessary for the establishment and functioning of the internal market and to avoid distortions of competition. the establishment of a minimum rate of vat is justified by the fact that vat is applied at the place of origin rather than at the place of destination in cross-border distance purchases and sales. this instrument thus constitutes a useful safeguard measure to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market. given that all member states currently apply a vat rate above 15%, there is still ample room for manoeuvre for national governments to adopt vat reforms. the extension of the current vat minimum rate mechanism should be the last stage before the adoption of the final version of the vat regime. the commission should present an action plan this year to achieve a definitive vat system that is simple, efficient and fraud-proof. i believe that such a system will be created in the near future.
in writing. ‒ a minimum standard rate of vat applicable in all member states provides an appropriate guarantee of the proper functioning of the internal market and the transparency of competition.
in writing. ‒ i did not support the proposal because i do not agree with tax harmonisation at european union level.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal because at the moment it is only a matter of extending the minimum vat rate, which has been in place for more than 10 years, for another three years. however, we know that in europe - at both the level of the member states and the european parliament - a complex debate has already begun on the harmonisation of tax systems. in the coming years, this discussion will continue and it will be important for slovakia to actively intervene in it. lower taxes are one way our country is trying to compete with other eu members in attracting investment. we're trying to compensate investors for the less developed infrastructure with a lower tax rate. therefore, tax harmonisation is acceptable from the slovak point of view only if it is linked to the guarantee of increased support for the completion of expressways, the modernisation of railways, as well as the improvement of suburban transport, etc.

in writing. ‒ the marine activities are developing and multiplying at an unusually fast pace, with increasing pressure on sustainability and the conservation of marine biodiversity. the international community recognises the need for a common international approach to better manage pollution, human activities and increased threats to marine biodiversity. the international legally binding instruments should be presented by the end of 2017. over the past few decades, human activity at sea has increased exponentially. the potential for growth and employment is enormous and should be used within the ecological limits of the marine environment. fisheries and aquaculture play an important role in the marine economy. responsible fishing and aquaculture are key to sustainable development and a healthy marine ecosystem.
in writing. the un convention on the law of the sea, which governs the rights and obligations of nations with respect to the use of the oceans and seas, is the fundamental instrument of international law governing the commercial exploitation, management and protection of the natural resources of the world's marine waters. the convention on marine biodiversity in outermost regions (cmbr) is an international agreement that reaffirms the need to protect marine fauna and flora from pollution caused by human activities and to ensure the sustainable use of natural resources in areas beyond the jurisdiction of states. i believe that effective measures that are binding on the entire international community are necessary to achieve effective regulation for the protection of marine biodiversity. in this context, i fully support the work of the un general assembly working group which aims to create and subsequently adopt such an instrument on un soil, as without binding rules it would be very difficult to make any progress. the new instrument could also bring dynamism to the process of exchanging information, best practices and methods or building qualified capacities at the level of signatory countries. in the spirit of its role as guardian of compliance with international agreements, the eu should continue to lead the development of this new legal instrument and its effective implementation. i vote in favour of the report as it stands.
in writing. ‒ the rapid development of marine activities is putting considerable pressure on the sustainability and conservation of marine biodiversity, which requires action by the european union. of course, we must not forget about fishing. this is one of the most active and important activities in the water sector and we must therefore seek to develop a tool that can also cover this sector. the motion for a resolution by the european parliament calls for this to be done, and that is why i voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ the international agreement on marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction takes into consideration both the economic and environmental arguments, therefore i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ europe has a rich variety of domestic livestock breeds, representing the largest genetic population of farm animals. the rearing of domestic animals of bovine, porcine, ovine, caprine and equine species, and to a lesser extent of other species, plays an important role in the union's agriculture and is a source of income for farming communities. the rearing of these species is best promoted by using purebred breeding animals of high genetic quality. the proposed regulation establishes, in a single legal framework, the principles concerning the approval or recognition and listing of breeding organisations, breeding associations and private undertakings, the registration and classification of animals in breeding books, performance testing and genetic examination, the content and format of the zootechnical certificate for breeding animals.

in writing. ‒ i did not vote in favour of the report on migration adopted today. the migration crisis should not be confused with the refugee crisis. the hundreds of thousands of people who are coming to europe are only a fraction of the real refugees, and the best way to help them is to support reception camps close to their home countries and to help resolve conflicts. if the refugee camps in neighbouring countries can provide decent conditions, health care and education, we will make it easier for them to return to their home countries once the situation has stabilised. although the report contains a number of suggestions that can be positively assessed and suggests a solution, i could not support the adopted report. the report calls for a permanent resettlement programme at eu level, binding on all member states, and for a central system to be set up to share responsibility for asylum seekers in the union. i believe that there are many forms of solidarity, but that the solution is not to impose artificial mandatory quotas.
in writing. ‒ the draft report does not address the situation of migrants already in the european union and does not take into account the position of some member states opposed to mandatory relocation. moreover, there is a debate about the fundamental rights of migrants and what moral right any institution or national government has to decide on their future placement or on their being sent to a country where they have no interest in living.
in writing. ‒ if the union is to maintain its integrity and be safe for its citizens, it must strengthen its position in the current migration crisis. the policy pursued so far in this area has created a natural distrust among eu citizens and in the authorities of some member states of the union's strength and ability to deal with this fundamental and ongoing problem. they see solutions as flimsy, ineffective and almost always adopted late. the union is still not sufficiently prepared for the migration crisis, lacking foresight and determination, as evidenced by the continued flourishing of smuggling, which has become a source of high illegal revenues, ultimately harming, inter alia, the economic and financial interests of the eu.
in writing. the complex migration crisis afflicting europe urgently requires a joint and coordinated approach by all eu member states in a spirit of solidarity and respect for international law principles, in particular the provisions of the geneva convention for the protection of refugees. under that instrument, a person who has been forced to leave his or her home country under threat of serious harm is entitled to asylum and is therefore entitled to international protection. i therefore regard a single asylum policy, which would include the establishment of a so-called common european asylum system, as a conditio sine qua non in terms of harmonising the process of assessing individual asylum applications, speeding up the administrative procedure involved and ultimately preventing the increase in the number of stateless persons. the solution, in my view, is not to introduce mandatory quotas which would significantly and de jure unduly encroach on the exclusive competences of each sovereign state, or to make factually unfounded suggestions that the schengen agreement should be abolished. the starting point, on the contrary, must be sought in a coherent policy and the efficient use of available resources. dialogue with our foreign partners, such as turkey, is key in this context, but should not be the way to win the promise of opening chapters in the accession process. i fully support the proposal to establish a list of safe countries, as well as the establishment of an action plan for the integration of asylum seekers in the eu, both in terms of work and social life.
in writing. ‒ we have not yet transferred the power to admit people to the eu and i do not see the need for that in the future. that's why i voted against mandatory quotas again today. the commission has also taken into account the fact that the number of persons resettled in the member states is increasing, and that the number of persons resettled in the union is increasing. the closure of schengen is unacceptable to us. a permanent distribution system would only encourage the hitherto hesitant economic migration from all parts of the world, which could trigger a new, larger wave of refugees. if some member states insist on central distribution, it is not only the uk that should be exempted. but this could be achieved not by lengthy international court proceedings but by negotiations. in addition, from a humanitarian point of view, i find the forced relocation of groups of people unacceptable, both for the local population and for immigrants.
in writing. ‒ the mediterranean migration crisis is a crucial challenge where the european union can demonstrate its co-operation and capacities. we need wisdom and compassion, as well as justice in tackling the different groups involved. sadly, what this report has advocated for is a 'red carpet' into europe without any discernment about who is being welcomed in. we cannot afford to continue the catastrophic open door policy for everyone, without discerning who are those genuinely fleeing for their lives. therefore i voted against this report because, despite many helpful suggestions for life—saving, resourcing and resettlement, it failed to honour the principles of the dublin regulations, where our external borders are strengthened so that our internal borders can remain open. it also advocated a more centralised approach, establishing a new european body to process all asylum seekers, again taking power away from sovereign nation states.
in writing. ‒ i did not support the motion for a resolution because the report again refers to a permanent mechanism for the redistribution of refugees, which i cannot agree with because the experience so far has shown that this mechanism does not work in practice. in their report, the rapporteurs described in detail the situation with refugees, the problems with smuggling groups, the ineffectiveness of the measures taken so far. for example, out of 106 000 asylum seekers awaiting transfer to other member states from italy and greece, only 660 asylum seekers had been relocated by 3 march this year. it is clear that even those states which have agreed to the permanent redistribution mechanism do not comply with this regulation. the report also identifies the causes of the migration wave and the strategy for cooperation with third countries, in particular in the context of regional protection programmes, resettlement, returns and addressing the root causes of migration. and they also focused on creating appropriate legal means of economic migration, which i also disagree with. the own-initiative report describes the problems in terms of the real situation on the basis of which the commission should take more effective action to address the refugee crisis in the eu.

in writing. ‒ i did not support the report drawn up on the initiative of two political groups, the european people's party and the group of the progressive alliance of socialists and democrats. the report was to outline the european parliament's position on migration and the asylum system in response to the agenda on migration published by the european commission in may 2015. the report speaks in particular of the need for a holistic approach to migration, but ultimately lacks any ambition and resolution. the main proposals to address the issue are centred around a mandatory relocation system, which i disagree with from the outset, as well as a new proposal for a centralised asylum procedure, whereby asylum seekers would no longer apply at the level of individual states, but at the level of the european union. i cannot support such a solution, as i am of the opinion that the asylum procedure should not be transferred to the hands of the european union and should remain the responsibility of the individual member states. i am also against mandatory quotas and have always been of the opinion that the refugee crisis can only be managed on the basis of voluntary solidarity between member states. for these reasons, i voted against the report.
in writing. ‒ the annual reports on the application of the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality examine how the eu institutions have managed to apply these two principles in lawmaking and law enforcement, and how these two principles have been applied in practice. the study is concerned with whether the eu institutions and bodies apply these two principles and, if so, how they work in practice. the report examines the development and status of these processes, and compares the practices of recent years.
in writing. ‒ the in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, in areas which do not fall within the exclusive competence of the european union, measures must be adopted only if the objectives of the action envisaged cannot be attained at the level of the member states, whether at central, regional or local level. the principle of proportionality, which applies to all the activities of the european union, requires that the european union, when acting, does not go beyond what is necessary to achieve the objectives of the treaties. the main points of contention in this particular report were the introduction of green and red cards by national parliaments, the enhanced yellow card procedure, mid-term and end-of-period evaluation and others.
in writing. ‒ the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality enshrined in the eu treaty are an essential instrument for regulating relations between the union's institutions and the member states. in order to adopt standards in the eu, it will always be important to properly assess in advance whether the policy objectives pursued can be achieved more effectively at the pan-european or national level. i agree that a repeated subsidiarity check and impact assessment should be carried out before the adoption of any final regulation or directive, thereby increasing transparency and the compliance of standards with union principles.
in writing. the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality are the basic building blocks on which eu law is built. they allow european legislators to assess whether the objectives set can be achieved as effectively as possible by adaptation at national, regional or european level. when drafting new legislation, the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality shall be examined at an early stage of the legislative process as part of an impact assessment. i agree with the rapporteur that, in order to assess credibly whether those principles have been respected, it is necessary to assess whether they have been respected also at later stages of the drafting of new legislation, which is in many cases lengthy. i also believe that the objective of quality law-making can only be achieved by working more closely with national parliaments, thereby ensuring a greater degree of continuity between the work of the european parliament and the national legislatures and thus a higher level of citizens' trust in european legislation, which i consider to be our ultimate objective. i vote in favour of the opinion as presented.
in writing. ‒ subsidiarity and proportionality are two very important principles of european union law. the basic idea of subsidiarity is that decisions are taken as closely as possible to the citizen, taking into account the individual characteristics of the group most affected. in order to improve the quality of legislation, it is necessary to assess, before the process begins, which eu, national or regional level can best achieve the given objective. the report, which i voted in favour of, calls for these two principles to be strengthened.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the annual report ’12-’13 on subsidiarity and proportionality in the european union as the idea of the report is in line with my stands on subsidiarity. it calls for a subsidiarity culture in the eu and that all reports should be checked on this matter as well.
in writing. ‒ i did not support the report because it did not pass important amendments, even though i consider the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality to be a key union policy-making tool that helps member states at national, regional or local level to effectively address the objectives pursued. the report again refers to cases where the principle of subsidiarity has not been given due consideration in the impact assessments carried out by the commission. in particular, i find unacceptable that more than 30% of the impact assessments reviewed by the committee in 2012 and 2013 refer to an unsatisfactory analysis of the principle of subsidiarity. and what's even worse is that this number has risen to 50% in 2014. i trust that the commission will take this issue more seriously in its review of the guidelines on impact assessments and will do everything possible to improve this unflattering situation in the next period. it is very important that we strengthen political dialogue not only in the case of a yellow or orange card but also as a general rule (if appropriate consider the green card procedure) in order to respect the principle of subsidiarity. i also expect the european institutions and national parliaments to continue to strive to promote a 'culture of subsidiarity' across the eu.
in writing. ‒ the the principle of subsidiarity and proportionality is a fundamental principle of eu law, which defines its competences. compliance with these principles is monitored by the european institutions and national parliaments. however, on the basis of the annual reports drawn up by the european commission, there is a need to involve national parliaments more actively in the decision-making process in order to ensure effective compliance with these principles.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal and fully support all efforts to increase the subsidiarity of decision-making in the european union. although the european union officially subscribes to the principle of subsidiarity, in practice it constantly violates it, which, together with the non-respect of its own rules, is the main root of the eu's current problems.
in writing. ‒ i supported the opinion on the 2012 2013 annual reports on subsidiarity and proportionality. in this opinion, the rapporteur stresses the importance of subsidiarity, proportionality and the need for greater involvement of national parliaments in the legislative process of the european union. i, like the ecr group, have long stressed the need for close monitoring of subsidiarity and proportionality, both through enhanced dialogues with national parliaments and through impact assessments of new legislative proposals. like the rapporteur, i am convinced that the subsidiarity check should not be carried out only at the beginning of the legislative process, i.e. at the initial draft, since we know from experience that the texts of the original drafts can change very significantly during the process. i therefore also call for further subsidiarity tests to be considered before the final draft of the new legislation is adopted.
in writing. ‒ the refit programme, launched in 2012, is now an important part of the eu's better regulation agenda. it aims to create a simple, clear and predictable regulatory system that is designed to make life, activity and operation in the union easier for eu citizens and businesses. its main objective is to eliminate bureaucratic burdens and to simplify and develop legislation. the commission's refit scrutiny of the whole of european legislation focuses on, inter alia, the identification of these burdens and on measures that impede legislation.
in writing. ‒ the this own-initiative report follows the better regulation report of february 2014. its main objectives are to reduce red tape, remove regulatory burdens, simplify and improve the design and quality of legislation. the european commission should give priority to the development of certain measures and focus on the quality of legislation and better enforcement of existing legislation rather than on the number of legislative acts. cost should not be a determining factor, but the quality of legislation is the only appropriate benchmark and refit must not be used to weaken sustainability or any social, labour, environmental and consumer standards.
in writing. i take a very positive view of the report on the regulatory fitness and performance programme (refit). we live in a time when every aspect of life is tightly regulated. while regulation by means of legislative acts is very necessary, in order to be effective and to fulfil its function well, legislative acts must be well prepared. in recent years, we have witnessed a kind of 'legislative shrinkage', with the member states and the european union literally overwhelming us with huge numbers of new legislation, often requiring renewed amendments and, moreover, increasingly case-by-case. this situation puts in question the proper functioning of the states and the union and, at the same time, undermines the legal certainty which is one of the hallmarks of the rule of law. today, with the number of 'eurosceptics' growing across the european union, it is essential to take measures that lead to simplification, clarity and what we commonly call 'common sense'. in this context, i am happy to vote in favour of the report presented, because i see it as a clear first step towards genuine improvement of the legal regulation.
in writing. ‒ the commission's strategic plan, known as the 'programme for a targeted and effective regulation', sets out objectives such as simplifying eu legislation and reducing administrative burdens. for many years we have been talking about excessive bureaucracy at both european and national level, the main enemy of efficiency and transparency. i welcome the report and am confident that a targeted and effective regulatory programme will bring about tangible changes.
in writing. ‒ the resolution on the regulatory fitness and performance programme gives an overview of the progress and implementation of eu legislation. as this resolution calls for a focus on better quality in legislation and standard checks on subsidiarity, i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ the regulatory fitness and performance programme (refit) emphasises that cost should not be the deciding factor, but that the quality of legislation is the only appropriate benchmark and that the refit programme must not be used to weaken sustainability or any social, labour, environmental and consumer standards. simplifying eu legislation and reducing the administrative and regulatory burden guarantees a reduction in red tape for citizens and smes. i see more flexible rules for smes as streamlining administrative processes, thus ensuring public interest objectives, workers' rights and the economic activity of the whole state.

in writing. ‒ i supported the report assessing the current state and future of the regulatory fitness and performance (refit) programme. in general, i consider the refit programme as a process of scrutiny of european union legislation to be a useful step towards clear and effective legislation. like refit, this report calls for a focus on quality rather than quantity in the design of legislation, and recommends, overall, a focus on clear, consistent and understandable legislation. other positive elements of the report include the recommendation to include 'sunset clauses' which would determine the lifetime of a legal act from the outset, the inclusion of revision clauses, but also a more rigorous monitoring of compliance with the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality. as i support all these principles in the development of european legislation, i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. the islands and coastal areas have been the focus of the european union's attention for some time. these are parts of europe whose culture, history and working areas have always maintained a traditional european way of life, of which fishing is an integral part. fishing is a common part of life for the inhabitants of the islands and coastal areas, it is a way of life for the local population, which, without exaggeration, literally 'keeps them alive'. the common fisheries policy is currently in force, through which coastal fisheries are to be jointly regulated. despite the great positive effects of this legislation, it does not harmonise small-scale fishing in europe and there is therefore a continuing lack of legislation to adequately regulate all the necessary areas of small-scale coastal fishing. this is a matter that will require a quick and high-quality solution through well-prepared regulations that clarify the concepts and make life easier for the many people who make an honest living. for the reasons set out above, i agree with the report submitted.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the proposal which highlights the importance of the coastal fishing tradition in the light of local culture and aims to protect and support local traditional forms of fishing. unfortunately, the legislators and the bureaucracy treat the sea as a whole and do not pay enough attention to the specificities of the fishing regions. the heritage of coastal fishing can be seen as a local culture, which i, and my country, have made a priority of protecting. a very important dimension of the report is the emphasis on small and family businesses at regional level, which is essential for the healthy functioning of the local economy.
in writing. ‒ small-scale coastal fishing in regions dependent of fishing is a very important form of fishing in the eu. the agreement takes into account both the economic and environmental sides, so therefore i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ coastal fishing is a particularly important form of fishing, provides a high level of employment and is socially and environmentally sustainable. some coastal and island areas are experiencing a significant economic decline, resulting in depopulation and displacement of the population, seeking opportunities in places where there are more opportunities for employment and education. in addition, some coastal fishing areas are located close to economically developed areas and are not able to achieve economic growth. it is in these areas that the pressure to exploit marine resources is increasing and that the fishing industry is being sidelined in relation to tourism. coastal fishing also faces many problems in relation to the prescribed choice of gear and fishing techniques. to protect coastal fisheries, the process of amending existing legislation needs to start. we have a new common fisheries policy, so we need to propose new frameworks and start the process of amending the regulation on management measures for the sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources in the mediterranean. this regulation needs to be aligned with the new cfp and the needs of inshore fisheries.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal and agree that when drawing up legislative proposals in relation to the regulation of the use of fishing gear and the method of fishing, the commission should first of all look at the actual impact of these measures.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report by ms tomašić. the report contains measures of particular relevance to member states where small-scale fishing is an important source of livelihood but also a traditional way of life. in order to preserve traditional fishing methods, the report therefore proposes that these be defined and that certain rules be relaxed, such as exemptions from the prohibition of certain fishing methods, quotas or rules on the obligation to land all catches. it also stresses the need to take account of the specificities of the individual regions and the need for innovation in the so-called blue industries. i think that in these cases it is necessary to take into account coastal fishing and its role in the regions dependent on it, since the european union should protect traditional methods and ways of life that would otherwise disappear, and should take into account the fact that general bans and rules could have a devastating effect on traditional fishing. at the same time, without small-scale fishing, many people in small coastal areas could lose their livelihoods, and given that these areas are already characterised by high unemployment, such bans would make the situation even worse.
in writing. ‒ the european union is now the world's largest market for fishery products and has one of the largest fleets in the world, and is usually ranked among the top three fishing powers. fishing outside european union waters also takes place in waters under the jurisdiction of third countries. this situation may arise in the framework of a bilateral agreement with that third country. the european union traditionally has about 15 to 20 such agreements in force at any one time. many fleets from countries such as china, korea and taiwan operate under generally less stringent environmental, safety and social standards and benefit from high subsidies and often lower tax levels. the best strategy for achieving the european union's objective of promoting sustainable fisheries is to use the european union's influence on the international scene to improve fisheries management and the transparency of standards. this means in particular improving the transparency of fisheries, the regional approach to fisheries management, including promoting the harmonisation of conditions for access of foreign fleets to third countries, and, last but not least, the establishment of a sustainability framework for joint ventures.
in writing. the rapporteur has produced a very well-crafted report, in which she has clarified the problems relating to fisheries and in particular the shortcomings of the common fisheries policy. there is an old saying that the criminal is always one step ahead of the policeman because he is not deterred by law enforcement. the report submitted shows that this is also the case here in a broader sense. eu citizens are suffering from the illegal actions of certain third-country entities, who are putting themselves at an economic disadvantage by complying with strict european standards. on the basis of the arguments put forward, i agree with the rapporteur that in order to deal with this situation, the emphasis should be on transparency not only when contracts are concluded between fisheries operators but also after they have been concluded in the form of a public database in which all the necessary data on agreements between eu ship-owners and third countries will be accessible. this simple tool will help to make eu citizens more competitive and thus improve their living standards.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the initiative to increase europe's influence in the international fisheries arena. this is particularly important at a time when there is a serious fight for fishing grounds. in the interests of transparency, i believe that we should support a union database providing the commission with easy access to private agreements concluded between eu shipowners and third countries. i also welcome the idea of using our international influence to promote a transparent and environmentally friendly fisheries. that is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ this resolution deals with the implications of the common fisheries policy. the resolution takes care of both the economic and environmental sides, so therefore i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the european union is still the largest market for fishery products in the world today. the sale of fish products is subject to strict measures in the eu in terms of traceability, catch verification and the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing. the new cfp contains significant improvements, improving eu standards for fishing in remote areas. european investments in fisheries in third countries under joint ventures must be covered by the common fisheries policy. the eu should, through its sustainable fisheries partnership agreements, promote dialogue with partner countries on the establishment of a regulatory framework to ensure that joint ventures in the fisheries, processing and marketing sectors operate transparently, do not compete with the local small-scale fisheries sector and contribute to the country's development objectives. i supported the motion for a resolution on common rules for the application of the external dimension of the cfp, including fisheries agreements.

in writing. ‒ on 16 february 2016, the commission adopted a proposal for a decision to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund for sweden to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant by five companies operating primarily in the upper norrland region of sweden. in support of the link between redundancies and the major structural changes in world trade due to globalisation, sweden argues that the commercial vehicle manufacturing sector, which is a relatively small segment within the automotive industry, is no longer dominated by european and north american companies, as emerging asian truck manufacturers (china, india) have gained access to new technologies through joint ventures with recognised western market leaders. the request concerns 500 redundant workers and is for the recovery of almost eur 1,8 million. the personalised services to be provided to redundant workers include a variety of measures, including entrepreneurship and start-up grants, education and training, and job-search support. since the commission has concluded that the application meets the conditions for a financial contribution from the european globalisation adjustment fund under the relevant provisions of the egf regulation, i have voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the the request concerns 647 redundant workers at volvo trucks and four suppliers and customers of the manufacturer volvo trucks. volvo trucks is active in the motor vehicle, trailer and trailer manufacturing sectors. the commission established the profitability of the sampled union producers by expressing the pre-tax net profit of the sales of the like product to unrelated customers in the union as a percentage of the turnover of those sales. in this particular case, it is an amount of eur 1 793 710 to help former employees to find a new job.
in writing. the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) provides support for people who have lost their jobs as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation. in the last ten years, since we first felt the effects of the financial crisis, we have seen that changes of this kind have affected even large and stable companies, often affecting manufacturing plants, and the automotive industry in particular. the rule is that the egf may only be granted to a specific company if more than 500 workers are made redundant, counting not only the employees of the primary company but also the employees of other related companies such as suppliers and downstream producers. the request from sweden egf/2015/009 se/volvo trucks indicates that 647 workers are made redundant in this case. sweden has also fulfilled all other obligations relating to the mobilisation of the egf. it follows that sweden is entitled to a grant of eur 1 793 710 and i therefore vote in favour of the report. furthermore, i would like to remind the commission to provide all the necessary information on the egf so that applicants do not have difficulty in accessing the necessary documents. it is also important that there is no unnecessary delay in deciding on the contributions, as was the case with volvo trucks.
in writing. ‒ in a rapidly changing global world, many unforeseen circumstances can lead to a change in the labour market, profound structural changes in world trade, economic crisis or other external causes that can lead to a large number of people losing their jobs at once. regions where a particular sector of the economy provides a large number of jobs are particularly vulnerable, and it is therefore difficult for residents who have lost their jobs to find new ones. i think the globalization fund was created with a good idea. the training of the unemployed has a positive impact on the labour market and can create a competitive workforce, thus helping the region's economy. however, it is important to emphasise that its task is not to correct globalisation and the global crisis, but to help. in many cases, large companies are unable to compete with foreign competitors (in this case asian commercial vehicle manufacturers) which often enjoy high levels of state support at home. it is welcome that sweden started to provide the necessary personalised services well before the decision to grant egf support. we can therefore be sure that the aid will be used efficiently and to its intended purpose.
in writing. ‒ i fully support measures aimed at setting policies that create growth and jobs. however, i do not consider the european globalisation adjustment fund to be the right and effective instrument for these policies. that's why i voted against it.
