in writing. ‒ the glyphosate is an active ingredient widely used in herbicides. the approval of the active substance glyphosate in the european union will expire on 30 june 2016. subject to that objection, this draft measure renews the approval of the active substance glyphosate for a maximum period of 15 years. there are conflicting views on glyphosate with regard to the who international agency for research on cancer, which classifies glyphosate as a probable human carcinogen after evaluating a large body of scientific evidence. on the other hand, the european food safety authority does not accept any danger. however, he based his claims on unpublished studies from the industry. this objection is against the draft measures on the grounds that the draft implementing act fails to ensure a high level of protection of human and animal health and the environment and fails to apply the precautionary principle. i am of the opinion that the european commission should not renew the approval of glyphosate and should ensure an independent review of its classification on the basis of the available scientific evidence and studies.
in writing. glyphosate is a substance that is known to be particularly effective against weeds. pursuant to regulation (ec) no 1107/2009, an active substance may only be approved if it is not or is not to be classified as a carcinogen category 1a or 1b. in march 2015, the international agency for research on cancer (iarc) classified glyphosate as 'probably carcinogenic to humans' and classified it as group 2a. the european food safety authority (efsa) concluded that glyphosate is unlikely to present a carcinogenic hazard to humans and that the evidence does not support a classification with regard to its carcinogenic potential under regulation (ec) no 1272/2008. it is worth recalling that the criteria used by the iarc for group 2a are comparable to the criteria for category 1b, therefore glyphosate continues to pose a threat. there are also concerns that glyphosate, in addition to its carcinogenic properties, may interfere with the endocrine system. the decision to approve or not to approve glyphosate is very important because, if it is included in the list of approved substances, the population will be in direct and frequent contact with it, especially in close proximity to the dwellings, due to spraying, as glyphosate has been commonly used in spraying with the intention of destroying different herbal species. the protection of human, animal and environmental health is paramount and decisions that may affect it in any way need to be considered carefully and responsibly.
in writing. ‒ i think it's important in a situation like this to make a decision based on professional reasons, excluding the influence of politics and emotions. glyphosate has been widely used in agriculture for a long time, and its substitution and alternatives are questionable. i am concerned about the safety and health of the public, and i support initiatives that promote more in-depth research and control of this material. however, i think that the results we have at present are not clear enough to make it commercially acceptable to ban the substance, let alone the potential ramifications for farmers. the ban on glyphosate, which has been on the market for more than 40 years, could cause serious difficulties for the agricultural sector, especially for small and family-owned businesses. i could not vote to ban the substance, but i am actively monitoring the results of new research and i am prepared to intervene in the event of a threat, supported by relevant results.
in writing. ‒ the systemic herbicide glyphosate is currently the most widely produced herbicide worldwide. in doing so, some bacteria in commercial glyphosate preparations have been shown to cause changes in antibiotic resistance, with glyphosate residues being found in water, soil, food and even in breast milk. i therefore voted in favour of the resolution rejecting the extension of the authorisation for glyphosate for a further 15 years and calling on the european commission not to authorise any non-professional use of glyphosate.
in writing. ‒ the herbicide glyphosate is currently the most produced herbicide worldwide and its use has increased dramatically over the last 40 years, with a worldwide use factor of 260, from 3200 tonnes in 1974 to 825 000 tonnes in 2014. glyphosate is a non-selective herbicide that kills all herbs, and up to 76% of it is used worldwide in agriculture, but it's also used in forestry, in cities and in gardens. for this reason, glyphosate and its residues have been detected in water, soil, food, beverages and goods not intended for human consumption, as well as in the human body. for these reasons too, we called on the commission in the resolution to submit a new proposal for the renewal of the authorisation of glyphosate in order to better take into account the sustainable use of herbicides containing it. at the same time, we requested the accelerated initiation of an overall toxicity review and classification of the herbicide of concern on the basis of all available scientific evidence on its carcinogenicity and possible endocrine disrupting properties. we also called on the commission to renew the marketing authorisation for products containing glyphosate for only seven years, and also for professional use only.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the motion because i do not share the criticism of the approval of glyphosate, which is, moreover, based on a number of factually incorrect claims.
in writing. ‒ i supported the envi parliamentary committee's objection against the renewal of the authorisation for glyphosate. this renewal of authorisation was proposed by the european commission on the basis of new studies showing that glyphosate is not carcinogenic. however, envi does not consider these conclusions to be sufficiently reviewable, in particular because some key studies are not published. moreover, this substance, which is in close contact with the public due to its widespread use as a herbicide in the member states, has long been considered by experts to be a substance with probable carcinogenic effects. that is why i support the view that, until the probable carcinogenic effects have been sufficiently, transparently and scientifically disproved, we are obliged to apply the precautionary principle and not to put the health of the citizens of the european union at risk.
in writing. ‒ the report, the role of the union in a changing global environment, sets out priorities for the eu's role in the world. the european union faces a number of complex challenges and threats that require decisive joint action to address them in a way that does not compromise europe's fundamental values. the union should therefore ensure its internal and external resilience, take greater responsibility for its own security and territorial defence, and take into account the intrinsic link between internal and external security. we must continue to cooperate with countries with close links to the union in order to build peace and stability. in summary, the report says that the eu must be a constructive, flexible and stronger actor in today's multipolar world. i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ this report highlights old and new security challenges for the european union and presents more effective methods to strengthen the european union's position and its strategic role as an international actor. the european union and its member states need to take greater responsibility for collective security and be more active in europe's neighbourhood, taking full advantage of the provisions of the lisbon treaty on csdp. the european union must make more effective use of the diplomatic, economic and other instruments at its disposal to promote stability, security and prosperity in the region. there is no doubt that the european union must act in conjunction with nato, but it must also learn to act on its own. if this does not change, the european union will face a serious challenge in the future in dealing with the constantly changing global environment and new security challenges.
in writing. europe has been facing a changed security situation in recent months. most of the threats identified in the 2003 european security strategy - terrorism, proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, regional conflicts, state failure and organised crime - remain relevant, even though 13 years have passed since its identification. in addition, other problems were added that no one had foreseen at the time. the strategy should be revised more frequently, which will provide a completely different view of the current threats and security environment, while allowing for effective and timely action to be taken as new situations require. i am critical of the fact that the commission has not fulfilled its tasks entrusted to it by the european council in 2013 in relation to the planned comprehensive pan-european security of supply regime, the planned green paper on the control of defence and sensitive security industrial capabilities, the monitoring of defence and security procurement, as well as interstate sales in the defence sector.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the report, which is parliament's contribution to the report drawn up by the european external action service last year, on the union's overall strategy for foreign and security policy. the eu faces a major challenge, a complex threat, and a situation that requires a well-thought-out strategy. i agree that preserving the union's achievements, values and social model is a serious task that no single member state can tackle alone. the threats identified in the 2003 strategy are not only still relevant, but have multiplied and become much more complex. if we want peace, we must recognize that without compromise and cooperation, it will be difficult to achieve it. we need to increase the union's influence on the international stage, and internal unity is essential for this. i support the idea that the union needs to be more independent and that the common security policy should be reviewed in the direction of greater strategic autonomy and increased defence capabilities and capacities in cooperation with nato. i think the report is a good policy guide, and i voted for it.

in writing. ‒ many of the current and future challenges and threats to the eu are complex and interconnected, emanating from state and non-state actors both within and beyond common borders, and strong political will and leadership is needed to lead to bold common action to respond proactively, collectively and effectively to these challenges, and to protect the values and the eu social model. the eu faces many threats terrorism, organised crime, regional conflicts, ... the eu must therefore aim to promote peace, its values and the well-being of its people, while ensuring the security of its citizens and territory. if the eu is to be able to address the changing global environment, its strategy must be based on identifying and prioritising threats and challenges, defining responses to these threats and challenges and identifying the necessary means. the eu must continue its efforts to promote development and resilience in its neighbourhood and, in areas that are key to eu interests, strengthen these efforts. the global strategy should be reviewed every five years in cooperation with the new ep and the new commission, which would allow verifying that its objectives and priorities are still in line with the threats and the security environment.
in writing. ‒ the many current and future threats to the eu are complex and interconnected, emanating from state and non-state actors, and therefore require strong political will and the ability of the eu and its member states to act proactively. the eu today faces many serious and unforeseen challenges, such as the efforts of revisionist powers to redraw borders by force in violation of international law and to challenge the rules-based world order, climate change, slow economic growth, large flows of migrants and refugees and the biggest refugee crisis since the second world war, as well as technological developments in space and cyber, financial crime, nuclear proliferation and arms race, hybrid and asymmetric warfare. the eu's ability to act globally and confront these threats requires more effective management of regional security, a willingness to cooperate and overcome institutional obstacles, and, of course, the allocation of sufficient and flexible financial resources.

in writing. ‒ i did not support ms kalniete's report on the role of the european union in a changing global environment. while the report identifies many current challenges facing not only the european union and looks for ways to address them in order to stabilise the situation in the european neighbourhood but also to strengthen cooperation with nato, it sees one of the main solutions in achieving permanent joint transnational military units, joint defence forces and the definition of a common defence policy, which should eventually lead to a european defence union. in my view, this rhetoric significantly interferes with the competences of the member states, since defence policy has always been and should always remain the exclusive competence of the member states. i therefore strongly oppose such interventions and voted against this report.

in writing. ‒ in the last two months, cases of zika virus have been reported in 39 countries and territories worldwide. this includes some areas in the outermost regions of the european union, although there is currently no risk of zika virus transmission to the rest of the european union, we must be vigilant as this may change in the summer months. i therefore welcome the action of the european commission, which has released eur 10 million for funding, research and prevention against the zika virus. we need to promote prevention through contraceptive control in many countries by all means available and actively prepare for the possibility of a virus outbreak in continental europe as well.
in writing. zika virus is one of a class of viral diseases that have a low mortality but a high infection rate. as no effective antibody is yet known, it is necessary for the eu, as well as the entire international community, to devote the maximum possible resources (both financial and human) to research and development of vaccines against the disease, and to combat it, under the auspices of the world health organisation. however, it should be remembered that maternal infection does not necessarily mean that the disease is passed on to the foetus. i firmly disagree with the claim that zika automatically causes damage to the central nervous system of the fetus, since we know of many cases of babies being born perfectly healthy. in this context, therefore, i regard proposals for a general liberalization of abortion as unfortunate and medically completely unfounded. as we have seen with rubella, many infected women who resisted social pressure and refused to have an abortion subsequently gave birth to healthy children. similarly, we must understand the zika virus - if we were to introduce a procedure whereby every infected mother was automatically recommended for an abortion, it could be argued that we would take the lives of 99 healthy babies in order to prevent a single harm. i believe that the rubella experience serves as sufficient proof that abortion is not and cannot be the way to fight zika.

in writing. ‒ zika virus, which is mostly transmitted to humans by the bite of an aedes mosquito in tropical areas, has spread dangerously in many countries in the past year, and with no vaccine or treatment available, prevention is currently based on personal protection measures. it has been reported in 28 countries, and the consequences of zika virus may be felt particularly by young and poor women, most of whom live in the least developed regions. i am therefore pleased that the commission has allocated eur 10 million for zika virus research with a recommendation to focus on cases of severe congenital brain malformations in latin america and their possible link to zika virus infection. in the ep's report, we called on the commission to draw up an action plan to prevent the spread of the virus in europe and to assist member states and third countries in combating the epidemic in the regions most affected (especially the caribbean and central and south america).

in writing. the european parliament's proposed legislative resolution is a timely response to the current challenges of personal data protection in the eu. the challenging digital environment is constantly opening up new frontiers, with neither sufficient harmonisation of the rules for its use nor their effectiveness to ensure adequate protection of personal data. directive 95/46/ec, which is to be replaced by the new legislation, has been a great help in the area of personal data protection in the eu, and the basis on which it is based is still relevant today. however, the digital environment, which i refer to in particular the use of e-mail communication, social networks and the like, requires a completely new approach. i would particularly like to stress that the proposal for a regulation does not neglect to make data easier to access, which means that users will have more information on how data is processed and that this information will be clear and understandable. i also see as a great benefit the so-called 'right to be forgotten', which allows a natural person to have his data deleted if he does not wish it to be processed further. the proposal also offers other new legal features that will improve the quality of service provision and the protection of personal data of ordinary individuals in the digital environment.
in writing. ‒ today, the european parliament finally adopted a new directive on the processing and transfer of personal data between member states, which it has been working on for years. the aim was to develop a harmonised data protection framework that is able to meet the challenges of globalisation and rapid technological change. the world has changed a lot and now we have products like google or facebook in our daily lives, so it is not surprising that the data protection directive, which has been in force since 1995 and varies from one member state to another, seems outdated. i am pleased that the long work has paid off and that we have been able to agree on a well-developed, comprehensible proposal that is uniform for all member states.
in writing. ‒ i am pleased that the development of the protection of personal data provided is being promoted. that is why i voted in favour of this regulation. i consider it important that providers of personal data have control over the transparent way in which they process that data, using modern information technologies. the regulation also provides for a clear means of controlling the transmission of sensitive consumer information.
in writing. ‒ the the first legislative proposal from the commission on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data came in 2012. since then, discussions have taken place in the council, where national governments have long held off on adopting the final version of the regulation. since 2014, discussions on this matter have been frozen. it is only recently that the dramatic events in paris and brussels have revealed in full view the failure of the security services to exchange the necessary information. in this context, the european parliament calls for the conclusion of the discussions and the entry into force of legislative measures for the protection of personal data. i therefore supported the council's position at second reading and i hope that we will finally go from words to action and that the regulation will be put into practice. this proposal is also part of the package, together with the proposals for directives on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data for the prevention of crime and on the use of airline passenger name record data. in order to enable the security authorities to detect, investigate and prosecute the perpetrators of terrorist offences effectively, it is essential that clear rules be established at european level within which national authorities can operate. national governments will need to show more determination and implement all these instruments without delay in order to be able to guarantee the security of their citizens.

in writing. the data protection directive on police and criminal justice authorities is a legal act designed to ensure modern and comprehensive data protection in the european union. it shall strengthen the fundamental rights and freedoms of natural persons with regard to the processing of their personal data. one of the reasons why the institutions of the european union have embarked on the preparation of different types of legal acts on the protection of personal data is the fact that the processing of personal data which is not the subject of an exchange between member states is not currently covered by eu rules. this in some cases creates practical difficulties for the police and other authorities, who have difficulty in determining whether the processing is purely national or cross-border. the more we use the digital environment, the more its legal regulation deserves attention. misuse of personal data or various other forms of crime in this area are not uncommon. the detection of this type of crime requires a coherent high level of protection of personal data of natural persons and the facilitation of the exchange of personal data between competent authorities. the new data protection directive will help law enforcement authorities to cooperate more effectively with each other, leading to confidence building and legal certainty.

in writing. ‒ the recent terrorist attacks in paris and brussels have shown us that terrorist activity in europe has been steadily growing in recent years. terrorist attacks are becoming bolder, more sophisticated, and more transnational. the european union must do much more to tackle organised crime and terrorism. the european commission is trying to respond to the situation by proposing the use of pnr data. pnr data is information provided by passengers when booking air tickets and is retained by airlines. the proposed directive also provides for the use of pnr data by law enforcement authorities and provides for harmonised rules for such measures. when analysed in depth, pnr data can be an effective tool for identifying and tracking criminal and terrorist activities.
in writing. ‒ transnational crime and terrorism are also adopting more sophisticated modes of action in the age of globalisation. in order to prevent, detect and investigate such activity, it is necessary that law enforcement authorities be able to use recorded passenger data, but only in a manner that is regulated by law, that does not constitute an unjustified and unjustified interference with their rights and that does not restrict the free movement of persons. when used lawfully, the pnr system can be an appropriate and effective preventive tool in the detection and detection of transnational crime.
in writing. the security situation in europe has been alarming for some time and the recent events linked to the brussels attacks have only reinforced the need to take the necessary steps also in the legislative field. the new directive would empower air carriers to provide so-called passenger identity data to competent authorities for the purposes of the prevention, detection, investigation and prosecution of criminal offences and serious crime. the new legislation is aimed in particular at combating organised crime and terrorism, activities which have become increasingly complex, sophisticated and transnational in recent years. passenger name record data, i.e. data relating to the routine booking of tickets and subsequently used by carriers for operational purposes, could potentially contribute to the identification and tracing of criminal and terrorist activities with a view to the detention, tracking, investigation and prosecution of the perpetrators of those offences. the eu's response to the serious deterioration of the security situation on our territory is essential. we must, as far as possible, avoid the threat of a repeat of the events in paris or brussels. we cannot allow our citizens to continue to live in fear of danger, because that is how terrorists win. i believe that the disclosure of personal records is an effective tool for law enforcement authorities to be able to trace dangerous elements, and i therefore vote in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the report on the passenger name record (pnr) file. we have succeeded in adopting a proposal which will enable the european union to act more effectively against terrorism. the pnr only makes available to the authorities information which is already in the possession of the airlines. the proposal is clear and transparent and ensures that fundamental freedoms will not be restricted in any case.
in writing. ‒ the passenger names register file has slowly moved through parliament to today’s historic vote. this third part of the data protection package allows data that our airlines currently have to be shared with law enforcement agencies. so that when we take off, our name, ticket number, travel details are sent to the central anti-terrorism agencies. it is hoped that this will prevent potential terrorists from boarding a plane, or travelling undetected. in the light of the recent tragic attacks across our continent, maybe this measure will allow smart data to work for us, so that peace can conquer. therefore i voted for.
in writing. ‒ the directive on the use of passenger name record data (pnr) by airlines is an integral part of the toolkit in the fight against terrorist crime. recent dramatic events have shown that european security has serious gaps. although some shortcomings can be found in the current draft, the basic objectives of the measure are covered and i therefore supported this form of legislative text. this tool concerns data provided by passengers, collected by air carriers and used for ticketing and reservations. as these are commercial information and contain a lot of sensitive personal data, these records require maximum protection. on the one hand, it is essential to continue to be committed to an effective approach to the fight against terrorism, but on the other hand, it is necessary to protect fundamental rights and ensure respect for the privacy of eu citizens. the authorities that use these records must ensure that the fundamental rights of citizens to privacy are not infringed and that pnr data are used only for law enforcement and security purposes in cases of terrorist offences and transnational crime. at the same time, the use of these data for in-depth data analysis and profiling must be prohibited in all circumstances. in these circumstances, the measure should also contribute to enhancing the internal security of the schengen area.
in writing. ‒ the attacks in paris and brussels were also the result of a failure to cooperate between european intelligence services. the passenger name record is the first step towards better control of who is entering the territory of the european union. the new measure requires airlines to provide eu states with data on passengers between the eu and third countries. the register will focus on people with a european passport, as most perpetrators of terrorist acts come from their ranks.
in writing. - i supported the motion. however, in order to effectively reduce the risk of terrorist attacks, it is also necessary to register persons entering the european union by other means of transport with the same degree of care.
in writing. ‒ i supported the long-awaited directive on the use of passenger name records for the prevention, detection and investigation of terrorist offences and serious crime. i welcomed the fact that after more than five years of work, the directive had finally reached the stage of being voted on in plenary, particularly because i believe it will be a very valuable tool in preventing terrorist attacks such as those that recently struck paris and brussels. i think it is high time that these rules were adopted, as they will enable member states to identify so-called foreign fighters who have previously escaped the spotlight, and as they were not among the suspects, member states had limited options to track them down. the proposal was, in my view, very well conceived and i am very glad that it was not taken off the table at the last minute. i believe that the clear rules do not represent any risk to passengers of misuse of their personal data or any new obligations, but on the contrary a major step forward in protecting their safety and combating terrorist acts.
in writing. ‒ the aim of the trade secrets directive is to provide protection for european businesses facing economic espionage, both at european union level and at international level. there is currently no europe-wide measure and legislation in individual member states ranges from nonexistent to very strict. this proposal has high support from businesses, including a large number of smes. it is necessary to find a solution that strikes an appropriate balance between avoiding unjustified proposals to fraudulently obtain or disseminate a trade secret and avoiding that information that should be shared and exchanged is kept secret by overly broad protection.
in writing. ‒ the protection of trade secrets against their unauthorised acquisition, use and disclosure. the trade secret represents a specific asset for each of the entities concerned, which increases its competitiveness and thus its market position. the proposal provides for the institute of trade secrets in products and services. the proposal aims to strengthen the competitiveness of european businesses by means of more precise regulation and increased protection of trade secrets, while ensuring consumer protection. the disclosure of a trade secret shall be possible only where union and member state law so permits, while ensuring the protection of the trade secret holder's rights.
in writing. a trade secret is a special property which has the character of an absolute right and which the owner can dispose of as he wishes, while deciding whether and to whom to disclose it and determining the form of its secrecy. this is an integral part of business and must be treated with great sensitivity, even in the context of regulation, because inadequate or poor regulation can restrict and endanger entrepreneurs. the aim of the proposal is to establish a sufficient and comparable level of redress across the internal market in the event of trade secret misuse. the current national rules do not provide the same level of protection of trade secrets against misuse in the eu, which threatens the smooth functioning of the internal market for information and know-how. the legislative proposal sets out good rules that will lead to an improvement in the competitiveness of european companies. i particularly appreciate that the rules apply not only to trade secrets relating to products but also to services. the directive also aims to ensure the protection of trade secrets already in the process of research and the creation of new ideas, which will significantly protect in particular small and medium-sized enterprises, which have significantly more limited financial and other means to protect their rights as large entrepreneurs.
in writing. ‒ trade secrets are confidential information that can give certain companies a competitive advantage they may include industrial secrets, manufacturing secrets. this is key information in the competitive battle and key elements of the company's competitive advantage. it is important to mention that trade secrets cannot be compared to intellectual property trade secrets are not exclusive, they are not the exclusive property of one person, and therefore it is necessary to regulate the use and protection of trade secrets in a precise and targeted manner so that business secrets cannot be accessed and used by persons other than the owner of the secret. the commission proposal lays down measures, procedures and remedies for the holder of a trade secret in cases where the secret is misused or disclosed, or is misappropriated or misused by third parties.
in writing. ‒ there is a lot of information that is essential for the competitiveness of an idea or a company and that is not covered by the protection related to intellectual property rights and that needs to be protected. it is important and necessary to regulate the acquisition, use and disclosure of trade secrets at european level.
in writing. ‒ i agreed to the draft directive on the protection of business secrets, as it managed to incorporate several improvements over the commission's original proposal through amendments. the aim of the directive on the protection of business secrets is to protect european companies that may be exposed to economic espionage at european or international level. there has been no action at european level to address this issue. at the same time, legislation on this matter varies across member states, as some have a high degree of protection of trade secrets and some have none at all. i am therefore pleased that we have been able to reach agreement on legislation that will protect innovative approaches by businesses in line with intellectual property agreements. i also welcome the fact that, despite the council's opposition, the protection of whistleblowers has been preserved, which is unprecedented in this directive. parliament also managed to remove freedom of the media and freedom of expression from the legislative text. strong guarantees have been provided for workers' mobility, workers' right to information and representation. overall, i assess the current form of the proposal as balanced and believe it will have a positive impact on a wide range of businesses.
in writing. ‒ one in five companies in the eu is a victim of theft of confidential business information. it is therefore important to enforce new european rules to help companies to obtain legal redress in the event of the unlawful acquisition or use of their trade secrets. member states will therefore be obliged to ensure that injured firms can seek compensation through the courts.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal and support the improvement of the mechanisms for protecting trade secrets.

in writing. ‒ the resolution adopted is based on a large number of petitions concerning children's rights received by parliament's committee on petitions. with free movement within the union, the number of crossborder family relationships has multiplied, and with it the need for crossborder settlement of disputes. the resolution calls on the commission and the member states to promote a more coordinated exchange of information and cooperation on cross-border issues in order to protect children's rights. the resolution, based on the questions raised by the petitions, deals with the circumstances surrounding the adoption of children, concerns court decisions to be enforced under the brussels iia regulation, and addresses the issues of placement of children, contact, withdrawal of custody, and the problems caused by adoption without consent and illegal removal abroad. increased european mobility has also brought about changes in the lives of families, which require union responses where appropriate. the parliament believes that, for example, in the case of adoption, children should be placed in a situation where they can learn, use and maintain contact with their cultural background in their mother tongue. parliament called on the commission to develop a website on the subject, which would provide practical information to eu citizens on child protection and parental rights in the various member states.
in writing. ‒ the eu charter of fundamental rights and international conventions emphasise the status of children as independent and autonomous rights holders. the protection of the interests and needs of the child must be a self-evident and natural priority for all public authorities, administrations and institutions that interfere in any way with the rights of the child. with regard to the free movement of persons and the content of petitions concerning abductions, child removal, maintenance and arrangements for contact with a child, it is essential that the member states of the union provide their citizens with sufficient information on their parental rights and obligations and on the procedures and rights of the child protection authorities in each member state. the commission must submit a proposal to unify the terminology of the child's habitual residence, which can eliminate many unnecessary conflicts in the adoption of a child in a cross-border area. any decision by the child welfare authorities should be taken only in the interests of protecting the rights of the child and after sufficient prior communication with the child welfare authorities of the member state of which the child is a national.
in writing in today's open-border europe, we increasingly encounter cases in the area of family law with international elements. marriages between people of different nationalities are not uncommon, nor is adoption of children from countries other than the parents' country of origin or residence. the reality naturally called for legislation at eu level to bring together the disparate national legislations. however, in my view, the brussels ii regulation does not sufficiently address the problems that citizens often have to face in their daily family life. the legal frameworks of the member states remain inconsistent, so convergence and close cooperation in areas such as justice, social protection and criminal proceedings in cases of cross-border child abduction are essential. children must be given appropriate access to the rights which they enjoy under international conventions binding on all member states of the union. it is necessary that family courts also ensure their proper application by setting up specialised chambers dealing with cross-border cases involving children. children must be able to communicate with their parents, unless, of course, it is against their interests. social workers must be specially trained to assess individual cases as expertly as possible, especially as regards adoption. i am in favour of the eu paying more attention to family law issues, and i therefore vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. ‒ the protection of children's rights must always be at the forefront of national legislation. the children of today will be the creators of the world's future, and their interests - which are the basis of child protection - must be considered paramount and conditions must be created to ensure that their rights are protected to the fullest extent possible throughout the european union.
in writing ‒ we have an obligation to protect children and to help parents care for their offspring rather than tear children from their families. adoption must always be a last resort when all else fails, including placing children within the wider family. in the event of a child being removed from his or her family, the children and the family must be guaranteed the right to contact, the use of the mother tongue, the principle of non-separation of siblings, etc., as required by the resolution adopted. furthermore, legal aid and support for parents as 'primary carers' is to be guaranteed. i am very pleased that the resolution contains these specific proposals, which is why i voted in favour. this is a concrete step towards ensuring the fundamental rights of both children and their parents in the increasingly frequent cases of children being taken from their families in another eu member state.
in writing ‒ in practice, we see many cases where the protection of the interests of the child is not always the first priority in some member states. in doing so, the best interests of the child must be paramount in all decisions concerning childcare at all levels. member states must put in place monitoring and evaluation systems with relevant socio-economic and country-specific statistics in matters concerning children. given that each member state has its own rules on the protection of the best interests of the child, it is necessary for the commission to provide a clear and easily accessible handbook with practical information for eu citizens on institutional mechanisms for the protection of children, with a particular focus on adoption and foster care, and on parental rights in different member states. member states must, through their well-funded policies, put in place early warning and monitoring mechanisms, with adequate support for families as primary and natural carers, especially in vulnerable communities at risk of social exclusion.
in writing ‒ the best interests of the child must be a primary consideration in all decisions concerning their care, at all levels. increased mobility within the eu can also have a negative impact on their development and lives. it is therefore essential that the protection of children and their rights be based on international and cross-border cooperation. i consider european judicial cooperation, social services for child protection, control of child custody and prevention of crossborder parental abductions to be among the most important mechanisms.
in writing ‒ member states must cooperate more in resolving crossborder disputes about children between divorced parents. children are the ones who pay the highest price for lengthy custody proceedings or for waiting for an adoption decision. i am very pleased that the resolution adopted proposes some concrete ways of speeding up this process. it is also important to improve parents' awareness of how to deal with child custody disputes. i feel sorry for every case where a family breaks up, but life brings such things and we should do our utmost to ensure that the legal relationship between parents is resolved quickly and with kindness to the children, even when the situation is complicated by the international dimension of the dispute.
in writing ‒ i supported the resolution of the committee on petitions. this resolution was in response to the many petitions received by the peti committee concerning adoption, international kidnappings, or child-care practices in general. the resolution is, in my view, very useful, particularly because it covers cross-border cases involving children, such as international parental child abduction or adoption. this is why minimum standards should be established for procedural rules, cooperation between countries should be strengthened, recognition of judicial decisions should be strengthened, but also the possibility of using alternative solutions such as mediation. as regards the issue of intercountry adoption, i appreciate in this context that the resolution advocates the right of the child to remain in contact with his or her original environment, culture and language, even in the event of adoption. and most important of all, the very assessment of the need to remove a child from the biological parents and the subsequent decision on its adoptability. in my view, such solutions should be resorted to only in extreme cases, when the family cannot fulfill its role even with the help of the state. in any case, such decisions should be carefully considered, giving the parents a chance to make amends, but also allowing the extended family to care for the child. only then can we say that the decision was made in the best interests of the child.

in writing ‒ in this particular case, it follows on from the three previous railway packages, which were primarily aimed at increasing the competitiveness and interoperability of european railways while maintaining a high level of safety. however, the three previous packages did not address the inadequate level of adjustment and tackle barriers to competition, discrimination and improvements in the business environment. the agreement on the final form of the fourth railway package was born with great difficulty and the negotiations between the council and the european parliament were very lengthy and demanding. the main objective of the fourth railway package is therefore to strengthen the position and powers of the era and thereby increase savings for railway undertakings and manufacturers across the european union. however, close and consistent cooperation between the national authorities of the member states and the era will be needed to achieve the objectives of the package, and the level of exchange of expertise and information will have to be improved.
in writing ‒ there are currently over 11,000 different national safety and operational rules, together with procedures and standards, in the eu. the european rail system is neither efficient nor transparent. i therefore support greater integration of the european railway area. this type of transport contributes to jobs and growth in a more sustainable way. the aim is to reduce costs for railway operators, manufacturers and thus also to provide users with better quality and less costly services, whether passenger or freight. the establishment of the eu railway agency eliminates the need for multiple applications. the agency will issue all authorisations for vehicles intended for cross-border operations and all safety certificates to railway companies providing cross-border services. with regard to vehicles and operators operating exclusively in national transport, the applicant will be able to choose whether his application is to be processed by the agency or by a national authority. we will allow the agency to set up a single point of contact to serve as a single point for all applications. this information and communication system will result in simpler and more transparent procedures.
in writing rail transport is an integral part of european infrastructure and as such contributes significantly to the development of the eu internal market. its modernisation, competitiveness and transparency in public procurement are issues that the eu has been dealing with for a long time. the new regulation would bring further changes aimed at increasing the competitiveness and interoperability of railways while maintaining the european standard of their safety. these changes are intended to help overcome the obstacles faced by the sector, whether in terms of competition, liberalisation, dynamism or a favourable business environment. the legislative proposal also addresses the strengthening of the competences of the european railway agency (era), which should be more closely linked to the activities of the railway agencies at member state level in order to make their cooperation more effective. the tasks of the era would include improving the technical compatibility of infrastructure, rolling stock, signalling parts of the rail system or simplifying the approval procedures for rolling stock. the main objective is to further integrate the european railway area so that the sector can contribute to jobs and growth in a more sustainable way. i also believe that speeding up administrative procedures and avoiding hidden discrimination will also contribute to the satisfaction of european travellers and to the development of business activities. i support the motion.

in writing ‒ the report is part of the so-called fourth railway package, which aims to improve the quality and safety of rail services. the main objective of the package is to remove the obstacles to the creation of a single railway area and thus to open up and improve the interoperability of the market. the report has, for example, simplified the issuing of permits for trains used for cross-border transport by the european railway agency, thus eliminating the need for multiple applications. overall, the adoption of this package will mean a modernisation of the rail sector and i believe that, once the transposition period is over, eu citizens will also see positive changes in rail services. i therefore supported this report and the other two reports forming the fourth railway package.
in writing ‒ the railway market in europe has undergone tremendous changes in the last decade. the european union has responded to this situation by gradually adopting three railway packages, the main priorities of which are to open up national markets, increase the competitiveness and interoperability of railways and, last but not least, continuously improve the safety of citizens of the member states when travelling by train. however, the european institutions must constantly work to improve the situation, as the railway market share in the european union is still very low, at only 6%. the european commission is trying to respond by removing the remaining administrative and technical obstacles through the fourth railway package.
in writing ‒ the proposed directive aims to increase the quality and efficiency of rail services and transport, which currently represents only 6% of the eu's internal market, by reducing the administrative burden and removing technical barriers to the coordination of the rail systems of the eu member states. the aim is to build a single european railway area, harmonising and unifying rules and procedures for railway undertakings and users of railway services. greater satisfaction with the rail services provided will also lead to a desirable increase in the rail transport market share.
in writing despite its undisputed advantages and potential, rail transport is generally experiencing a downward trend in transport market share at european level. moreover, surveys show that more than half of citizens are generally dissatisfied with the services provided by railways. the eu's efforts are therefore focused on improving the quality and operability of european railways while maintaining the highest possible level of safety. the legislative proposal on interoperability of european railways, as part of the so-called fourth railway package, aims to reverse the current situation, in particular by measures aimed at removing remaining administrative and technical barriers through the introduction of a common approach to safety and interoperability rules in order to increase economies of scale for railway undertakings operating in the eu. reducing administrative costs and speeding up harmonised administrative procedures are also of great importance. those measures, together with the decision-making powers of the european railway agency, will serve to build a functioning single european railway area in order to improve the quality of rail services for citizens and the competitiveness of railways. i vote in favour of the report as it stands.
in writing. ‒ ensuring the interoperability of the rail system is key to creating an integrated european rail network. one of europe's major achievements is the single market and interoperability, the results of which are undeniable in many areas. in the rail sector, while progress is being made, there are still many market barriers to interoperability that need to be addressed. the interoperability directive is a key step towards opening up national markets, which aims to reduce costs, eliminate discrimination and relieve businesses of bureaucratic burdens through harmonised administrative procedures, thus having a positive impact on the economy as a whole. despite its many advantages, the rail transport share in the eu market is only 6% and more than half of users are not satisfied with the services. i therefore voted in favour of the report in the hope that the fourth railway package will be implemented without undue delay and that it will demonstrate the positive impact of the achievements of the single european railway network on the daily lives of citizens.
in writing ‒ the system introduced by this new directive will bring europe closer to building a single european railway area. it will reduce administrative costs and speed up procedures while maintaining the current high level of security. at the same time, it will help to prevent any hidden discrimination, especially for new companies wishing to enter the railway market. this is expected to help increase economies of scale for eu railway undertakings and manufacturers and improve the competitiveness of eu businesses. i support this legislative resolution.
in writing ‒ in recent decades, rail transport has shown a steady decline compared to other modes of transport and national monopolies persist in this sector. this is confirmed by statistical indicators which show that the overall share of rail transport in the eu market is stagnating at 6%, and according to eurobarometer, up to 54% of users are dissatisfied with rail services. i supported the resolution because i believe that with the introduction of the fourth railway package, which includes the interoperability directive, we will be able to improve the quality and efficiency of rail services in the eu. i believe that the adoption of the new directive will bring europe closer to building a single european railway area and will also gradually remove the remaining administrative and technical barriers to the market, thus avoiding any hidden discrimination, especially for new companies wishing to enter the railway market. i am confident that the directive will contribute to the creation of new investment opportunities, new jobs and new opportunities and benefits for passengers, public authorities and the european economy as a whole, thanks to the single european railway area.
in writing ‒ this is one of three legislative proposals to remove technical barriers to better functioning of the eu's railways. both carriers and wagon manufacturers today face different standards in different member states. the new rules remove these obstacles and will lead to increased efficiency and reduced certification costs for both transporters and manufacturers. once all the planned changes have been adopted, the conditions should be created to make rail transport more attractive to passengers not only through prices but also through a high european quality guaranteed in each member state. i think we need such a guarantee in slovakia.
in writing ‒ the safety level of the railway system in the european union is generally high, especially compared to road transport. in line with technical and scientific progress, safety should be further improved where feasible and taking into account the expected improvement in the competitiveness of rail transport. in order to further enhance safety, the national safety authorities should be completely independent in terms of organisation, legal structure and decision-making from railway undertakings, the infrastructure manager, the applicant and the contracting entity. they should carry out their tasks in an open and non-discriminatory manner and cooperate with the era to create a single railway area and coordinate their decision-making criteria.
in writing ‒ the directive aims to increase railway safety in the european cross-border area. the european railway agency will issue railway safety certificates to undertakings operating in more than one member state. an undertaking operating exclusively in the territory of one member state will be able to choose between a national authority or era when obtaining a safety certificate. the verifiability and mutual awareness of compliance with safety rules will be increased and the investigation of detected infringements will be improved.
the eu has long sought to establish a single framework of railway safety rules, which was partly achieved by the adoption of the previous third railway legislative package. the latest proposal for an amendment to the railway safety directive aims to continue the efforts to create a single market for rail transport services, which will include a common regulatory framework for safety. it is important that this legislative framework should aim to overcome the differences in principles, approaches and cultures between the member states which have long made it difficult to overcome technical barriers. the main objective of the proposed amendment is the transition to a union single safety certificate, in the issuing of which the european railway agency will play an important role. i believe that the proposed amendments will contribute to further harmonising the content of safety regulations, the safety certification of railway undertakings, but also the safety conditions that their staff must strictly observe. these rules are directly related to the safety of european citizens and, in my view, will contribute to increasing it. for that reason, i support the motion.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the european union should be the guarantor of a quality safety standard. we have made a number of progresses in the area of uniform safety rules, but we have not yet achieved harmonisation of the safety certification system at union level. the safety certificates under national competence shall be issued on the basis of national guidelines, technical and operational approaches. the divergence of principles and methods makes it difficult to remove technical barriers, and i therefore welcome the renewal of the fourth railway package, which gives the european railway agency a key role in the field of safety certification. harmonisation brings a number of benefits, such as mandatory control of the rules on working and rest times for train drivers, but also increases public safety. the european railway agency enables a close exchange of information between the actors concerned, which is key in the light of the security threats experienced in recent months. i consider it a major step forward to ensure the efficiency of cross-border information exchange, which is particularly important in cases where a railway vehicle is used in more than one member state. that is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing ‒ member states will be obliged to monitor drivers' compliance with the rules on work, driving and rest, which will increase safety on the roads. the directive will improve the awareness of relatives of accident victims. coordination of rescue services will also be improved. i support this legislative resolution.
in writing ‒ the although the safety level of the union's rail system is generally high, especially compared to road transport, i still consider improving the safety of european rail transport and building a safe and modern integrated rail network to be one of the eu's most important tasks and priorities. unfortunately, we are again convinced that at the level of individual member states, where safety regulations have been developed according to national guidelines, large differences are emerging which prevent the removal of technical barriers and the introduction of international activities. i believe that in order to ensure a high level of railway safety and a level playing field for all railway undertakings, these undertakings should be subject to the same safety requirements. i supported the resolution because i believe that by creating a common regulatory framework for rail safety we can more successfully proceed to create a single market for rail services. i also expect that this directive will lead to a more thorough review of the tasks of the national safety authorities and the subsequent redistribution of responsibilities between them and the agency.
in writing in the eu, manipulation of indices that serve as benchmarks in financial instruments is also not uncommon in the financial sector. these developments clearly highlight areas where european legislation is not sufficiently effective and therefore more targeted regulation is needed. the benchmarks are of great importance not only for financial institutions and investors but also for ordinary consumers. the eu must therefore avoid a repeat of incidents such as libor or euribor, known cases of interest rate manipulation. such cases seriously undermine confidence in the market, financial instruments, disrupt the economy, deprive investors of profits and negatively affect the mortgage and loan market. i agree with the content of the new proposed legislation, which aims to strengthen governance to ensure that conflicts of interest are avoided, to ensure that benchmark creators are subject to strict scrutiny, and to ensure adequate protection for users of benchmarks by increasing transparency and guaranteeing the right to redress. i see the proposed measures as an attempt to strengthen europeans' confidence in financial market instruments, whose high level of transparency must be guaranteed in relation to the management of citizens' funds and savings. i therefore support the proposal as it stands.
in writing. ‒ each benchmark is very important for the proper functioning of financial and commodity markets. their manipulation is an illegal activity that has a negative impact on the economy of the european union, among others. in this context, the european union needs a comprehensive framework that strengthens benchmark standards and increases transparency, thereby preventing manipulation and abuse. that's what the report is calling for, and that's why i support it.
in writing, i support the efforts to prevent benchmark manipulation. i therefore voted in favour of this european parliament resolution on a regulation to enhance the credibility of benchmarks that are critical to the stability of european financial markets, such as the london interbank libor and the euro area interbank euribor.
in writing ‒ although the application of administrative and criminal sanctions for index manipulation is already provided for in the market abuse directive and regulation, i believe that the risks of manipulation associated with the creation and use of indices need to be regulated and prevented. i consider it a serious shortcoming in particular that the supervisory authorities supervise financial instruments but not the creation and management of indices, which are the determining factors of the risk, performance and economic value of these instruments. given the scale and impact of the indices on our financial system as well as on the physical energy markets, i consider the current state of self-regulation to be ineffective. i am concerned that many indices and benchmarks, due to their incorrect construction or manipulation, cause damage in the real economy, ultimately affecting in particular many businesses, households, investors and financial institutions. i supported the resolution because i believe that the new regulation will help us to improve the conditions for the proper functioning of the internal market, in particular the financial market, and to ensure a high level of consumer and investor protection.
in writing ‒ i fully support the adoption of new legislation that will increase the credibility of benchmarks that are critical to the stability of european financial markets. the new rules aim to make the process of setting benchmarks, so-called indices or benchmarks, more transparent and to prevent conflicts of interest such as those that led to the libor manipulation scandal.

in writing ‒ this particular vote concerns the discharge for the budget of the european aviation safety agency.
in writing ‒ i supported the discharge to the executive director of the european aviation safety agency (easa) as the agency's final annual accounts were approved by the court of auditors. according to the financial statements, the agency's final budget for the financial year 2014 was approximately eur 181 million, representing an increase of 8,47% compared to the previous year. the court of auditors in its report states that the agency's annual accounts are reliable and that the underlying transactions are legal and regular. however, the report also highlights the shortcomings of the agency in public procurement matters, as it should improve in particular the planning of framework contracts. the agency was found to have failed to comply with several statutory rules for the renewal of framework contracts. it is therefore essential that progress is made in this matter and that the agency submits a supplementary report to parliament. on the other hand, it is to be welcomed that the agency has set out in its code of conduct for staff a comprehensive policy on the prevention of conflicts of interest as well as a policy on gifts and hospitality. despite these reservations, the report notes that in 2014 the agency made substantial changes in the way it operates and also reviewed its organisational structure. i therefore hope that it will succeed in the future in ensuring aviation safety throughout europe, as civil aviation is a very fast-growing sector.
in writing, ‒ the european parliament has granted discharge to the european aviation safety agency in respect of the implementation of the agency's budget for the financial year 2014, and has also approved the closure of the accounts.
in writing ‒ this particular vote concerns the granting of budgetary discharge to the european asylum support office.
in writing ‒ i have agreed to grant a discharge to the executive director of the european asylum support office (easo) as the final annual accounts of the agency have been assessed positively by the court of auditors. according to the financial statements, the final budget of the office for the financial year 2014 was over eur 15,5 million, with up to 94% of its resources coming from the union budget. the court of auditors in its report states that the agency's annual accounts are reliable and that the underlying transactions are legal and regular. however, the authority has visible shortcomings in budget planning, which have been reflected in several irregularities. for example, the agency carried over eur 1,3 million of appropriations not covered by legal commitments and almost one third of payments were made after the deadline set in the financial regulation. the high turnover of staff, including in key positions, is also a consideration which, in a situation of increased asylum applications, may impair the agency's ability to meet its objectives. these budgetary shortcomings will need to be addressed urgently, as additional tasks are expected to be assigned to the agency and its staff will need to be increased proportionately in the context of the refugee crisis. i believe that the easo's functionality needs to be consolidated, as the agency faces major challenges in the near future.
in writing ‒ in this turbulent time of the refugee crisis, our support for the bodies dealing with the issue is important. i therefore voted in favour of granting discharge to the european asylum support office in respect of the implementation of the office's budget for the financial year 2014, and at the same time approved the closure of its accounts.
in writing ‒ this particular vote concerns the discharge for the european banking authority.
in writing ‒ i supported the discharge to the executive director of the european banking authority (eba) as the final annual accounts of the agency were positively assessed by the court of auditors. according to the financial statements, the authority's final budget for the financial year 2014 was over eur 33,5 million, representing an increase of 29,39% compared to the previous year. however, this increase was due to the fact that the authority was only recently created. the court of auditors in its report states that the agency's annual accounts are reliable and that the underlying transactions are legal and regular. the creation of this body is part of the steps to create a new and comprehensive european system of financial supervision, which has been called for by the events following the financial crisis. the eba's role is to support member states in ensuring financial stability and thereby achieving a better integrated, more efficient and safer financial market. however, the support of this body is essentially technical in nature and any political decisions are the prerogative of the union legislator. it also shows that the financial allocation to eba is insufficient to achieve its objectives. it is therefore possible to expect that the authority's budget will increase due to a shortage of highly qualified staff. i hope that the technical regulations that the authority will develop and the technical advice that it will provide to the legislator will help to maintain the stability of the financial system.
in writing ‒ the european parliament has granted discharge to the european banking authority in respect of the implementation of the authority's budget for the financial year 2014, and has also approved the accounts.

in writing ‒ i have agreed to grant the director of the european centre for disease prevention and control (ecdc) discharge as the final annual accounts of the agency have been assessed positively by the court of auditors. according to the financial statements, the final budget of the centre for the financial year 2014 amounted to approximately eur 60,5 million, representing an increase of 3,72 per cent compared to the previous year. the court of auditors in its report states that the agency's annual accounts are reliable and that the underlying transactions are legal and regular. the centre's outputs are generally rated as high quality, despite the fact that in the course of 2014 the centre's management was dominated by continuity issues such as the need to make a balanced selection and to re-align planning to address high priority threats. the biggest challenge of the year was the ebola outbreak, with more than 100 staff working to support the eu's response to the challenge. the centre's work has proven to be flexible, service-oriented and committed to scientific excellence. i therefore believe that, even on the basis of this current experience, the centre's work will move forward and contribute to the prevention of diseases.

in writing ‒ this particular vote concerns the discharge for the european chemicals agency.
in writing ‒ i supported the discharge to the executive director of the european chemicals agency (echa) as the agency's final annual accounts were approved by the court of auditors. according to the financial statements, the agency's final budget for the financial year 2014 was approximately eur 114 million, representing an increase of 6,37 per cent compared to the previous year. the court of auditors in its report states that the agency's annual accounts are reliable and that the underlying transactions are legal and regular. as regards the agency itself, its task since 2012 has been to manage and implement the technical, scientific and administrative aspects of the regulation on the making available on the market of biocidal products. the agency's operations were affected by far lower than expected biocidal product-related fees in 2014, which led to budget shortfalls. the agency's management is therefore concerned that if this situation were to continue and not be compensated by a higher subsidy, it would be extremely difficult for the agency to continue to meet its obligations. it will therefore be necessary to consider ways of financing the agency in the future in such a way that its activities are sustainable.

in writing ‒ this particular vote concerns the discharge for the budget of the european food safety authority.
in writing ‒ i supported the discharge to the executive director of the european food safety authority (efsa) as the final annual accounts of the agency were approved by the court of auditors. according to the financial statements, the final budget of the office for the financial year 2014 amounted to approximately eur 79,7 million, representing an increase of 2,11% compared to 2013. the court of auditors in its report states that the agency's annual accounts are reliable and that the underlying transactions are legal and regular. the main objections raised against the office concerned its transparency and objectivity. although the office allocates 74% of its human resources to scientific activities, evaluation and information gathering, as well as communication, it is of the utmost importance that all information is available to the media, as public interest in the office's decision-making is high. the authority should also take into account a decision of the european ombudsman that the authority should review its conflict of interest rules. it is necessary to ensure that experts in the academic field provide the authority with all relevant information. for these reasons, i believe that the authority should undertake a systematic review of its policy on independence and scientific decision-making as soon as possible, which would benefit its credibility.
in writing ‒ the european parliament has granted discharge to the european food safety authority in respect of the implementation of the authority's budget for the financial year 2014, and has also approved the accounts.
‒ this particular vote concerns the granting of budgetary discharge to the european institute for gender equality.
in writing ‒ the public resources invested should be used to promote the equal status of men and women in society on the basis of their equal human dignity, not on the basis of ideological motives. the work of the european institute for gender equality can in no way serve as a tool for promoting gender ideology, which forces us to adopt a number of new gender identities in addition to quotas and self-styled control and monitoring mechanisms. similarly, this ideology cannot seek, under the pretext of ensuring gender equality, to control the lives of citizens to such an extent as to interfere with their private lives. the european commission's recent proposals go so far as to mandate a 50/50 split of household work. ideological control of the lives of citizens has been a common practice here for years in the non-democratic socialist political system. on the contrary, we expect the eu to protect and ensure justice, democracy and pluralism. i also believe that the eu budget as a whole should first receive a positive opinion from the court of auditors. that is why i voted against the discharge of this institution.
in writing ‒ i agreed to grant the director of the european institute for gender equality (eige) discharge, as the final annual accounts of the agency were confirmed by the court of auditors. the financial statements show that the institute's final budget for the financial year 2014 was around eur 7,3 million, representing a reduction of 3,08% compared to 2013. the court of auditors in its report states that the agency's annual accounts are reliable and that the underlying transactions are legal and regular. the institute was established to help and strengthen the promotion of gender equality in all union policies and subsequent national policies, as well as to combat discrimination on grounds of sex. according to the available data, the institute's planned outputs in 2014 were achieved at 95 percent. the present nature of the agency means that it can best pursue its objectives and tasks provided that the status of the institute as a separate, specialised body within the eu institutional framework is preserved. i believe that the problems of gender discrimination still persist and that the institute should therefore continue its work and intensify its activities in particular in raising awareness among eu citizens of these problems.
in writing ‒ the european parliament has granted discharge to the european institute for gender equality in respect of the implementation of the institute's budget for the financial year 2014, and has also approved the accounts.
in writing ‒ this particular vote concerns the granting of budgetary discharge to the european insurance and occupational pensions authority.
in writing ‒ i supported the discharge to the executive director of the european insurance and occupational pensions authority (eiopa) as the final annual accounts of the agency were approved by the court of auditors. according to the financial statements, the authority's final budget for the financial year 2014 was approximately eur 21,5 million, representing an increase of 15% compared to 2013. this increase is explained by the fact that the authority was established only recently and its resources account for 40% of the union budget. the court of auditors in its report states that the agency's annual accounts are reliable and that the underlying transactions are legal and regular. eiopa is part of the new and comprehensive european financial supervisory system that was established in response to the financial crisis. the main task of the authority is to promote a common supervisory regime across the single market in order to ensure financial stability and a better integrated, more transparent, more efficient and more secure financial market. at the same time, however, all political decisions remain the prerogative of the legislator and the nature of the body is purely technical. the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 264 concerning the establishment of a european supervisory authority. i therefore believe that the institution will be able to ensure that it has sufficient capacity to fulfil its mandate.
in writing ‒ the european parliament has granted discharge to the european insurance and occupational pensions authority in respect of the implementation of the authority's budget for the financial year 2014, and has also approved the closure of the accounts.

in writing ‒ i have agreed to grant discharge to the director of the european police office (europol) as the final annual accounts of the agency have been positively assessed by the court of auditors. according to the financial statements, the agency's final budget for the financial year 2014 was approximately eur 84,3 million, representing an increase of 2,2% compared to 2013. the court of auditors in its report states that the agency's annual accounts are reliable and that the underlying transactions are legal and regular. however, it would be appropriate for europol to also publish its consolidated annual report on a regular basis on its website, which would contribute to the overall transparency of the agency. it is also striking that the agency had a high rate of cancelled commitments due to delayed it projects provided by external contractors. on the other hand, i believe that the new code of conduct with guidelines on the prevention and management of conflicts of interest and the so-called revolving door phenomenon will contribute to greater transparency and functionality of the agency.
in writing ‒ the european parliament has granted discharge to the european police office in respect of the implementation of the office's budget for the financial year 2014, and at the same time approved the accounts.
