in writing. ‒ today, the european investment bank's annual report for 2014 was adopted, with a strong focus on investment to stimulate the economy and increase productivity. this economic stimulus has meant a high level of support for smes and the financing of projects outside and within the union in 2014. the improvement of financing opportunities for smes and the support of innovative start-ups have a positive impact on economic development. the report also mentions that unemployment is high in several eu member states, affecting young people and recent graduates. young people are the future of europe and it is worth investing in their education and employment. this is exactly what the report encourages the european investment bank to do, and i was very pleased to vote in favour of it.
in writing ‒ the main task of the european investment bank is to provide financial support for projects which contribute to the development of the internal market and to social, economic and territorial cohesion, thereby helping to strengthen employment. the 2014 annual report on the eib's operations appropriately reflects this role of the eib. at the same time, however, i cannot support the effort to prevent the financing of infrastructure projects such as motorways, which is the result of this resolution. that is why i abstained.
‒ the european investment bank (eib) financed 285 000 smes in 2014, saving 3.6 million jobs. it has signed contracts for a total of 413 projects within the eu worth €69 billion. its main task is to provide financial support for projects of union interest which contribute to the balanced development of the internal market and to social, economic and territorial cohesion, and thus to the strengthening of european integration. while the eib creates the conditions for investment at all sectoral levels, it is necessary to establish a communication policy on eib activities in order to ensure that all levels of government are informed about eib programmes. it is also necessary to simplify the rules governing the support provided by the european structural investment funds to eib financial instruments. for future reports, a more comprehensive and detailed analysis of investment requirements by sector in the eu needs to be included in the report in order to identify all areas where investment is lagging behind requirements with regard to the fulfilment of eu priorities.
‒ investment is what the eu needs for its economy today. i joined the majority of the european parliament in welcoming the 2014 annual report of the european investment bank, which emphasises the importance of investments to accelerate recovery and increase productivity, support youth employment and innovation in smes.
in writing ‒ sadly, even in the 21st century, we are witnessing a great number of armed conflicts around the world. during these armed conflicts, the parties to the conflict have absolutely no respect for international humanitarian law, and we must therefore concentrate all our efforts on the creation of a very detailed and concrete action plan with a time limit, which will use the influence of the european union and thus help to put an end to the violation of the law. we must unequivocally condemn together the attacks on hospitals and schools and call on the international community to do much more to protect and secure health and school facilities as neutral, protected spaces during situations of armed conflict. it is necessary that the competent authorities investigate in greater detail and transparency the attacks that have already occurred in the past and seek to hold accountable those who have committed these heinous acts. in addition to direct and physical harm to schools and hospitals, attacks result in the forced closure or disruption of these institutions and cause serious harm to health and damage to the education system as a whole. the international community must step up its efforts, in particular in the area of the protection of humanitarian workers, but also to improve the monitoring of attacks against humanitarian workers, who are often the only help and rescue for areas that are being squeezed by armed conflict and war.
in writing ‒ the attacks against some countries, particularly in north africa, are evidence of an unprecedented violation of international law. european companies are also suspected of supplying weapons used in the fighting. the paradoxical situation is thus created, with europe supplying weapons of destruction on the one hand and providing humanitarian aid to save lives, property and rebuild destroyed infrastructure on the other. in 2015 alone, €909 million was allocated from the eu for humanitarian aid. it is necessary for member states, in cooperation with union bodies and international security institutions, to thoroughly investigate violations of international humanitarian obligations and to give serious consideration to authorising arms exports to vulnerable countries.
the eu defines the protection of international humanitarian law as one of its most important principles. i regard the situation in the middle east as a profound humanitarian crisis, which the international community has been struggling with for a long time, but without much success so far. the escalation of armed conflicts is often accompanied by attacks on the civilian population. attackers from terrorist organisations such as al-nusra and islamic state will not stop at attacking medical facilities and schools, which are inviolable under the provisions of the geneva conventions or the rome statute, and therefore any attack on them fulfils the factual nature of a war crime. i am shocked by the flagrant violation of international law, attacks against civilians cannot be justified by anything. helping the victims and taking effective steps to bring this situation to an end once and for all is our duty as members of the international community, for whom 'international humanitarian law' is not just a vague concept contained in international agreements. it is necessary for the union to take concrete action, through the instruments at its disposal under the common foreign and security policy and through hr mogherini, to prevent the recurrence of attacks against innocent civilians. i support the motion for a resolution because we must provide the people of the countries in conflict with the greatest possible assistance and protection from suffering and violence. however, linking the issue of respect for the law of armed conflict with the issue of access to abortion is absolutely unacceptable.
in writing. ‒ in the past year, 63 hospitals supported by the humanitarian organisation doctors without borders (msf) have been attacked by armed groups in different parts of the world. the damage caused is incalculable, since hospitals and schools are shelters for people in distress during armed conflict. for children today, school is a place where they can forget the horrors of war. international humanitarian law is the law of war. in times of armed conflict, it protects civilians, humanitarian workers, hospitals and schools. to violate it is not only an offence against the civilian population, but an affront to the dignity of all humanity.
in writing. ‒ war is a tragedy; and the killing of innocents during armed conflicts is a double tragedy. this report focused on calling to account the united states over its helicopter attacks on medical facilities in afghanistan, yemen and syria. the us government has apologised and offered compensation for these errors. the report called for an increased recognition of the need to follow international law during wartime – something i of course support. however i did not see this report serving any purpose in urging all state and non-state actors to adhere to ihl principles, and so i abstained.
in writing ‒ in recent years, and even now, we are witnessing a terrible, unprecedented trend of attacks on hospitals and schools in armed conflicts around the world, such as the recent attacks on doctors without borders health centers in kunduz, afghanistan, raza, yemen, and many syrian cities in the ongoing conflict. in this respect, hospitals and medical personnel enjoy special protection under international humanitarian law and any deliberate attack against civilians and civilian infrastructure is prohibited under international humanitarian law and is considered a serious violation of that law. the rome statute of the international criminal court defines attacks on humanitarian workers as war crimes. the lack of respect for humanitarian law is therefore a matter of grave concern and requires that all states in the world under the auspices of the un permanently point out such attacks, condemn them and punish the perpetrators of such attacks.
in writing ‒ the current humanitarian crisis has led to serious violations of international law, in particular in relation to attacks on the most basic civilian infrastructure, such as hospitals and schools. i therefore supported the adoption of a resolution condemning similar attacks and calling on hostile parties to armed conflicts to respect the main principles of international humanitarian law.

in writing ‒ the european parliament resolution on attacks on hospitals and schools was drawn up in response to recent incidents in areas of armed conflict. these attacks result not only in a large number of innocent victims, but ultimately also in the denial of children's access to education, further depriving these children of their chances for a full future. in the health sector, they force health workers to leave the area, leaving residents without any help. attacks on humanitarian workers are defined as war crimes in the statute of the international criminal court, as schools and health facilities must be protected and neutral. parliament condemned these attacks, as well as the use of schools and hospitals by parties to the armed conflict for camouflage purposes, and urged that such acts be properly investigated and targeted measures be taken to prevent their recurrence. he also called for strict compliance with international humanitarian law. however, the resolution contained several provisions which i could not support. i therefore abstained on the final vote on the resolution for these reasons.
in writing ‒ it is critical to acknowledge that the european parliament, the council and the european commission do not take sufficient account of the resolution on public access to documents. any refusal of public access to documents must be based on clear and strictly defined legal exceptions and must be accompanied by a justification stating specific reasons, so that citizens understand the refusal of access and can effectively use the legal remedies available. the european union continues to distance itself from ordinary citizens and the principles of direct representative democracy, and citizens' access to information from the institutions of the european union continues to be difficult, as the institutions have not established a common procedure aimed at facilitating citizens' access to documents and based on full and effective transparency and communication.
‒ the eu treaties, the charter of fundamental rights and the regulations of the european parliament and the council guarantee the right of access to documents to natural and legal persons residing or having their registered office in an eu member state. transparency, the provision of information and the making of documents available with regard to the security and protection of personal data will increase public confidence in the eu institutions and bodies, while preventing the spread of disinformation and various misleading, often even conspiracy theories.

in writing ‒ the increasing number of carers is linked to demographic trends in europe, changing family roles, increasing life expectancy and an ageing population. the vast majority of carers of the elderly or disabled are women. the creation of a common protective framework for care in the european union, which is being proposed, is one of the prerequisites for a strict respect for the dignity of women. the work of a nanny cannot be underestimated, as is so often the case today. at the same time, it is necessary to effectively prevent women performers from being treated as inferior beings. it's important to realize that this is a 24-hour work shift, which is extremely demanding. at the same time, it is necessary to prevent the abuse of family carers to perform different types of domestic work.
in writing ‒ demographic and socioeconomic changes in the union in recent years have taken their toll in the form of an ageing population and thus an increased need for care and support for families. work in the field of care and domestic help is specific and requires protection in the form of legislative regulation, especially given that this mentally and physically demanding work is mainly carried out by women. however, in addressing the issues of population ageing, i also believe that all available options should be explored to provide support and assistance to young people, in particular in their integration into the labour market, the creation of permanent jobs and conditions that will motivate them to start families and to return to traditional family values. this will also make it easier and more accessible to address the issue of providing care for older generations.
in writing the right to dignity belongs to all individuals, regardless of gender. women and men deserve to be treated with dignity in the exercise of their profession and this right must be respected and duly respected in a developed society. however, we often see cases where women are denied this right to a greater extent and in a more serious way. this negative phenomenon is especially evident in the areas of domestic work, since the majority of workers and caregivers are of the fairer sex. these are mostly migrant women with lower levels of education and economic difficulties. in many cases, they are not sufficiently protected by the social system of the country of residence when carrying out their work, and have limited or no access to health care or trade union organisations where they could collectively assert their rights. nursing and domestic work are often illegal, making them more vulnerable to exploitation. i am therefore strongly in favour of the eu working closely with the member states to ensure that the rules in force are strictly observed and to develop innovative methods to protect against ill-treatment or violence and to provide adequate access to information so that workers have a sufficient understanding of their rights and can enforce them effectively.
in writing ‒ the resolution contains many useful proposals and addresses important aspects of this area of labour law, which has not been dealt with sufficiently so far. some of the proposed measures unfortunately encroach on the competences of the member states and thus again violate the principle of subsidiarity, which is why i abstained. for example, the submitted report insisted on the accelerated adoption of the international labour organization convention no. 189, which slovakia has not ratified. this would mean that several slovak laws in force would have to be adapted to comply with the convention. i am firmly convinced that if legislation is to be changed in this area, it must be at the will of the elected members of the national assembly of the slovak republic, and not at the will of brussels. however, the sr could take this resolution as a good practice and pay at least a minimum wage benefit to family members who take care of dependent members of their own family or allow the expenditure on professional care or household work paid to third parties to be applied as tax relief.
in writing ‒ i would like to start by thanking the rapporteur for her report on women domestic workers and carers in the eu. it describes in great detail the current problems in this sector, where women account for 83% of all domestic workers. the finding that in most member states domestic work is carried out as illegal work in the shadow economy, which allows for unequal treatment, abuse or harassment, must legitimately require the commission to take effective measures as soon as possible to eliminate these unfair practices and to combat illegal domestic work. domestic workers and carers must be included in all national labour, health, anti-discrimination and social welfare and insurance laws. for example, the swedish tax deduction for domestic services, the french 'cheques de paiement pour services fourni à domicile' or the belgian 'cheques de services' could serve as good models for new legislation on domestic work and carers as an effective tool in curbing illegal work, improving working conditions and ensuring proper labour rights for domestic workers and carers.
‒ recognising domestic and care work as a genuine professional sector will help to reduce illegal work and contribute to social integration. i therefore support the professionalisation of this sector, which has the potential to create new jobs and growth.
in writing ‒ domestic work and care services, which are carried out illegally in many countries mainly by migrant women, deserve better labour law protection. there are two main reasons. first, because of the demographic crisis and the growing number of elderly people, caring will be an increasingly important service, used by an increasing number of households. however, the legalisation and harmonisation of employment and pay rules in this sector also effectively helps to combat trafficking in human beings and forced labour. i think it's important that we start talking about this work seriously and understand its growing value. then we may be more likely to realize how little we appreciate the unpaid care that women and mothers give to children and dependent family members.
in writing ‒ mrs kuneva's report deals with a subject which is becoming increasingly important in the context of an ageing population and the increase in the number of people with disabilities. the rapporteur has sought in particular to identify current problems in the sector, such as the often illegal nature of care work in the shadow economy, the lack of regulation, or the wide disparities between national legislation. it also addressed the issue of abuse and the risks of domestic work. the main objective, according to the rapporteur, is in particular the professionalisation and recognition of domestic and care work as genuine work, with all the protection that comes with such work. although i do not consider this report to be flawless and, in my view, to have contained some significant shortcomings, the fact remains that the state will have to make an increasing effort to provide quality care as the number of people entrusted with such care increases. at the same time, there is a need to improve the working conditions of caregivers, whose work is not appreciated today. i therefore regard this report, despite its shortcomings, as a step in the right direction which helped to open up the debate on this subject and which i therefore supported in the final vote.
written ‒ the european commission must not neglect the status of women and it is therefore very important that it includes specific measures to promote the integration and participation of women in the information society in the upcoming 2016-2020 strategy for equality between women and men and that it strongly supports women's internet networks. access to free broadband internet for all, at least in public spaces, would improve women's access to digital opportunities and increase their chances of accessing the labour market, which would also contribute to greater social inclusion and positive developments in environmental and economic issues. it is essential that we continue to ensure gender mainstreaming in education by promoting digital literacy and the participation of women and girls in ict education and training, by mainstreaming programming, new media and technologies into the curricula at all levels. member states and the european commission must commit to providing more funding in the future, improving access to existing funds and, where appropriate, making available funds for female entrepreneurs to set up ict businesses and digital start-ups, as well as for women mentoring and peer exchange networks, thereby fostering innovation and investment within the european union.

in writing today's digital world presents a wide range of opportunities in the areas of rapid access and exchange of information, education and employment. in this context, i am very positive that the constantly evolving information technology-based society brings with it new job opportunities and professional opportunities. however, recent studies have clearly demonstrated a large male predominance in ict in terms of study or subsequent practice. i am in favour of the eu and the member states promoting technical engineering and other technology sectors, which have great potential for the future, among girls and women. i also believe that women and men doing the same work in the same workplace are entitled to equal pay. but i still don't subscribe to the idea of artificially creating mandatory quotas for women in management positions. the rapid development of information technology has also brought with it the possibility of flexible working, which i see as important in terms of promoting a natural work-life balance and the possibility for women to reconcile the fulfilment of their desire to be a mother with their work responsibilities. however, the digital age brings with it, alongside its positive aspects, threats in the form of privacy violations, misuse of personal data, photographs and harassment. the union, in cooperation with the member states, must also set up an effective policy in this area in order to counter these negative aspects.
‒ digitalisation has revolutionized and fundamentally changed the way people obtain and provide information, communicate, meet, study and work, creating new opportunities for participation in public and political debates, education and the labour market. there is currently a significant gender gap in access to vocational and educational opportunities in information and communication technologies and computer skills. digitalisation has a huge impact on the labour market by changing value chains and creating new job opportunities and more flexible working models. and it is precisely the improvement of digital skills and it literacy that presents a unique opportunity to increase the inclusion of women and girls, but also of people with special needs, such as people with disabilities, in the labour market. increasing the number of women in the it sector, which is one of the highest-paid sectors, would contribute to the strengthening of women's financial position and independence, which would ultimately lead to a reduction in the gender pay gap.
in writing ‒ in europe, there is a significant gender gap in access to professional and educational opportunities in the field of information and communication technologies. i support women's empowerment and women's rights and freedoms in these areas.
in writing ‒ i abstained in the final vote on this report because i do not agree with the blurring of the terms which it promotes. if we want to promote women's empowerment in the digital economy, it's counterproductive to talk about gender and lgbti. we're talking about women, the problems they face because of the preconceived notions and prejudices about their competence in information technology. these prejudices have nothing to do with sexual orientation or perceived identity. the use of the ambiguous term 'gender' creates a smoke screen behind which the original laudable objective is lost and does not help women who are seeking to apply their skills in the digital economy.

in writing. the 1994 anti-dumping agreement contains detailed rules concerning, in particular, the calculation of dumping, the procedures for initiating and conducting an investigation, including the establishment and handling of facts, the imposition of provisional measures, the imposition and collection of anti-dumping duties, the duration and review of anti-dumping measures and the disclosure of information relating to anti-dumping investigations. in order to ensure the proper application of its rules, the terminology should be introduced into union legislation. in view of the failure of the multilateral negotiations to date and pending the outcome of the referral to the wto anti-dumping committee, union legislation should contain provisions to address practices, including the assembly of goods in the union or in a third country, aimed at circumventing anti-dumping measures. the negative consequence of the dispersion of many provisions in several legal acts is the search for and subsequent comparison of legal acts in order to identify positive law. i therefore consider it necessary to highlight the need for codification to provide legal certainty in finding the law applicable at a particular moment in time to protect against dumped imports from countries which are not members of the union, taking account of course of the standard procedures for the adoption of union acts. i therefore fully support this proposal to codify the regulation on protection against dumped imports from countries which are not members of the european union.

in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal for a regulation on protection against subsidised imports from countries not members of the union, since it is mainly a question of a clear and simple codification of the existing texts without altering the substance of the text. the purpose of this regulation is to incorporate into european law the provisions on subsidies and countervailing measures arising from the agreement with the world trade organisation (wto). this should ensure the proper and transparent application of the anti-subsidy rules. as a whole, the regulation lays down detailed conditions defining the existence of subsidies and the principles governing the application of countervailing duties which may be imposed as countervailing against a direct or indirect subsidy. this measure concerns in particular the production, extraction, export or transport of any goods whose free circulation in the eu could be detrimental to the union market, and also the criteria used to calculate the amount of countervailable subsidies. i think it's important in the current state of the world economy that economic exchange takes place on the basis of clear conditions. i am therefore pleased that the eu is adapting its legislation to be in line with wto agreements.

in writing. ‒ the present proposal for protection against dumped imports from countries not members of the european union is merely a clear and simple codification of the existing texts without altering their content and substance.
in writing. the purpose of anti-dumping and anti-subsidy measures is to prevent the negative effects of unfair trading practices, including subsidised imports. in establishing the existence of a subsidy, it is necessary to prove that a subsidy has been granted by a government or a public authority within the territory of a country, or that some form of income or price support within the meaning of article xvi of the gatt 1994 has been provided and thus benefited the recipient undertaking. it is necessary to develop detailed guidance on the factors which will allow the assessment of whether the subsidised imports have caused or are likely to cause material injury. in order to demonstrate that the import volumes and prices are the cause of the injury suffered by the union industry, it is necessary to take into account the impact of other factors, in particular the prevailing market conditions in the union territory. the decision shall be taken only after all parties have been given an opportunity to comment. in this examination, attention should be paid to the need to eliminate the impact of injurious subsidies and to restore effective competition. the proposal thus seeks primarily to codify the regulation on protection against subsidised imports from countries not members of the european union. the new regulation replaces a number of acts which are the subject of codification. the proposal fully preserves the content of the codified acts and is limited to merging them into a single act, the formal changes not exceeding the purpose of codification. the motion before you has my support.

in writing. ‒ the two existing exemptions for commodity traders expire on 31 december 2017. commodity traders will therefore lose a stable regulatory framework at the end of 2017. it is therefore important that we extend the validity of the currently valid exemptions. that extension should take into account the time needed to complete the review of investment firms and should include the development, adoption and application of any legislation that may result from that review.
in writing. ‒ the current waiver of the large exposure and own funds requirements for commodity dealers whose main business is to provide investment services or perform investment activities, which is valid until 31 december 2017, is hereby extended for a period until 31 december 2020. given that regulation (eu) no 575/2013 requires the commission to draw up a report on the appropriate regime for the prudential supervision of investment firms, which may follow legislative proposals, it is necessary to extend that deadline.
in writing. the prudential regime applicable to investment firms results from the obligations imposed on credit institutions and adjusted in relation to the investment services function they provide. the commission decided to conduct a single review on the suitability of the system for commodity dealers and the supervision of investment firms in general and to draw up a report. this approach was considered necessary to ensure the development of a coherent prudential framework for all types of investment firms. the commission considers that the exemption from the obligation to notify the commission of the results of the review is justified by the fact that the commission has not yet adopted a legislative proposal for the exemption. that carries certain risks. first, commodity traders would become fully subject to the requirements of the crr/crd without a conscious decision that such treatment is most appropriate for them. second, assuming that the result of the examination of investment firms would be an adapted prudential framework for commodity traders, they would lose a stable regulatory framework. it is necessary to extend the validity of the existing derogations provided for in the crr. that extension should take into account the time needed to complete the review of investment firms and should include the development, adoption and application of any legislation that may result from that review. i therefore vote in favour of the proposal as it stands.
in writing. ‒ in the plenary we voted for the exemptions for commodity traders. the requirements of the cr and crd apply to credit institutions and investment firms. the capital requirements regulation exempts commodity traders from the provisions on large exposures and capital requirements. the two exemptions expire on 31 december 2017 and the aim is therefore to extend the existing exemptions provided for in the crd, thereby avoiding the regulatory framework for commodity traders becoming unstable.
in writing. ‒ i support the extension of the exemption for commodity traders until 31 december 2020 regarding their exemption from the capital requirements and own funds requirements, as the examination and report that the commission was to prepare on this matter have not yet been completed. the original deadline for exemption (31 december 2017) therefore had to be extended.
in writing. ‒ the european union has established specific rules for the functioning of credit institutions and investment firms in the capital requirements regulation and the capital requirements directive of 2013. the original text provided for the exemption of commodity traders from large capital requirements and own funds requirements until the end of 2017. in order to identify an appropriate system for commodity traders, the commission decided to carry out an investigation and prepare a report. however, it appears that this review will not be able to be completed in time and therefore it is very unlikely that any legislation that may result from this review could be prepared, adopted and applied before the expiry of the current exemptions for commodity traders. it is unfortunate that the commission's report is being delayed in this way, but i have nevertheless voted to extend these exceptions. this will prevent commodity traders from being subject to requirements about which they are not sufficiently informed and from losing a stable regulatory framework. according to the draft regulation, these traders will be exempted from the requirements until the end of 2020.
in writing. ‒ the current regulation grants specific exemptions to commodity traders, in particular with regard to minimum own funds and capital requirements. as both these derogations are only valid until the end of 2017, we have extended their validity by notification for a further three years, i.e. until the completion of the work on the revision of the regulation. i agree with that principle. i think that if the work on the revision of the regulation is already underway but the exemptions have not been terminated by the time they expire, it would be useless to change the existing rules for commodity traders for a short time and burden them by having to meet all the requirements all at once. the special status of commodity traders is due to the riskiness of this type of business and i believe that extending the exemptions until new binding rules are in place will be beneficial, in particular in the interest of their legal certainty. that's why i supported the report.

in writing. ‒ the the directive on the conditions of entry and residence of third-country nationals entering the eu has been under discussion since 2013. as cultural exchange is one of the cornerstones of understanding between countries, i supported the council's position. i believe that we should not put unnecessary obstacles in the way of foreigners who are interested in studying, doing research, volunteering or au pair services in the eu. moreover, it is clear from the draft regulation that it is mainly a question of technical and administrative details which have hitherto complicated the process of obtaining a residence permit for certain categories of third-country nationals. in particular, this directive aims to improve the legal framework applicable to third-country nationals and to introduce new categories of applicants. the directive will make it compulsory to include students, researchers, trainees and volunteers, although each member state will be able to introduce its own measures in respect of pupils or au pairs. no longer will there be a distinction between paid and unpaid trainees, but volunteers using the european voluntary service will be favoured. students or researchers will also be able to stay in the territory of a member state for up to nine months to look for work, provided they meet the conditions laid down in the directive. i hope that this text will help to reduce red tape and simplify the residence of applicants from third countries.

the theme of reconciling work and family life has been particularly resonant in slovakia for several days now. the emotional debate was triggered by the refusal to allow a member of the national council to enter the negotiating room with her several-month-old daughter. the vice-president of parliament justified the ban, which will remain in place, by the high number of mps sitting in the chamber who could infect the baby and also by the fact that the child could disturb the mps during the vote. but more than these words, i regret the reaction of a large part of society, which has condemned the action of the member a priori, saying that the mother should take care of her child at home, not go to work, and certainly not with the child. the debate also included the argument that it is not fair to deal with a member of parliament when there are workplaces where a woman simply cannot bring her child. yes, there are certain occupations where that is not possible, but that does not mean that we should give up where that is possible. as politicians, we should try to do everything possible to ensure that mothers who want to stay at home with their children for as long as possible have decent conditions for doing so. on the other hand, we should also create decent conditions for working mothers.
in writing. the rules on parental leave at european level are governed by a directive which was formally amended in 2010. however, the basis for this legislation goes back two decades to 1996. it is not a modern legislative norm reflecting the current economic or social conditions in the european union and its member states. support for motherhood, but also the subsequent deepening of childcare, which is made possible by properly adjusted parental leave, requires improved standards, including a higher financial valuation, during this type of family leave. the lack of financial support associated with parental leave is one of the reasons why there has been little interest on the part of fathers in taking it over time. this is true of most countries of the european union. a change in this area would lead to a better and more equal participation of women in the labour market. this would also have a demonstrable positive effect on the level of economic development in individual countries. it would also contribute to achieving the 75% employment rate target in the european union set in the europe 2020 strategy. in the case of men, this meta has already been fulfilled, but unfortunately, women are still very far from it.
in writing. the problem of cross-border tax avoidance and aggressive tax planning is a growing challenge. the current union legal framework does not provide for the sharing of tax information between member states on companies. this is one of the commission's measures to prevent tax avoidance, a tangible proposal aimed at increasing transparency by strengthening european cooperation. new provisions are introduced in the directive to define the scope and conditions for the mandatory automatic exchange of information on country-by-country reports. the econ and taxe committees of the ep have advocated the introduction of country-by-country reporting for multinational groups of companies in order to combat aggressive tax planning. multinational groups of companies with aggregate consolidated revenues of at least eur 750 million will be required to report on a country-by-country basis in the member state in which the ultimate parent company of the multinational group of companies or any other reporting entity has its tax residence. the competent authority of the member state which received the country-by-country report shall communicate the report to all other member states in which one or more of the economic units of the multinational group of companies is resident for tax purposes, by means of an automatic exchange of information. the country-by-country report will contain a range of information on the business of the group, including the amount of revenue, profit before tax, profit tax paid and payable, number of employees, registered capital, profit reserve and tangible assets.
in writing. ‒ the european union has long been frustrated by the deliberate and deliberate evasion of tax obligations by entities. this state of aggressive tax planning and harmful tax burden will continue unless we work together to increase transparency, which can only be achieved by adopting improved tools and mechanisms in the legislation to be drafted. i therefore welcome the initiative of the european commission to introduce a new article into the existing directive defining the scope and conditions for the mandatory automatic exchange of information on country-by-country reporting. the adoption of this legislation will mean that multinational groups with headquarters or operations in the european union whose total consolidated revenue is equal to or exceeds eur 750 000 000 will be obliged to report on a country-by-country basis.
in writing. the proposed directive defines the scope and conditions for the mandatory automatic exchange of information on country-by-country reporting, the application of which will help to detect tax evasion in cross-border activities. the obligation for multinational groups established or operating in the eu, whose total consolidated revenue is equal to or exceeds eur 750 000 000, to report annually, as from 2017, in the member state in which the main parent entity of the multinational group or any reporting entity is resident for tax purposes is introduced. the report must contain information on the amount of income, profit before tax, income tax paid and accrued, number of employees, declared capital, retained earnings and tangible assets. the exchange of this information between the member states concerned will help to increase the monitoring, control and detection of tax fraud and evasion.
in writing. cross-border tax avoidance, harmful tax competition and aggressive tax planning are not just problems within the european union, but have already reached global dimensions. the european parliament is working towards greater transparency of tax information, in particular by introducing country-by-country reporting for multinational groups. under directive 2011/16/eu on administrative cooperation, member states do not yet exchange country-by-country reports with each other. transnational groups established or operating in the eu whose total consolidated revenue is equal to or exceeds eur 750 000 000 will be required to report on a country-by-country basis. the competent authority of the member state in which the country-by-country report has been received shall communicate the contents of the report by automatic exchange to all other member states in which one or more individual entities of the multinational group concerned are either resident for tax purposes or subject to tax in respect of an activity carried out through a permanent establishment. the country-by-country report must be filed in the member state in which the parent undertaking of the multinational group or any reporting entity is resident for tax purposes. i welcome this proposal as regards the establishment of a lower threshold for multinational groups and i also believe that as a whole it will contribute to greater transparency. he has my support.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the mandatory automatic exchange of information in the field of taxation. the report aims to reduce cross-border tax avoidance and tax competition. this is done through the submission of an annual country-by-country report by multinational companies. member states receiving these reports shall forward the report to all other member states where the reporting multinational company is active. this automatic exchange of information helps to ensure transparency and thus reduces the risk of tax evasion.
in writing. ‒ in the case of the european parliament resolution amending the directive on the mandatory automatic exchange of information in the field of taxation, i voted in favour of its adoption. the tax 'optimisation' of multinational companies and their efforts to avoid taxing billions in revenues requires us to introduce an exchange of information between tax administrations and to demand information on what profits they make and where they tax them. however, this effort to stop profits from flowing into tax havens must not be linked to tax harmonisation in the eu.
in writing. ‒ given the increase in tax fraud and evasion in recent years and their serious impact on member states' tax revenues, which are thus lost billions of euros. tax evasion and fraud is a global problem and cannot be tackled at eu level alone. the eesc believes that, for the sake of simplicity and efficiency, as well as cost savings and for the benefit of all stakeholders, it is necessary to harmonise the various information exchange systems resulting from the various initiatives and to transform them into a single system. this should happen at least at european level. in addition, the related rules should be clear, unambiguous and proportionate to the objectives pursued. i supported the resolution because the proposed directive is one of the measures of the action plan to strengthen the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion. i believe that these amendments will help in the automatic exchange of information in the field of taxation. as there are currently considerable differences within tax systems and these differences can be an obstacle to the implementation of the automatic exchange of information, i expect the commission and the member states to step up their efforts to simplify and harmonise tax legislation.
in writing. ‒ cooperation between the tax authorities of the member states is essential in the fight against tax evasion. corporate tax planning has become a way of using legislation to reduce tax liabilities in recent years. i therefore see the proposed directive as a positive step towards greater transparency, which will significantly strengthen international cooperation to combat tax evasion.
in writing. this proposal introduces an interesting innovation in the field of taxation and the fight against tax evasion. there are unfair tax practices in the eu that need to be changed to enhance transparency and reduce harmful tax competition. the report was prepared in response to the ep's so-called panama papers lists of companies and individuals who have circumvented or exploited tax laws. we demand that the commission has unrestricted access to information circulating between the tax authorities of the member states in order to assess whether the tax practices of the member states are in line with state aid rules. this is particularly important for small and medium-sized enterprises that operate in one country and should not be disadvantaged by their size. transnational companies are also called upon to increase transparency in their management and annual reporting.
in writing. ‒ several studies demonstrate a very poor level of labelling of fishery and aquaculture products sold on markets in the european union. individual member states must strengthen national controls, including on unprocessed fish in restaurants and catering establishments, in order to combat fraud more effectively. the european commission should regularly monitor the extent to which the required consumer information is labelled and published on labels. member states should include in the voluntary labelling all available information to enable the consumer to make an informed choice.
in writing. i support a system of rigorous tracing and control of the origin of fishery products from catch to consumption. the spread of poor quality and unhealthy food will be prevented, the responsibility of producers for quality at all stages of production and processing will be increased, and the protection of the consumer and his right to full information about the product, its composition and its origin will be promoted.
in writing. the european union is the largest seafood market in the world, supplied by the union fisheries sector and by imports from third countries. consumers have the right to information on the coastal and geographical catch zones and should be able to rely fully on the whole chain that brings fishery products to the market, as the union and the member states have an obligation to protect its citizens from fraudulent activities. all products imported must comply with the rules and standards of the european union. the results of various studies have confirmed a high rate of mislabelling of fishery products sold on the union market, including in restaurants of the union institutions. it should be underlined that deliberate and fraudulent mislabelling of fish species constitutes a breach of union rules, including the common fisheries policy, and may even constitute a criminal offence under national law. national controls should therefore be strengthened, including controls of unprocessed fish in restaurants and the catering sector. it is also necessary to promote the creation of a working group to harmonise the application of traceability systems in all member states and the establishment of an external structure for the certification of voluntary information on fishery and aquaculture products on the union market. in view of the above, i fully support the proposal.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution. consumers of fishery products have the right to receive information in plain language. several studies have shown that mislabelling is common within the european union. since a large proportion of these mislabelling is intentional, national controls on products intended for the restaurant and catering sectors should be strengthened. the proposal proposes to monitor the entire process from landing to consumption, thus ensuring consumer confidence.
in writing. ‒ i welcome this resolution, which calls for monitoring and combating fraud in the area of origin labelling and mislabelling of fish and fishery products. the results of various studies indicate a high rate of mislabelling of fishery products sold on the eu market, including in the restaurants of the eu institutions. it is necessary to identify where fish is mislabeled in the supply chain and to strengthen national controls, including controls on unprocessed fish in restaurants and the catering sector.
in writing. ‒ the a study published by oceana late last year found that up to a third of all fish served in restaurants in brussels is not properly labelled. the discovery that sellers are actually offering substitutes of lower quality (for example, cod being mistaken for pangasius) instead of the declared quality fish has caused public outrage. i therefore agreed to the resolution which aims to describe this problem and to put pressure on the commission to come up with possible remedies. however, it is unacceptable that the consumer should be so directly misled. each seller must comply with certain minimum standards for the labelling of fish and seafood. in order to give consumers confidence in the products they consume, the seller must act in a transparent and responsible manner. on the other hand, the competent authorities need to be able to trace the origin of fish, as illegally imported fish damage the economy, have an impact on the protection of fish resources and can also pose a health risk. we therefore ask the commission to come forward with a proposal for a precise, reliable and consumer-friendly way of labelling fish and seafood. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the consumer is informed of the risks and benefits of the product.
in writing. as regards the labelling of fishery and aquaculture products (targeted, planned management of water resources) in the catering and retail sectors, we voted in favour of a sound labelling system from landing to the consumer, which could win the trust of consumers and consolidate the eu market. through this resolution, we ask the commission to assess the benefits of introducing a european labelling system which should ensure transparency and credibility of the certification process, such as the application of a dna barcode which could help identify species.
in writing. ‒ the i was happy to support the european parliament's resolution based on the oral question. as consumers, we are often misinformed about the type of fish we buy, the region from which it comes, and whether it is caught or farmed. in fact, misinformation prevents us as consumers from making informed choices and sometimes borders on misleading. it is not unusual to buy cod instead of salmon, or grated protein instead of crab sticks or lobster. not to mention that such tactics are not only wrong for consumers but also for fishermen who are losing money. this is why we have called on the member states to strengthen controls at national level and to set up a system for tracing the origin of fish and compulsory labelling of the data provided. i hope that this resolution will help change the situation soon and that we will always have the right information about what we eat.

in writing. eu-china trade is currently worth over eur 1 billion a day. although china has committed to allow all its prices to be determined by the market, the disproportionate level of state interference in the chinese economy causes prices and costs not to reflect and respond to market supply and demand, resulting in overproduction of production. therefore, china does not meet the requirements of a market economy, which ultimately undermines the union market and economy in the context of mutual trade and puts millions of jobs at risk. this is currently felt most strongly by the steel producers and the mining industry in the union. therefore, i support the proposal that the commission should make every effort to meet china's commitments and that the eu should use a non-standard methodology for determining price comparability in anti-dumping and anti-subsidy investigations of chinese imports in accordance with the protocol on the accession of china to the wto.
in writing. china is the second largest trading partner of the european union and the union is china's largest trading partner. the two countries trade more than eur 1 billion a day. any decision concerning the treatment of products imported from china after december 2016 must ensure compliance of union law with the rules of the world trade organisation. in the context of china's accession to the world trade organisation, a specific methodology for the calculation of dumping was agreed. the commission therefore concluded that the chinese excess capacity in the union was not a sufficient reason to maintain the measures in place. i consider it necessary to recall that 56 of the 73 anti-dumping measures currently in force in the eu apply to chinese imports and that china is not a market economy and therefore the five criteria identified by the union for determining this status have not yet been fulfilled. i agree with the motion for a resolution.

in writing. ‒ the even though china is the eu's second largest trading partner and the eu is china's largest trading partner, with trade between them amounting to more than eur 1 billion a day, i am of the opinion that china does not meet the criteria of a market economy. china joined the world trade organization (wto) in 2001. the accession protocol provides that china's transition to a market economy will be automatically recognised after 11 december 2016. china currently meets only one eu criterion for being recognised as a market economy. the government heavily subsidizes various industries, allowing them to export and sell their goods at significantly lower prices. this week in strasbourg and last week in brussels, representatives of the eu steel industry came to express their concerns. if we had recognised china as a market economy, we would have completely paralysed european steel producers, eliminating 3.5 million jobs and reducing annual gdp turnover by some eur 300 billion. as i come from košice, where the biggest employer is the iron and steel giant and 10,000 people would lose their jobs, i voted to give china market economy status only if it meets all five criteria that the eu defines a market economy. until then, appropriate customs measures should be applied to imports from china.
