in writing. ‒ i am committed to families being encouraged in their parenting, enabling them to spend time away from work, especially when children are young. i agree that we need to promote and support more and better family-work balance. we also ought to recognise the overall value of informal work provided by parents at home and its benefits for a whole society. but the best way for these measures and regulations to be formed is by national governments and not by the eu. this report interferes strongly in the running of the institution that forms the foundation of our society, namely the family. it promotes so called ‘same-sex parenting couples’ - something that is a biological impossibility; insists that despite failed attempts to get men to do more housework by legislation being passed, the eu will continue to push forward with new proposals. that is unacceptable! how parents divide up the responsibilities in their family should be left just to themselves. neither the states/governments nor any of the eu institutions have the right to meddle in a private sphere of citizens and dictate how people shall live their family life! i therefore voted against this proposal.
in writing. ‒ based on eurostat findings and eurofound research, we continue to see significant differences between men and women in the use of maternity, paternity and parental leave, which shows clear gender discrimination in childcare and women's participation in the labour market. i am particularly concerned that all the measures that have so far been taken to encourage men to take on an equal share of family responsibilities have not produced satisfactory results in many member states. although the original framework agreement/directive played a significant role in helping working parents in europe, i would like to thank the rapporteur for the report, as i believe that this framework agreement will improve women's labour market prospects, improve work-life balance and reduce gender gaps in wages, pensions and lifetime earnings. i also believe that the measures taken in the new framework agreement on parental leave will ensure a more balanced distribution of responsibilities within the family between men and women and encourage fathers to make more use of parental leave.
in writing. ‒ balancing family and work life while maintaining the economic security of the family is an important factor in parental involvement in childrearing. the framework agreement demonstrates an effort and modernises the approach to ensuring increased participation of fathers in parental leave and also takes into account the diversity of labour force and societal developments, including the increasing diversity of family structures.
in writing. the non-legislative resolution on parental leave highlights, inter alia, the wide differences in the rules on parental leave, in particular as regards who has the right to take it. for example, employees in the public sector have greater protection than those in private companies. the resolution calls on the commission to draw up a study on the state of implementation of the directive in the member states and stresses that everyone must be guaranteed the right to parental leave without discrimination, regardless of the sector of employment or the type of employment contract under which fathers and mothers are employed. i have reservations about some of the specific requirements in the report, because the eu should only set the framework and the detailed solutions should remain the responsibility of the member states. the national legislation and the culture of the individual nations must be taken into account. the ep also expects detailed rules on the granting of parental leave to parents of children with disabilities or serious illnesses. certainly, in such cases, the union should set minimum standards so that these families are not discriminated against and their fundamental right to respect for human dignity is not violated. i supported the report and was pleased that the rapporteur, who is from the socialist political group, had praised the work done by mothers and fathers in childcare and domesticity. i have stressed its value throughout my mandate, and it is the left-liberal political groups that have not recognised this work as a contribution to gdp.
in writing. ‒ the report by ms arena aimed to assess the implementation of european legislation on parental leave in the individual member states. i welcomed the fact that the report dealt largely with the issue of reconciling work and family life, as this issue is controversial in many member states. in slovakia, the case of a member of the national council who was denied entry to the negotiating room with a child is currently resonating in the media. i have always held the view that, where possible, taking a child to work should be permitted in certain situations, since the child feels best and most naturally in the presence of the parent. among the other positive aspects of the report, i particularly find that it deals with paternity leave and the question of how to motivate fathers to take up the paternity leave option. however, despite the positive aspects, the report also contained negative aspects, including calls for a revision of the maternity leave directive or the introduction of a single maternity leave for the whole of the european union. in view of these facts, i have decided to abstain from the final vote.
the fight against human trafficking must be the priority of our society. it is, of course, incompatible with human dignity. so i welcome any proposal that seeks practical solutions to stop this modern slavery. i was unable to support mrs. bearder's report. i see the continued emphasis on the special status of lgbti groups as a way of exploiting a sensitive issue like human trafficking to advance their agenda. and calls for 'systematic recognition of the right of access to abortion' are also a chronic overstepping of the european parliament's powers. the protection of life from conception to natural death is one of the fundamental pillars of european civilization. when will lgbti and pro-racial leaders understand that eu legislation should not be ideologically coloured just to advance their interests? and when will the legislators of this institution understand that they cannot arbitrarily violate the sovereignty of the member states? that's my question.
in writing. ‒ trafficking in human beings is a violation of fundamental human rights and a serious organised crime under the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. directive 2011/36/eu aims to better protect victims of trafficking in human beings and to reduce the vulnerability of potential victims. official statistics clearly show that the vast majority of victims, 80 percent, are women and girls. in the context of the drafting of the legislation, the eu institutions emphasised in article 1 of the directive that member states are obliged to integrate gender considerations into their anti-trafficking initiatives. however, it should also be borne in mind that trafficking in human beings can take many forms, including sexual exploitation, forced labour, forced marriage, domestic servitude, organ trafficking, forced begging, illegal adoption and other activities. statistics do not give an accurate picture of the real situation, which form of trafficking is the most widespread, or who the victims really are. the different definitions result in data that are not comparable. prevention is essential, and awareness-raising initiatives for the public are also important. although the subject requires special attention and targeted action, the report contains a number of wording which is either within or outside national competence, so i regret to have abstained from voting on the report.
in writing. trafficking in human beings is now a serious crime with a transnational dimension, which is complex and costly to detect. in addition to the fundamental violation of human rights, the humiliation and harm to victims, it also has a significant economic dimension, as it is a source of illicit income. human trafficking has various and increasingly sophisticated forms of perpetration, ranging from sexual exploitation, forced labour and begging, to various forms of discrimination and organ harvesting. it affects vulnerable groups, especially women and children. it is necessary for member states and the commission to eliminate, detect and punish these crimes in a timely manner and to provide timely and effective assistance to victims through the proper application, monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of directive 2011/36/eu on preventing and combating trafficking in human beings.
in writing. trafficking in human beings is considered a serious organised crime and, in the case of victims, a serious interference with the personal integrity of a person as a fundamental human right recognised by both the international and european systems of protection of rights. the gender dimension is strongly reflected in this issue, as the vast majority of the population according to official statistics are women, which is attributed to barriers to access to education, gender pay gaps, unemployment and underemployment, the feminization of poverty and other factors. i consider it of the utmost importance that member states, as part of their initiatives, identify victims, treat them and provide them with the highest possible protection and support. support services should take into account the gender dimension and take into account that different gender groups have different needs for support. in the context of prevention, it is also important to focus on education and empowerment programmes for women, girls and marginalised groups. given the seriousness of this problem, the motion for a resolution has my full support.
in writing. ‒ i support the fight against human trafficking. this is a terrible crime, a grave violation of human rights, and we must take action against it by all means possible. the number of victims is significant, including women and children, who are often the victims of sexual exploitation. i think it's important that awareness campaigns are an integral part of the fight, because by hiding behind anonymity and taboos, the perpetrators can operate much more effectively. trafficking in human beings is not just a problem of third countries; it is a global problem, and unfortunately, in many cases, it also occurs within the european union.
in writing. ‒ trafficking in human beings now crosses national borders and is therefore one of the most serious crimes in the world. although more attention has been paid recently at eu level to the investigation and prosecution of trafficking cases, i am concerned that the overall number of prosecutions in the eu remains low. i am aware that identifying victims is very difficult, but i believe that in the coming period we will strengthen support and protection for victims, including the right of victims to settle and work legally in the member state to which they were sold. i supported the resolution because i believe that, in order to protect victims, prevention needs to be stepped up, taking into account the main causes of vulnerability to trafficking in human beings and the fight against it. i expect that adequate mechanisms will be established to protect, assist and integrate victims of trafficking in accordance with the measures taken. i also expect that we will find a way to improve coordination and cooperation between the key players in this field.
in writing. ‒ trafficking in human beings is a crime that belongs to a modern form of slavery and is mainly linked to inequalities in our society. when we talk about trafficking in human beings, we are talking about a complex transnational phenomenon that can only be effectively tackled if the european institutions and member states act proactively together. it is necessary to provide for strong sanctions not only for criminal groups but also for individuals involved in trafficking in human beings.
in writing. in the ep, i have also been involved in the issue of trafficking in human beings since my election in 2004. this modern form of slavery, which thrives even in countries that pride themselves on humanism and democratic regimes, is a disgrace to modern society. for many years, we have talked mainly about prosecuting traffickers and helping victims. i've always felt a deficit in prevention activities. i welcome the fact that this report also focuses on the prevention of trafficking. at the same time, the report specifically highlights the growing market for children. i am very sorry that i could not support the report because the resolution supports abortion (paragraphs 71 and 75). one life in danger is the one we're trying to protect in the report, and the other one we're destroying. it also shows the weakness of our policies. the message is also ambiguous. in the french text, it talks about solving the problem from the perspective of equality between men and women, in the english text and in others from the perspective of gender. the problem is that in the dictionary of eu documents we use the word gender, which is not defined in european or international legislation. this certainly does not help victims of human trafficking.
in writing. ‒ the femm workshop report aimed to assess measures to combat trafficking in human beings, in particular from a gender perspective. in the text, the rapporteur focused on the administrative procedures for identifying victims of trafficking in human beings and on the different ways in which we can provide support and assistance to them. in my opinion, the main idea and message of the whole report was very good and, especially in the light of the current migration and refugee crisis, very timely and important. however, i do not support the practice of the groups putting their own agenda into this type of report, which is controversial for many member states. as a result, we may not be able to support reports that we would otherwise agree with. this was also the case with this report, where i did not endorse it because of certain negative aspects and abstained from voting on the report as a whole.
in writing. the commission of the european union is calling for the widespread, rapid and effective introduction of e-government and the availability of tools and online services for cross-border electronic identification. digital borders have now been completely erased, and politics must respond. the use of electronic tools and online services strengthens the digital internal market and responds to the challenges of digital public administration, such as the emergence of new technical elements, the daily availability and use of electronic services. the commission promotes accessible e-government through various action plans and campaigns, such as the e-government action plan 2010-2015 and the horizon 2020 innovation programme thereafter. e-government has led to the emergence of electronic identification (eid) to facilitate cross-border administrative procedures such as setting up a business abroad, moving and taking up a job abroad, settling pension rights online, enrolling in schools and universities. digital systems make the work of public administrations transparent and open, allowing citizens and businesses to keep track of their affairs and transactions.
in writing. in view of its irreplaceable role in all activities of daily life, i consider energy to be an important asset that should enable every citizen, without distinction, to live in dignity. while it is gratifying that europe has largely overcome its previous energy problems, i am concerned about the global situation where 1.2 billion people still lack access to electricity and 2.8 billion people still use wood or other biomass for heating or cooking. although some progress has been made in europe in the field of energy, energy poverty is nevertheless reflected in the growing number of people (more than 50 million) who have problems paying for energy or who have limited access to energy because of low income, uninsulated housing, low-powered equipment (heating, cooking, hot water heating) or very high energy prices. as i consider this situation unacceptable, i am in favour of introducing such a system in the eu to ensure that overall costs are kept low and that the deficit caused by electricity tariffs does not increase further. i believe that the measures taken will protect all citizens without distinction from energy poverty and prevent their social exclusion.
in writing. after years of being seen as an ineffective recipe for dealing with the economic crisis, there is finally a much greater need to focus on the needs of the most vulnerable. in terms of the risk of poverty, this group is demonstrably women. the fight against their poverty is a matter of social justice. effective measures to improve the living standards of women mothers also reduce the threats associated with child poverty. the persisting problem is the inexorably high pay gap between women and men, which on average is close to 20%. this is then reflected even more strongly in the different pension levels. women's are also more than a third lower. it is a vicious circle that must finally be broken. the measures must be positively targeted towards women. at both european and national level, we must follow a path of firmly established priorities with clear, enforceable penalties for non-compliance. otherwise, the injustices of women's pay will persist for decades to come.
in writing. ‒ virtual currencies are innovative products, an opportunity to be seized, but as a novelty, they need to be regulated with great care. it can provoke opposition among its traditional peers and the competent bodies of the member states can only react late with regard to their regulation. these factors weaken these new products, including the largest virtual currency player, bitcoin. virtual exchanges can provide the internal market with new opportunities for development and are certainly useful as a tool for functioning as a basic account or for facilitating online purchases. consumers, on the other hand, should be given adequate guarantees as to the safety of the product. it is important to consider the possibilities for technical developments in relation to virtual currencies. the parliamentary report contributes to this.
in writing. ‒ the virtual currencies offer enormous opportunities and benefits in the area of payments. the priority is to reduce transaction costs and ease of use while ensuring resilience and different levels of privacy protection. however, it should be recalled that transaction costs remain at a very high level, representing up to 7% of the value of cross-border transfers. however, more competitive transaction costs can be achieved within the single market. in the medium term, competitiveness could be further enhanced by the introduction of a non-proprietary and interoperable single wallet.
in writing. ‒ the virtual currencies are changing the world's financial systems and contributing to their economic development. they make cross-border financial transactions easier and cheaper, and many companies trust them more than institutionalised currencies. despite all the advantages, i consider it important to create the conditions and regulatory environment so that these systems are not misused for money laundering, illegal and criminal activities and to prevent their misuse for possible support of terrorism.
in writing. bitcoin is one of the most significant virtual currencies (vms) and it is clear that the innovation in question, distributed ledger technology (dlt), will have a significant impact on the financial sector and beyond. in principle, this technology is a fast, flexible and relatively secure way of recording any transaction together with the history of previous transactions in the so-called distribution list. investment in dlt is increasing rapidly and some uses may spread rapidly throughout the system. in the area of payments, vms and dlt help to reduce transaction costs and contribute to ease of use while ensuring resilience and different levels of privacy. however, transaction costs for payments remain surprisingly high. the commission considers that the proposed amendments to the dlt are not in line with the requirements of the directive. the commission considers that the use of dlt in the private sector is not appropriate for the purposes of the assessment of the compatibility of the aid with the internal market. however, in a broader sense, they can be used in smart contracts, intellectual property rights transfers, supply chain management and some government services. however, they also entail risks in the form of the misuse of certain applications for criminal activities, including money laundering and terrorist financing. therefore, the proper functioning and resilience of those systems is essential, which requires well-functioning governance and supervisory structures. the motion in question has my support.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal on virtual currencies because in today's fast-paced world we need to keep up with technological developments. there are many opportunities in the emerging virtual currencies and technologies in this new space. the report also mentions the simplification of cross-border money transfers, reducing the costs, which can reduce the total global transaction cost by a significant amount. we need to take advantage of this new opportunity, this new technology, and we need to monitor the evolution of the system, but we also need to be aware that there may be risks that have not been mapped yet.
in writing. ‒ in today's modern age, based on rapid technological progress, it is clear that the standard forms of banking and financial operations as we know them are changing in a significant way. one change is the introduction of virtual currencies, such as bitcoin. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, which gives due weight to the positive attributes of these systems, such as the reduction of transaction costs or a decentralised, fast, flexible and relatively secure way of recording transactions, but at the same time points out the considerable risks that these systems entail and calls for the setting up of a working group to actively monitor the development of these technologies and thus to respond in good time to the preparation of the legislative framework that will be needed in this area.
in writing. ‒ the according to reuters, there are currently around 600 virtual currencies (vms), with 90% of the market covered by bitcoin. the sector is worth about $7 billion, which is not a lot globally, because the transactions on the world's stock exchanges are about $5 trillion a day. while recognising that vcs provide certain benefits to consumers, businesses, charities and the economy, it is also important to bear in mind that vcs in many cases pose a threat to consumers related to criminal activities, such as terrorist financing, money laundering, tax fraud and tax evasion, as well as other potential illegal activities and problems. although there is currently little evidence of the use of vcs as a means of payment in criminal activity, i am convinced that it is in the interest of consumers that the proper functioning and resilience of these systems should be ensured at eu level. from the point of view of the report presented, i appreciate and support the eu's inherent interest in understanding the functioning and impact of the vm on the economy and thus ensuring consumer protection, in particular with regard to cybersecurity, algorithms used, contact persons and contact details.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade. on 7 april 2016, the commission adopted a proposal for a decision to mobilise the egf in favour of france in order to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant by moryglobal. the request concerns 2132 workers made redundant. according to the french authorities, the redundancies were caused by the bankruptcy and liquidation of the company. the commission notes that the french authorities have not provided any evidence that the measure is imputable to the state. this is due to the global financial and economic crisis, which led to a decrease of 13,7% in the eu and 21% in france in road freight transport by vehicles over 3,5 tonnes between 2007 and 2012. personalised services for redundant workers include advice and guidance from a team of experts training workshops on general knowledge, training on the use of the internet, job fairs and meetings with staff from educational institutions. the french authorities have provided all the necessary guarantees for the following and, therefore, by today's decision, the european parliament has agreed that france is entitled to a financial contribution of eur 5,1 million to be granted under that regulation.

in writing. ‒ as part of the common asylum policy, the treaty on the functioning of the european union provides a specific legal basis for dealing with emergency situations. the transitional measures provided for in the tfeu are exceptional. they should only be applied when the urgency and severity of the problems caused by the sudden influx of third-country nationals into the asylum system of the member state or member states reach a certain level. by letter dated 8 december 2015, sweden formally requested the suspension of its obligations. eurostat data confirmed that the number of asylum seekers in sweden has increased exponentially, with an increase of more than 60% to 112 040 persons for the period 1 january to 31 october 2015 compared to the same period in 2014. moreover, the monthly number of applicants for international protection has increased even more recently. this exemption also demonstrates that the transitional measures adopted in the original decision, the mandatory allocation of quotas to migrants, are not adequate to address the problem. the system established in the decision is not working, migrants are going to countries that pay higher social security contributions, such as sweden, regardless of the distribution according to quotas. this also shows that the transitional measures should be suspended as soon as possible and that all member states should be exempted from the mandatory allocation mechanism under quotas.
in writing. ‒ sweden is facing an emergency situation due to a sudden influx of third-country nationals into its territory, caused by significant changes in migration flows, and as a result sweden formally requested on 8 december 2015 to suspend its obligations. sweden had by far the highest number of applications for international protection per capita in the european union in 2015.
in writing. sweden is facing an emergency situation due to a sudden influx of third-country nationals into its territory caused by significant changes in migratory flows. on 8 december 2015, sweden formally requested the suspension of its obligations under the council decisions. the aim is to introduce a temporary measure, suspending sweden's relocation commitment for one year in view of the gravity of the situation caused by the influx of third-country nationals. sweden had the highest number of applicants for international protection per capita in 2015, putting considerable pressure on the country's asylum system. sweden also faces a difficult situation given the recent significant increase in the number of unaccompanied minors one in four applicants claims to be an unaccompanied minor. i support the commission's proposal in its original form and disagree with the rapporteur's amendment.

in writing. ‒ the council decision on temporary international protection measures for sweden concerns the recently approved relocation mechanism for 160 000 asylum seekers from italy and greece. under the scheme, sweden would take in nearly 6,000 refugees from the two countries. however, the commission has proposed that sweden should be temporarily exempted from this scheme. in the commission's view, sweden is facing an emergency situation due to the increased number of applicants for international protection, which is putting an unmanageable strain on the swedish asylum system. the current number of asylum seekers in sweden is already causing practical problems, as refugees cannot be provided with adequate living conditions and their applications are dealt with late. according to the latest data, sweden received a total of more than 170 thousand applicants in march 2016, of which more than 70 thousand were children. in view of this information, i am convinced that sweden has shown a sufficient degree of solidarity in the other periods. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the eu-russia joint action and the eu-russia joint action, and will continue to monitor the implementation of the eu-russia joint action. for these reasons, i supported the commission's proposal to grant sweden a one-year derogation from participation in the relocation mechanism.
in writing. protecting personal data means protecting the individuals whose information is processed, and this protection is one of the fundamental rights recognised by the european union. the commission is obliged to assess the content of the rules applicable in a given country and resulting from national law or international obligations, as well as the procedures to ensure compliance with those rules, as it must take into account all the circumstances of the transfer of personal data to a third country. such assessment should not only concern the laws and practices relating to the protection of personal data for commercial and private purposes, but also cover all aspects of the framework applicable to that country or sector, and in particular, but not exclusively, enforceability, national security and respect for fundamental rights. i maintain that legal certainty as regards transfers of personal data between the union and the usa is an indispensable prerequisite for consumer confidence, the development of transatlantic trade and law enforcement cooperation, making it indispensable for their effectiveness and the long-term implementation of the instruments allowing for the compliance of such transfers with primary and secondary union law. the privacy shield agreement must comply with eu primary and secondary law as well as with the relevant judgments of the court of justice and the european court of human rights. i therefore support the motion in question.
in writing. ‒ the importance of the protection of personal data is also recognised in the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. it stresses that the union has a duty to ensure and balance the protection of these rights. in particular, strict rules apply to cases where the possibility of sharing data with third countries arises. the united states is seen as one of the european union's most important partners in many ways, including the high-level data flows it receives on a daily basis. i therefore think it is high time that a new, effective directive was adopted. the so-called privacy shield is a much more sophisticated tool that will finally enable us to do all the things that were not possible with the predecessor known as secure data ports.
in writing. ‒ the fight against international terrorism has to be waged through smart intelligence sharing between nations, in order to prevent attacks like those we have seen on mainland europe. i was glad to support my colleague timothy kirkhope’s hard work in this area and to see problematic amendments voted out.
in writing. ‒ the in october 2015, the european court of justice annulled the safe harbour decision by its judgment in a case brought by austrian citizen maximilian schrems. the safe harbour was an agreement that allowed companies like facebook, google or microsoft to transfer sensitive personal data from the eu to the us. the court of justice recognised that the personal data of european citizens were not sufficiently protected in this way and held that an adequate level of protection in a third country was to be understood as 'essentially equivalent' to the level of protection guaranteed within the union. according to the eu's founding treaties, the protection of personal data is one of the fundamental rights, since protecting data means protecting the people who are affected by the information processed. the commission has come up with a bilateral agreement between the us and the eu called the privacy shield, which is intended to be a remedy in response to the court's reservations. it is recognised that key definitions such as 'personal data', 'processing' and 'controller' have been incorporated into this agreement, but privacy protection must continue to be part of the wider dialogue between the eu and third countries, including the us. the new data protection measures recently adopted by the ep in april will therefore need to be incorporated. i also agreed to the resolution because we call on all stakeholders to respect the principles underlying eu legislation.

in writing. the third energy package aims to ensure a truly competitive retail energy market that is favourable to consumers. however, this objective has not yet been achieved in all member states. this is particularly evident in the persistently high levels of market concentration, the failure of falling wholesale prices to be reflected in retail prices, the low numbers of consumers switching to other offers and the low level of consumer satisfaction. i believe that open, transparent and competitive, well-regulated markets are important to keep prices low, stimulate innovation, improve customer service and remove barriers to new innovative business models that can benefit citizens. measures should be taken to ensure that the benefits of increasing the interconnection of national networks are not passed on to distribution system operators but are directly translated into benefits for final consumers. furthermore, i believe that improving the interconnection rate of national networks must have a positive impact on the price of energy for consumers and therefore it is necessary to avoid that the benefits are limited to distribution system operators. in view of the above, i support the motion.

in writing. ‒ the illicit trade in tobacco products poses a serious threat to public health. it also causes eu countries financial losses in the form of unpaid taxes and duties of more than eur 10 billion a year. the protocol is an international agreement on cooperation in combating illicit trade in and smuggling of tobacco products. the aim is to track and detect this crime through a system of measures in place. as a substantial proportion of illicit tobacco products originate from third countries, the protocol will also commit those countries to its objectives.
in writing. the criminal activity of the illicit trade in tobacco products, in particular cigarette smuggling, is a serious threat to public health, as it not only weakens tobacco control policies but also provides access to cheap tobacco products. such action causes the european union huge revenue losses in the form of unpaid taxes and duties. the trend is currently strong with the so-called cheap white cigarettes, which are bought outside the union and imported without paying taxes and duties. the protocol is a global regulatory initiative to combat illicit trade in tobacco. it aims to create a secure supply chain for tobacco, tobacco products and manufacturing equipment through the establishment of a global tracking and tracing system. other measures to ensure more effective controls defined in the protocol include, in particular, the regulation of internet sales, the granting of licences or the keeping of records. i am convinced that ratification of the protocol will ensure a more effective fight against the illicit trade in tobacco, which will also be beneficial for public health. the motion has my full support.

in writing. the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality, enshrined in the treaty on european union and the protocol on the application of those principles, are the basis for the functioning of the eu and the main principles on which european law is built. they govern the system of taking specific decisions at eu level to ensure that the cases in which the union is competent to adopt binding legislative acts are precisely defined. such a mechanism contributes to decision-making as close as possible to the citizens. in the current period of deep crises, it is more necessary than ever to rediscover our common european identity, including through closer integration in different areas. one such area is cooperation in internal affairs, which, because of their sensitivity, are a priori the responsibility of the member states. i believe that we must be particularly careful in defining cases in the internal sphere where it is functional and useful to strengthen cooperation, since the measures in question will directly affect the lives of citizens. i consider that the matrimonial property regime falls within areas which should be left to the exclusive competence of the member states and where measures taken at eu level pose a serious risk. the council proposal, moreover, by referring to registered partnerships, violently overrides this issue, despite the fact that it seriously conflicts with the interests of some member states, including slovakia. i consider such action unacceptable and i am voting against the recommendation that has been put forward.

in writing. ‒ the as far back as 2011, the commission proposed two regulations aimed at establishing a common regime on the property relations of international couples. after lengthy negotiations, it became clear last year that there would be no clear agreement in the council. the commission therefore proposed that matters of matrimonial property regimes be dealt with by so-called enhanced cooperation. 18 member states have requested this procedure, the other states will have an exemption from these measures (slovakia should be among them). since the negotiations on the commission's original proposals were blocked by all the member states, i am glad that at least a compromise was found between the majority of the states. this enhanced cooperation is intended to enable the acceding countries to have their civil law authorities deal with matrimonial property regimes and registered partnerships on the basis of the application of a single legal system. international couples will be able to choose the legal system that will apply to their property relations. this will increase the legal certainty of married couples, since the law of the country closest to them will apply to their relationship. diverse proceedings in cases of divorce or death of one of the spouses will be heard by the same court in order to avoid parallel and contradictory judicial decisions. for these reasons, i have agreed to the draft council decision and i hope that other member states will follow in the future.

in writing. ‒ the treaty on the functioning of the european union allows member states to agree on enhanced cooperation in certain areas. such cooperation also needs to be approved by the european parliament, although it does not concern all eu member states. if approved, it can be joined by other states at a later date, but this is a voluntary step. i voted against the resolution on enhanced cooperation in the area of jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matters of property regimes of international couples, as regards matters of matrimonial property regimes and the property consequences of registered partnerships. i consider that the property relations in marriage form part of the protection of the family which has gradually developed in european law. this increased protection is intended to compensate for the greater vulnerability of families with children in crisis situations, which may be caused for example by the death of one of the spouses or their separation. in the case of registered partnerships, such protection is not necessary. although slovakia has not signed up to this enhanced cooperation, i consider its creation to be a step towards reducing the importance of the natural family and therefore i could not support the resolution presented.

in writing. in relation to securities markets, investment firms and trading venues, regulation (eu) no 600/2014 of the european parliament and of the council and directive 2014/65/eu of the european parliament and of the council are the main financial regulations. those legal acts set out the requirements for the authorisation and operation of investment firms, regulated markets and data reporting services providers and harmonise the position limitation regime for commodity derivatives in order to enhance transparency, promote orderly price formation and prevent market abuse. a new data collection infrastructure has been developed reflecting a more harmonised and efficient data collection. without such data, it would not be possible to establish a precise definition of the financial instruments falling within the scope of the new framework. in addition, it will not be possible to adapt the pre- and post-trade transparency rules to determine which instruments are liquid and when a waiver or deferral of publication should be granted. the non-reporting of positions in commodity derivatives will make it difficult to enforce the limitation of positions to those contracts. if no position reporting takes place, the capacity to effectively detect breaches of the position limitation is limited. many requirements related to algorithmic trading are also data-dependent. the motion has my full support.

in writing. ‒ the 2014 markets in financial instruments directive is part of the key legislative measures adopted by the eu in the wake of the financial crisis. it is one of the main financial regulations concerning securities markets, investment firms and trading venues. together with other regulations, they lay down requirements for the authorisation and operation of investment firms, regulated markets and data reporting services providers. they also introduce rules on high-frequency trading and improve financial market surveillance by harmonising administrative sanctions. this new regulatory framework was developed by the commission together with the european securities and markets authority (esma), which was only established in 2010, and these legislative texts were its first major task. the whole new control system was to be operational on 3 january 2017, but in recent years it has become clear that neither esma nor the national authorities have been able to put in place the necessary information systems. as this proposal is intended to extend the implementation period of the individual measures for 2018 once, i decided to support it. both parliament and the council were assured that one year was the necessary time to fine-tune the systems. i hope, however, that there will be no further postponement in the future.

in writing. ‒ several member states are already involved in operations in africa and the european union could create real added value by supporting these operations more in the future. i therefore welcome the new peace facility for africa action programme, which addresses the shortcomings and emphasises exit strategies, a higher level of engagement of african countries, more targeted support and better decision-making procedures. strengthening european military cooperation would increase the efficiency and effectiveness of the european contribution to un peacekeeping missions. the european union and its member states should not act in isolation in support of peace support operations, but should rather take into account the contribution of international actors, coordinate better with them, respond more rapidly and focus their efforts on certain priority countries, with the member states and african states with the most experience taking the lead.
in writing. ‒ the instability, civil and military conflicts in africa, combined with terrorism, also threaten the safety, health and lives of people in other continents and, given the geographical distribution, particularly in europe. the effects are now being felt in the form of the refugee crisis and the spread of terrorism. i agree with the need for eu and un support and assistance in addressing these problems, but at the same time it must be said that the african union itself needs to be more active and engaged in addressing the problems of countries on its continent. through the peace instrument created in 2004 and financed by the member states, the eu spends around eur 1.9 billion a year to tackle africa's problems. i believe it is important to control the use of these funds so that they do not become the object of corruption or other illegal activities that further aggravate africa's problems.
in writing. the objectives of a peace support operation shall be to prevent armed conflict, to restore, maintain or build peace, to enforce peace agreements and to address the complex and pressing problems and challenges arising from a disintegrating or malfunctioning state. recently, the number of failed states has increased in connection with terrorist groups operating on the african continent. accessible borders on the african continent allow the spread of violence, reduce security and provide opportunities for crime. under the new sustainable development agenda, peace is a key objective. the european union itself is the largest contributor to the un system, in particular in the form of financial assistance to un programmes and projects. the union has spent some eur 1,5 billion in recent years on mine clearance support procedures and assistance to victims of landmines, making it the largest donor in this field, as anti-personnel mines have been the biggest obstacle to post-conflict reconstruction. i greatly appreciate the union's efforts and commitment to help strengthen the african peace and security architecture. however, we should not forget to examine the use of the funds allocated in view of the deep-rooted corruption in africa and i also think that the african peace facility should be linked in order to encourage the african union to increase its own contributions to peace support operations. i support the motion.
in writing. ‒ i support the report as a form of response to the crisis. peace support operations aim to create stable, secure and more prosperous environments in the long term; good governance, justice, greater respect for the rule of law, protection of the civilian population, respect for human rights and security are essential prerequisites for this. unfortunately, in the last few decades, the security situation in africa has changed dramatically. terrorist and insurgent groups have emerged and are emerging in somalia, nigeria and the sahel-saharan regions. in these places, counterterrorism operations have become a part of everyday life. the eu should adopt a more active and coherent economic policy to combat terrorism by preventing the import of 'blood raw materials', since the main source of terrorism financing, alongside drug and human trafficking, is the exploitation of natural resources not only in africa. the legal origin of raw materials should be demonstrated to importers by means of a central system that can be traced.
in writing. ‒ i was happy to support my colleague mr van orden as he examined the success of peacekeeping missions by forces from member states in africa. it is vital that developed nations with capacity to help stabilise african nations take a stand against terrorist organisations like boko haram, torturing and martyring at will – particularly persecuting christians.
in writing. ‒ the security situation in africa has changed dramatically over the last decade, with the emergence of terrorist and insurgent groups in somalia, nigeria and the sahel region. overall, then, africa is a continent of interstate and domestic conflicts. although we have recently seen increased cooperation between the eu, the un and the african union (au), especially in peace operations, i do not consider the security situation to be adequate in terms of a stable and secure environment in the long term. i am particularly concerned that more and more people in the au are affected by poverty, injustice, corruption and violence. i supported the resolution because i see peace support operations and eu cooperation with the un and au as one of the possible responses to the current crisis. i expect peacekeeping operations to help solve the pressing problems that arise from a failing or malfunctioning state. i am pleased that the new peace facility for africa action programme addresses the shortcomings and puts more emphasis on exit strategies, a higher level of engagement of african countries, more targeted support and better decision-making procedures.
in writing. ‒ it is important that the european union acts as a guarantor of stability and peace in its immediate neighbourhood. to do this, we should use not only diplomatic and military instruments but also economic and financial cooperation.
in writing. ‒ the the current protection of retailers and small food producers from unfair trading practices by large chains is not enough. the continued disproportionate fall in the prices of milk, pigmeat and related products is also exacerbating the difficulties. the unfair practices of large retail chains consist mainly in imposing unfair contractual terms, threatening or demanding disproportionate discounts. small producers are not able to defend themselves. they are concerned that the commercial relationship will be terminated. the problem affects many european countries, including slovakia. several eu member states have therefore taken concrete measures against unfair practices by wholesalers. but the question is, above all, their effectiveness. we still have a lot of catching up to do. we need to focus on what works. more effective action to curb unfair practices by large chains will provide small producers with opportunities to invest and maintain employment in this important sector.
in writing. ‒ unfair practices take many forms, but the most common is the abuse of a position of power. because of the fear factor, they're difficult to detect and detect. they affect the eu economy, harming the economy and businesses, especially smes, and ultimately consumers themselves. in food chains, up to 96% of respondents reported being exposed to at least one form of these practices. addressing this problem will require stronger regulation in the future, which will establish transparent and fair relations between food producers, suppliers and distributors and which will contribute to strengthening the functioning of the internal market.
in writing. the european union has a long-standing interest in protecting small food producers and retailers from unfair trading practices, which often occur in trade relations where there is a diversity of market forces. unfair trading practices can have a devastating effect on the union economy as a whole, as they can cause businesses to lose their ability to invest and innovate and to not seek to expand their business in the single market. in practice, it is often the case that the weaker party does not take any legal action and accepts unfair practices despite their harmful effect, because it is afraid that the stronger party will stop cooperating. however, the rules in this area differ from one member state to another. in parallel, market participants are also trying to address this problem by developing best practice principles in vertical relationships and self-regulatory frameworks for their implementation, as exemplified by the supply chain initiative. it is therefore necessary to take decisive and consistent action aimed at completely eliminating unfair trading practices occurring in the food supply chain. the scale of the problem requires the introduction of legislation to guarantee the proper functioning of markets and fair and transparent relationships between all actors in the food supply chain. that motion has my support.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the report, as farmers in the food supply chain are particularly vulnerable to unfair trading practices. following negotiations with unfavourable outcomes for producers, producers sometimes operate at high losses and unfair practices have adverse effects on the entire supply chain. small, medium and micro-enterprises account for almost 90% of the economic fabric of the european union and are the ones most affected by unfair practices, and therefore need to be protected by the european union through appropriate regulations and mechanisms.
in writing. ‒ it is important that we make the fight against unfair trading practices in the food supply chain more effective. that is why i voted in favour of this resolution, which aims to help farmers get a fair return for their products, while at the same time providing consumers with a wider choice.
in writing. ‒ although individual eu member states already have regulations to combat unfair trading practices (utps), i find the behaviour of retail chains across the eu, especially in the supply-side relationships when selling food, very problematic. this is also reflected in the result of a march 2011 study which found that up to 96% of respondents in the food supply chain confirmed that they had been exposed to at least one form of noc. i consider this a serious problem, particularly because npas affect smes and micro-enterprises, which account for over 90% of enterprises in the eu and are much more vulnerable to npas than large enterprises. i think that unless there is a common initiative and a common framework for the behaviour of the chains across the eu, we will hardly expect to see an improvement in the position of domestic farmers and food producers vis-à-vis the strong, dominant economic power and position of the chains. i am convinced that only good eu legislation will guarantee the proper functioning of markets and fair and transparent relations between all actors in the food supply chain.
in writing. ‒ fair trade can only work if there is mutual trust between seller and buyer. today, there are already a number of non-legislative self-regulatory instruments, such as codes of ethics. we should be encouraging this kind of behaviour, not introducing new regulations. they lead to increased bureaucracy and do not solve the problem themselves.
in writing. ‒ it is natural that small firms have less bargaining power in business relationships than large firms. however, if they abuse it to impose conditions that are clearly unfavourable to their suppliers and often contrary to good morals, the result is a restriction of consumer choice and the risk of producer failure, particularly in the agricultural sector. i am not entirely convinced that we need new european legislation against unfair trading practices today. however, i voted in favour of the report, which calls for this, because i see it as a warning to big companies to start applying fair play rules to small ones too.
in writing. ‒ the the european union must think about the future of the agricultural sector, which continues to receive the largest share of subsidies, and therefore fully support innovation and new agricultural technologies, which many experts and farmers themselves believe are the only answer to today's challenges. the european union must ensure that the benefits of technological innovation are available to all farmers. the european union and the member states, academia and industry, farmers and food producers need to work together to improve the transposition of research results into practice. it is also important to create a regulatory environment that is more conducive to innovation and to ensure that eu legislation does not become an obstacle to innovation. without a supportive regulatory regime, european industry will move to more dynamic markets. too often, eu legislation places restrictions on products and technologies without sufficient evidence of risk. to support innovation, this legislation must be evidence-based.
in writing. ‒ the the growth of the world's population and the need to provide for its livelihood, together with climate change, require the search for innovation and new technological solutions also in the field of agriculture. by 2050, the world's population is estimated to increase by 2.4 billion to 9.6 billion. food demand will increase by 70%. this situation requires close cooperation between farmers and scientists in the research and development of new solutions to ensure healthy, high-quality and sufficient nutrition, always taking into account food safety, with a focus on health and environmental protection. the commission and the member states must jointly seek a path to a long-term sustainable economy and create the conditions for constructive cooperation between the agricultural and scientific sectors.
in writing. agricultural technologies are needed to achieve productive and sustainable agriculture. european agriculture continues to lag behind many of its international competitors. only sustainable and priority investments in research will reverse this trend. the european union should become a world leader in agricultural technology, innovation and sustainability. to do so, it is essential to ensure that the benefits of technological innovation are available to all our farmers. finding solutions that work on a small scale in rural communities is as important as addressing the problems faced by many of our large farmers. the solution should be, in particular, targeted investment in applied and translational research. i am convinced that cooperation between the european union and its member states, academia and industry, including breeders, the agrochemical industry, farmers and food producers, would also help. creating a regulatory environment that is more conducive to innovation is also very important. without a supportive regulatory regime, european industry will move to more dynamic markets. in view of the above, i fully support the proposal.
in writing. ‒ we need to emphasise the importance of technology, innovation and sustainability in the agricultural sector as well, as this is the only way for european agriculture to be able to face the challenges posed by globalisation. in particular, attention should be paid to ensuring that research and development in the field of agriculture is of benefit to the actual end-user and is accessible to all, including smes and disadvantaged regions. moreover, the long-term predictability and sustainability of individual sectors must not be overlooked, since investments are useless if the operation is dependent on aid and the aid system is constantly changing.
in writing. ‒ the world is currently facing very worrying challenges, which also affect agriculture to a significant extent (decreasing availability of land, environmental damage and degradation, water scarcity, increased demand for energy, the arrival of new pests and diseases). sadly, today more than 1 billion people suffer from malnutrition, and farmers are finding it increasingly difficult to produce food sustainably. i supported the resolution because i consider technological innovation to be an essential part of the solution to this serious problem. i also believe that only through agricultural technology can agriculture be more productive and sustainable. but i also see as a worrying signal that the world's population will reach 9.6 billion by 2050, an increase of 2.4 billion compared to today, and that the world will have to produce 70% more food, feed, fibre and biomass on smaller agricultural land and under climate stress. i expect the eu and its member states to take measures that will help farmers produce more food for the people of the eu and the world that is safe, healthy, nutritious and with less impact on the environment.
in writing. ‒ technological progress is not going to bypass agricultural production either, and the european union should support any innovation that makes it possible to produce more, safer and cheaper food.
in writing. ‒ the meeting the growing demand for quality food and nutrition is one of the major challenges facing europe today. it will also require much greater support for technological innovation in agriculture. the european union and its member states have the capacity and resources to become global leaders in this area. however, real cooperation and the reaping of the benefits of the common agricultural policy are needed. unfortunately, however, the reality today is primarily one of rivalry and cross-pollination between countries. there must also be greater links between the scientific community and the agricultural sector. solutions that work equally well for small rural farms and large farmers need to be sought. early practical implementation of research results on individual farms, farms or cooperatives is important.
in writing. ‒ on the one hand, we are looking for innovative solutions and new technological approaches to the economic development of farms in order to provide food for a constantly growing population. on the other hand, we have almost no measures against food waste. yet, each year, 1.3 billion tons of food is wasted. this also affects the environment. strengthening innovation in agriculture is of course very important. but we also need to address the other side of the problem, and in the process of the circular economy, we need to address it urgently.
in writing. agriculture is one of the most dynamic economic sectors. leading the way in the introduction of new technologies is a guarantee of a thriving rural economy and keeping pace with wider economic development. the potential of innovation in agriculture has not yet been fully recognised, and the european regulatory framework is not ready to keep pace with rapid developments. the common agricultural policy should focus more on the real needs of farmers. more knowledge and information on ecosystems associated with the production process on the farm will enhance development, as exemplified by integrated pest management, which makes smarter use of the interaction of chemical and biological measures. targeted incentives in the production process and investments are essential. on the other hand, outdated legislation should be updated to adapt to new solutions. better harmonisation with other industries, such as chemicals, healthcare and technology, is needed through more intensive knowledge-combination, integration of resource use and better understanding of interactions. moreover, innovation in technologies and practices can create new jobs and new revenue streams throughout the agri-food value chain. it is important to remember that agriculture is a key economic pillar of the union, and that is why i am voting in favour of this proposal.
in writing. ‒ the european agricultural sector plays a very important role in our daily lives. it is primarily about food, which is a challenge in the face of changing food habits and the employment of millions of people. the growth of the world's population and the difficulties it brings, with hunger on the one hand and waste and excessive waste on the other, call for a clear support for innovation. i am pleased that the report makes specific recommendations.
in writing. ‒ the european agricultural sector is of fundamental importance to the union in general, as it provides food and is also a key economic pillar, providing jobs for 25 million people directly employed in agricultural enterprises. although agriculture is one of the most dynamic economic sectors, in recent years we have seen problems worldwide with the decline of natural productivity and fertility of soils caused by soil degradation, in particular soil erosion, due to the loss of ecosystem functions such as tillage, humus production, pollination, water retention and nutrient cycling. i supported the resolution because i believe that the proposals and measures put forward by the current administration can contribute to strengthening innovation and economic development in the field of farm management, especially for small and medium-sized farmers. however, helping farmers and their groups to introduce innovative products will require stronger financial support from the eu and the removal of all barriers to access to loans to help them expand their businesses.
in writing. ‒ european small farms as well as smes could become leaders in agricultural innovation. we should in future allocate to this purpose some of the funds that are now being wasted in the common agricultural policy.

(the speaker agrees to answer a question under the 'blue card' procedure under rule 162 (8) of the rules of procedure)
answer to a question on the 'blue card' procedure. you don't have to throw them back in the sea, you don't have to shoot them. you can take them back to where they came from. the european union must, of course, set up central camps there, as it has done in lebanon and turkey. there may be some in libya. they are also in lebanon. that's the solution. not to distribute them all over europe and then send them back like a parcel from zalando. that's not how it works.
it is crucial, i believe, in this migration crisis that we set up the right entry integration process for those who are granted asylum and stay in the european union. adepts must undergo a rigorous social program with language instruction, an understanding of our culture, history, moral principles, and the foundation of the christian spiritual tradition, all of which will prepare them for their asylum stay. they need to understand that under our roof, we have our rules. they cannot create foreign ghettos with a closed structure, they cannot dictate to us how we live, especially they cannot bring religious intolerance to christian symbols and traditions. they must also be warned that such depraved behaviour as assaulting defenseless women, as was done in cologne earlier this year, will be strongly condemned and punished. respect for women, children and the weak is a fundamental european and christian value. many refugees come from countries where conversion is a crime. but we in europe proclaim freedom, and therefore we will not hide the christian message. our principles of tolerance, help and respect are based on the gospel of jesus christ, which cyril and methodius brought back from greece, and so today christian groups in europe help those in need and trouble. but they can't take advantage of it.

the investment plan for europe, which is financed by the european fund for strategic investments (efsi), is designed to finance high-risk investments and to finance those areas where the market does not work. this appropriation is intended to cover the cost of the european union agency for fundamental rights' activities in the field of human rights and fundamental freedoms. the efsi is financed from the budget at the expense of horizon 2020 and the connecting europe facility (approximately €5 billion). that's the money we're missing for high-value projects. the efsi-supported projects include projects that do not require any risk to be borne (e.g. insulation of 40 000 flats and houses in france). in slovakia, we are also making such investments without the efsi. on 22 february 2016, the european parliament, in its report on the european semester for economic policy coordination annual growth survey 2016, invited the commission to verify that efsi funding is only granted to high-risk projects that comply with the principle of additionality; in this context, parliament will assess projects and their leverage in order to ensure that the efsi guarantee fund is used appropriately within the eu budget. the commission has not yet submitted such an assessment. i assume that the commission has not found enough projects to implement the juncker investment plan. in the further use of this fund, it is necessary that we use it for the purpose for which it was intended.

in writing. ‒ relations between the european union and the republic of palau are governed by the partnership agreement between the members of the african, caribbean and pacific group of states, of the one part, and the european union and its member states, of the other part. by amending regulation (ec) no 539/2001, the republic of palau has become one of the third countries whose nationals are exempt from the visa requirement when crossing the external borders of the member states. the agreement was signed in 2015 and has since been applied on a provisional basis, pending the approval of the european parliament. the agreement provides for visa-free travel for citizens of the european union and residents of the republic of palau for travel to the territory of the other party for a period of 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa waiver agreement would simplify travel for entrepreneurs, facilitate investment and have a positive impact on tourism. palau has significant development potential and the union is negotiating a comprehensive economic partnership agreement with palau. the union-palau agreement would strengthen the relationship between the member states and palau. visa-free travel is also important for european and pacific peoples. the european parliament gave its consent to the conclusion of the agreement today, which i also voted in favour of.
in writing ‒ this particular agreement is a continuation of the deepening of the eu-republic of palau's above-standard relations. the visa waiver agreement will have positive effects for both parties involved, as it simplifies travel conditions for business people, while facilitating investment and boosting tourism. the agreement has the potential to strengthen the area of investment and trade, which has a strong potential for future development.
in writing relations between the european union and its member states and palau are governed by the so-called cotonou agreement. citizens of the republic of palau shall be exempt from the visa requirement when crossing the external borders of the member states. citizens of the union and citizens of palau may travel without a visa to the territory of the other party for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa waiver applies to all categories of persons (holders of ordinary, diplomatic, service/official and special passports) travelling for any reason other than the pursuit of a paid activity. the agreement on the short-stay visa waiver significantly strengthens economic and cultural relations and is the basis for political dialogue on respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, in particular in the area of gender equality. the constitution of the republic of palau enshrines respect for human rights, the role of democracy and the rule of law, and palau is also a signatory to international human rights treaties. this agreement also helps entrepreneurs by facilitating investment and adjusting their travel conditions and improving tourism in the country. in view of the above, i shall vote in favour of the proposal.

in writing ‒ the eu-republic of palau agreement on the short-stay visa waiver will allow eu citizens and citizens of palau to travel without a visa to the territory of the other contracting party for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. the abolition of the visa requirement will make it easier for all categories of travellers to travel for any reason. the positive effects of visa liberalisation will certainly be reflected in the facilitation of travel for business people, in tourism and in other activities. palau enjoys one of the highest standards of living in the pacific. this country has made great progress in recent years, especially with regard to women's rights. palau women are increasingly appointed to senior positions in government and are gaining representation in elections. palau has signed all international human rights agreements and has eu support in their ratification and implementation. despite the fact that this country poses no threat to illegal immigration, security or public order, i support the rapporteur in calling on the commission and the palau authorities to ensure full reciprocity in visa waivers, which must allow equal treatment for all citizens.

in writing. ‒ the republic of colombia has been included in the list of third countries whose nationals are exempt from the visa requirement when crossing the external borders of the member states through the amendment of regulation (ec) no 539/2001. the agreement was signed in 2015 and has since been provisional, pending the approval of the european parliament. citizens of the european union and of colombia may travel without a visa to the territory of the other party for a period of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. the short-stay visa waiver would strengthen economic and cultural links between the european union and colombia. colombia is the fourth most important economic partner of the union in the region and the second most important trading partner of the eu with colombia. the natural and agricultural features of colombia attract investors and therefore the visa exemption would facilitate the travel of investors and thus facilitate the development of the colombian economy and trade. the number of colombians visiting the union for holiday purposes is increasing and this number could therefore increase further with the visa waiver. in addition, colombia can be an important partner in the fight against organised crime and drug trafficking, as stated in the cooperation declaration. the european parliament gave its consent to the conclusion of the agreement today, which i also voted in favour of.
in writing ‒ this particular agreement is about continuing to deepen the eu-republic of colombia's above-standard relations. the visa waiver agreement will have positive effects for both parties involved, as it simplifies travel conditions for business people, while facilitating investment and boosting tourism. the agreement has the potential to strengthen the area of investment and trade, which has a strong potential for future development.
in writing. colombia is one of the few latin american countries whose nationals still require a visa, which is still a significant vector of rapprochement between the european population and colombians. this agreement will further strengthen economic relations between the member states of the union and colombia, as the union is its second largest trading partner. the agreement also contains a joint declaration on cooperation in the area of illegal immigration, in which the union and colombia recall their commitment to readmit their own illegal migrants. colombia can also become a key partner in the field of security and the fight against organised crime, in particular drug trafficking, which can be an important part of cooperation. these are all challenges faced by member states and colombia alike, which justify the importance and the need to strengthen cooperation through an agreement on the short-stay visa waiver. i therefore consider the abolition of visas to be mutually beneficial and therefore vote in favour of the motion.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and colombia on the short-stay visa waiver. this agreement offers an excellent opportunity to further boost tourism, facilitate investment and boost trade. colombia is now the eu's fourth most important economic partner in the region. in addition, the agreement offers new allies to join forces on major issues such as the fight against terrorism. we also welcome the emergence of political dialogue, most often aimed at joint action against corruption, criminal organisations and trafficking in human beings.
