in writing. ‒ the european parliament agrees to conclude, on behalf of the european union, the agreement on the extension of trade in information technology products. the extension of the first information technology agreement (ita) is a milestone. this is the first large-scale tariff reduction agreement with significant job creation and gdp growth potential since the establishment of the world trade organisation (wto). the first it agreement was concluded in 1996 and now has 82 participants. the agreement requires all participants to eliminate tariffs on information technology products. the exemption of products from customs duties has significantly improved trade in the sector. these developments have transformed the information technology industry. in 2012, the eu, the us, japan, korea, taiwan and costa rica initiated negotiations to change the subject. in 2015, an agreement was reached on an additional list of 201 it products. these products are estimated to have a turnover of over 1.3 trillion dollars. the products on the list include new generation semiconductors, gps navigation systems, medical products containing magnetic resonance imaging devices, printed circuit board machine tools, telecommunications satellites and touch screens. the tariff reductions will lead to lower prices and more competition in the markets. the effectiveness of the above can be increased by the accession of more states to the agreement.
in writing ‒ the ita requires each party to eliminate tariffs and bind them to zero under a most-favoured-nation clause for all it products covered by the agreement. in 2012, 6 countries, including the eu, started talks and negotiations aimed at increasing the number of products covered by the ita. in 2015, an agreement was reached on an additional list of 201 it products. the new wording of the agreement and its reform will bring lower prices to consumers but also to manufacturers who are dependent on imported parts.
‒ the ep has voted in favour of extending the agreement on trade in information technology products, which extends the current list of 201 marketable it products. the agreement contains commitments by the parties to reduce the duties progressively. the current volume of trade in eu exports of these goods is eur 189 billion. after the removal of the duties, this volume will increase significantly, which will help economic development and increase the transparency of competition.
in writing. the agreement on trade in information technology products requires each party to remove tariffs and bind them to zero under a most-favoured-nation clause for all information technology products covered by the agreement. these are mainly computers and telephones, but also input devices, components and apparatus for the production of information technology products. new products covered by this contract include the new generation of semiconductors, gps navigation systems, medical products including magnetic resonance imaging devices, instruments for the production of satellite communications, telecommunications satellites and touchscreens. the agreement requires the submission of timetables containing commitments for the gradual reduction of duties for all products over a period of up to seven years three years for common products, five years for sensitive products and seven years in exceptional cases. the agreement will bring lower prices to consumers but also to manufacturers who depend on imported parts and has huge potential in terms of job creation and supporting gdp growth. that is why i am voting in favour of the motion.
in writing. ‒ the first information technology agreement (ita) was signed 20 years ago. the parties to the agreement have eliminated tariffs on products such as computers and telephones. the duty-free regime has contributed significantly to the rapid development of the sector. information technology has developed very rapidly in the last few years, but the ita product range has not changed. the extension of the product range is necessary to allow the latest developments to be incorporated into the agreement. the latest agreement covers products such as gps navigation systems, touch screens, and telecommunications satellites. i voted to pass the bill because ita is a big step, because it's a tariff-cutting agreement that can create jobs.
in writing. ‒ i am in favour of phasing out and abolishing import duties on new products covered by this treaty, such as the new generation of semiconductors, gps navigation systems, medical products including magnetic resonance imaging devices, satellite communications instruments, telecommunications satellites and touchscreens by 2019. this will help develop technologies and lower prices for consumers. i voted yes.
in writing ‒ the first agreement on trade in information technology products (ita) was concluded in december 1996 at the ministerial conference in singapore and entered into force in 1997. the agreement was originally signed by 29 wto members and now has 82 signatories. the ita requires each party to eliminate tariffs and bind them to zero under a most-favoured-nation clause for all it products covered by the agreement. the ita covers some 200 customs items, including computers and telephones. in may 2012, six countries (eu, usa, japan, republic of korea, taiwan and costa rica) started negotiations to expand the number of products covered by ita. they were joined by 21 other wto members. in july 2015, an agreement was reached on an additional list of 201 it products. the annual trade volume of these 201 products is estimated at over usd 1.3 trillion per year, representing approximately 10% of the current total world trade. the expansion of the ita, the first substantial tariff reduction since the establishment of the wto, is a major event with huge potential for job creation and support for gdp growth. that is why i supported the motion for a resolution approving the agreement.
in writing. ‒ information technology is becoming an increasingly important business asset. europe has the potential to become a future leader in this area. we have to do everything we can to make that a reality. one tool is the removal of trade barriers.
‒ α-pvp is a strong psychostimulant controlled under the 1971 un convention. its presence in powder and tablet form was detected in 28 member states of the union, with china as the country of origin. the commission has reason to believe that, given the acute toxicity of this substance and the potential for serious harm to human health, there are grounds for subjecting it to control measures across the eu. the ep has approved this procedure. member states must take measures to control this substance, including criminal sanctions, in accordance with their national legislation.
in writing the substance α-pvp is a potent psychostimulant and its presence has been confirmed in all member states of the union as well as in turkey and norway. it is primarily imported into the european drug market from china and subsequently distributed throughout europe. at present, there are no relevant studies available to comprehensively assess the risks associated with α-pvp, in particular chronic and acute toxicity, but animal observations have shown similar effects to those of other stimulants and i therefore believe that this substance should be subject to close scrutiny. member states should take the necessary control measures and criminalise those who traffic in it. subjecting this substance to control measures across the union would help to avoid the emergence of obstacles to cross-border law enforcement and judicial cooperation and would help to protect against the risks that their availability and use may pose. in the light of the foregoing, i support the proposal in question.
in writing. ‒ the scientific committee of the european monitoring centre for drugs and drug addiction has produced a report on the new psychoactive substance α-pvp, concluding that α-pvp is a potent psychostimulant. the substance has been detected in the 28 member states as well as in turkey and norway and is known to be present in the seized and collected samples mainly in powder and tablet form. the information available indicates that α-pvp is imported from the prc into the union in multi-kilogram packages and is then placed on the market within the union. if α-pvp becomes more widely available and its consumption increases, this could have significant implications for individual and public health. i therefore support the report that the new psychoactive substance should be subject to control measures in the european union.

in writing. ‒ we need to respond flexibly and in a timely manner to the discovery of new, potentially dangerous substances and subject their production, storage and distribution to strict controls.
in writing ‒ the conclusion of the 2010 protocol to the hns convention ensures the uniform application of the rules on liability and compensation for accidents caused by ships carrying dangerous and harmful substances at sea throughout the eu. at the same time, sufficient funds shall be made available to compensate victims of such accidents. in order to ensure the uniform application of the rules on liability and compensation for accidents caused by ships carrying dangerous and harmful substances at sea throughout the eu, given the nature of shipping as a global sector with cross-border implications, an international regime is preferable to regional solutions. the european parliament, the council and the european commission must work together in the future to establish a framework for a coherent eu policy on liability and compensation for environmental damage caused by the transport of dangerous and harmful substances at sea.
in writing ‒ the ratification of this protocol will allow for the uniform application of the rules on liability and compensation for damage caused by accidents involving ships carrying dangerous and harmful substances at sea throughout the eu. this international regime will help to ensure that rights and obligations are enforced in a transparent and more efficient manner for all actors concerned.
in writing the international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea, 1996, governs liability and compensation for damage caused by the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea, including liquefied natural gas and liquefied petroleum gas, which has not yet been ratified. the 2010 convention establishes the objective liability of the owner of a ship carrying dangerous and harmful substances for any damage resulting from an incident related to the transport of dangerous and harmful substances at sea and on board the ship concerned. a special compensation fund has been set up to compensate persons who have suffered damage in connection with the carriage of dangerous and harmful substances at sea and who have failed to obtain full or adequate compensation from the shipowner or his insurer. the existing union legal framework does not require compulsory insurance, with the convention specifically laying down this obligation for shipowners together with the right of claimants to directly sue the insurer. given the nature of shipping as a sector with cross-border impact, an international regime is more appropriate than regional solutions. the motion has my support.
in writing. ‒ i think it is important that a special compensation fund has been set up under this convention to compensate persons who have suffered damage in connection with the carriage of dangerous and harmful substances at sea and who have failed to obtain full or adequate compensation from the shipowner or his insurer. i voted yes.
in writing ‒ liability and compensation for damage arising from specific types of shipping activities are regulated at international level by a series of conventions of the international maritime organisation which are based on the same basic principles. these principles include: the objective liability of the shipowner, compulsory insurance to cover damage caused to third parties, the right to assert its rights directly with the insurer in the case of persons who have suffered damage, the limitation of liability and, in the case of oil and dangerous and harmful substances, a special compensation fund that pays for damage as long as it exceeds the limits of the shipowner's liability. the 2010 convention establishes the objective liability of the owner of a ship carrying dangerous and harmful substances for any damage resulting from an incident related to the transport of dangerous and harmful substances at sea and on board the ship concerned. the conclusion of the 2010 protocol to the convention on liability and compensation ensures the uniform application of the rules on liability and compensation for accidents caused by ships carrying dangerous and harmful substances at sea throughout the eu.
in writing. ‒ only qualified persons and designated institutions must have access to dangerous substances and their movement must be subject to control by national states as well as by authorities at pan-european level.
in writing the 2010 hns convention lays down rules on jurisdiction of courts and the recognition and enforcement of judgments. its scope thus overlaps with the rules contained in the recast of the brussels i regulation. the commission notes that the hns convention contains a relatively restrictive regime of jurisdiction which is contrary to a number of the criteria of jurisdiction available under the revised brussels i regulation. in view of the highly specific nature of the regime of jurisdiction under the hns convention, as well as the foreseeable legal and practical difficulties in applying a separate regime of jurisdiction within the union compared to the regime applied to other parties to the hns convention, a derogation from the general application of the recast brussels i regulation is justified. given the significant share of dangerous and harmful substances in maritime freight transport, the global nature of the shipping industry and the likely cross-border impact of accidents involving dangerous and harmful substances, i believe it is in the interest of the union to establish the most effective way without compromising the unity, integrity and effectiveness of the common rules of eu law and without undue discrimination for the victims of pollution and the shipping industry. in view of the above, i support this proposal.
in writing. ‒ i think it is important that a special compensation fund has been set up under this convention to compensate persons who have suffered damage in connection with the carriage of dangerous and harmful substances at sea and who have failed to obtain full or adequate compensation from the shipowner or his insurer. i voted for this resolution.

in writing ‒ aggressive tax planning by multinational corporations costs the national budget up to $240 billion a year. the main objective of the proposed anti-avoidance measure is to ensure that companies pay tax where they make a profit. one of the ways in which tax collection could be made more efficient in this context is through the harmonisation of taxation in europe. such corporate taxation will later be the basis of the single market and its proper functioning, and will also prevent tax evasion by multinational companies.
in writing ‒ the current legal environment allows multinational companies to shift their profits to tax havens. this is damaging to the economy of the union and its member states and reduces their ability to invest public funds in the areas of social affairs, employment, health or the fight against poverty. this results in a loss of between $100 billion and $240 billion a year to governments worldwide. the rules we propose go against the practice of tax avoidance. this will have a direct positive impact on the functioning of the internal market. i support a way for businesses to pay taxes where they make a profit. it is therefore not appropriate to introduce provisions which regulate more precisely the seat of a multinational company, but also to introduce a tax on exit when transferring patent profits to low-tax countries, because it is precisely in this way that multinational companies artificially reduce their profits. at the same time, we are strengthening the ep's role in monitoring the effectiveness of this directive. these objectives cannot be sufficiently achieved by the action of individual member states acting alone.
in writing aggressive tax planning by multinational corporations represents a huge loss of revenue for states, reducing their ability to invest to promote employment, fight poverty, create effective health care systems for all. the creation of economic and monetary union requires the harmonisation of taxation in europe. fair and effective taxation of corporate income must become a cornerstone of the single market. for the single market to be reliable, member states must agree on taxation. i consider a coordinated and harmonised approach to the application of tax systems to be the key to success. the means to pay taxes in a fair way is to show that the multinational company is properly established in the country. until now, multinationals have used patent incentives to artificially reduce their profits. this is proving to be detrimental to truly innovative countries. therefore, it is necessary to subject these multinationals to exit tax when they shift patent profits to low tax countries. that is why i am voting in favour of the motion.

the european union is founded on respect for democracy, the rule of law, human rights and fundamental freedoms, respect for human dignity and respect for international law, not only in its internal policies but also in its external dimension. human dignity and fundamental freedoms should also be respected in the fight against terrorism. it is therefore necessary to condemn the cia's extradition and secret detention programme under the auspices of the usa, which has resulted in numerous human rights violations, including unlawful and arbitrary detention, torture and other ill-treatment. the prohibition of torture is a human right that cannot be derogated from under any circumstances and forms the so-called hard core of international and european treaties for the protection of human rights. the use of enhanced interrogation techniques, which are prohibited under international law and which violate, inter alia, the rights to liberty, security, human treatment, protection against torture, the presumption of innocence, the right to a fair trial, legal aid and equal legal protection, is also unacceptable. effective counter-terrorism measures and respect for human rights are not mutually exclusive, but complementary and mutually reinforcing. i welcome the actions of us president barack obama in his ongoing efforts to close the detention facility at the us military base at guantanamo bay, cuba, and to release detainees who have not been charged.
in writing. ‒ i support the motion for a resolution. the european parliament has already called for respect for the rule of law, human dignity, human rights and fundamental freedoms in the fight against terrorism. parliament strongly condemned the programme of extradition and secret detention by the commonwealth of nations, with the assistance of the cia, which has led to numerous human rights violations, including unlawful and arbitrary detention, torture and other ill-treatment, and called on the us authorities not to impose the death penalty on guantanamo detainees.
in writing. ‒ i would condemn all use of torture by any government; and if these allegations are true, i am appalled by an important partner like the usa stooping this low. a strong message should be sent that europeans will not stand by in silence if partners abuse human rights in this way. however i could not support this oral question because the eu has no competence in this area, and must rely on international law to conclude this matter, not the european parliament.
in writing. ‒ transatlantic cooperation based on shared values must remain a key priority of the eu's external relations. it is therefore in the common interest of citizens on both sides of the atlantic to continue political dialogue on security and counter-terrorism issues, including civil and human rights. i regret to read the motion for a resolution which deals with the alleged transportation and interrogation and illegal detention of prisoners in european countries by the cia. i therefore welcome with great dismay the report of the secretary general of the council of europe on the closure of the investigation, despite the fact that investigations in several member states remain unresolved. it is essential that lithuania, romania and poland investigate transparently, thoroughly and effectively the existence of secret cia detention facilities on their territory, taking into account all factual evidence that has been made public, allow investigators to thoroughly examine all links to the detention of prisoners on their territories and bring perpetrators of human rights violations to justice.
in writing. ‒ torture is a serious breach of both european and international law. all such suspicions must be thoroughly investigated, regardless of who is concerned.
in writing ‒ space capabilities and services play an important role in european security and defence. they provide the member states and the eu with a better operational capacity to implement the csdp, but also other policies, such as maritime security, agriculture, the environment, disaster management, humanitarian aid and transport. it is therefore important to continue developing the csdp and to integrate space into future eu policies already in the above areas, but also to use space capabilities in the fight against terrorism and terrorist organisations by locating and monitoring their training camps.
space policy is essential for the strategic autonomy that the european union must develop in order to maintain sensitive technological and industrial capabilities as well as independent assessment capabilities. space capabilities for european security and defence are important and in some cases even essential for a wide range of situations, from everyday peaceful uses to crisis management and more pressing security challenges, including outright war. developing such abilities requires long-term effort. research and development of space technologies is a high-return sector, which also produces high-quality software and hardware by-products with various commercial applications. i believe that member states should improve access to capabilities in satellite space communications, space situational awareness, precise navigation and earth observation, and ensure europe's independence in key space technologies and access to space. cooperation between member states and the usa, whose experience could be helpful in space innovation, should also be encouraged. i fully support the motion.

in writing ‒ the lack of respect for the rule of law and the separation of powers in venezuela has resulted in violations of fundamental human rights and freedoms, and political instability. this affects the economic and social situation in venezuela. this has created a serious humanitarian crisis, with food and medicine shortages, basic infrastructure collapsing, and crime rising. the poverty rate in venezuela has doubled since 2013. this instability poses a potential danger to the entire region. i therefore support the call for increased mediation efforts by the union and international organisations and institutions, leading to constructive cooperation between the legislative, executive and judicial branches in venezuela. it will help to establish democratic processes in the country.

in writing ‒ in order to safeguard health and the environment, the commission was required to adopt delegated acts concerning the definition of scientific criteria for the determination of endocrine disrupting properties of active substances and biocidal products with a view to prohibiting dangerous substances. however, the commission did not adopt such delegated acts by the deadline and the eusr therefore decided that the commission had an unconditional obligation to adopt such acts without accepting the request. the eu ds rejected the legal argument of the ec and stated that the adoption of an act does not require an impact assessment of scientific criteria. however, the commission continues to fail to meet its obligations and to adopt delegated acts as required by the regulation, with endocrine disruptors being largely responsible for serious diseases, whether neurobehavioural disorders, adverse pregnancy outcomes or various oncological diseases.
in writing ‒ regulation (eu) no 528/2012 of the european parliament and of the council concerning the making available on the market and use of biocidal products, in its article 5, obliged the commission to adopt delegated acts, by 13 december 2013 at the latest, defining scientific criteria for the determination of endocrine disrupting properties of active substances and biocidal products. although the commission has been dealing with endocrine disruptors since 1996, it has not fulfilled its obligation and no such acts have been adopted so far. in doing so, scientists and scientific institutions point out that endocrine disruptors can disrupt the endocrine system of the human body and cause adverse developmental, reproductive, neurological and immune effects in humans, animals and nature. this breach of the commission's obligations was also found by the court of justice in its judgment of 16 december 2015, which stated that the temporary criteria laid down in regulation (eu) no 528/2012 cannot be understood as providing a sufficiently high level of protection. the commission has failed to fulfil this obligation and has breached the institutional obligations arising from the tfeu. i therefore supported the ep's call on the commission to fulfil its obligations without delay.
in writing the european commission has infringed union legislation by not taking action and not adopting delegated acts to specify scientific criteria for the determination of endocrine disrupting properties. the world health organisation has identified endocrine disruptors as a global threat, citing, inter alia, the increasing trend of many endocrine disorders in humans and wildlife populations. there is also increasing evidence of adverse effects of exposure to endocrine disruptors such as infertility, cancer, various deformities and effects of these chemicals on thyroid and brain function, obesity and metabolism, and on insulin and glucose homeostasis. these substances are able to cross the placenta to the fetus, where their presence has been clearly demonstrated in current studies. i fully share the view that the commission must adopt without delay scientific risk-based criteria for the determination of endocrine disrupting properties and therefore support the proposal.
in writing. ‒ i support the motion for a resolution because in a previous report the who called endocrine disruptors a global threat and referred, among other things, to the high incidence of endocrine disruption and its increasing trend today. today, new evidence is available that hormonal disruptors can cause reproductive disorders, including infertility, cancer, and birth defects. i support the commission's commitment to develop scientifically based criteria for endocrine disruptors as soon as possible.
in writing. ‒ i was pleased to support this non-legislative resolution, which sends a clear critical message to the european commission for delaying the publication of scientific criteria for the determination of the properties of endocrine disrupting substances. both the united nations environment programme and the world health organization consider them a global threat to public health. by not defining the criteria, which were to be published by the end of 2013, the commission committed breaches of eu legislative rules and thus delayed the possibility of introducing measures to restrict these disruptors.
in writing ‒ according to the judgment of the general court of the european union of december 2015, the commission infringed eu legislation by not taking action and not adopting delegated acts concerning the specification of scientific criteria for the determination of endocrine disrupting properties. as it is unacceptable for the commission, as guardian of the treaties, not to act in matters arising from its institutional duties, i supported parliament's resolution on endocrine disruptors. the commission is required to carry out impact assessments for legislative and non-legislative initiatives expected to have a significant economic, environmental or social impact. eu provisions do not allow the use of substances that may have endocrine disrupting properties. so-called endocrine disruptors can only be banned on the basis of specific scientific criteria. the commission was required to define these criteria by means of delegated acts, but this has not been done for more than two and a half years. the world health organization considers endocrine disruptors to be a global threat, as its latest report revealed the prevalence and increasing trend of many endocrine disorders in humans. in addition, there is increasing evidence of adverse effects of endocrine disruptors on the reproductive system, resulting in infertility, cancer or deformity. i therefore hope that the commission will finally fulfil its political commitment and propose the necessary scientific criteria for the determination of endocrine disrupting properties by the summer of this year.

in writing. sygenta france sas has submitted to the competent authorities of germany an application to place on the market foods, food supplements and feed containing, consisting of, or produced from bt11 x mir162 x mir604 x ga21 maize (and their sub-combinations). the application also covered the placing on the market of gm maize in products for purposes other than food and feed, with the exception of cultivation. following the positive opinion of efsa, the commission prepared a draft decision authorising products consisting of, or produced from, or containing the genetically modified maize. the standing committee on the food chain and animal health did not deliver an opinion on the commission proposal in question. it should be noted that some of the genetically modified maize tolerate glufosinate ammonium and glyphosate-based herbicides, while the international agency for research on cancer has classified glyphosate as a probable human carcinogen. moreover, the use of any new gm food or feed should not be allowed taking into account the current insufficient legal framework. i consider that the draft implementing decision of the commission goes beyond the scope of the implementing powers that are laid down and the commission should withdraw its draft implementing decision.

in writing. ‒ the as early as 2009, sygenta france sas submitted to the german authorities an application to place on the market food, food ingredients and feed consisting of, or produced from specific genetically modified maize. that application was extended in 2013 to include all subcombinations of the individual modifications constituting that maize. certain parts of this maize express the protein mepsps, which gives it tolerance to glyphosate-based herbicides. subsequently, following that application, glyphosate was included in 2015 by the international agency for research on cancer as a substance with probable carcinogenicity in humans. moreover, in its 2015 explanatory report, the commission regretted that it had taken authorisation decisions without supporting the opinions of member states' committees and that returning the dossier for a final decision had become the norm in the authorisation of genetically modified food and feed. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that the commission proposal goes beyond the scope of the implementing powers and i support the motion for a resolution of parliament asking the commission to withdraw its draft implementing decision.
in writing. ‒ the the draft commission implementing decision authorising the placing on the market of genetically modified carnation is contrary to the protection of health and the environment enshrined in directive 2001/18/ec. it goes beyond the implementing powers provided for in this directive. this type of nail contains substances toxic to nature and animals and dangerous to humans as well, and i therefore support the proposal to withdraw this implementing regulation.
in writing. in march 2013, a notification was submitted by suntory holdings limited (osaka, japan) concerning the placing on the market of a genetically modified carnation by the competent authority of the netherlands. the notification covered the import, distribution and retail of cut flowers of genetically modified carnation for ornamental purposes. following a favourable assessment by the competent authorities of the netherlands, some member states raised objections to the placing on the market of the product. efsa has therefore produced two expert opinions on which there is no scientific evidence that they have adverse effects on human health or the environment. on the basis of these opinions, the european commission has drawn up a proposal for a decision authorising the placing on the market of a genetically modified carnation. the spread of wild species cannot be excluded and resistance to sulphonylurea herbicides could encourage the use of these herbicides with possible adverse effects on biodiversity and cause chemical contamination of drinking water. personally, i believe that the proposal does not meet the objectives of protecting health and the environment and therefore exceeds the implementing powers laid down in the directive.
in writing. ‒ i supported the parliament's resolution asking the commission to withdraw its draft implementing decision on the placing of genetically modified carnation on the european market. i agree with the rapporteur that the draft decision does not meet the objective of protecting health and the environment, as the possible negative effects of using this type of nail have not been sufficiently analysed. the european food safety authority (efsa) has issued an opinion on the decision, but it does not contain a complete impact study. for example, efsa has not assessed the possible consequences of the deliberate consumption of genetically modified carnations on humans, has not addressed the deliberate or accidental consumption of carnation flowers by animals, or has not addressed the composted carnation waste that may be released into the environment. the placing on the market of this genetically modified carnation was notified to the dutch authorities by the japanese company suntory holdings limited as early as 2013. despite the time lag, there are still doubts about the effects that the specific surb gene contained in this type of carnation may have. this gene provides resistance to the highly toxic herbicide sulfonylureas, and it is unclear how its proliferation would affect the environment. i therefore take the view that the commission should withdraw its decision and examine in detail the possible public health implications.
mr president, i am glad when any administrative burden to european citizens is reduced. however, i am concerned that new definitions and ideological changes are being pushed through in seemingly practical proposals. as the documents affected by this regulation primarily concern family and marriage, citizens are concerned that ease of document flow should not impose new terms, definitions and laws on other member states. for example, the term ‘parenthood’ dilutes the more precise terms ‘father and mother’. a child’s birth certificate is fundamental to their very identity, and the names of ‘father and mother’ are sacrosanct. these irreplaceable roles must be respected, as all of us were born of a father and a mother, forming a family unit, which has greater importance even than democratic government in the establishment of other societies. every society knows that to have a child, you need a mother and a father, which is the only natural thing. we forget this natural, god-given principle at our peril.
mr president more than 10 million eu citizens enjoy the opportunities of free movement. during their stay in another member state, citizens encounter a new system of administration, education and social security that is foreign to them. this raises a number of administrative difficulties. the regulation aims to facilitate the cross-border acceptance of documents relating to marital status and other rights by simplifying administrative formalities, and i therefore respectfully welcome this initiative. with hundreds of thousands of documents being authenticated each year, this is a step towards building trust between member states, which could save eu citizens time and money. the main achievement of the regulation is the creation of multilingual forms. multilingualism is a burden on the administration, and the fact that forms can be produced in all the official languages of the eu will change this. i am particularly pleased that from the point of view of a community which, for example, has a connection with another member state because of the similarity of language, i will be able to present, as a slovak hungarian, a form, if necessary, in hungary, which was prepared for me by the slovak authorities without any extra translation costs. this regulation is therefore a good starting point, which i respectfully support.

in writing. ‒ more than 10 million eu citizens benefit from the opportunities offered by free movement. even today, there are a number of administrative obstacles to staying in another member state, whether for a shorter or longer period. proof of marital status, a birth certificate or even a certificate of good conduct may be required when applying for a job, starting studies or even when using services abroad. the european parliament has therefore adopted a resolution on the european union's future strategy for the fight against terrorism, which calls for the eu to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that it is not simply a matter of putting the eu on the wrong side of the atlantic. the regulation will soon facilitate the cross-border acceptance of, in particular, marital status and other rights documents by simplifying administrative formalities. the main achievement of the regulation is the creation of multilingual forms. multilingualism is a burden on the administration, and the fact that forms can be produced in all the official languages of the eu will change that. multilingual forms do not affect the content, but they will help the case managers in their work. what is displayed in one member state can be more easily processed in the target country in its own language. the only way is to inform citizens about simplification in as many forums as possible.
in writing. the proposed regulation simplifies the arrangements and procedures for handling public documents on marital status, residence, nationality and criminal records, which will be exempt from legalisation and apostille. the legality and authenticity of the documents will be demonstrated by the institutions and bodies directly concerned. this will facilitate the mobility of persons within the union.
in writing. while citizens and businesses of the european union are exercising their rights to free movement or the freedoms of the internal market, they may face administrative difficulties when submitting authentic instruments to the authorities of another member state. the regulation thus covers documents on marital status as well as certain other documents often requested by citizens, such as residence, nationality and criminal records. the regulation provides for exemption from legalisation and apostille, two administrative formalities traditionally required for cross-border authentic instruments. simplified reception arrangements are also provided for certified true copies and official translations. this simplification for the citizen is balanced by the possibility for the administrative authority receiving the document to contact the issuing administrative authority directly and electronically with a request for authentication of the document. the regulation includes the creation of multilingual standard forms for most of the relevant authentic instruments. the free movement of citizens will be greatly facilitated by the simplification of the adoption of certain authentic instruments in the member states of the union. this legislation does not concern the recognition of the content of authentic instruments, in order to preserve the sovereignty of the member states in the area of family law. in view of the above, i fully support the proposal.
in writing. ‒ i support the draft resolution. it is important that we, as citizens of the european union, live our citizenship as a reality, as part of our daily lives. think of the right to free movement. the mobility of eu citizens is a reality, with almost 12 million people studying, working or living in a member state other than their own. when eu citizens and businesses exercise their rights of free movement or internal market freedoms, they may encounter administrative complications. such complexities are quite natural, such as the submission of authentic instruments to the authorities of other member states, the preparation of authentication processes and certified translations. the regulation, which i support, helps to alleviate these situations by providing for exemption from the double-certification and apostille requirements for authentic instruments, which are traditional administrative formalities for cross-border authentic instruments. finally, the main element of the regulation is the creation of multilingual forms for the majority of the public documents concerned, which i also consider very important. these multilingual forms are issued by the national authorities and are attached to the national document when an authentic instrument is to be lodged in another member state. this annex contains the text of the authentic instrument in question and thus exempts citizens from the obligation to submit a translation of the administrative document. this makes the daily life of a mobile, free and multilingual european citizen much easier.
in writing. ‒ parliament has long sought to uphold the right to free movement and residence of persons within the eu, which it considers to be a key principle of the european union. although this right was established by the maastricht treaty as early as 1992, its practical implementation was not as clear-cut in the past and is not so clear-cut at present. i am glad that today there is a directive on the right of eu citizens and their family members to move and reside freely within the territory of the member states. although citizens and businesses of the union currently exercise their rights to free movement in accordance with the legislation in force or the freedoms of the internal market, they are exposed to many administrative obstacles to the cross-border use and reception of authentic instruments when they submit authentic instruments to the authorities of another member state. i supported the resolution on the current report because i believe that, on the basis of the measures taken, we will improve the free movement of citizens by simplifying the adoption of certain public documents in the eu, which is aimed at fulfilling the very important task of facilitating formalities for citizens crossing borders. i believe that the proposed regulation will succeed in reducing costs for individuals as well as cutting down on the often unwanted red tape.
in writing. ‒ the simplifying the requirements for the verification of public documents is of great importance for anyone applying for a job or wanting to settle in another eu member state. today, a number of documents need to be officially authenticated in such a case. the proposal adopted also helps students who go to study at european universities and need to present public documents relating to birth, name, residence, citizenship and nationality, or the absence of a criminal record. all such documents shall be exempt from any formality of legalization or similar nature. the authorities will also not be able to require the simultaneous production of the original of the document and of a certified copy thereof issued by the authorities of other member states. in addition, they will have to accept a non-certified copy if the original document is presented together with such a copy, and also accept certificates issued in other member states. this will certainly save students not only money but also time in completing the necessary paperwork. that's why i supported the motion.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report of the parliament on the draft regulation delegating to the general court of the european union the power to give a preliminary ruling on disputes between the union and its servants. the report is one of the documents on the reform of the court of justice, based in luxembourg, which streamlines and improves the procedure for dealing with cases involving 28 member states, in this particular case disputes between the eu institutions and their staff. the regulation is the fourth piece of legislation reforming the court of justice. the first amendment concerned the composition and procedure of the court of justice and the general court, the second the substitute judges of the civil service tribunal. the third concerned an increase in the number of judges of the general court. the original proposal would have increased the number of judges from 28 to 40. at the end of the procedure, a decision was taken which fixed the number of judges at 56, allowing each member state to nominate two judges. the civil service tribunal shall be abolished and civil service disputes shall revert to the jurisdiction of the general court. the proposal also covers the way in which proceedings pending before the civil service tribunal are to be transferred to the general court. the cases pending before the civil service tribunal shall be assigned to the tribunal on 31 august 2016 in accordance with their order of the day.
in writing. the proposal for a regulation concerns the reform of the court of justice, where the last reform increased the number of judges to 56, two for each member state, subject to the abolition of the civil service tribunal. this regulation repeals the civil service tribunal and at the same time provides for a procedure for referring civil service disputes initiated back to the general court.
in writing. this regulation concerns the reform of the court of justice and builds on the previous regulations. in parallel with the increase in the number of judges of the general court from 40 to 47, the civil service tribunal, which has seven judges, must be abolished. the proposal concerns the procedure for referring to the general court proceedings brought before the civil service tribunal. the proceedings before the civil service tribunal which are not concluded by 31 august 2016 shall be transferred as they stand on that date. in the interests of legal certainty, the rules of procedure of the general court will apply to these proceedings. not only will the rules of procedure of the general court have to be amended, but also its internal organisation. i believe that a higher number of cases should be allocated to the larger panels where their importance so requires, in order to ensure the consistency and quality of the case-law. the possibility of adapting the rules and procedures governing the allocation of items should also be considered. i agree with the motion that has been tabled.
in writing. ‒ i believe it is important that the court of justice of the european union should have the appropriate powers to deal with disputes between the european union and its staff and that the court of justice should be continuously reformed and technical amendments made to ensure the impartiality, independence and transparency of the judiciary.
in writing. ‒ the proposed regulation on the delegation of the power to adjudicate at first instance in disputes between the union and its servants to the general court of the eu is the fourth in a series on the reform of the court of justice. i consider this proposal to be a necessary process in the continuation of the reform of the general court decided by the union legislature in order to address the problem of the increase in the number of cases heard by that court. i supported the adoption of this regulation because i believe that the amendments will contribute to better regulation and that all civil service cases transferred from the civil service tribunal to the general court will be heard as they stand at that date and will be open to appeal to the court of justice. i expect that the reform and the proposed measures will increase the flexibility of the general court in dealing with the contentious agenda, and improve the quality and dignity of justice delivered on behalf of european citizens. i believe that the rules of procedure of the general court will also be amended shortly, which should take account of the specific rules currently laid down in the rules of procedure of the civil service tribunal.
in writing. it is important to clarify the relations between the various institutions and to make their activities transparent.
in writing. today's vote called on the commission to adopt a regulation laying down precise procedural rules for the administration. it will apply to the institutions, bodies, offices and agencies of the union, with the exception of activities in legislative, judicial and non-legislative procedures which are directly based on the treaties, delegated acts or implementing acts. i support this proposal because it aims to establish transparent, understandable and unambiguous rules and procedures without increasing the administrative burden and complexity, which will be in line with good governance and will strengthen the legal certainty of the parties concerned. this regulation shall not apply to the public administration of the member states.
in writing. the union does not have a uniform set of codified rules of administrative law and it is therefore difficult for citizens to understand the administrative rights conferred on them by union law. both the excess and the lack of rules and procedures can lead to maladministration, which may also result from the existence of conflicting, inconsistent or unclear rules and procedures. the aim is to establish a set of procedural rules that the union administration should follow in the exercise of its administrative activities. these procedural rules aim to ensure an open, efficient and independent administration, while ensuring the proper enforcement of the right to good administration. the right to good administration imposes an obligation on the union administration to state clearly the reasons on which its administrative acts are based. the recital should state the legal basis of the act, the general situation which led to its adoption and the general objectives to be achieved by it. the reasoning of the competent authority which adopted the act should be published in a clear and unambiguous manner so as to enable the parties concerned to decide whether to defend their rights by means of a request for judicial review. i am convinced that the establishment of a common set of rules of administrative procedure at the level of the union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies will strengthen legal certainty, close the loopholes in the union legal system and contribute to respect for the rule of law. i vote for the motion.
in writing. ‒ i fully support the report. eu citizens are increasingly coming into direct contact with the eu institutions and therefore rightly expect a high level of transparency, efficiency, rapid implementation and responsiveness from the eu institutions, bodies, offices and agencies. citizens also have the right to adequate information on their case. article 41 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union also provides for the right to an adequate administration, which states that everyone has the right to have his or her affairs handled impartially, fairly and within a reasonable time by the institutions, bodies, offices and agencies of the union. however, at present the union does not have a comprehensive and harmonised codified system of administrative law, which makes it difficult for union citizens to understand their administrative rights under union law. the exercise of the right to good administration would be greatly facilitated by the establishment and institutionalisation of an open, efficient and independent european public administration system.
in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament's motion for a resolution on an open, efficient and independent administration of the european union. this regulation lays down procedural rules governing the administrative activities of the union administration. as eu competences develop, citizens are increasingly confronted with the union's institutions, bodies, offices and agencies without their procedural rights always being adequately protected. citizens have the right to expect a high level of transparency, efficiency, speed and responsiveness from the union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies. citizens also have the right to receive appropriate information on the possibility of taking further action on the matter. since the union does not have a uniform and comprehensive set of codified rules of administrative law, it is therefore difficult for citizens to understand the administrative rights conferred on them by union law. the purpose of this regulation is therefore to lay down a set of procedural rules to be followed by the union administration in the performance of its administrative activities, so that every eu citizen is guided in the handling of any administrative matter, is not hampered and the whole process is as transparent and efficient as possible.
in writing. ‒ the european administration is less robust than that of some large cities. nevertheless, it is of the utmost importance that we continuously make its work more efficient and save european citizens' money.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament resolution on the competitiveness of the european railway supply industry points out that the railway supply industry is a key industry, both in terms of european competitiveness and innovation capacity. it is directly responsible for 1 million jobs and indirectly for 1.2 million jobs in the union. the resolution stresses that competitors outside the union, mainly in china, are aggressively expanding in europe and around the world, often with strong political and financial support from their countries of origin. this trend could lead to unfair competition that threatens european jobs, which is why it is important to guarantee a level playing field in global competition. the european parliament's report adopted today, which i voted in favour of, contains a number of proposals to help and encourage the competitiveness of the european railway sector. it calls, inter alia, for the rapid introduction of an integrated e-ticketing system compatible with other modes of transport and other possible services provided by single ticketing services, and draws attention to the urgent need to implement modern rail, tram and other lines and the necessary accessories in the common european market. considers that the commission should consider establishing a european-level forum to bring together companies with innovative ideas in the railway sector, in particular in relation to digitalisation, in order to share good practices and facilitate the establishment of partnerships;
in writing. the european rail supply industry is characterised in particular by the production of components with a lifespan of up to 50 years, a high capital intensity, a high dependence on public procurement and the need to comply with very strict safety standards. given the particular contribution of the railway sector, the european commission needs to underpin the objectives of the modal shift to rail passenger and freight transport set out in the 2011 transport white paper with concrete policy actions and targeted investments. the creation of a single european railway area will be key to maintaining the leading position of the european rail supply sector at global level. i believe it is essential that the commission makes better use of the european structural and investment funds to support railway research and development projects at regional level. the future of the rail supply sector after 2020 also needs to be given greater attention. in this context, i must point out that the teaching of appropriately selected skills is also an investment necessary to maintain the world-leading position of the european rail supply industry in terms of technology in the long term and to maintain its innovative capacity. that is why i am voting in favour of the motion.
in writing. ‒ the rail sector contributes to climate change mitigation and to coping with other current megatrends such as urbanisation and demographic change. the rail supply sector is a key industrial sector for europe's competitiveness and its capacity for innovation. measures should be taken to ensure that europe maintains its technological and innovation edge in this sector. that's why i supported this resolution.
in writing. ‒ the european rail supply industry employs around 400 000 people and is linked to a number of smes. currently, the industry is under great pressure from foreign companies. i therefore supported the parliament's resolution calling on the commission to do more to remove the main non-tariff barriers which prevent the european railway sector from accessing foreign markets. the whole railway sector is special in particular because it produces components with a lifespan of up to 50 years, is highly capital intensive, relies heavily on public procurement and has to comply with strict safety standards. on the other hand, the european rail supply industry can rely on several favourable factors, as it is a mode of transport with good environmental performance, can rely on a large market and on the ability to facilitate mass transport. in the rail supply sector, the eu is very open to third-country competitors, but third countries have introduced a number of barriers that disadvantage european companies. competitors from third countries, such as china, are rapidly and aggressively penetrating europe and other regions of the world, often with the strong political and financial support of their countries. it is therefore necessary for the commission to guarantee the new generation of commercial contracts and to revise the existing ones.

in writing. political tensions, internal armed conflicts, corruption, human rights abuses, the gap between rich and poor, and the absence of a middle class, all combined with hunger and lack of basic needs for the majority of the population, make up the current picture of the democratic republic of congo. paradoxically, this is a country with vast mineral resources. yet 75 percent of the population lives on less than $1 a day. 60% of all the world's minerals are congo minerals. only 30 percent of diamonds and tantalum are exported via the normal trade route, the rest being traded illegally, which then finances the armament of various warring groups. i support the proposal that the european union use all diplomatic and commercial efforts to achieve and ensure internal stability in the congo, the establishment and development of democracy and the rule of law, and through development cooperation policies to help eliminate corruption and the illegal trade in the country's mineral wealth.

in writing. ‒ the ep adopted a resolution on the inclusion of measures adopted by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas for farming and fishing of bluefin tuna in the regulation. the aim is to ensure that all measures are applied uniformly and effectively throughout the european union, which is why i supported the proposal. in view of the effectiveness of the measures applied, a positive trend in the recovery of the stock of this species has occurred in recent years and therefore higher catch quotas have been authorised for the years 2015 to 2017.
in writing. the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas is the regional fisheries management organisation responsible for the management of tuna and tuna-like species in the atlantic ocean, of which the european union is a member. in 2006, the commission adopted a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna, which expires in 2022. in order to restore the stock, the plan provides for a gradual reduction of the total allowable catch between 2007 and 2011, fishing restrictions in certain areas and periods, a new minimum size, measures concerning sport and recreational fishing activities, as well as measures concerning breeding and fishing capacity. the bluefin tuna biomass has shown a significantly positive trend since 2008. the regional organisation decided in 2014 to increase the total allowable catch for the next three years by 20% as there is reliable scientific data demonstrating that stocks have reached healthy levels. the aim of transposing the recommendations of the international commission is to ensure uniform application throughout the european union. this should mainly aim at ensuring a level playing field for all operators involved in tuna fishing, including operators from non-eu countries. the effort and restrictions applied to eu fishermen will otherwise be of no use if different rules are applied to foreign fleets. i vote for the motion.
in writing. ‒ the positive development of the recovery plan adopted between 2012 and 2014 is a welcome development, as one of its important objectives, the increase of bluefin tuna stocks in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean, has been achieved. i voted in favour of the proposal to consolidate the various measures in a single regulation so that we can continue to maintain these favourable trends. the healthy tuna stock is established to allow all tuna fishermen to continue their activities.
in writing. ‒ the european union is a contracting party to the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat). the iccat commission has the power to adopt decisions (recommendations) for the protection and management of fishery resources in its area of competence (including the fixing of total allowable catches for a given period). these acts shall be binding. they must be transposed into union law. in recent years, there has been a significant recovery of the bluefin tuna stock, which could mean that the total allowable catch increases more than originally planned. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ the eu is a contracting party to the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat), the regional fisheries management organisation (rfmo) responsible for the management of tuna and tuna-like species in the atlantic ocean and adjacent seas. bluefin tuna is the most important species regulated by iccat. fishermen made a considerable effort to adapt their catches to the reduced tacs resulting from the decisions taken in 2006, by complying with the strict fishing conditions set out in the plan. in view of the positive development of the stock situation, the iccat commission decided to increase the total allocated quota slightly to 13 400 tonnes in 2013. the total allowable catches for 2014 were not changed. the regional organisation decided to increase the allowable fishing effort for the next three years (2015 2017) by 20% as there is reliable scientific evidence that the bluefin tuna stocks are declining. the aim of the approved proposal is to apply the same conditions throughout the eu to all operators involved in tuna fishing. the same rules should apply to all operators outside the eu.
in writing. ‒ the commission's proposal is based on a multi-species management plan for fish farming and recovery in the baltic sea. the aim is to ensure a balanced relationship between fish farming and restoration and the provision of jobs and livelihoods for fishermen. this proposal has positive effects on ecosystems and at the same time on the maintenance of jobs.
in writing. in 2014, the european commission published a multiannual plan for the baltic cod, herring and sprat stocks and the fisheries exploiting those stocks. the proposal aims to establish a framework for the multispecies management of cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea, with fishing primarily targeting these three species. the multi-species management approach is much more effective than single-species management. the plan should ensure the balanced and sustainable exploitation of these stocks and the stability of fishing opportunities and thus the livelihoods of fishermen. at the same time, it should ensure that management is based on the most up-to-date scientific advice on the state of stocks, species interactions and other aspects related to ecosystems and fisheries. in view of the above, i agree with the proposal.
in writing. ‒ i consider the direction of the proposal, which foresees a long-term economic plan for the baltic sea, to be very important. the balanced regulation of several species takes into account a number of problems that arise. demonstrate the need for responsible and sustainable objectives to protect the environment. i therefore voted in favour of the proposal, which could bring about a guiding stability in the face of a highly sensitive ecosystem. this will bring us closer to ensuring that fishing opportunities continue to be available to those who make their living from fishing.
in writing. ‒ in recent years, cod, herring and sprat have accounted for more than 94% of catches in the baltic sea. the general focus of the commission's proposal on the need for a multi-species management plan in the baltic sea is correct. the multi-species management approach is much more effective than single-species management. the plan should ensure the balanced and sustainable exploitation of these stocks and the stability of fishing opportunities and thus the livelihoods of fishermen. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ i have agreed to the proposal for a regulation by which the commission intends to regulate the stocks of cod, herring and sprat in the baltic sea, as these three fish species account for more than 90% of the catches in this area. the baltic sea is essentially a closed body of water in which these three species are ubiquitous and constantly interacting with each other. it is therefore of particular importance to allow for a management of their populations that takes account of their interactions. cod populations are affected by the size of herring and sprat populations, as cod is a predator of sprats and herring. given that cod, herring and sprat are important components of the baltic ecosystem, it is desirable to adapt their exploitation rates and techniques to new scientific knowledge on the interactions and changes of environmental conditions. the proposal for a regulation addresses these biological interactions and the environmental effects of fish stocks in the baltic sea. a first step towards the flexible management of the stocks of these three species is a proposal to include all relevant stocks in a single management plan. this will allow for more flexible access to resources during the annual fixing of fishing opportunities and improve responses to changing situations.

in writing. ‒ parliament gave its consent today to the conclusion of an agreement between the eu and peru on the short-stay visa waiver. peru is one of the few latin american countries whose citizens require a visa to enter the eu. the agreement on visa-free travel for short stays could be both a step towards deepening relations between the european union and the republic of peru and a further means of strengthening economic and cultural links and encouraging political dialogue. the eu is peru's third largest trading partner and the main recipient of peruvian exports. the eu is the largest investor in peru, with more than half of foreign direct investment coming from the eu. it is important that the agreement includes a joint declaration on cooperation on irregular migration, in which the union and peru recall their commitment to take back their own irregular migrants. last but not least, peru can become a key partner in the fight against organised crime, such as drug trafficking and human trafficking. this may also be indicated by the country's interest in signing a strategic cooperation agreement with the european police office.
in writing. ‒ the taking into account the generally positive assessment of may 2015, the council adopted a decision on the conclusion of a bilateral agreement between the eu and the republic of peru. the signed agreement allows eu citizens as well as peruvian citizens to travel without a visa to the territories of both parties for a period not exceeding 90 days. the decision to lift the visa requirement applies to all persons and travellers with the exception of paid employment. the eu expects the agreement to strengthen trade and investment relations in particular, but also to boost tourism.
in writing. ‒ the the conclusion of this agreement shall abolish the visa requirement for short-stay nationals of peru when crossing the borders of the union for a period of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. this right shall apply to all persons except those travelling in the course of a paid activity. peru has had the strongest sustained economic growth in latin america over the last decade, at over 80%, placing it among the top ten countries in the world. the agreement will boost mutual trade and investment, expand tourism and help consolidate and stabilise democracy in peru.

in writing. ‒ the proposal presented here aims to improve the regulation of harmful emissions from engines installed in so-called non-road mobile machinery, which encompasses a wide range of machinery such as construction machinery, inland waterway vessels and others. the emissions in question contribute significantly to air quality in the european union and must therefore become an important part of air quality legislation at european union level and help member states to achieve national air quality objectives.
in writing. ‒ the protection of the environment and the air is a continuous process which must respond flexibly to technical developments and the associated potential threats. off-road mobile machinery produces around 15% of nitrogen oxides (nox) and 5% of particulate matter emissions within the eu. the proposed resolution seeks to introduce new emission limits in order to achieve the objectives of eu policy on air protection and public health.
in writing. this proposal covers a wide range of combustion engines installed in machinery ranging from small hand-held devices, construction machinery to railway wagons, locomotives and inland waterway vessels. all these engines account for about 15% of nitrogen oxide and 5% of particulate matter emissions in the european union. the new rules will simplify the implementation phase for the introduction of new emission levels and type-approval procedures to reduce the burden on manufacturers. a new service has also been established in the monitoring system to assess engine performance, bridging the gap between laboratory engine testing and real-world emissions. a number of exemptions will be provided to address specific needs relating to some important sectors such as agriculture or railways (narrow-gauge tractors, engines incorporated in locomotives with a power range of up to 2000 kw and also engines incorporated in locomotives which are part of a project at an advanced stage of development). in view of the above, i support the proposal.
in writing. ‒ the european union currently has the strictest rules on emissions. it is very important that we formulate harmonised rules. our aim is to further improve the quality of the environment and thus the health of european citizens. predictability is important to maintain the competitiveness of industry, which can increase employment. i supported the report, which seeks to strike a reasonable balance between health and the competitiveness of the european union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this legislative resolution. in line with eu air quality policy, the aim is to gradually reduce emissions from engines placed on the market and thus replace older engines that pollute more over time. generally, the limit values will be aligned with those of the us and japanese markets, whose limits are currently stricter than those of the eu.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution because i believe that achieving the union's air quality and air protection objectives in a sustainable way from now to 2020 and beyond requires the adoption of additional emission limits also for non-road mobile machinery. i agree that the new emission limits should also apply to agricultural machinery and vehicles, which should make the share of emissions from non-road mobile machinery more proportionate to road vehicles. i expect that the proposed measures will not only extend the scope of union legislation on market harmonisation, but also simplify the current legal framework, including measures to simplify administrative procedures and improve the general conditions for enforcement. i welcome the fact that, in order to reduce emissions from non-road mobile machinery, we are going to deepen direct cooperation between manufacturers and other related enterprises on the one hand and well-established scientific and research institutions on the other. i am convinced that better cooperation in the development of new products and technologies will also improve air quality and reduce emissions from off-road machinery and agricultural vehicles.
in writing. ‒ given that greenhouse gas emissions are also largely influenced by machinery, environmental considerations are also needed in this respect. the proposed regulation has two objectives, namely to reduce emissions and to reduce red tape. such an arrangement can have a positive impact not only on the health of citizens but also on the business environment and competitiveness in europe.
in writing. ‒ the i supported the european parliament's legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation to amend the emission limits for non-road mobile machinery. non-road machinery such as cranes or other construction machinery, trains, snowmobiles or even lawn mowers can make a significant contribution to air pollution, resulting in a number of health problems for the european union's population, among other things. the aim of this proposal was therefore to introduce uniform conditions for the emission limits or authorisation of these machines, thus replacing the current legislation represented by the directive, under which not one but 28 different systems were in operation. the new regulation not only introduces a uniform system but also stricter emission limits that are closer to japanese or american limits, thus unifying international standards. in addition to the benefits for the environment and human health, the regulation will also contribute to increasing the competitiveness of european industry in these sectors, as european producers will have lower costs, less administrative burden resulting from uniform requirements and thus easier access to third country markets.

in writing. ‒ the trafficking in human beings continues to be the worst form of human rights violation and is part of organised crime. trafficking in human beings reduces people to commodities, violates their integrity, dignity and rights. often, the condition of poverty is abused. according to the 2014 trafficking in persons report, girls and women account for 75% of victims, especially in the area of sexual exploitation. human trafficking can therefore be characterised as a gender-based crime. according to europol, the worldwide spread of internet access is facilitating the growing development of trafficking in human beings in the online environment. there is also a link between migrant smuggling and trafficking in human beings, as it is the smuggling groups that offer their services via the internet and it is not a transient phenomenon. it is illegal migration flows that increase the risk of trafficking in human beings and that threaten to target unaccompanied minors.

in writing. trafficking in human beings is one of the worst forms of human rights violations, because it deeply and persistently violates the dignity, integrity and rights of victims and affects entire families and communities, while also deliberately exploiting a state of vulnerability, such as poverty or isolation. complex and interconnected factors such as systemic and structural discrimination, human rights violations, poverty, inequality, corruption, violent conflicts, lack of education, unemployment and dysfunctional labour migration regimes increase the vulnerability of persons and their exposure to exploitation and abuse. this is a complex regional and global problem that cannot be solved at national level alone. criminal networks increasingly use the internet and social networks to recruit and exploit victims, therefore member states need to invest adequately in technology and expertise to identify and track the abuse of the internet by criminal networks for recruiting victims, as well as to offer services aimed at exploiting victims, as part of their efforts. member states must strengthen cooperation with third countries to combat all forms of trafficking in human beings, with particular emphasis on the gender dimension of trafficking in human beings.
