in writing. network and information systems and services play an important role in facilitating the cross-border movement of goods, persons and services. a significant disruption of these systems in one member state may have an impact on other member states and the european union as a whole. the resilience and stability of network and information systems are therefore essential for the proper functioning of the internal market. the scale and intensity of security incidents caused by human error or malicious attacks are increasing. there is currently no effective mechanism in the european union for cooperation and secure information sharing between member states. it is the digital service providers that are considered to be a significant resource and will be subject to a simplified procedure concerning security requirements. they will be subject to a fully harmonised approach to ensure a uniform approach across the european union. in the event of non-compliance, it is for the member state to lay down the appropriate penalties. a strategic coordination group will also be established to aim at a more coherent approach to cybersecurity across the union. i support the motion.
in writing. ‒ the proposal seeks to create a trusted and secure digital environment. i am voting in favour of this proposal because information systems, and in particular the internet, as a means of communication without frontiers, are interconnected in the member states and play an important role in facilitating the movement of goods, services and people across borders. the proposal aims to deepen cooperation between member states in tackling cyber threats. each country of the union must adopt its own information security strategy. well-functioning computer emergency response teams should be established in all member states. secondly, the competent national authorities should cooperate within a network that allows for safe and effective coordination, including coordinated exchange of information, as well as detection and response at eu level. through this network, member states should exchange information and cooperate. the proposal aims to ensure that a risk management culture is developed and that information is exchanged between the private and public sectors. a cooperation mechanism should be established at union level to allow for the exchange of information and coordinated action. the european network and information security agency should assist member states by providing its expertise and advice and by facilitating the exchange of best practices.
in writing. - i voted yes. i support a final agreement that sets out the basic measures to improve the security of information systems in europe and reflects the benefits that can be derived from the mutual exchange of information between eu member states on the threats we face in the field of information systems security.
in writing. ‒ the the security of network and information systems is increasingly important for the functioning of our societies and economies and, last but not least, an important prerequisite for creating a secure environment for global trade in services. unfortunately, we are increasingly seeing information systems affected by security incidents, and they are occurring more frequently and on a larger scale. these unfair practices are also reflected in the commission's finding that up to 57% of respondents had experienced network and information security incidents in the past year. as there is currently no effective mechanism at eu level for effective cooperation and confidential exchange of information on network and information security incidents and risks between member states, i supported the draft directive as i believe it is right to ensure a high level of network and information security (nis) at all levels. given that networks and information systems are interconnected and that the resilience and stability of networks and information systems are essential for the proper functioning of the internal market, i agree that we should continue with the strategy we have started and contribute to facilitating the cross-border movement of goods, services and persons by harmonising the rules.
in writing. ‒ we are currently witnessing a rise in cyber attacks, not only by criminals but also by certain states. the consistent protection of information systems cannot be ensured by states alone. to do this, we need to work closely together in the emerging digital single market.
in writing. ‒ i supported the second reading of the proposal to increase cybersecurity of networks, as i consider it important to set minimum requirements for the security of the digital environment at eu level. the proposal will require providers of essential services, such as energy, transport, banking and healthcare, and digital services, including search engines and clouds, to strengthen their resilience to cyberattacks. the new directive should lay down safety and reporting obligations for operators of so-called essential services in sectors such as energy, transport, health, banking and the supply and distribution of drinking water. however, the list of specific operators in each sector to be covered by those requirements will be left to the discretion of each member state.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a regulation sets out a framework for energy efficiency labelling and repeals directive 2010/30/eu. the proposal aims to provide greater transparency for consumers and authorities on energy-related products placed on the union market. the labelling allows consumers to compare products and therefore make an environmentally conscious and cost-effective choice. the energy label has helped to raise awareness among citizens about the environmental impact of products. however, many shortcomings were identified during the review of directive 2010/30/ec. that's what i'd like to correct with the amendments. a new energy classification of product models is proposed: energy classes a-g, with a transition within 5 years. the commission also proposes to set up a product database accessible to consumers. a platform where the customer can find all the information about the products.
in writing. ‒ the since its inception, the label has enabled citizens to better understand the environmental impact of products and their life cycle. the evaluation of directive 2010/30/ec has revealed a number of shortcomings. if addressed, they can lead to significant additional energy savings. we cannot remain the only major market without the central system of mandatory product registration and public database that the us, china, australia and other countries created a few years ago. the revised database represents a real driver of the changes needed to empower citizens as protagonists of the eu's energy transformation.
in writing. the proposal aims to ensure continuity while stimulating development, balance between citizens, businesses and other stakeholders. the allocation of product models to energy efficiency classes a to g after the adjustment of the scales will have a significant impact on the market. a flexible approach to its management shall be maintained, with three options for reducing the intensity of the change of gears: c to g (with two empty classes at the top), b to g (one empty class) and a to g (no empty classes). these ranges of scales will also depend on the trigger mechanisms mentioned. the objective is to converge to the a g scale within 5 years. emphasis is also placed on information flows and planning tools. together they should create a knowledge-driven transition that will include tailor-made solutions for newly labelled product groups and small-scale products. it is also necessary to ensure that information of relevance to consumers relating to energy-related products is stored and organised in an easily accessible and usable form, while encouraging businesses to develop innovative applications that deliver key value to citizens, industry and society. i support the motion.
in writing. ‒ the energy labelling is environmentally friendly because it allows consumers to obtain accurate, relevant and comparable information on the energy efficiency and consumption of energy-related products anywhere in the union, enabling them to make informed, cost-effective and environmentally sound purchasing decisions that are good for the environment and save money. most consumers know, understand and use energy labelling in their purchasing decisions. for several products, the lower energy label classes are empty, as ecodesign measures have banned low-efficiency models and manufacturers have responded to technological progress with increasingly efficient products. there is a systematic need to 'scale up' products by returning to the original a to g energy label scale. member states should be required to carry out promotional information campaigns to inform consumers of the change of scale on labels. establish a database of products subject to energy labelling. the new product registration database will allow market surveillance authorities much faster access to the necessary information. the product registration database only creates a new obligation for suppliers to register the product model by submitting information. this technical development leads to the development of products belonging mainly to the highest energy labelling classes. in order to maintain the credibility of the energy label in the eyes of consumers.
in writing. ‒ the rapid technological progress achieved in the field of energy efficiency of products in recent years needs to be taken into account in the legislation concerning energy efficiency of products. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ energy efficiency is not only a matter of protecting the environment, but also of our efforts to save costs and reduce the load on the networks. our focus must be on the consumer and his comfort.
in writing. ‒ the legislation on energy labelling applies to products that have a significant direct or indirect impact on energy consumption. i supported the tightening of energy efficiency criteria to reflect technological progress, i also support the division of appliances into seven efficiency classes, from a to g. the majority of electrical appliances today fall under class a, under which subclasses a+, a++ and a+++ have been created, on the basis of the 2010 requirements. this loses the incentive of manufacturers to further increase the efficiency of the appliances they produce. however, the label on a household appliance should inform the consumer not only of the energy efficiency class of the product but also of its absolute energy consumption in kwh over a year or other period of time. the adopted proposal also calls for the creation of an internet product database with information on each product and an electronic platform to support the work of market surveillance authorities. the new rules will not apply to used products (purchased second-hand), nor to lifts, escalators and conveyor belts.
in writing. ‒ migration has put unprecedented pressure on the eu's external borders, leading many eu member states to re-introduce internal border controls. the ebcg, which will replace frontex, would consist of a new european border and coast guard agency and a pool of national authorities responsible for border management, including coast guards to the extent appropriate to their border control tasks. the proposal includes a 1500-strong border guard force to be made available to all member states without exception, a procedure to be followed in situations requiring immediate action at borders, and increased cooperation with third countries. the european border and coast guard is in fact created by extending the tasks, powers and mandate of frontex. the establishment of the agency could significantly improve the effectiveness of the protection of the external borders and restore the functioning of the schengen system. one of the agency's positive outcomes is that it will operate with 1500 border guards on standby, who can be deployed within seven days in any member state where the protection of the external borders is not adequately ensured. while the protection of the external borders remains a national competence, the agency will play an important role when they are under pressure from migration or other unforeseen security threats such as international crime. i voted in favour of the proposal because i am convinced that it will contribute to increasing solidarity between member states, strengthen integration in border management and prevent border crises.
in writing. ‒ the schengen area, currently made up of 26 member states, is one of the greatest achievements of european integration. it allows the free movement of persons, goods and services. terrorist attacks, but also the poorly regulated movement of refugees, continue to put enormous pressure on it. the challenges of guaranteeing internal security and order in the countries of the european union are linked to the ability to protect our common external borders consistently. the speed of the creation of a common european border and coast guard is absolutely essential to its preservation. consistent protection of the external borders is not a panacea. however, it is an important part of the mosaic in effective migration management. so is the detection and punishment of smugglers profiting from human misery. the slovak presidency of the council of the eu has also placed emphasis on the establishment of a european border and coast guard, while preserving the sovereignty of the member states, within the framework of the priorities set. the people and the adequate material equipment of the newly strengthened agency will be particularly important. up to 1500 border guards from each member state should form some kind of rapid deployment unit. continuous monitoring of the external borders is necessary in order to identify and eliminate weaknesses.
in writing. ‒ the migration crisis increases the risk of terrorist attacks and threatens security in europe. the task and objective of the creation of a european border and coast guard to replace the existing frontex is to protect the external borders of the schengen area and to establish a european integrated border management system. coordination and assistance with member states' national authorities is increased, risk predictability is emphasised, liaison officers are deployed to problem areas and a reserve of 1500 border guards is created, which all member states will make available for rapid deployment. the proposal lays the foundations for the necessary enhanced protection of the eu's external borders. i consider it essential that this institution should operate in a transparent manner and that, in order to control and take the necessary measures in a timely manner, it should regularly draw up reports on its activities, which will be submitted to the ep.
in writing. the proposal to establish a european border and coast guard addresses the need to ensure proper control of the schengen external border as a basic prerequisite for effective migration management, to ensure a high level of security in the schengen area, while ensuring the free movement of persons within the union. innovative elements of the proposal include the introduction of a vulnerability assessment as a preventive mechanism to prevent ineffective checks at the external border, the deployment of liaison officers to member states, the handling of border situations requiring urgent action and the creation of a reserve of 1500 border guards to be made available by member states without exception for rapid deployment. the proposal also envisages a much stronger role for the agency in the field of return, closer cooperation with third countries and the establishment of european cooperation in the exercise of coast guard functions. in an area of free movement without internal borders, the management of the union's external borders must be a common responsibility of all member states. in view of the above, i agree with the proposal.
in writing. ‒ i support the call for greater efforts to address the migration crisis in a comprehensive manner, including strengthening border management to better manage the growing mixed migration flows. european integrated border management is essential to improve the management of migration and to ensure a high level of internal security within the union. while member states retain the primary responsibility for the management of the relevant section of their external borders, the role of the european border and coast guard agency should be to ensure the application of union measures relating to the management of the external borders by reinforcing, assessing and coordinating the actions of the member states in the implementation of those measures. in cases where a specific and disproportionate pressure is exerted on the external borders, the european border and coast guard agency should organise and coordinate rapid border interventions from the rapid reaction pool and provide technical equipment, at the request of a member state or on its own initiative. the rapid reaction pool shall consist of a standing corps of at least 1500 members immediately available to the agency and which may be deployed from each member state within three working days. a separate budget should be allocated to the agency, the revenue of which should be derived mainly from a contribution from the union, in order to guarantee the independence of the agency.
in writing. ‒ i was proud to support the approved resolution on a european border & coast guard, to develop the role frontex had been playing. the security of our external borders is vital, especially at this time of great migration flows. this resolution not only mandates the sharing of resources among those patrolling our coastlines and external borders, but also crucially provides for return capacities for those illegally entering the eu, something my group have campaigned hard for.
in writing. ‒ i would like to take this opportunity to thank the rapporteur for the report on the european and border and coast guard. although i myself have considered the freedom of movement at internal borders to be one of the greatest and most significant achievements of european integration, i must admit with concern that the instruments and mechanisms that allow the free movement of persons within the schengen area are proving inadequate in the wake of the current migration crisis. the movements of irregular migrants, which are considered a serious threat to internal security and public order, force us to address this unwanted phenomenon also by setting up a european border and coast guard. i am firmly convinced of the need to monitor the external borders more effectively and to address the challenges of migration and, where appropriate, future threats at the external borders. i expect the european border and coast guard to increase the level of internal security in the union and to guarantee the functioning of the schengen external border and at the same time the free movement of persons within the union. i am aware that the present regulation is not a panacea to eliminate the shortcomings identified, but i also believe that this proposal will help to prevent crisis situations at the external borders.
in writing. ‒ the migration crisis has shown the importance of common border protection. the european border and coast guard is a practical expression of the desire for close cooperation between all member states. however, they must have sufficient competence and capacity to act. its formation and deployment will depend in particular on the willingness of the member states to cooperate, since it is a partial interference with their sovereignty. the establishment of a joint unit does not in any way remove the obligation of the member states to protect the external borders.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal as it will lead to better protection of the eu's external borders. the need to urgently address border security was highlighted by the 2015 migration crisis and the threat of terrorist attacks. we have approved the proposal to set up an eu border and coast guard by a large majority. on the one hand, the new legislation leaves the day-to-day management of the external borders in the hands of the member states, as this is a very sensitive issue of state sovereignty. however, in the event of increased external pressure, it will allow them to request the assistance of the european border and coast guard agency (ebsa), which will rapidly deploy its teams to the vulnerable parts of the border. the european union agency for asylum should also play an important role in the return of migrants to their countries of origin. however, the return operation itself may only take place in accordance with a decision of the national authority. the extended powers of the agency in this area have also been strengthened by additional guarantees of respect for fundamental rights. the esdc will not participate in returns between third (non-member) countries. the european border and coast guard regulation will ensure that the eu's external border is safer and better protected. it is not a panacea for the migration crisis or for all the problems associated with the functioning of internal schengen rules, but it is a much-needed first step.
in writing. ‒ the main role of the european maritime and security agency, in cooperation with the european border and coast guard, is to support national authorities in their efforts to perform their functions at national level, but also to share capacities, including the planning and implementation of multi-purpose operations and the sharing of assets and other capabilities across sectors and borders. in the future, the european commission is expected to adopt a practical handbook on european cooperation in the field of coast guard functions in the form of a recommendation, which will contain guidelines, recommendations and best practices for the exchange of information and cooperation at national, union and international level.

in writing. the aim of this proposal is to support national authorities in their coast guard functions at national and european level by enabling cooperation between the three european agencies, the european fisheries control agency, the european maritime safety agency and the european border and coast guard agency. they will thus be able to share their operational capacities and exchange information generated by the synthesis and analysis of data available in ship reporting systems and other information systems operated by or accessible to the agencies, in accordance with their respective legal bases and without prejudice to the ownership of data by member states. the agency shall also support national authorities by providing surveillance and communication services based on advanced technologies, including space and ground infrastructures and sensors located on any type of platform, and by sharing capacities, including the planning and execution of multi-purpose operations and the sharing of assets and other capabilities across sectors and borders.

in writing. ‒ there is a need to improve cooperation and coordination between european coastguards. at the same time, the security of the eu's external borders needs to be increased and measures and management improved in order to effectively address the migration crisis. this will be further supported by new tasks for the european maritime safety agency, such as: exchanging information and data available in the ship reporting system; providing surveillance and communication services; building capacity by developing guidelines, recommendations and best practices, as well as providing training and exchanges of personnel; enhancing the exchange of information and cooperation in relation to coast guard functions; sharing capacities through the planning and execution of multi-purpose operations and sharing assets and other capabilities. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ in the eu, we have 1 200 commercial ports, 100 000 km of coastline, 90% of external trade by sea, 40% of internal trade and 400 million passengers. i regard the compromise reached in the field of maritime safety as a chronicle of success. the key tasks are to increase security by monitoring vessels' movements, providing assistance where needed, adhering to an environmental strategy, reducing bureaucracy in ports and fighting piracy.
in writing. ‒ the european fisheries control agency contributes to the control of fisheries operations but cannot currently act in other maritime areas. the aim of this proposal is to strengthen the capacity to respond to maritime threats and risks within the european union, in particular by improving cooperation between european agencies, but also between all civil and military actors. at european union level, there are currently 316 national authorities performing functions in a variety of areas including protection, security, rescue at sea, border control, customs control, environmental protection and law enforcement in general. they work together through 70 different structures. the current cooperation system is therefore slow and lacking, in particular due to the lack of information on the competences, powers and capacities of other bodies.
in writing. ‒ the in 2005, a regulation of the ep and the council established the community fisheries control agency. the proposed regulation, which is part of a package of measures to protect the eu's external borders, aims to strengthen cooperation and coordination between all institutions, bodies and organisations performing the coast guard function more efficiently and effectively. the coast guard function is currently carried out by more than 300 entities, whose coordination at national level is complex. the unification of rules and informed cooperation will help to make the work of the coastal border protection units more efficient, which is why i supported the proposal.
in writing. the aim of this proposal is to enable the three european agencies to coordinate their operations at sea and to exchange information useful in carrying out their activities. national authorities performing coast guard functions are responsible for a large number of tasks in a variety of areas, including protection, security, rescue at sea, border control, customs control and law enforcement in general. at european union level, there are currently around 300 such national authorities, which work together through 70 different structures. the current cooperation system is therefore slow and fragile, in particular due to the lack of information on the competences, powers and capacities of other bodies, the limited number of operational assets, the lack of interoperability of systems and assets and the constraints related to planning and joint operations. i am convinced that the proposal will enable the agencies to act jointly and effectively to ensure in particular control, safety and surveillance operations by providing them with information, equipment and training, as well as by ensuring the necessary coordination of multidimensional operations. such cooperation is necessary in view of the current migration situation. in view of the above, i agree with the proposal.

in writing. ‒ while there are currently 316 national authorities that perform the function of coast guard and are responsible for protection, safety, rescue operations at sea, border control, customs control, environmental protection and law enforcement in general, the crisis has revealed clear weaknesses and shortcomings in the current mechanisms that need to be addressed. unfortunately, cooperation between national authorities in the 70 different structures is generally slow and inflexible. i therefore believe that the time has come to move to a much more efficient system of cooperation between european agencies with enhanced powers, which will also address, among other things, crisis situations at sea. i supported the ep's draft legislative resolution because i believe that it will lead to better coordination of surveillance, prevention and maritime surveillance operations at european level, in order to improve maritime situational awareness and promote coordinated and cost-effective measures. i believe that the european fisheries control agency, by strengthening its mandate, will contribute to strengthening the capacity to respond to maritime threats and risks within the eu, in particular by improving cooperation between european agencies, but also between all civil and military actors.

in writing. ‒ this report assesses all budgetary aspects of the current multiannual financial framework for the years 2014 to 2020. the budgetary appropriations made available for the years 2014 to 2020 are much lower than for the period 2007 to 2013. despite this reduction, the european union has had to deal in recent years with the migration crisis and a high number of unemployed people, with significant consequences in particular in the area of competitiveness for growth and employment. the available resources will not be sufficient to address the needs that have arisen, even if we continue to make full use of all the flexibility mechanisms that exist under the current multiannual financial framework. we must work together to prevent a new payment crisis, which is forecast to emerge at the end of the current multiannual financial framework.

in writing. ‒ the international whaling commission banned commercial whaling of all large whales in 1982, and this ban came into effect in 1986. despite this international ban, japan continues to hunt whales on various unfounded pretexts. despite the eu court of justice ruling banning whaling, japan resumed whaling in 2015 as part of its research plan. parliament supports the maintenance of a global moratorium on commercial whaling and the prohibition of international trade in whale products, calls for an end to so-called scientific whaling and supports the designation of sufficiently large ocean and sea areas as protected areas where whaling would be permanently prohibited. it is therefore very important that the european union calls on japan to stop whaling immediately.
in writing. ‒ in 2014, the international court of justice issued a ruling ordering japan to stop its whaling on the basis of a special permit because it did not serve the original scientific purpose. i supported the ep's call for japan to immediately stop whaling and to respect international treaties and conventions in this area in order to conserve biodiversity and end unnecessary suffering.
in writing. ‒ in november 2015, the japanese fisheries agency informed the international whaling commission that it was resuming whaling under a revised plan. i welcomed the fact that the motion for a resolution urged japan to end its whaling immediately. japan is seriously threatening biodiversity by allowing whaling. i would like to see marine mammals in the future more protected and respected.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the introduction of a moratorium on commercial whaling in 1982 and its observance. i am strongly against the hunting of all whales (whale, dolphin and porpoise), except by indigenous people for a clearly defined subsistence need. whaling involves unacceptable abuse. only well-managed, responsible tourism is the only truly sustainable use of these animals. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ the in 1982, the international whaling commission introduced a moratorium, which came into effect in 1986, on zero quotas for all commercial whaling, which is still in place to protect whale populations from extinction and allow them to recover. since then, japan has been able to fish under a special permit in limited quantities, exclusively for scientific purposes. in fact, since the moratorium was put in place, the number of whales killed has increased, and japan has been doing this for decades. i was personally concerned when in november 2015 the japanese fisheries agency announced that it would resume whaling for the 2015-2016 season under a new scientific programme, which again appears to be an even bigger front against the moratorium. i therefore join japan's criticism that it has resumed fishing activities and does not sufficiently take into account the guidance provided in the 2014 iuu advice, and express my deep concern that the decision to resume whaling under the new programme allows the killing of 333 small cetaceans in the antarctic ocean in the 2015-2016 season and a total of almost 4 000 000 whales over a 12-year period. i therefore join the authors of the resolution in calling on the eu and its member states to make every effort to resolve this issue through political dialogue.
in writing. ‒ japan needs to be reminded of its commitments to the protection of marine mammals. the japanese fisheries agency notified the international commission of the resumption of whaling, demonstrating that it ignores the ruling of the international court of justice, which in its judgment of march 2014 ordered japan to end the annual killing of whales in the southern ocean, as it concluded that japan is not hunting whales for research purposes, as japan had claimed.
in writing. ‒ the ep rejected by resolution a commission delegated act to ease restrictions on belarus and to provide it with eu guarantees on loans from the european investment bank. given that belarus remains a centralised autocratic state that does not respect human rights and freedoms, continues to legislate for and implement the death penalty, and fails to meet economic, social and environmental requirements, i supported the proposal to reject the commission's delegated decision.
in writing. ‒ i did not wish to vote in favour of the proposal because the principles on which the european union is founded are not being respected in the country in question. human rights are seriously violated, and the death penalty is still an institution. it is true that some positive progress has been made in recent years, but i think that a stronger presence of democratic principles is needed. for democracy to work, an independent opposition would be needed, which has not been in the country for years.
in writing. ‒ i abstained in the vote on the objection to the council decision granting a guarantee to the european investment bank for losses resulting from financing operations in support of projects, in particular in belarus. i'm afraid that perhaps today is not the right time to pass such a resolution. the former political prisoners' civil and political rights have unfortunately not been restored, nor have any formal institutional measures been taken to ensure freedom of association and assembly. the country has also not yet taken any measures to abolish the death penalty. on the other hand, the upcoming parliamentary elections to be held in early september 2016 represent an opportunity for belarus to end its previous practice of rigged elections. i therefore hope that these elections will be the decisive criterion for assessing the real will of the belarusian authorities to reconcile with their own citizens and to establish constructive relations with the eu.
in writing. ‒ belarus remains a centralised autocratic state controlled by president lukashenko. the problem of counting and manipulating votes remains a sticking point in the upcoming elections in september 2016. despite the progress made through participation in the eastern partnership, belarus remains the only country in europe where the death penalty is still applied. however, i believe that belarus will take the path of respect for human rights, fundamental freedoms and democracy.
in writing. ‒ i did not support the objection to the commission delegated act setting out minimum requirements for own resources and eligible liabilities. i consider that the arguments raised against that delegated act were not well founded. the commission's objective is to amend the directive establishing a framework for the recovery and resolution of credit institutions and investment firms. although the european banking authority issued an opinion earlier this year expressing disagreement with some of the proposed changes, these reservations are essentially technical in nature. nevertheless, i believe that any shortcomings that may be found in the commission's proposal will be taken into account and will be worked through accordingly.
in writing. ‒ systemically important institutions should meet the minimum requirement for own funds and eligible liabilities in order to avoid over-reliance on forms of financing that are excluded from rescue. the ability of institutions to absorb losses and recapitalise may ultimately have a positive impact on resolution and thus lead to the safeguarding of financial stability.

in writing. ‒ in december 2010, the eu became the first regional integration organisation to accede to the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities (crpd). the crpd deals with a wide range of rights covering all areas of life, including those that fall outside the eu's remit. member states are therefore obliged to implement the convention in the same way at all levels, including regional and national levels. the report adopted today, which i voted in favour of, is intended primarily to address the issues raised in the concluding observations. it considers as a priority those recommendations which fall within the eu's competence and whose implementation may therefore present problems at national level. in the field of human rights, there is no hierarchy and discrimination on the basis of disability must be treated in the same way as discrimination on other grounds. this is particularly important for women and children with disabilities, the elderly and people who require complex support, including those with intellectual and psychosocial disabilities. the crpd differs from other human rights treaties in that persons with disabilities and the organisations that represent them have been involved in its development from the drafting stage.
in writing. ‒ the european union acceded to the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities in december 2010 as the first regional integration organisation. it was the first international human rights treaty to be ratified by the european union as a whole and the only one to date. i am of the opinion that there is no hierarchy of human rights and that discrimination on the grounds of disability should be treated in the same way as discrimination on other grounds, including discrimination on more than one ground. this is particularly important for women and children with disabilities, older people and individuals who need comprehensive support, including those with mental retardation and psychosocial disorders.
in writing. the convention on the rights of persons with disabilities is part of the eu legal order. it shall be binding on the eu and all its member states. however, its consistent implementation and enforcement requires more active action by the eu institutions. all member states must strictly implement the obligations of the convention and adopt strategies that create, to the extent possible, appropriate and appropriate conditions and an environment for the active participation of persons with disabilities in all spheres of working, socioeconomic, social and political life. to this end, the commission and the member states should make the most of communication with the organisations concerned representing persons with disabilities and ensure, in close cooperation, the regular preparation and submission of reports on the fulfilment of the obligations of the convention.
in writing. the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities was the first international treaty to be ratified by the european union as a whole and is therefore subject to the scrutiny of the committee on the rights of persons with disabilities. the convention covers a wide range of rights and covers all areas of life, some of which fall outside the union's competence. member states are therefore required to implement the convention equally at all levels, including regional and national. the committee assessed the union under the expedited procedure and concluded in its recommendations that the declaration needs to be regularly updated. particular attention should be paid to the union institutions themselves, which are to be the model for the implementation of the convention. i believe that there is no hierarchy of human rights and that discrimination on the grounds of disability should be treated in the same way as discrimination on other grounds, including discrimination on more than one ground. this is particularly important for women and children with disabilities, older people and individuals who need comprehensive support, including those with mental retardation and psychosocial disorders. in the light of the above, i agree with the proposal submitted.
in writing. ‒ in the european union, an estimated 80 million people live with a disability and deserve equal rights and equal treatment. discrimination on the grounds of disability shall be treated as a matter of priority. this is particularly important for women and children with disabilities, the elderly and people who require complex support, including those with intellectual and psychosocial disabilities. i wanted to contribute to this by voting in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ people with disabilities must have full access to all rights in all situations. it is one of the hallmarks of a society that respects the dignity of every human being. but sexual and reproductive rights in many lands include the so-called right to abortion, thus undermining the human dignity of the unborn child. this is a matter of principle for me, and i cannot in good conscience vote for any bill that would consider the act of killing an unborn human fetus to be a right belonging to another human being. therefore, i could not support the motion in the final vote and abstained.
in writing. ‒ the european commission was to set out by january 2009 the specific nutritional profiles that certain types of food must meet in order to be labelled as nutritious or beneficial to health. however, the european commission has not yet established these nutritional profiles. the voluntary code of practice for the sale and labelling of energy drinks, which is intended for the energy drinks sector, only provides for an undertaking not to sell energy drinks to children under 12 years of age.
in writing. the commission has failed to fulfil its obligation under regulation (ec) no 1924/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 20 december 2006 on nutrition and health claims made on foods. the regulation required it to establish the specific nutritional profiles of certain foods and their labelling so that they could be labelled as nutritious or beneficial to health. these are mainly energy drinks containing excessive amounts of substances (caffeine, sugar) that are not beneficial for children and young people who drink these drinks frequently. the ep therefore rightly objected to the commission regulation amending regulation (eu) no 432/2012 on the list of permitted health claims made on foods other than those referring to the reduction of disease risk and to children's development and health. the commission should fulfil its obligation to establish nutritional profiles and consider restricting the sale of energy drinks to children and young people.
in writing. the european commission has not yet established specific nutritional profiles to which a food or certain categories of food must conform in order to be labelled as nutritious or beneficial to health and the conditions for the use of such labels on foods or categories of food with regard to those nutritional profiles. adolescents represent the largest group of energy drink consumers. i am convinced that the use of nutrition and health claims should not encourage or justify excessive consumption of food. energy drinks have been linked to headaches, sleep problems and behavioural problems in children and adolescents who regularly consume them. each product must contain the exact labelling of the ingredients it contains. consumers must not be misled and care must be taken to maintain their confidence in the products. i fully support the motion.
in writing. ‒ since 2016, the eu has had uniform rules for the use of health claims on food. all claims must be scientifically proven and the results verified by the european food safety authority. i personally think that there is a need to promote public health instruments which distinguish between genuinely necessary interests, because member states already regulate and protect the weaker categories of people.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution by which parliament vetoed the commission's proposal to include health claims on the packaging of energy drinks. as a doctor, i know the negative health effects of high sugar consumption, especially on young people. energy drinks, in particular, contain a high amount of sugar and are often consumed by adolescents, even children. i consider it wrong to promote the sale of these drinks by claiming their positive effects.

in writing the emissions scandal exposed several global car manufacturers for their deliberate misrepresentation of passenger and commercial vehicle emissions data. it also caused a decline in consumer confidence. the european parliament has therefore set up a committee of inquiry to try to recover it. it deals with the measurement of emissions in the automotive industry and with compliance with applicable regulations, whether by the european commission or by the competent authorities within the member states. the committee of inquiry is currently collecting and analysing information on the use of jamming mechanisms in the measurement of emissions by individual cars. this should continue into the autumn of this year. the follow-up report and the recommendations resulting from it will be of particular importance. compliance with them should help to avoid similar situations on such a large scale in the future. the functioning of the automotive industry is a significant factor in economic growth and employment. the issue case showed the importance of greening the entire industry. it is also necessary to focus on reducing the use of heavy metals and other harmful substances in individual components and components in cars. member states committed themselves to this in 2003. nevertheless, there are still many exceptions. however, modern materials and advances have made many of them unnecessary. this concerns, for example, the use of lead in car batteries. there are already proven technologies that can fully replace conventional lead-acid batteries.

in writing. european territorial cooperation has been an objective of cohesion policy since the 2007-2013 programming period, but it has not received sufficient attention. however, several paragraphs suggest that cohesion funds, territorial development instruments, should also be used to support the social integration of migrants, to address the challenges posed by the refugee crisis, and to support measures in the area of migration and asylum. this proposal ignores the original objective of cohesion policy as set out in article 174 tfeu, which is to reduce disparities between the levels of development of the different regions and the backwardness of the least favoured regions and to strengthen economic, social and territorial cohesion. i cannot agree that cohesion funds, which are so important for european regions, should be used for migration-related purposes.

in writing european territorial cooperation (interreg) is a key instrument for achieving territorial cohesion through a variety of programmes and projects with european added value and impact on 60 european border regions. european territorial cooperation is currently used by 28 member states and is one of the two objectives of cohesion policy. in the 2014-2020 programming period, cross-border, transnational and interregional cooperation shall be supported under interreg by the european regional development fund. despite their small budget, crossborder cooperation projects are delivering positive results, whether in removing obstacles to better security, transport, education, energy, healthcare, training or employment. for the better functioning of the ets in the future, it will be important to focus on more efficient use of funds, the establishment of appropriate coordination mechanisms, the reduction of red tape in the management and implementation of european territorial cooperation, as well as greater involvement of the private financial sector in ets projects.
in writing. ‒ i fully support the report on european territorial cooperation. the programme, which began some 26 years ago with a modest budget, is now one of the main objectives of the european union's cohesion policy. programmes supported by european territorial cooperation contribute to improving the state of the environment and to increasing research and innovation in ways that are directly felt by the inhabitants of the territories concerned. slovakia has also benefited from european cooperation programmes in a number of areas. as an example, i would like to mention the project that led to the construction of a bridge over the morva river, linking slovakia and austria, providing easy access for cyclists and pedestrians. the project has also produced long-term results: the boom in tourism has created a need for rest areas and restaurants, which has led to the start-up of businesses and thus the creation of new jobs. our country is once again involved in many projects, and our main partners in the coming period will be austria, the czech republic, hungary, romania and ukraine.
‒ i see european territorial cooperation (etc) as a cornerstone of european integration, playing a particularly important role in the creation of a common european area. i am pleased that the esf has been effective for some time, but i am also sorry that, due to a lack of resources, its potential has not yet been fully developed in some areas (single market, mobility, employment, research, education, etc.). i voted in favour of the resolution because it does not only talk about achievements, but also presents proposals and innovative measures that can contribute to achieving a balanced integration of the different eu territories. although more flexibility has been introduced in recent years into european territorial cooperation and the administrative burden on the bodies responsible for the programmes has been reduced in the implementation of cooperation programmes, there are still significant differences between rural and urban areas. i therefore expect that the linkage and coherence of the esf programmes with national and regional programmes will be strengthened more significantly. i also expect that more attention will be paid to geographically and demographically disadvantaged areas in the implementation of cohesion policy.
in writing ‒ border regions are natural natural, economic and sociological entities that have often been divided by political decisions in the past. many of them represent the poorest regions within their own country and in europe. the european union is trying to promote their natural cooperation, both financially and through the sharing of know-how and information.
‒ european territorial cooperation, as one of the two objectives of cohesion policy, provides a framework for the implementation of joint actions and policy exchange between national, regional and local actors from different member states, playing an important role at all these levels and currently benefiting all 28 member states. cross-border cooperation is generally a key tool in the development of border regions. interregional cooperation also allows cities and regions to work together on many issues. that is why i believe that european territorial cooperation offers a significant european added value and contributes to stability and integration. this cooperation is particularly important in isolated regions or sparsely populated and rural areas, as ms mihaylov's report correctly identified and encouraged, and called for, the full potential of this territorial cooperation to be exploited. for all these reasons, and for the sake of the balance of the report, i have decided to give her my vote.
in writing ‒ the emissions scandal exposed several global car manufacturers for their deliberate misrepresentation of passenger and commercial vehicle emissions data. it also caused a decline in consumer confidence. the european parliament has therefore set up a committee of inquiry to try to recover it. it deals with the measurement of emissions in the automotive industry and with compliance with applicable regulations, whether by the european commission or by the competent authorities within the member states. the committee of inquiry is currently collecting and analysing information on the use of jamming mechanisms in the measurement of emissions by individual cars. this should continue into the autumn of this year. the follow-up report and the recommendations resulting from it will be of particular importance. compliance with them should help to avoid similar situations on such a large scale in the future. the functioning of the automotive industry is a significant factor in economic growth and employment. the issue case showed the importance of greening the entire industry. it is also necessary to focus on reducing the use of heavy metals and other harmful substances in individual components and components in cars. member states committed themselves to this in 2003. nevertheless, there are still many exceptions. however, modern materials and advances have made many of them unnecessary. this concerns, for example, the use of lead in car batteries. there are already proven technologies that can fully replace conventional lead-acid batteries.
in writing ‒ in december 2015, the european parliament set up a temporary committee of inquiry in accordance with article 226 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. its task is to investigate shortcomings in the application of union legislation on emission measurement in the automotive industry. the committee shall draw up an inquiry report and make any recommendations it deems necessary in this matter. since the results of the investigation can be the basis for the added value of the union type-approval framework, the fulfilment of the mandate of the temporary committee requires more time for the investigation. it is therefore necessary for the commission and the member states to cooperate with the european parliament and to give the committee maximum synergy.

in writing ‒ on many occasions, requests for waiver of the immunity of members of the european parliament have been submitted to the european parliament's plenary on the basis of various facts. my view of these reports is that, as regards a request for waiver of immunity for an act committed while the member concerned was already a member of the european parliament and at the same time the act in question was committed in the course of his mandate (for example, in relation to his statements in plenary), he should not be deprived of his parliamentary immunity. however, as regards events which are not related to the performance of the member's mandate or which occurred before the member's term of office began, i see no reason to vote against such a request. i think the rules are sufficiently clear in the case of waiver of the immunity of members, and that is why i voted for waiver of immunity in this case as well, since at the time of the incident the member was not yet a member of the european parliament.

in writing. the customs union of the european union was enlarged by the accession of the republic of croatia. consequently, under the rules of the world trade organisation (wto), the eu is obliged to open negotiations with wto members with which croatia has hitherto had a so-called preferential tariff list. this becomes necessary if the tariff level resulting from accession to the union tariff system is increased for this reason beyond the level agreed by the acceding country in the wto. the council authorised the commission to open negotiations on 15 july 2013. following those negotiations, the commission proposed to the council that the agreement be signed on behalf of the union. i voted in favour of parliament's agreement to the draft council decision.
in writing ‒ in this particular case, the agreement is purely technical. its main objective is to conclude an agreement between the european union and china, taking into account the accession of croatia to the european union, in line with the requirements of the world trade organisation. the european commission has negotiated with china the issue of the withdrawal of special concessions in connection with the termination of the accession plan of croatia to the european union.
‒ the european parliament has given its consent to the conclusion of an agreement reducing the contractual common customs tariff duties on selected industrial products and adjusting the quotas for selected agricultural products from china in the context of the accession of croatia to the union. the proposal is in line with wto rules and the interests of the parties in balanced trade between themselves.
in writing. ‒ i accepted the recommendation because we voted to take a step which is a natural consequence of croatia's accession to the european union. with the new member state, the eu's customs union has also expanded, which has an impact on the other wto members, including china. i think we've managed to set up a win-win situation on this subject.
in writing i voted in favour of granting the agreement. with the accession of the republic of croatia, the european union has enlarged its customs union. the people's republic of china has a right under the gatt to re-establish its original trading rights. their partial breach was a consequence of the enlargement of the eu customs union following the accession of croatia . this compensation agreement can therefore be seen as another sign that the eu is part of the multilateral rules-based trading system at the heart of which is the wto. the commission has chosen to increase the tariff quotas and also to reduce the current binding tariff rates as compensation tools for the losses of the chinese products concerned.
in writing ‒ taking into account the opinion of the committee on international trade, i have decided to support the conclusion of an eu-china agreement amending the tariff and quota concessions in connection with the accession of croatia to the union. i agree that the people's republic of china has the right to restore its original trade rights, which were only slightly impaired as a result of the eu customs union enlargement with the accession of croatia. the eu is thereby implementing the articles of the gatt agreement which set out the rules for the functioning of free trade. this applies the principles of the multilateral trading system, with the wto at its centre. this agreement on the accession of croatia is, moreover, part of the common practice that the eu has followed in previous enlargements. it concerns several tariff lines for which import quotas are applied. for certain industrial and agricultural products imported into the eu by china, either the customs duty rate is reduced or the import quota is increased. the adjustment of those rules resulting from the accession of croatia thus favours china and should therefore be positively received in the mutual trade relations.
in writing ‒ the essence of the common market, which is the basis of european economic cooperation, is the principle that agreed rules apply also to states which have acceded to the european union only after the relevant directive, regulation or international agreement has been adopted. china is an important partner for the european union and extending cooperation to new member states strengthens our position.
in writing ‒ since the enlargement of the customs union took place in 2013 at the same time as the accession of croatia to the european union, it is necessary to open negotiations on compensatory adjustments under the rules of the world trade organisation. such negotiations should be initiated when the originally agreed tariffs are changed as a result of the enlargement of the customs union. and since there has been such a change in the case of china, specifically for shoes, air conditioners, mushrooms and garlic, i supported the agreement.

in writing ‒ following the accession of croatia, the eu customs union was enlarged and it was therefore necessary to settle trade relations with the eastern republic of uruguay with regard to the customs concessions schedule. under wto rules, in view of the 1994 gatt agreement, the eu was required to adjust its tariff quotas or to agree to a compensatory arrangement with uruguay. the agreement with uruguay was finally negotiated in late 2015 in nairobi. it provides for the eu to include in its customs territory charter changes concerning tariff quotas, in particular for beef. to this end, the commission is also preparing an implementing regulation for several other tariff quotas. as it is a level playing field between uruguay and the eu within the wto rules, i supported the conclusion of this agreement. we will thereby contribute to maintaining trust between countries that respect the principles of international trade relations.

in writing ‒ based on the revised 2007 methodology, the collection of data on natural gas and electricity prices charged to final customers was carried out on a voluntary basis. this regulation aims to make the collection of data from voluntary to mandatory in order not to impair the quality of statistical price surveys in the household sector and to ensure that these data continue to be of high quality. the national regulatory authority or the government should propose a cost allocation methodology. the notification of price information will become mandatory for large non-household customers.
in writing ‒ the aim of this proposal is to make the current voluntary collection of gas and electricity price data compulsory in order to improve the quality of statistical surveys while preserving the protection of sensitive consumer and supplier data. data collection will continue to be carried out by the national authorities. i therefore support the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on european gas and electricity price statistics and repealing directive 2008/92/ec of the european parliament and of the council on a community procedure to improve the transparency of gas and electricity prices charged to industrial end-users.
in writing the european commission has been collecting data on gas and electricity prices for a long time through eurostat, but the principle of voluntariness has been applied to final customers households. this regulation aims to convert voluntary collection into compulsory collection. this would allow better collection of price data for the largest possible market share and in high quality. the collection of price data should not be a burden for the authorities active in this process, but should clarify objectives, simplify certain provisions concerning reporting authorities and avoid misunderstandings that could have a negative effect on the comparison of data. the report also points to the need to change the breakdown of charges and thus the current situation which allows for the shifting of charges from the grid to energy and vice versa. emphasis is also placed on the responsibility of national regulatory authorities or governments to propose a cost breakdown methodology and provide the required information for its implementation after consultation with stakeholders and verification by eurostat, thus allowing for cross-country comparability. the document also emphasises the need to increase the protection of sensitive consumer and supplier information. current statistics are based on invoice searches from supplier databases. however, invoiced prices should not be published if a certain consumption band does not have a minimum number of customers. i therefore support the proposal.
in writing. ‒ i have adopted the report on european statistics on natural gas and electricity prices. the only way to compare data from different member states effectively is to establish common criteria before starting to collect data. in order for the european union to produce statistics based on real data, we must first define precisely the conditions under which this is done.
‒ natural gas and electricity prices can be significantly reduced by applying innovative technologies, reconstructing and connecting existing networks and finding new, efficient and environmentally friendly sources.
in writing ‒ i supported the proposal for a regulation requiring member states to collect and transmit statistics on electricity and gas prices for households and industry. in addition to the obligation to collect data on energy prices, network charges or taxes, member states will also be required to report these data to the european commission (or eurostat) on a regular basis. this data will then be used to better monitor the internal market and to tailor specialised policies. at the same time, as member states have been obliged to collect data, with the exception of household data, which will also be mandatory under the new regulation, this additional obligation should not impose any significant burden.
in writing. recent developments such as new technologies, fluctuating commodity prices and the rapid expansion of renewable electricity generation have fundamentally changed the european energy market. the report aims to achieve three objectives. firstly, a union-wide electricity market should be established, providing clear price signals for new investments. secondly, we need to create a european infrastructure for secure energy supply. third, regional cooperation in energy policy should be strengthened, in particular with regard to the development of new energy generation equipment, interconnectors and support schemes, and the integration of renewable energy sources into the european internal market. achieving these objectives is in europe's common interest, as the integration of electricity markets will improve the secure, cost-effective and environmentally sound supply of energy. the general structure of the national energy mix of the member states should be respected in the development of the new strategy.
in writing ‒ the subject of this report is the european energy market and, in particular, the presentation of the structure of how this system should look, taking into account the ability to achieve energy policy objectives. the challenges we face in the energy sector include in particular increased dependence on oil and gas imports, but also a lack of diversification. in addition, energy prices are also driven up by government taxes and global energy demand. security risks are also a concern, whether in countries where mining directly occurs or in transit countries. the european commission's communication is based on three major policy objectives for the future of the electricity market.
‒ the commission's proposal for an internal energy market sets three policy objectives: 1.to create a pan-european electricity market with clear price signals for new investment; 2.to establish a european approach to security of energy supply; 3.to strengthen regional cooperation in energy policy, in particular in relation to investments in power plants and the integration of renewable energy sources into the single european market. the consistent implementation of these objectives in all policies affecting the internal energy market will ensure self-sufficiency, sustainability and an abundance of affordable and secure energy for the union and its people, taking into account environmental protection and employment in the sector.
europe faces several major energy challenges, including increased dependence on oil and gas imports, lack of diversification, high energy prices, rising global energy demand, security risks in producer and transit countries, the fight against adverse climate change, slow progress in energy efficiency, increasing the share of renewable energy, the integration and interconnection of energy markets and market distortions caused by different subsidy schemes. better integration and coordination of energy markets brings with it many opportunities to achieve the common european objectives of a secure, affordable and green energy supply. however, energy markets, in particular electricity markets, are still today strongly characterised by national responsibility for the energy mix. measures to promote national energy mix are very diverse and include, for example, significant subsidies to promote renewable energy sources and the establishment of capacity mechanisms to ensure security of supply in some member states. the proposal aims to strengthen the internal market in electricity with clear price signals for new investment, to ensure security of energy supply and to strengthen regional cooperation in the field of energy policy, in particular in relation to investments in power plants, interconnections, support schemes, as well as the integration of renewable energy sources into the european single market, to which individual markets need to be adapted appropriately. i agree with the motion and i vote in favour.

in writing. the eu strategy for the region covers 48 regions in seven countries, five of which are eu member states, and two others in switzerland and lichtenstein. macro-regional strategies allow these countries to create strategic investments for the benefit of the whole region, taking into account the principle of the three genders (no new eu fund, no new formal eu structure, no further eu legislation). the strategy is based on three pillars of development. the first pillar aims to increase the competitiveness and cohesion of the alpine region, including the promotion of sustainable and competitive tourism. the second pillar aims to improve accessibility, providing adequate transport and energy infrastructure. the third pillar is based on the keywords of sustainability, environmental protection, biodiversity and the protection of ecosystems. the alpine macro-region, which is an example for other regions, has a significant potential which can be further exploited through cooperation. i voted in favour of the report.

in writing ‒ the reconciliation of work, private and family life is finally recognised as a fundamental right, although it remains an area where we need further progress to ensure a satisfactory work-life balance for all. to achieve this, it will be necessary to change the working environment and to integrate a lifelong approach to work-life balance policies so that everyone is supported and can participate actively in the labour market at different stages of their lives. society is undergoing demographic change, new ways of organising work are emerging, we have a continuing high unemployment rate and a growing diversity of family relationships and parenting patterns, which unfortunately continues to have a negative impact on women's employment rates. we therefore need the european commission to come forward as soon as possible with proposals for directives on maternity leave, on paternity leave, on the implementation of the parental leave directive and to propose a directive on carer's leave.
in writing ‒ the balance between work, private and family life affects the quality of life on the one hand and at the same time the efficiency and productivity of the work performed on the other. it affects the quality of life of the individual and of society as a whole. creating this balance requires all competent authorities to address existing problems at several levels, from discrimination in labour market applications, the organisation of working time, gender equality in pay, childcare, access to quality education from pre-school to lifelong learning, and access to care and security for the elderly. i believe that demographic developments in the eu require the union not only to prepare for and deal with an ageing population, but also to give priority to creating economic, social and working conditions for starting families.
in writing the draft resolution underlines the need to improve work-life balance through legislative and non-legislative initiatives and is the starting point for the document prepared by the european commission, roadmap: a new start to address the challenges of work-life balance faced by working families. i did not vote in favour of the proposal for a number of reasons: family policy is the exclusive competence of each member state. this includes the question of revising maternity leave, improving parental leave, creating a new paternity leave and the definition of the family. the proposal therefore infringes the principle of subsidiarity, which ensures that decisions are taken as closely as possible to the citizen. the union shall therefore act only if the objectives of the proposed action cannot be sufficiently achieved by the member states and can, by reason of the scale or effects of the proposed action, be better achieved at community level. the proposal defines parenting as one of the biggest barriers to employment. the eu treaty sees fathers and mothers as employees only, and therefore the union's intervention in family life and its efforts to guide values and norms within the family are, in my view, outside its scope.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i believe it is time for the eu to act to ensure that member states are properly aligned on work-life balance solutions. a favourable work-life balance in the labour market can only be achieved if people have sufficient time for personal development outside of work. it is important that we build a society in which women and men can be equal as seekers and carers.
in writing ‒ i agree that the reconciliation of the working and private lives of women and men should be facilitated to the maximum extent possible, especially with regard to their family responsibilities and commitments. and if we are to deal effectively with europe's catastrophic demographic situation, we must first of all support the natural family and its healthy functioning. however, the resolution adopted again seeks to intervene in areas which are the exclusive competence of the member states. in addition, the report proposed that housework and family care be shared equally between men and women. we see here again and again the attempt by the european institutions to interfere with the responsibilities, but also the rights, of spouses or partners living in a common household. it should be stressed that this is an absurd and unacceptable interference with the rights and privacy of legitimate and free citizens. the issue of work-life balance is about giving women and men free choice, not about integrating as many women as possible into the labour market and involving more men in domestic work. and that's what all the proposals and policies have to respect. that's why i voted against it.
in writing ‒ work-life balance is a very important factor, as an appropriate work-life balance contributes to economic growth, competitiveness, overall labour market participation, gender equality, poverty reduction and solidarity between generations. the eu must take action to promote upward convergence between member states in the area of work-life balance. if we are to achieve real equality between women and men, it is essential to combat the poverty of workers, children and women, to make better use of people's skills and talents and to tackle demographic challenges in the eu. conditions in the labour market that are favourable to work-life balance can only be created and quality of life achieved when people have sufficient time outside work for personal development, for example through education and training, and for leisure. it is therefore important that member states implement the working time directive rigorously, but also that they introduce measures to promote leisure and education and training.
in writing ‒ the new technologies and profound changes in the structure of the economy that we are currently witnessing will also bring about a redefinition of work processes. however, we should not intervene directly in the employee-employer relationship, but rather create space for free choice and adjustment of the form of work performance by mutual agreement.
in writing ‒ the draft resolution on creating conditions in the labour market which are favourable to work-life balance sought to find the best possible solutions to the increasingly pressing issue of reconciling work and private life. this area is receiving a lot of attention at european level, as is evident not only from legislative proposals but also from various initiatives or reports. this resolution also deals in particular with the demographic problems caused by low fertility and consequent ageing of the population. it identifies the need to address these issues and put in place concrete measures to eliminate gender stereotypes, increase women's employment and, in particular, provide opportunities to support a family. this is why it is concerned not only with the availability of childcare services and dependants, but also with motivating men to take up parental leave. in my view, the report contained many positive elements, such as calls for paternity leave and proper recognition of the work of informal carers. however, since it also interfered with the subsidiarity of countries in family policy, i abstained in the final vote.
