in writing. ‒ given its geographical and cultural proximity, and in particular its political and economic importance, the union of 28 member states is switzerland's most important partner. accordingly, the union has established closer relations with switzerland through a number of agreements than with any other country outside the european economic area (eea). following the rejection of switzerland's accession to the eea agreement in 1992 and the mutual recognition of the crucial role of cooperation, a series of bilateral agreements were concluded. these covered, inter alia, the free movement of persons, land and air transport, agriculture, research and technical barriers to trade and public procurement and entered into force on 1 june 2002. as switzerland has access to and benefits from the internal market and its enlargement in the same way as the member states of the union, it benefits politically, economically and culturally from a wider internal market in which free movement is a key element and the restriction of which by switzerland is unacceptable. i therefore voted in favour of the recommendation in accordance with the rapporteur's opinion.
in writing ‒ the first series of bilateral agreements between the eu and switzerland entered into force in june 2002. they are part of the agreement on the free movement of persons. a new phase called protocol iii was launched with the accession of croatia to the european union in 2013, which was initially blocked by switzerland as a direct consequence of the swiss referendum, which was aimed at mass immigration. the european union has reacted to these developments by suspending negotiations with switzerland on several other agreements. on 4 march 2016, switzerland and the european union definitively signed protocol iii on the extension of the agreement on the free movement of persons to croatia. protocol iii contains a seven-year transitional period during which switzerland may restrict access of croatian citizens to the labour market.
in writing ‒ by the approval of the protocol to the agreement on the free movement of persons concluded between the eu and switzerland, this agreement is extended to the citizens of the republic of croatia. the swiss authorities have also agreed to extend the period of validity of the residence permit for croatian nationals to the period of validity of the residence permit for croatian nationals. at the end of the transitional period, switzerland may extend this period by a safeguard clause, i.e. for a further 3 years. i support the draft protocol because it is in the interest of both countries and is in line with the agreements concluded between the eu and switzerland.
in writing. ‒ i support the draft resolution, first and foremost because it is important that we, as eu citizens, support and live the freedom of movement that the union offers. switzerland, like the eu member states, benefits from the internal market and its enlargement. the agreement will facilitate the provision of services and will enable switzerland and croatia to maintain control over the organised labour market.
in writing i voted in favour. the accession of croatia to the eu did not automatically extend to croatia the agreement on the free movement of persons signed in the framework of bilateral agreements between the eu and switzerland, which granted the right to citizens of the contracting parties to enter, live and work in the territories concerned by mutually removing most restrictions. it was necessary to activate protocol iii (template of the agreement) which provides that for a period of 7 years from the entry into force of this protocol, switzerland may restrict access of croatian citizens to the labour market (quotas, preference for local workers, control of working conditions and wages). during the last two years of this transitional period, these restrictions shall be agreed by the joint committee switzerland - eu.
in writing ‒ switzerland has a special relationship with the eu, which is based on a number of bilateral agreements. as the economic, political and cultural links have long proved to be mutually beneficial, i also support croatia's accession to the agreement. since switzerland refused to join the european economic community in 1992, several bilateral agreements have been negotiated with the eu. this agreement on the free movement of persons gave citizens of the contracting parties the right to enter, live and work in both territories, with most restrictions removed. two protocols were added to the agreement following the accession of new member states in 2004 and 2007, establishing at the same time quotas, a regime for access to the labour market, restrictions and safeguard clauses. after the accession of croatia to the eu, it was necessary to negotiate a third protocol in a row in order to allow croatian citizens to benefit from the benefits of free movement. although the protocol contains a safeguard clause allowing switzerland to restrict access to the labour market for croatian citizens for a maximum of ten years, i am convinced that in the end the agreement will be beneficial for both countries.
‒ switzerland, as a non-member state of the european union, is obliged to allow free movement of citizens of the european union on its territory in exchange for access to the common market. this applies both to new member states and to those which will join the european union in the future. this model can serve as a basis for the future settlement of relations with the united kingdom.
in writing ‒ in the context of croatia's accession to the european union in 2013, it is necessary to amend many bilateral or multilateral agreements that have already been concluded and in which the enlargement of the european union needs to be reflected. this is also the case for the agreement on the free movement of persons between the european union and switzerland. the report by ms jazłowiecka was aimed at concluding a protocol which would take account of the accession of croatia. in this case, i voted in favour of the conclusion of the protocol, even though the situation regarding the free movement of persons between the eu and switzerland is currently uncertain in view of the results of the 2014 'against mass immigration' referendum. i hope therefore that switzerland will be able to stabilise the situation as soon as possible and that free movement between it and the eu will not be affected by the referendum.
‒ the tripartite social meeting (tss) was established by a council decision in march 2003. its role is to facilitate the exchange of views between the commission, the eu presidency and the eu social partners on employment and social affairs issues. the proposed council decision reflects the institutional changes of the lisbon treaty and the practical results of the tripartite social assembly's work since its inception. it defines the roles and membership, the organisation of the activities and the provision of information. i support the motion.
in writing the tripartite social summit for growth and jobs (tss) was formally established by a council decision of 6 march 2003. it aims to exchange views at the highest level on the employment and social aspects of the lisbon strategy and, later, the 2020 strategy. until the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, meetings were co-chaired by the presidency of the council and the president of the commission. the treaty of lisbon introduced a number of institutional changes which require a revision of the 2003 decision. it institutionalised the european council and created the post of president of the european council; recognised the role of the tripartite social dialogue as part of the eu social dialogue; and abrogated article 202 of the ec treaty, which had been the legal basis for the 2003 decision. the revision provides that the president of the european council, the presidency of the council and the two successive presidencies, the commission and the social partners, the ministers of the three presidencies and the commissioner responsible for employment and social affairs shall attend the meetings of the tss. the regularity of meetings shall be fixed twice a year, each time before the spring and autumn european council meetings.

in writing ‒ the tripartite social summit was set up by a council decision in march 2003 to act as a forum for discussion between the eu institutions and the representatives of workers and employers, i.e. the social partners. the summit is also part of a dialogue across different industry sectors, providing the social partners with the opportunity to contribute regularly to the eu's economic and social strategy. the summit is always held once a year before the european council and is attended by the european institutions, represented by the three presidencies of the council and the commission, and the social partners, represented by ten representatives of workers and ten representatives of employers. the adoption of the treaty of lisbon requires an update of the functioning of this summit. as it was finally agreed with the council that the chair of the ep's committee on employment and social affairs would also be able to attend the tripartite summit, i agreed with the report. i am convinced that the european parliament, as co-legislator, is an indispensable link in this dialogue with the social partners. this is also a way of putting more pressure on the eu to develop more socially balanced policies.
in writing ‒ tripartite negotiations play an important role in the construction of employment and wage relations. as always, however, i also advocate the principle of subsidiarity, that is to say, that agreements should be reached in direct dialogue between the employee representatives and the employer. any representation of a higher degree necessarily entails distortions and approximations, the implementation of which in specific cases may be rather counterproductive.
in writing. the purpose of the review of directive 2006/87/ec is to harmonise technical standards for inland waterway transport, taking into account the specifications of the european committee for the elaboration of standards for inland waterway transport (cesni). cesni was established to promote the harmonisation of standards for the european inland waterway sector. the standardisation would ensure an appropriate level of safety and efficiency for inland navigation, taking into account scientific and technical developments in the sector. the review will provide a higher degree of legal certainty and allow for timely adaptations to technical progress, and will contribute to the maintenance of high safety standards throughout the union without restricting innovation and safety. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing ‒ inland navigation in the individual member states is of fundamental importance to the european union and it is very important that we continue to work towards continuously increasing the high level of safety and efficiency of inland navigation, which will include, inter alia, the scientific and technical progress made in this area in recent years. after lengthy negotiations, the european parliament and the council agreed on a coherent and harmonised framework to ensure the same level of safety for ships used in inland navigation.
in writing ‒ the proposed directive aims to establish a common and uniform set of technical standards for inland waterway vessels, setting out requirements for the stability, safe distance, watertightness, equipment, construction and transport of containers and specifying specific requirements for passenger ships. the commission shall be empowered to further specify those conditions by means of delegated and implementing acts. the proposal aims to ensure maximum safety on inland waterways and to maintain safety standards, while taking into account the scope for further innovation in this area.
in writing inland waterway vessels seeking a union certificate to operate on european inland waterways must comply with the uniform technical requirements developed by the european committee for standardisation in inland navigation (cesni) under the auspices of the central commission for the navigation of the rhine. technical standards developed to provide a harmonised and coherent framework for ensuring the same level of safety in inland navigation will be incorporated into eu legislation. the proposal passed its first reading, the key being an agreement on parliament's rights as co-legislator. parliament could not support the use of a dynamic link to automatically adapt the annex to the directive to the european standard developed within cesni. this dynamic link would give the council exclusive decision-making power, bypassing parliament's prerogatives as co-legislator. i support the motion with my vote.
in writing. ‒ i support the vote and adoption of the report, as the safety and smooth operation of inland navigation requires due attention. this will create a harmonised and uniform framework allowing for the same level of safety in the navigation of the internal waters of the member states.
in writing ‒ the inland waterway sector is relatively small, but it still contributes significantly to the eu's transport system, with a volume of 140 billion kilometres. i am very positive that, compared to other land transport modes, inland waterway transport is energy efficient, safe, almost free of congestion and quiet. unfortunately, the less stringent emission limits and long life of engines are a major sign of the lack of progress in reducing air pollutants. i consider that the eu's inland waterway infrastructure is not well connected to other modes of transport, and therefore i support the building and completion of missing links, the removal of major bottlenecks, the introduction of innovative technology, the improvement of intermodal connections and the development of smart infrastructure. i supported the resolution because i believe that the harmonization of the rules will ensure the same level of safety for inland waterway vessels. i also expect the proposed directive to improve research, development and innovation in the inland transport sector, with the measures taken, to green the vessel fleet, which is low compared to other modes of transport.
in writing, ‒ shipping is growing in importance. although the construction of waterways is demanding and permanently alters the landscape, modern technology has reduced the environmental impact. in the context of ambitious plans to build new interconnectors, it is also necessary to redefine the minimum technical requirements for the competence of river vessels engaged in european inland waterway transport.
‒ mr belett's report concerned the adoption of a new directive aimed in particular at simplifying the decision-making process in relation to the adoption of technical standards for inland waterway vessels, while providing a harmonised framework of technical standards for the eu and the ccnr (central commission for rhine navigation). the first edition of these harmonised standards was drawn up by the recently established standards committee in november 2015. since i believe that in such a highly technical area there should be certain common standards within the european union and at the same time these standards should be aligned with the regime given by the committees for the various areas, i voted in favour of adopting this directive.
in writing. economic partnership agreements (epas) are a system of trade and development agreements between african, caribbean and pacific states and the eu. its purpose is to support the acp countries' regional and global trade integration. gmp is another important step towards deepening regional integration, provided that the effectiveness of control is adequate and the necessary follow-up measures are in place. in addition, the involvement of civil society as a partner in economic processes is essential and can be facilitated by the appropriate allocation of available resources. monitoring of the contribution to sustainable fair trade will be particularly important in the context of gmp. i voted in favour of parliament giving its consent to the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the economic partnership agreement between the european union and its member states, of the one part, and the countries associated with the economic partnership agreement of the southern african development community, of the other part (sadc gpm countries).
‒ the economic partnership agreement between the european union and the sadc epa states was signed on 10 june in botswana and its main benefit is the creation of duty-free, quota-free access to the european union market for botswana, lesotho, mozambique, namibia and swaziland. all relevant measures should help to create sustainable development in the african countries concerned. however, it is very important that civil society is also involved in this process, which will monitor the respect of human rights and labour standards in the partner countries. the european commission will therefore have to provide clear guarantees in the area of respect for human rights and freedoms.
in writing ‒ i support the conclusion of economic partnership agreements with botswana, lesotho, mozambique, namibia, swaziland and south africa. these countries are at different stages of economic and social development. by integrating them into development cooperation and trade, we will enable them to participate in the global economy. this will help the eu on the one hand, and monitoring their development on the other hand will help to strengthen the democratization processes in these countries. we will create the conditions to strengthen their sustainable development. the agreement also leaves room for other areas of cooperation in the future.
in writing in july 2014, following negotiations between the ec and the southern african development community (sadc), the two sides initialled the text of an economic partnership agreement (epa). the southern african development community comprises the african states of botswana, lesotho, mozambique, namibia, swaziland, the republic of south africa and angola, which is not part of the epa by virtue of its decision not to accede to the agreement. this development-oriented regional trade agreement currently only covers provisions on trade in goods, development cooperation and sustainable development, but also leaves open the possibility of negotiating other provisions on services, investment and others. the agreement is asymmetrical in nature, which introduces so-called positive discrimination of the sadc epa partner countries. this model guarantees them duty-free access to the eu market while mutually removing barriers to virtually any trade, ensuring wto compatibility and more. trade relations between the sadc epa states and the eu are based on a contractual agreement, i.e. the sadc epa states will liberalise 86% of their trade with the eu, excluding sensitive agricultural products, over a period of 10 years, according to agreed provisions. i consider the adoption of this treaty to be a significant step in the union's trade relationship with africa, which for the first time is based on a regional rather than a unilateral agreement, which may lead to the conclusion of further economic partnership agreements. i therefore vote in favour of the motion.

in writing ‒ workers in the fisheries sector face a number of risk factors in the exercise of their profession, such as a high rate of fatal accidents and risks of occupational diseases compared to other sectors in the labour market. it is therefore important to provide special protection for those workers. it is therefore very unfortunate that to date only 2 member states have signed the fisheries labour convention, as the european union and its member states should be leaders and take the lead in promoting decent wages and working conditions in the fisheries sector.
the european fishing industry is the fourth largest in the world and employs over 100 000 people in the european union alone. as early as 2013, the eu's social partners in the fisheries sector reached an agreement that proposes to align eu legislation with the 2007 fisheries labour convention, a document issued by the world labour organisation (ilo). the convention itself promotes decent work for fishermen, and provides a framework of minimum global standards for living and working conditions and health care. the eu is also a leader in the global fight against illegal fishing. the implementation of the social partners' agreement in eu legislation can be a positive example for third countries to ratify the 2007 ilo convention as well. this is of particular importance in the fight against illegal fishing. implementation of this proposal will therefore not only improve the working conditions of fishermen at sea, but also reduce the incentive to engage in illegal fishing and contribute to healthy and sustainable fisheries. i therefore support the implementation of the agreement.

in writing ‒ the recent political developments in poland, in particular in the composition and effective functioning of the constitutional tribunal, but also in the publication and publication of constitutional tribunal decisions, as well as the total ban on abortion, up to new laws that threaten media freedom, increase police powers, constitute an unthinkable and unjustifiable interference in the legal system of the state, as well as a threat to the fundamental freedoms of citizens and their way of life. following these steps, the european commission has opened a dialogue with the polish government to ensure respect for the rule of law. the polish authorities have not satisfactorily explained the threats to the rule of law and therefore the european commission is forced to activate the mechanism and move to the second phase of supporting the legal framework by issuing concrete recommendations to the polish authorities to address the problems related to the protection of the rule of law.
in writing ‒ under the treaty on the functioning of the european union, matters of public morality and family law are the exclusive competence of the member states of the union. in the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, poland stressed the exclusive competence of the member states to legislate in the fields of public morality, family law, the protection of human dignity and respect for the physical and moral integrity of persons. the application of the charter to poland is therefore legitimately restricted. poland shall not be bound by the principles of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union unless those principles are recognised in the polish legislation or practice. meps confirmed in their resolution that they respect the rights of the republic of poland as a sovereign state and recognise that areas of legal relations to which the republic of poland did not commit itself upon accession to the eu are its internal affairs. the ep pointed out that the new internal legislation of the republic of poland (the law on combating terrorism, the criminal code, the law on the public prosecutor's office, the law on public broadcasting, etc.) should not apply to the eu institutions in view of the principle of subsidiarity. the objectives and tasks of these laws can be better achieved by the polish authorities. i supported the motion for a resolution because it is based on respect for the law in force in the union.

in writing. ‒ i abstained from voting on the report because, instead of defining the concept of 'social dumping', the report sought to define the posting of legally employed workers to another eu member state as social dumping. the report aims to combine the status of workers legally posted to another member state under existing eu legislation, and of carriers providing crossborder services, with the situation of, inter alia, undeclared workers and those working in the domestic and care sector (especially in home care). in addition, the report goes beyond the subsidiarity threshold in many cases, including the guarantee of a minimum income for eu citizens and the integration of national pay policies.
in writing ‒ the phenomenon of social dumping is based on unfair economic and social competition practices. this is a long-term negative phenomenon in social conditions in europe, which is detrimental to the high level of social protection in the european union. increased competition between economic operators forces them to continuously reduce the expenditure associated with labour costs. this leads to a weakening of the social standards in force in the various member states of the european union and progressively undermines all the rights of european workers. this asymmetry between economic freedoms and social rights gives the impression that europe is weakening individuals and communities instead of protecting them. it follows that the spread of unfair practices and unfair competition undermines the stability of the internal market of the european union and undermines confidence in the construction of a common europe. the situation is often not helped by the unilateral decisions taken by individual member states in the social field.
in writing ‒ any dumping is contrary to the values and objectives of the european union. the social field is a priority area for the member states, and therefore the protection of workers and the social policy related to it are regulated differently in different countries. this diversity is felt by union citizens when they benefit from the free movement of persons and capital, under which workers enjoy different degrees of social protection and social security, as well as different employment benefits. social dumping by reducing labour costs in a targeted manner reduces the protection of workers' rights. at the same time, it creates an environment for unfair competition practices. this ultimately has a negative impact on the internal market. i support the proposal that the commission should create a european pillar of social rights, which sets minimum social rights so as not to reduce the existing social and labour protection afforded to workers in individual member states. however, this framework must be developed in cooperation with individual member states and must take into account the possibilities of individual countries. it must therefore be set up in such a way that it is also feasible.
in writing i agree with the trend that the european union has been making in recent years in strengthening the social rights of european citizens. i believe in the laws of the market economy, but at the same time i believe that the strong social base present in europe is sufficient to build a certain framework of social protection which does not conflict with the principles of the free market. however, it cannot be ignored that the eu's powers in dealing with social issues remain limited. i believe that the introduction of the so-called european minimum wage would already have exceeded the threshold of competences that the member states have renounced in favour of the union. i therefore believe that the determination of the minimum wage must remain in the hands of the member states, as must the decision itself whether or not to introduce a minimum wage. i also believe that the optimal and fair level of such a wage can only be achieved as a result of an open dialogue between governments and the social partners and transparent collective bargaining, as follows from the principles of the international labour organisation's minimum wage convention. the direct fixing of a minimum wage at european level would risk making the wage so set unrealistic to the real state of the economies of the member states and, on the contrary, ignoring national conditions which vary considerably from one member state to another.
i welcome the efforts to improve the status of workers and to ensure equal access to the labour market. at the same time, however, it is necessary to take account of the specificities of the labour markets of the member states and to respect that social security policy is a matter for the member states, and i therefore abstained.
in writing ‒ strong safeguards to protect the rights of posted workers and to prevent social dumping are laid down in the posting of workers directive (96/71/ec) of 1996, which constitutes the basic set of mandatory rules on employment conditions to be guaranteed to workers posted to work in another member state. i regret that 'social dumping' has no legally recognised and common definition, and that is why in practice we often encounter unfair practices and situations that allow unfair competition to develop. i supported the resolution because i expect the reform of the directive to remove the shortcomings of social dumping, which contribute to different national solutions and are contrary to the fundamental freedoms of the single market. i also consider the reform of the directive to be important because the proposal creates a clear, fair and easier to enforce legal framework for the posting of workers. i believe that, in order to achieve a strong and sustainable competitiveness in all member states, the posting of workers will not be a source of social dumping but will facilitate the posting of workers in an environment of fairer competition and respect for the rights of workers employed in one member state and temporarily posted by their employer to work in another member state.
in writing ‒ i consider any attempt to introduce a single european minimum wage unacceptable. this would be a serious interference with the exclusive powers of the member states and a distortion of free competition with the inevitable consequence of the collapse of domestic firms, especially small and medium-sized ones.
‒ the report on social dumping in the european union was drawn up on the own initiative of the members and is intended to express the european parliament's opinion on the subject of social dumping in advance of new legislative proposals from the european commission. the report touches on a variety of topics, such as labour inspectorates, the principle of equal pay for equal work, and at the same time seeks to define social dumping (particularly in the field of transport). unfortunately, however, many parts of this report infringe the principle of subsidiarity and proportionality, and as this problem was not resolved during the vote on the report, i decided to vote against it.

in writing ‒ prospectuses are documents required by law which provide information about a particular company so that an investor can decide on the basis of them whether to invest in securities issued by that company. it is important that the proposed directive eliminates the unnecessary administrative burden of drawing up a harmonised prospectus. a prospectus approved by the national authorities will be accepted by all the member states of the union without further approval in another member state. at the same time, conditions are being created for the provision of more relevant data to potential investors, which can ultimately revitalize the capital market.

in writing the 17th meeting of the conference of the parties to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) will be held in johannesburg from 24 september to 5 october 2016. the objective of the convention is to ensure that international trade in these animals and plants does not endanger the survival of these species in the wild. the union, which has been a party to the convention since july 2015, considers cites to be the key international convention for the protection of biodiversity and the fight against illegal trade. the union will focus on the following priorities at the conference: making full use of cites instruments to regulate international trade in endangered species of animals and plants subject to international trade in an unsustainable manner, in accordance with a scientifically sound approach, further strengthening the international community's response to wildlife trade, and also focusing on improving transparency and accountability within cites and ensuring that appropriate procedures are agreed. the objectives and priorities set by the union are consistent with the relevant policies of the union and its international commitments in this area, and i therefore vote in favour of the resolution.

in writing ‒ i supported the resolution on the eu strategic objectives for the conference on trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora, as i consider it irresponsible to trade in species on the verge of extinction. cites, the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora, brings together 181 countries from around the world. i therefore welcome the fact that the eu finally became a signatory to this agreement in 2015. the conference of the parties to the convention will take place in late september and early october, where the eu should take a clear and unified position as wildlife trade has become the fourth most lucrative black market after drug trafficking, human smuggling and arms trafficking. in addition, the eu is a major transit and destination destination for the most endangered species protected by the convention, such as wild birds, turtles, reptiles and various plant species. i therefore support the resolution calling for tougher penalties to combat corruption and organised crime in the smuggling of endangered species. it will also be necessary to take effective action against illegal trafficking on the internet, as well as to advance international cooperation in law enforcement. last but not least, consumer sensitivity to products from endangered species will need to be increased. the conference will be a unique opportunity to consolidate international cooperation, which is indispensable in environmental protection.
in writing ‒ illegal trade in rare and protected species can only be prevented by cooperation between governments and relevant institutions at global level. as in many other cases, the european union is the entity that sets a high-quality legal framework that serves as a model for other countries.
‒ the resolution of the envi parliamentary committee outlines the views and objectives of the european parliament in relation to the 17th meeting of the conference of the parties to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites), to be held in johannesburg at the turn of september and october this year. the aim of cites is to ensure that international trade does not threaten the survival of endangered plant and animal species. the conference will discuss 62 proposals to increase or reduce controls in international trade, affecting many endangered species. the commission will also discuss how to bring the greatest possible transparency to decision-making processes and how best to tackle the smuggling of endangered species and corruption. in addition to the general provisions, the report also deals in more detail with several endangered plant and animal species.
in writing. the third postal services directive paved the way for the completion of the internal market for postal services in 2008. by 2013, market opening was achieved in all member states. however, significant changes have occurred in the postal services market in the recent period which require a review of the application of the directive. traditional paper-based communications - the delivery of letters and newspapers, magazines - are declining rapidly, while the volume of parcel delivery is increasing thanks to electronic shopping. despite the growth of e-services and online shopping, the provision of traditional postal services is still important today, especially in areas without adequate internet coverage. access to cross-border postal services at transparent and affordable prices is also an essential requirement, to which modern technologies (e.g. tracking of the parcel) contribute. one of the main priorities of the sector is to maintain and promote effective competition while taking into account the needs of users. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing ‒ although the postal directive was revised only relatively recently in 2008 and achieved the key objectives of liberalising the market for postal services in the european union, significant changes have taken place in the fully open market for the postal services sector. new technologies are simplifying online shopping and thus increasing the number of parcels and parcels transported by postal service operators. consequently, parcel and express revenues represent more than half of the total revenues of the postal sector. over the last five years, and as a result of the growth of e-commerce, the business-to-consumer parcel and parcel delivery market segment has experienced strong growth, but competition in the letter market is developing only slowly despite the full opening of markets across the european union. if the european union is to continue to make progress in this area, it must complete the single market for parcel delivery. the european commission must focus on promoting and protecting fair and efficient competition in this sector, which will undoubtedly benefit the european economy as such.
in writing ‒ the universal postal service sector employs 1.2 million people in the european union. hundreds of thousands more are employed in the follow-up services. the commission and the member states must create the conditions for innovative solutions in this sector in order to further support employment growth while modernising activities in these services. in order to protect workers, it is necessary to monitor compliance with labour law in the performance of this work and to take measures to improve the working and social conditions of workers.
in writing the 2008 revision of the postal services directive has achieved the key objectives of liberalising european postal services. good postal services are an important part of communication in the eu internal market, even though technological progress and digitalisation have significantly changed the postal sector. the volume of letter items in the eu is decreasing as paper mail is replaced by digital tools, while demand is growing in the express sector. the provision of services is of key importance for regional development, social inclusion and the economic and territorial cohesion of the eu, and plays an important role in rural and remote areas. promoting and protecting effective competition in the postal services sector is a priority. promoting greater economic cooperation is important for achieving the europe 2020 objectives of a competitive and resource-efficient economy.
in writing ‒ the significant changes in postal markets have also affected the universal postal service framework and changed the traditional nature of the services provided under it. i am pleased that the application of the postal services directive has also led to a significant strengthening of the legislative framework for postal services in the eu member states, their modernisation and adaptation to customer requirements. as the main trend is likely to be most towards parcel delivery services as a result of the development of e-commerce, the eu should continue with its plan to complete the single market for parcel delivery. i believe that the harmonisation and interoperability of postal systems, technological innovation and the creation of standardised conditions for measuring the quality of postal services will further accelerate access to the enlarged eu postal market. i call on the eu and its member states to maintain postal services in rural and mountain areas and to guarantee decent working conditions for all postal workers, including the required level of occupational safety and health, in order to ensure communication between people and to guarantee the provision of irreplaceable postal services.
‒ postal services are undergoing major changes with the overall digitalisation of the economy and society as a whole, to which both national and european legislation must respond adequately. on the one hand, we must preserve the historical role of the universal service, which also operates in areas and cases that are not profitable for commercial providers. on the other hand, it is necessary to open up as much space as possible to innovative types of services and alternative operators, thereby increasing competition, improving the quality of services and lowering prices for the customer.
in writing ‒ the european parliament resolution on the application of the postal services directive focused on the changes that the sector has experienced since the full market opening in 2008. the changes concern mainly the reduction in the number of letter items and, conversely, the increase in the number of parcels, which are a consequence of the increasing popularity of online shopping. in addition to issues relating to the prevention of discrimination against new entrants and the prevention of distortions of competition, the resolution focused on ensuring a minimum range of services to be provided in the european union, but also, for example, the affordability of postal services, not only within individual member states but also for shipments abroad. the accessibility of postal services is of utmost importance in sparsely populated areas or, beyond the locality, for the elderly or disabled. in this respect, it is very important to ensure that access to postal premises is not only free but also ensured. as the motion for a resolution reflected all these comments, i voted in favour of it.
‒ the financial crisis has affected smes' access to finance for their activities. the funding problems are particularly acute for cultural and creative businesses, which play a significant role in bridging regional disparities and creating interregional cooperation, but their funding is problematic. if smes are to play a leading role in development and employment as economic drivers, the banking and financial sectors must also take a more active approach to providing financial assistance. i therefore consider it important that the commission, in cooperation with the member states, explores all appropriate options for financing investments in smes' businesses, including the provision of state aid that does not distort competition. facilitating access to finance will help to bridge the gap between smes in different countries and to boost employment growth.
in writing smes and mid-caps make up a significant part of the eu economy. the issue of their access to finance is therefore an important topic on the political agenda. access to finance for smes was more limited during the crisis than for most companies. the strong dependence of smes on bank loans and the reduction of risk in banks caused by the crisis have contributed to this situation. the 'capital markets union' initiative has had as one of its priorities the diversification of funding opportunities for smes. however, bank loans are and will remain the most important source of financing for smes, as they can be adapted to the specific financing needs of different smes, but it is important to offer improvements in this area as well. the report encourages smes to harness the potential of the single market for their financing needs and to see the eu as their home market. it calls for the removal of barriers to the use of market and other innovative financing methods and stresses the need for convergence of rules and practices across the eu and the implementation of the small business act (the eu's sme policy framework). i vote in favour of the motion.
‒ the european commission and the european central bank consider access to finance the second most important problem facing smes. i am sorry that we keep talking about how much we have done for smes, but i too have often seen that there are serious shortcomings in the financial market in terms of lending, especially in terms of financing for new and small enterprises. many smes fail mainly because they have difficulty accessing external financing in the initial phase of expansion. unfortunately, i also find that investors and banks are often reluctant to finance early stage and early stage businesses. i supported the resolution because i believe that the measures taken will make it easier and simpler for micro-enterprises and start-ups to access finance. as access to finance is certainly one of the most important conditions for the creation, survival, performance and growth of smes, i support all initiatives that allow for financing from multiple sources and a reduction in capital costs. i expect the commission and the member states to promote a holistic approach to disseminating information on all eu funding opportunities at european, national, regional and local level, which would be an important step for smes in their funding.
in writing ‒ one of the biggest obstacles to the growth of smes is the lack of access to investment capital. the european union is seeking to facilitate and accelerate their development by offering new types of financial instruments that promote innovation, competitiveness and job growth.
in writing ‒ this report focuses in particular on the contribution of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises to the european union economy and looks at ways to facilitate their access to finance. micro, small and medium-sized enterprises contribute significantly to employment growth as well as to value added in the non-financial sector. unfortunately, however, these enterprises still face many obstacles and most of them do not engage in foreign business. at the same time, the possibilities for financing them remain limited, with banks providing up to 77% of their financing. this is why we have called on the commission in this report not only to assess in depth the discrimination, obstacles and challenges faced by these enterprises, but also to promote, together with the member states, the widest possible range of funding options for these enterprises, including a variety of innovative approaches. as these businesses are demonstrably the driving force of the european economy and make a significant contribution to stable job creation, i was happy to support the report.
in writing ‒ one of the eu's biggest problems is the high unemployment rate. in 2015, there were 23 million unemployed people in the eu, including 4.5 million young men and women under 25. the situation is further complicated by the large influx of migrants whose social integration requires the provision of employment. smes have created 85% of jobs in the last ten years and thus have the potential to tackle unemployment and create jobs. however, due to the different conditions in each member state, there are still clear differences between smes from some member states, as reflected in their size and economic impact. this situation persists in particular in the countries of central and eastern europe that joined the eu after 2004. member states must therefore provide smes with effective and efficient assistance in removing administrative and regulatory barriers to their establishment and business. it is necessary to create the right conditions to improve access to skills, apprenticeship and vocational training, taking into account the needs of the labour market. a fair regulatory framework and a level playing field will make it possible to stimulate more interest and activity of smes.
in writing europe is facing a number of challenges, the most serious of which are the current wave of migration and the issue of unemployment. high unemployment in europe has a negative impact on many areas, threatening demographic prospects, as many young unemployed postpone starting a family, which in turn puts pressure on social security and pension systems. high unemployment in southern and eastern europe and the subsequent exodus of young people from these countries to the central member states are fuelling social tensions in the host countries. smes have created up to 85% of jobs in europe over the last decade, so it is important that they become a central theme in shaping eu entrepreneurship policy and the necessary steps should be taken to strengthen the job creation potential of this sector. smes are a diverse group and there are different models of small businesses in europe. the proposal emphasises the need to ensure a level playing field for smes in terms of their competitive position compared to large companies. smes are particularly disadvantaged by excessive regulation in the administrative system and high fixed costs in the bureaucratic system. it is therefore necessary to implement specific measures for smes in order to reduce their market disadvantages, to enable their internationalisation and to increase their job creation potential. i support the motion with my vote.

in writing ‒ the adoption of the equal treatment directive 15 years ago was a major step forward for the european union in creating a level playing field in the labour market and improving conditions for the quality of employment and occupation. it should be noted that some member states go much further in their transposition of the directive into national law, extending its scope to include racial equality. however, despite the progress made, there are still many unresolved challenges for the future. surveys regularly point to discrepancies between the rate of discrimination expressed and the reported cases of discrimination. victims still have difficulty recognising discrimination. efforts should be made to intensify dialogue between governments, civil society and social partners on all grounds of discrimination and to raise awareness among the public. most member states have shifted the responsibility for disseminating information on and raising awareness of anti-discrimination legislation to national specialised bodies without necessarily providing them with adequate resources.
‒ the union declares in its documents that it will combat social exclusion and discrimination. these values touch on all spheres of life. although member states have also transposed these values into their national legislation, in practice they are violated and not respected in a variety of ways and forms. however, it is difficult to prove the existence of discrimination and unequal treatment in everyday life. it requires a determined approach by the authorities concerned and the cooperation of the victims, who are usually afraid to talk about their bad experience. the commission, the member states and all institutions and organisations must cooperate in obtaining information on discrimination and unequal treatment, exchange practical experience and practices and, from this practice, propose new solutions which must also be reflected and supported in the legislative process.
written the report addresses many areas of non-discrimination in employment and occupation and proposes a number of important measures, for example in relation to people with disabilities. but it is also pushing for the adoption of a highly controversial horizontal anti-discrimination directive, which has been blocked for years and which also places undue emphasis on combating homophobia and transphobia, as well as on specific protection for transgender and intersex groups. the resolution adopted, with its proposals and recommendations, also touches upon areas which are the exclusive competence of the member states, which is why i voted against it.
in writing ‒ the employment equality directive sets minimum requirements, but member states may provide for a higher level of protection in their national legislation. however, we still face problems in implementing the equal treatment directive. according to data from the eu agency for human rights, discrimination is faced by many roma jobseekers, discrimination is in the employment of women, the elderly, the disabled and in the remuneration of men and women. efforts should therefore be made to intensify dialogue between governments, civil society and social partners on all grounds of discrimination and to raise awareness among the public. the surveys have clearly shown that there is a large discrepancy between the rate of discrimination manifested and the reported cases of discrimination. therefore, involving the general public would help to overcome this inconsistency, discriminated individuals should know where and to which institution to turn for help and, above all, victims should be able to recognise a discriminatory situation. i supported the motion for a resolution because i consider the application of the equal treatment directive to be very important.
in writing ‒ any discrimination in employment on grounds of sex, age, race, belief or other factors which are subjective personal considerations is unacceptable. but it would be a mistake to go down the road of quotas in the pursuit of equality, which solves nothing and is just another form of discrimination.
in writing ‒ the aim of the equal treatment in employment and occupation directive, which is also part of the slovak legal order, is to ensure that people are not discriminated against in accessing the labour market or in the exercise of their profession. the directive sets out only minimum requirements to ensure a certain minimum standard throughout the european union, and member states have the possibility to introduce stricter rules. the general principle of equal treatment has already been incorporated in most states' constitutions and subsequently in their laws, but not everywhere is it strictly observed in employment. the european parliament's report therefore dealt with the persisting discrimination in employment, for example in the employment of women, of people with disabilities, but also of older people and people of different religious beliefs. although the proposal correctly identified many of the shortcomings that are apparent in the member states, it was in breach of the principle of subsidiarity in some of its provisions, which is why i abstained in the final vote.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was set up to support and show solidarity with workers made redundant in excess of 500 per enterprise as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns. between 2009 and 2011 and from 2013 the egf was extended to cover workers who lost their jobs as a result of the global financial and economic crisis. it shall enable solidarity with workers who have lost their jobs as a result of major structural changes in world trade due to globalisation, where such redundancies have a significant negative impact on the regional or local economy. in addition, from 2013, the scope of the fund was extended to self-employed persons and to young people not in employment, education or training in regions eligible for support under the youth employment initiative, corresponding to the number of targeted beneficiaries. the primary objective of the egf is to contribute to smart, sustainable and inclusive growth and to promote sustainable employment by preparing and supporting redundant workers for new employment. i voted in favour of the report adopted today, which summarises the activities and impact of the egf between 2007 and 2014 and makes recommendations for the future.
in writing ‒ following the achievements of the european globalisation adjustment fund between 2007 and 2014, it can be concluded that the fund provided individualised and well-coordinated measures to redundant workers. targeted, individualised and intensive support for redundant workers often leads to positive results. the ability to develop measures that complement national measures is also essential, as is the flexibility embodied in this instrument. other positive outcomes for beneficiaries include a positive psychological impact, increased adaptability and labour market flexibility. in addition, the egf has been shown to contribute to social cohesion by helping large groups of people in urgent need. this has had a positive effect on families and the wider community. the organisations involved have achieved positive results in the field of education. this includes building capacity to manage these measures effectively and developing partnerships in the implementation of the european globalisation adjustment fund measures. however, in many cases, it was suspected that funds from the european globalisation adjustment fund had been used by several member states for compensation and national employment and worker support schemes.
‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to help workers who have lost their jobs as a result of globalisation and structural change. the resources of this fund shall be used as a matter of priority to implement measures to enable redundant workers to re-enter the labour market. between 2007 and 2014, 20 member states requested eur 542,4 million for 131 interventions for 121 380 workers. the average time taken to decide on an application for assistance from the fund is up to 41 weeks, and it is therefore necessary to adopt mechanisms to shorten this period. small and medium-sized enterprises, which account for 99% of all eu enterprises and employ more than 100 million people, benefit only marginally from the fund. it is therefore appropriate to ask the commission and the member states to focus aid also on smes and to pay close attention to the respect of the fund's rules for the reintegration of workers into the labour market. timely data provision will allow a better assessment of the effectiveness of the fund.
the european globalisation adjustment fund 2007-2014 was established to provide solidarity to workers who have lost their jobs during large-scale redundancies due to major changes in the structure of world trade due to globalisation, where these redundancies have a significant negative impact on the regional and local economy. since its creation in 2006, the fund has undergone several reforms, reducing the intervention criterion from 1 000 redundancies to 500, making it more accessible to regions and smaller member states. the scope of the fund was extended in 2013 to include workers who lost their jobs as a result of the global economic crisis, and also to include self-employed persons. the report on the activities, impact and added value of the fund revealed several shortcomings. one of the objections to the egf is that some member states have used significant funds from the egf to compensate national schemes to support workers' incomes, whereas such use of european funds does not bring added value. another shortcoming is awareness, the fund suffers from a lack of awareness on the part of some member states, social partners and businesses, communication needs to be improved. i am in favour of the motion.
‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was set up to support and show solidarity with workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade. the egf aims to promote sustainable employment by training redundant workers for new jobs and was set up to deal with emergencies by providing rapid intervention and short-term assistance in response to urgent and unforeseen labour market problems involving large-scale redundancies. the report clearly shows the need to increase the use of the egf by member states to support demand, which will require an increase in its funding and an increase in the rate of eu co-financing. it is to the detriment of the commission that the report did not include an analysis of the beneficiaries by region, which would have shown how the egf is used in the individual regions of the member states. for this reason, we have asked the commission to include in its next report information on the type and quality of jobs found by people reintegrated into the labour market.
‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund is one of the instruments by which the european economy is coping with the decline in its competitiveness. its purpose is to provide means for the retraining and re-employment of redundant staff. it is a pity that slovakia has not yet made use of this possibility, even in justified cases.
in writing ‒ mrs harkin's report summarised very realistically the information on the european globalisation adjustment fund, which was originally set up as an expression of solidarity with workers who lost their jobs in the context of mass redundancies as a result of globalisation changes in world trade. the framework of this fund was extended in 2009 2011 and further after 2013. while it is generally true that people who lose their jobs need to be helped, it is also necessary to monitor whether the funds spent are producing results, whether they have helped redundant workers to get back into employment and whether these funds could be used more successfully in another way. it is also necessary to consider how to help not only large enterprises but also small and medium-sized enterprises, which are also significantly affected by global change. however, this report finds that there are insufficient data to make a comprehensive assessment of the value added to the fund, that the evaluation of re-employment is not set correctly and that there are no statistics on what kind of employment and what quality the redundant workers have managed to find. that is why i think that to assess the contribution of this fund correctly, we will need to collect even more relevant data and encourage all the institutions to cooperate as effectively as possible.
there are currently wide differences in the quality of legal aid offered in the member states, and i therefore welcome the european commission's proposal and the amendments we have proposed in parliament, and consider it an important step towards ensuring a minimum level of legal aid in all member states. the issues raised are quite complex and it is therefore understandable that the european commission took longer to prepare the relevant instruments. however, it is very important that we work together to ensure that adequate and high-quality legal aid is provided. suspects must not feel that their rights are being denied and that the level of legal certainty and the administration of justice in the european union is being reduced. we must therefore seek to bring together the different national criminal procedures and systems, since harmonisation in this area is very important to ensure a high standard of legal aid in the european union. i expect that member states will have no difficulty in implementing the relevant legislation in order to increase legal certainty for citizens of the european union.
in writing. ‒ at the paris climate conference in december 2015, 187 countries adopted the un framework convention on climate change, whose main objective is to achieve an early global cap on greenhouse gas emissions and climate neutrality by the second half of the century. the negative impacts of climate change have become so severe that global action on the issue is essential. the agreement requires, inter alia, that global warming be kept below 2 degrees celsius above pre-industrial levels, that the temperature increase be limited to a maximum of 1,5 degrees celsius, and that a global transition to clean energy be made essential. the paris document calls for a global review meeting to be convened every five years from 2023 to discuss the results achieved, assess the situation and develop further steps. the member states of the union are collectively responsible for making such a major decision, according to the rapporteur. the signing of the climate agreement cannot happen without the eu, the continent's leading role in the fight against global climate change. ratification by the other parties should take place later this year to achieve real results. i voted for the report.
in writing. ‒ the european union and its member states have for many years been leading the world in the fight against climate change. the paris agreement represents a major step forward for the world in the fight against climate change, leading to many collective actions at the global level. these measures are intended to contribute to the creation of a globally climate-neutral global economy that is resilient to climate change. currently, only 2% of global emissions are still short of the ratification targets, as the requirement for at least 55 parties to the convention has already been met. the paris agreement needs to be ratified by the end of 2016 at the latest, thereby linking it to the kyoto protocol.
in writing. ‒ the paris agreement aims to achieve climate neutrality through a fundamental shift in greenhouse gas emissions reductions and a gradual transition to new technologies. in the second half of this century, only as many emissions will be able to be released as nature can handle. the agreement sets out obligations for all parties not only in the area of monitoring but also in the area of emission reductions. the european union accounts for around 12% of global greenhouse gas emissions. the paris agreement requires the ratification and deposit of relevant instruments at the un by at least 55 parties to the convention, which together account for an estimated 55% of global greenhouse gas emissions, in order to enter into force. i am pleased that slovakia is among the seven member states of the union that have completed the national ratification process of the paris agreement.
in writing. the paris agreement, adopted on 12 december 2015 under the united nations framework convention on climate change (unfccc), represents a decisive shift from small-scale actions to comprehensive and collective action at the global level the agreement now has 191 signatories. the agreement shall be open for signature from 22 april 2016 and shall enter into force when at least 55 parties to the convention, which together account for at least 55% of global greenhouse gas emissions, have deposited their instruments of ratification, acceptance, approval or accession at the united nations. to date, the agreement has been ratified by 62 parties, which together account for approximately 52% of global greenhouse gas emissions. i believe that a decision to ratify the conclusion of the paris agreement at member state and eu level by the end of 2016 at the latest would contribute to highlighting the position of the eu and its member states, their continued efforts to address climate change at international level, as well as the overall international effort to combat climate change. i therefore vote in favour of the motion.
in writing. ‒ the paris climate agreement is not just about the environment, but it is one of the last possible global peace agreements. expected climate change could trigger a major migration of peoples, which is already causing armed conflict. the promotion of clean alternative energy sources is in turn deliberately replacing oil and natural gas, for which mankind has waged increasingly bloody wars in recent decades.
in writing. ‒ i consider the decision to ratify the paris treaty to be the most important vote in the ep this year. each of us must be aware of the urgency of protecting the air and the need to reduce greenhouse gases to keep our planet green for future generations. the seriousness of the vote was also shown by the fact that un secretary-general ban ki-moon visited the european parliament in person and, in his short speech to meps, urged the swift adoption of the paris agreement and its implementation in practice. the paris agreement sets a long-term objective of limiting global warming to well below 20c compared to pre-industrial levels and to work towards limiting the temperature increase to 1,5c. the agreement establishes a framework for greater transparency and accountability, including the biennial submission of greenhouse gas inventories by all parties, as well as the submission of information needed to monitor their progress. the eu has always been at the forefront of climate and air protection, and today's vote, with 610 meps voting in favour of the paris agreement, is a testament to that.
in writing. ‒ the paris agreement is a major success of european diplomacy. countries like china have joined our cause, without which any climate agreement would be ineffective. i am glad that the slovak republic was among the first countries to ratify it.
in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament's resolution giving its consent to the conclusion of the paris agreement. the ratification of the paris agreement by the european union and its 28 member states will thus be a landmark ratification that will help to fulfil the necessary conditions for the paris agreement to enter into force. the long-term objective of the new agreement is to keep global warming below 2°c, with countries committing to take measures that, ideally, will increase global temperatures by a maximum of 1.5°c. the paris agreement is a historic milestone in the fight against climate change and a legally binding instrument that has set itself ambitious targets. these objectives will be pursued by all parties, in particular by reducing greenhouse gas emissions but also by increasing the share of renewable energy. i hope that countries will take responsibility for meeting their commitments and that together they will succeed in achieving the goals of the paris agreement.
in writing. ‒ in november 2015, the greek island of ionia was struck by an earthquake measuring 6.1 on the richter scale. the greek authorities have established damage of more than eur 66 million, with significant damage to infrastructure in addition to personal damage and to sites of great importance for tourism. in february 2016, the government submitted its request to the european commission to receive support from the european union solidarity fund, which is set aside for such cases. the european commission also approved the aid of eur 1 651 834. the european union solidarity fund aims to enable the union to respond to emergencies in a rapid, efficient and flexible manner and to express solidarity with the population of regions affected by disasters, which is why i supported the proposal.
in writing. ‒ the european union solidarity fund is used to provide financial support to member states coping with the consequences of natural disasters. in this particular case, it is a release of eur 16 551 834 for greece, whose regions have to cope with an earthquake of magnitude 6,1 on the richter scale. the total cost is estimated by the greek authorities at eur 66 million. the financial assistance in question shall not constitute an increase in the budget for 2016.
in writing. ‒ the ionian islands, which were hit by a strong earthquake in 2015, are among the less developed regions. the earthquake caused direct damage of eur 66 million, including deaths and injuries and the destruction of residential buildings. the transport infrastructure was destroyed and the cultural heritage was also damaged. greece shall receive from the solidarity fund, in accordance with its rules, assistance of eur 1 651 834 for emergency measures and for the rehabilitation of affected infrastructure and assets.
in writing. on 17 november 2016, greece was struck by a major earthquake. the region affected was the ionian islands, with the islands of lefkada and kefalonia being the most affected, where the intensity of the earthquake reached 6.1 on the richter scale. two people were killed, eight were injured, and about 120 housing units were damaged. in addition, extensive damage was reported to regional and municipal infrastructure networks, private and public buildings (including the local hospital) and other infrastructure, as well as to cultural monuments. the total damage amounted to eur 66 073 345. greece has submitted an application for a financial contribution from the eu solidarity fund in relation to the earthquake, fulfilling all the conditions set out in the application, and i therefore support the mobilisation of the financial assistance from the eu solidarity fund of eur 1 651 834. as this mobilisation is fully financed by using part of the eur 50 000 000 included in the 2016 budget, no amending budget is required for this purpose.
in writing. ‒ the european union solidarity fund aims to enable the eu to respond quickly, flexibly and effectively to emerging disaster situations. this is exactly what greece needs right now. in the earthquake in the ionian islands, hundreds of people lost their homes, and now we have the opportunity to help them. after a disaster like this, we're really struck by how powerless we are in the face of nature's forces. the european union is built on solidarity and we must show that we can count on each other in times of need. i hope that with the money from the fund, we can finally start rebuilding the housing estates and we can relieve some of the burden from the shoulders of those affected by the disaster.
in writing. ‒ the european union solidarity fund was set up in 2002 to provide financial assistance to eligible countries affected by a major natural disaster or an exceptional regional disaster. on 17 november 2016, greece was struck by a series of earthquakes that affected the region of the ionian islands, causing damage amounting to 2,1% of the total gdp of those islands. i therefore voted in favour of granting financial aid to greece in connection with these earthquakes.
in writing. ‒ the last november, the ionian islands of greece were struck by an earthquake measuring 6.1 on the richter scale. as a result, two people were killed, eight were injured, 120 housing units were damaged, 20 of which are uninhabitable. the damage to infrastructure networks, other buildings and cultural monuments was also extensive. i supported the release of funds for greece, as i believe that the eu solidarity fund is intended for such events. the total cost of the earthquake damage was estimated by the greek authorities at almost eur 66,1 million. this means that this disaster can be considered a regional natural disaster and therefore greece is eligible for the fund. in march this year, the commission paid 10% of the expected contribution as an advance payment. the total amount of the proposed aid would be more than eur 1,6 million, based on the 2,5% rate applied by the commission. these funds should reach the people affected by the disaster as soon as possible so that they can cope with the consequences and return to normal life.
in writing. ‒ solidarity between member states and mutual assistance in the event of unforeseeable events, such as natural disasters, is also one of the pillars of european cooperation. slovakia also received eur 5,7 million from the solidarity fund when the high tatras were hit by a catastrophic storm in 2004.
in writing. ‒ i supported greece's request to mobilise the solidarity fund. in february this year, greece requested the mobilisation of the solidarity fund in relation to the damage caused by the earthquake in the ionian islands in november 2015, which amounted to 2,1% of regional gdp. i supported this proposal not only because the disaster caused by the earthquake in greece qualifies for financial assistance from the solidarity fund, but also because of the principle that the european union also means aid and support for member states which, for various unforeseeable reasons, may find themselves in a crisis situation. i believe that with the financial assistance provided by this fund, greece will be able to repair the destroyed infrastructure and cultural monuments and thus restore the disrupted tourism.
in writing. ‒ while globalisation generally creates economic growth, it can also bring about changes that have a negative impact on the labour market in one or more member states. to remedy this, the union has established the european globalisation adjustment fund, a body of legislative and budgetary instruments designed to provide support for workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade patterns or made redundant as a result of the global financial and economic crisis, and to support their reintegration into the labour market. finland has submitted an application for a financial contribution from the egf, following redundancies in microsoft mobile oy and eight related suppliers and downstream companies, involving 2161 persons. according to the finnish authorities, the main reason for microsoft's downsizing is the declining market share of its mobile phones. the authorities link the labour shortages to the significant structural changes in world trade due to globalisation, recalling that the eu decreased its share of ict employment while china and the usa increased theirs. although nokia dominated the markets in the first decade of the 2000s, android and ios operating systems used by various asian manufacturers have since taken over the market leadership. the commission has concluded that the conditions for a financial contribution from the egf are met. the parliament approved the request at its sitting today, and i voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund is designed to cover losses incurred by businesses and companies in the member states which are facing the consequences of a financial and economic crisis, often resulting in redundancies. the case in point is the request of microsoft and 8 of its suppliers in finland. it concerns the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 1 365 000 from the egf for finland and 1 441 redundancies out of a total of 2 161.
in writing. ‒ major structural changes in the global trade pattern have led to the dismissal of 2 161 workers at microsoft mobile oy and its 8 other suppliers and downstream manufacturers. this is mainly due to the decline of this company in the global mobile phone market, with the assumption that the restructuring of this company will also lead to further redundancies. finland has therefore requested the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund to the amount of eur 1 365 000. this aid is in accordance with the fund's rules and will affect 1 441 redundant workers.
in writing. ‒ support from the european globalisation adjustment fund has also found its way to finland where it is really needed. i remember in the early 2000s, nokia dominated the entire mobile market, and then over the years, ios and android became more and more popular, and that led to nokia's slow decline. the downfall of a company of this size has a serious impact on the entire labour market, resulting in the loss of many jobs. finding a new job is not easy, it takes a lot of energy, patience and help. the aid focuses on areas such as the start-up of new businesses and reimbursement of travel or relocation costs.
