in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund is an important tool for addressing the impact of structural changes in the world trade pattern. it has a long track record as a support mechanism for workers who have lost their jobs due to the bankruptcy of their employer and are also in a less developed region where employment opportunities are scarce. this was also the situation of microsoft employees in several locations in finland, and i therefore agreed to the release of funds from the globalisation adjustment fund. according to the information provided by the finnish authorities which submitted the request, the main reason for the redundancies at microsoft is the declining share of the company in the mobile phone market. the application also states that the entire electronics industry in finland is under pressure due to the bankruptcy of nokia, which sold its mobile phone division to microsoft. the commission accepted an aid application for finland in july this year, with the intention of supporting the re-entry of workers made redundant by microsoft and eight of its suppliers and downstream manufacturers. finland should be paid almost eur 1.4 million to be used for the retraining of 1 441 of the 2 161 redundant workers. these former microsoft employees will be provided with personalised services such as coaching, business support, wage subsidies or travel allowances.

in writing. ‒ i did not support finland's request for eur 5.3 million from the globalisation adjustment fund. microsoft will have to make mass redundancies in finland due to changes in world trade and the funds from this fund should be used to help these employees to re-employ themselves or to start their own business. in this case, the funds from the fund were to be used to support career guidance, individual coaching, training or start-up services. however, as in all previous requests to mobilise the fund, i do not think there is sufficient data to demonstrate its effectiveness. all available data indicate that the re-employment rate of redundant workers varies greatly from one country to another and, of course, their successful re-employment depends more on their education, skills and the possibilities of the region than on the training provided with the help of the fund. that is why i think that the existence of the fund as such should be assessed much more thoroughly than it has been so far, and only on the basis of such an assessment should it be decided whether these funds cannot be used in a better and more efficient way, which would not only help the redundant employees, but at the same time would not only apply to large companies, but would also help the employees of small and medium-sized enterprises.

in writing. ‒ on 30 november 2009, the council adopted a roadmap to strengthen the rights of suspects and accused persons. the timetable identifies the right to legal advice and to legal aid the latter is inextricably linked to the right to have recourse to a lawyer. for those who do not have the necessary financial means, only the exemption from costs can ensure the exercise of this right. the difficult interinstitutional negotiations have finally led to the adoption of a text acceptable to all, which parliament approved today and which i also voted in favour of. the text adopted today has introduced a number of changes and clarifications compared to the original draft directive presented by the european commission in 2013 and, inter alia, has extended the scope of the directive from temporary immunity from costs for suspects and accused persons deprived of liberty to ordinary immunity from costs, so that the directive will cover a much wider range of persons.
in writing. ‒ the there are currently wide variations in the quality of legal aid offered in the different member states. the european commission's proposal is an important step towards ensuring a minimum level of legal aid in all member states. the issues raised are quite complex and it is therefore understandable that the european commission took a relatively long time to prepare the relevant instruments. it is very important that we work together to ensure that adequate and high-quality legal aid is provided. suspects must not feel that their rights are being denied and that the level of legal certainty and the administration of justice in the european union is being reduced. we must work together to bring together national criminal procedures and systems, since harmonisation in this area is very important to ensure a high standard of legal aid in the european union. in this case, a good compromise was reached for citizens living in the individual member states of the european union. member states should have no difficulty in implementing the relevant legislation in order to increase legal certainty for citizens of the european union.
in writing. ‒ the judicial cooperation in criminal matters in the eu is based on the principle of mutual recognition of judgments and other judicial decisions. in practice, however, the internal procedures of the member states differ. the need has therefore arisen to establish a minimum level of protection for persons without reducing the higher protection afforded by individual member states. the proposed directive of the european parliament and of the council on provisional legal aid for suspects or accused persons deprived of liberty and on legal aid in european arrest warrant proceedings regulates the right to a minimum legal aid in all member states, the right to access to a lawyer and the right to a fair trial. member states will be required to ensure that suspects, accused persons and requested persons have effective remedies in cases of violation of their rights under this directive, such as the right to judicial review. i support the proposal because it guarantees a minimum level of protection for persons in criminal matters, which will certainly help to eliminate unjustified and unlawful prosecution, investigation and conviction.
in writing. the european union has long sought to strengthen cooperation in areas such as mutual recognition of judgments and criminal law. the establishment of a common framework for the rights of accused persons or persons deprived of liberty necessarily falls within the scope of judicial cooperation. i believe that harmonisation in the form of some kind of european human rights standard is required in this context. eu legislation has been converging the criminal law of the member states for some time, but there is still room for improvement. one weakness is the implementation of the right to guaranteed legal aid provisional, regular and in all circumstances. however, we also need to take into account the practical aspects of ensuring effective legal aid, such as the remuneration of legal counsel, when drafting legislation. the financial possibilities of citizens vary considerably from one member state to another, so it is important to eliminate the risk of neglecting clients who are not sufficiently solvent from the point of view of a lawyer. the report deals with this sensitive issue and i therefore support it.

in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the draft directive on provisional legal aid for suspects or accused persons deprived of liberty and on legal aid in european arrest warrant proceedings. this directive complements the directives on procedural rights in criminal proceedings already adopted, namely the directive on the right to interpretation and translation, the directive on the right to information and the directive on the right of access to a lawyer. in particular, the main objective of this directive is to lay down minimum standards to ensure that a basic level of entitlement to legal aid is respected in all member states. i think that this directive is useful from a practical point of view, as the situation in the provision of either provisional or ordinary legal aid differs from one member state to another. at the same time, the establishment of minimum standards will be beneficial, in particular, in terms of strengthening trust between member states and the recognition of judicial decisions, as states will know that at least common minimum standards have been maintained in the context of criminal proceedings.
in writing. ‒ the report concerns an amendment to council regulation (ec) no 1236/2005 concerning trade in goods liable to be used for capital punishment, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. the amendments are primarily aimed at reducing the use of the death penalty and torture, in particular by respecting human rights. the amendments supplement and clarify the regulations already in force and introduce new aspects. they clarify, inter alia, the definition of the exporter and the definition of transit. it also supplements the omnibus provisions and extends the list of devices suitable for detention and torture and the list of medicines that can be used for lethal injection. it recommends the creation of expert groups to improve export controls and the publication of annual reports summarising the annual activities of the member states. it is also essential to prohibit the activities of brokers that may be associated with prohibited products in order to achieve this objective.
in writing. ‒ the european union has a privileged position worldwide in the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms. it is therefore essential that the european union continuously updates the export control and eu control legislation targeting the trade in instruments of torture. it is necessary to ensure consistency of eu export controls with regard to the lists of military goods, dual-use goods, firearms and goods intended for torture, in order to avoid duplication of controls on these items. in addition to technical assistance and brokering services, the eu should, where possible, also seek to control other services that may contribute to the proliferation of goods that could be used for torture or capital punishment, such as, inter alia, marketing or financial services.
in writing. ‒ i support the adoption of an amended regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending the council regulation on trade in certain goods which can be used for capital punishment, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. the regulation is part of the eu's long-term policy to abolish the death penalty and prevent torture worldwide. the measures included in the draft regulation strengthen controls on trade and exports of goods and substances that may be used for inhuman means of capital punishment. the commission will regularly review the implementation of this regulation every three years and present a report to the ep on the outcome.
in writing. the anti-torture regulation contributes to the protection of human rights by controlling items and activities that are used or could be used for the purpose of capital punishment, torture or other cruel and inhuman treatment. it is a combination of prohibitions and licensing requirements for trade in said goods. the legislative update of the regulation is a positive step. on the one hand, there is a need to control the export of goods that could be used for torture or the death penalty, but the requirement to avoid unnecessary burdens that restrict legitimate trade is also appropriate. adjusting control regimes to be more flexible and adaptable to developments in the world and changing technologies and aligning eu export controls on the lists of military goods, dual-use goods, firearms and goods intended for torture so as to avoid double checks on these items are necessary steps. regulating legal access to medicines and pharmaceutical products, of which the eu is a key producer, is of great importance. the effective performance of controls and verification of the application of sanctions, the provision of guidance and the provision of support activities by national authorities is key. in this case too, it is necessary to ensure a level playing field and a community approach and adequate monitoring of the fulfilment of the commitments by the member states.

in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a european parliament resolution on the proposal for a council implementing decision approving the conclusion by europol of a strategic cooperation agreement between the ministry of public security of the people's republic of china and europol. this strategic agreement excludes the exchange of personal data. the information exchanged could include expertise, general situational reports, crime outcomes, training activities and the provision of advice and support in individual cases of criminal investigations. according to europol, china is increasingly important as a country of origin, a country of destination and a country of transit in the fight against organised crime such as organised illegal immigration, trafficking in human beings, drug crime, counterfeiting of the euro, infringement of intellectual property rights, corruption in education, as well as cybercrime and money laundering-related activities. this agreement will therefore facilitate and strengthen the fight against organised crime and contribute to improving cooperation in the field of international law enforcement.
in writing. ‒ organized crime today often extends beyond the borders of a single country or continent. the expansion of cooperation with other states, including the exchange of data on suspects or financial transactions, is a valuable contribution to the global fight against crime.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposed approval of the china-europol strategic cooperation agreement. i think that if the country with which europol wants to conclude a cooperation agreement meets all the requirements and cooperation with it can be beneficial for europol, there is no reason not to support these agreements. the importance of china in this case is not to be underestimated, as cooperation with it will be beneficial in the fight against organised crime, in particular that linked to illegal migration, trafficking in human beings and money laundering. there are many criminal organisations, against which china is making significant progress, which can help the european union to move forward in this area through the exchange of expertise or strategic analysis. it is also important that, as it is a strategic cooperation agreement, no personal data will be exchanged under it.
as a member of the acp-eu parliamentary assembly and also a member of the development committee, i have been working on development cooperation issues for more than 10 years. i supported the report because i believe that it is our duty to help the less developed countries. moreover, the migration crisis has shown what happens when we fail to deliver effective aid where people suffer from hunger and deprivation. we must therefore take seriously the commitments we make, whether in terms of funding or in terms of providing know-how to improve the functioning of state institutions, education or health. we have received a number of reports in the acp-eu parliamentary assembly. however, i lack reports to assess whether our recommendations made sense for improving the situation in developing countries, and at the same time to evaluate the efficiency of the use of the funds spent.
in writing. ‒ the basis for acp-eu cooperation is provided by the cotonou agreement, which expires in 2020. it is therefore time to evaluate the results of the current agreement and to outline the next agreement, which will hopefully lead to a more effective partnership. the resolution adopted today, which i also voted in favour of, contains proposals for the draft which is being prepared. the report recalls that the acp-eu relationship should be maintained in the future as a political relationship rather than a mere donor-beneficiary relationship. it therefore stresses that the principles of eu development assistance should be applied equally to all developing countries and that the advanced acp countries should be gradually excluded from the eu development assistance system. it calls for the fight against poverty and inequality and the promotion of sustainable development to remain the main objective of this cooperation. it also called for the fundamental elements of the cotonou agreement on human rights, democratic principles and the rule of law to continue to form the basis of the new agreement and for good governance to be included among the fundamental elements. the new convention should also reflect recent political, structural and demographic changes, and should pay greater attention to the role of the regions and encourage greater involvement of society and the private sector.
in writing. ‒ cooperation between the european union and the acp countries may bring both sides economic and financial benefits in the future if the obstacles it faces are overcome. the effectiveness of cooperation needs to be improved and adapted to new challenges, and a new structure needs to be adopted that preserves those parts of european union law that are universal in nature, such as the commitment to respect human rights, gender equality, human development, good governance and democracy, the objective of the rule of law and the exchange of best practices within a common framework, with the main work being carried out under the principle of subsidiarity.
in writing. ‒ the partnership agreement between the 79 members of the african, caribbean and pacific group of states and the european community and its member states was signed in cotonou in 2000. it was subsequently revised in 2005 and 2010. it is based on three pillars of cooperation: political development cooperation, economic and trade cooperation. 80% of the least developed countries are from the acp regions. cooperation with these countries is important not only for them but also for the eu itself, as the problems of these countries affect it in various ways. i support the ep's calls for cooperation beyond 2020 to create the conditions to tackle poverty in these countries, to promote investment and to set the stage for economic and social development. at the same time, it is necessary to help establish institutions in these countries that respect the laws of democracy and the rule of law.
in writing. the roots of the acp-eu partnership date back to 1963, and since then several treaty frameworks have been signed, with the last revision of the treaty bases taking place in 2000, known as the cotonou agreement. however, this agreement expires in 2020 and therefore a discussion on the future of the acp-eu partnership beyond 2020 needs to be launched. the cotonou agreement is considered beneficial and therefore the maintenance of its provisions will be part of the future relationship. the report also examines several possible scenarios for the future of the partnership: stronger regionalisation, an edf budget, a strengthening of political dialogue and greater participation of civil society and the private sector. the 2030 agenda and the sustainable development goals should form the basis of the new agreement. the fight against poverty remains a central objective of acp-eu cooperation, but the new agreement must be primarily a political project and must leave behind a donor-recipient mentality. cooperation should be pursued in areas of common interest where mutual benefits can be expected, not only in economic aspects but also in peace and security, human rights and the rule of law, good governance and democracy, migration, the environment, climate change and other areas related to the prosperity of both acp and eu citizens.
in writing. ‒ the european union has excellent relations with the countries of africa, the caribbean and the pacific. i support the continuation of political and trade cooperation beyond 2020 on the successful track it has taken so far. i am satisfied with the objectives, and i regard as a particular positive the support for regional development, which can be the first step towards eradicating poverty.
in writing. ‒ the partnership agreement between the members of the african, caribbean and pacific group of states, of the one part, and the european community and its member states, of the other part, was signed in cotonou as early as 2000. it was revised in 2005 and 2010. the objective of the cotonou agreement was to reduce and finally eradicate poverty in line with the objectives of sustainable development and the gradual integration of the acp countries into the world economy. this agreement shall expire in 2020. this resolution maps the current situation in three areas: political dialogue, development aid and economic and trade cooperation. it also looks to the future by emphasising the principle of private ownership and the importance of private investment (smes). for these reasons, i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ i regard the cooperation between the acp/african, caribbean and pacific countries and the eu as a unique achievement, which has strengthened the ties between the acp peoples and countries and the eu member states and their parliaments over the past 40 years. although the partnership agreement with the acp governments was concluded with the aim of increasing the overall performance of their economies, it regrets that the existing acp-eu cooperation has not yet produced the expected results. i am convinced that if we want to improve the effectiveness of cooperation, we must adapt it to new challenges and areas of common interest where common benefits can be expected, not only in terms of economic aspects, but also in terms of peace and security, human rights and the rule of law, good governance and democracy, migration, the environment, climate change, but also other areas related to the prosperity of the acp-eu population. i believe that the new agreement will lead to a better political dialogue between the partners of the agreement, which has not been sufficiently exploited so far. as half of the acp member states are still among the world's least developed countries and the acp member states together account for less than 5% of world trade and around 2% of world gdp, i expect there to be a greater eradication of poverty and integration of the acp countries into the world economy.
in writing. ‒ it is important that the european union maintains close relations with the african, pacific and caribbean states, including the provision of development aid. as some of these countries are sources of mass migration (africa) or are home to companies involved in tax fraud schemes, we must always make this aid conditional on legislative and economic reforms.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the future of relations between the european union and the african, caribbean and pacific group of states after 2020. currently, relations with 79 countries, most of them among the world's least developed, are governed by the cotonou agreement, which deals with new global challenges, including climate change, migration and the threat of terrorism. however, this agreement expires in 2019. the report highlighted the unique success of the mutual cooperation and confirmed that the main objectives will be to fight poverty and promote sustainable development even after the cotonou agreement has expired. it also called for the essential elements of the cotonou agreement in the field of respect for human rights, democratic principles and the rule of law to form the value base of the new agreement. the resolution also proposes new elements to the cotonou agreement to allow the new agreement to reflect the changed situation, in particular in the area of the donor-recipient approach. in addition to these aspects, it also deals with financing, the institutional system, but also with commercial aspects. i believe that if the new post-2020 agreement can meet the expectations expressed in this report, it will become a useful tool for deepening relations between the european union and the acp states.
the commission has already done so. in 1970 a german mark cost 9 drachmas. thirty years later, in 2000, 170 drachmas had to be paid for one deutsche mark. if the euro had not been introduced, one deutsche mark would today cost 250 drachmas. but no, the creators of the euro have decided that for all eternity a deutsche mark will cost 174 drachmas. the result is that the euro is far too strong for greece - even tomatoes are imported from holland - and for germany the euro is far too weak, which is why germany is the world's leading exporter. the situation in greece is a disaster. all macroeconomic data are negative, e.g. industrial production is at the level of the 1970s. today the greeks are the victims and not the perpetrators of the whole thing. the only real possibility is that greece leaves the eurozone.
in writing. greece is currently under renewed intense pressure in relation to the delay in structural reforms. the acceleration of these measures is a condition for the use of the third rescue loan. the greek debt problem has been going on for too long, with no noticeable improvement. the result of forced austerity is an economic decline, unemployment well above 20%, with young unemployed with no prospects in the country almost half. this situation only serves to fuel populist and extremist political forces promising unrealistic miracles to a desperate population. it is known that greece will virtually never be able to repay its debts with the current structure of its economy. the conditions and the orientation of the aid should therefore be considered in order to achieve the objectives of consolidating the local economy. this is one of the persistent destabilising elements that is part of the wide mosaic of current european problems. the country's current situation is not only the result of irresponsible governments but also the failure of european control mechanisms to bring it into the monetary union. no one has been held responsible for this to date. the delay or even the limitation of aid would hit ordinary people within the already hard-pressed middle class the hardest.
the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the application of the 'blue card' procedure. i'm not going to tell you. you are complaining about austerity policies which should be abolished and you want investment instead. we have the juncker package: 315 billion. of this, more than 100 billion have already been invested. and we have the southern countries, they're all in debt. mr juncker is very lenient with spain, portugal, france - all of them are in deficit of more than 3%. my question is, why isn't it working? what do you want to invest more and save less?
the bratislava summit was meant to be a landmark event, but it's already been reported that the leaders see it as a missed opportunity or as a personal goal. i think that the leaders' meeting was overshadowed by the unfortunate statement of prime minister robert fico when he threatened, as prime minister of slovakia, to veto the withdrawal of the united kingdom from the union. let me say that i find that statement inadequate. i do not take the slovak government's position, it is not my place to do so, but as a private citizen i think it is necessary to apologize for such a statement, and for two reasons. in his opening speech here at the opening of the slovak presidency, prime minister fico said that he would propose solutions that are good for the member states and for the eu as a whole, and strained relations with britain or various quarrels certainly do not fit well into such an agenda. secondly, what causes the duplicity of national politicians when the pro-eu rhetoric here in brussels alternates with strong anti-brussels rhetoric at home. only anger among the people, only incomprehension and alienation from the idea of cooperation between european nations and eventually populism and extremism will grow. so i call on european leaders to abandon such populism at their next meeting and, in the words of donald tusk, to engage in brutal honesty.
the debate in the european parliament's plenary shows a picture that the citizens of the member states of the european union cannot like. we who are elected and who are paid to accept solutions, we rush to criticize individual policies. we can't agree on how to deal with the refugee crisis, we can't agree on brexit, we can't agree on how to operate in africa, syria, what our relationship should be with russia, with ukraine. it must be said very clearly that in this respect the bratislava summit was a success, a success simply because the leaders met and talked about the importance of adopting common solutions, because there are no brussels officials, there is no indifferent european union, these are our common solutions and prime minister robert fico has shown that he is interested in these common solutions being sought. that is why i ask for criticism of the bratislava summit. in conclusion, i would like to say that i expect the commission to make a much greater effort to appeal to the leaders of the member states that it is important that they seek common solutions, and not that they go out to press conferences after the summit, where, after the bratislava summit, orbán and renzi criticized the first summit without coming up with concrete solutions. this is not a solution for the european union, it is only the destruction of the functioning of the institution.
in writing. all the heads of government and presidents at the bratislava summit declared that there was nothing better for their people than the eu. it was a strong positive signal to the eu people. they showed that we have learned from the migration crisis, and from our own mistakes, that we are prepared to prevent a repeat of this situation. they pointed to concrete measures that reduce the flow of migrants and address major problems outside europe. they offered measures to contribute to growth and employment, in particular youth employment. they have set aside six months to bring the process they started in bratislava to a conclusion, with the ultimate aim of setting clear priorities and planning concrete actions. this year, we are adding a border and coast guard with new powers of return policy, we are launching a system that records data on people entering and leaving the eu and into the eu, we are implementing our priorities, such as fighting tax fraud, tax evasion, taxing profits where they are made, completing the banking union, so that people's deposits are protected and that when banks have problems, it is the owners who are involved, not all the residents, we are continuing the energy union project to guarantee the security of energy supply and the cheapest energy possible. we'll protect our steel industry from low prices from china. we will get people to use their mobile phones in the eu for the same price as at home from the summer onwards.

in writing. ‒ the 1980 hague convention was established to prevent and combat the illegal removal of children. the convention has been ratified by all eu member states. under the convention, the law of the state in which the child is present is applicable and the court of that state has jurisdiction. the convention also provides for the immediate return of children who have been illegally removed. the eu now has exclusive external competence in such matters. in the absence of the convention, the party from the other state tends to exploit the lack of cooperation between the states in order to obtain custody of the child, in which case the courts of both states concerned may assign the case to their own jurisdiction and award custody to the parent of their own nationality. it is therefore important that as many states as possible become parties to the international convention. following the accession of peru to the convention, a council decision authorising the accession of two member states (austria and romania) which have not yet accepted peru's accession is required. this will allow the entry into force of the convention between peru and the eu. the accession of peru to the convention will help to increase the number of eu citizens of peruvian origin. i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ the european union has a very strong position in guaranteeing fundamental rights and is committed to ensuring that citizens of the member states are not exposed to danger and that their fundamental rights are protected. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 is one of the instruments adopted by the european union to protect the rights of the child. the convention allows the parties to cooperate and seek common solutions to international child abduction cases that still occur in the 21st century. following the accession of peru to that convention, it is necessary for the council to adopt a decision authorising the two member states, austria and romania, which have not yet accepted the accession of peru, to accept the accession. this will allow the entry into force of the convention between peru and the whole of the european union.
in writing. ‒ the hague convention has been ratified by all the member states of the union. it shall be based on the cooperation of the parties in ensuring the prompt return of children who have been wrongfully removed or retained in another state and in ensuring that custody and access rights under the law of one state party are respected in the other states parties. the convention applies to all children who are habitually resident in the territory of a contracting state. i therefore welcome the fact that by acceding to the convention, peru will also be providing such protection to children who are in some way bound to the peruvian community.
in writing. ‒ the increasing trend of broken marriages, open borders and visa-free travel make this issue more timely than ever. even when parents are separated peacefully, it can be a serious psychological burden on the children, as in the case of families where one of the parties tries to evade the court's decision on the placement of the child by various practices. in some cases, this may even lead to a parent's abducting his or her own child and fleeing abroad. the hague convention aims to avoid this possibility by proposing solutions such as speeding up the judicial process or minimising administrative burdens. i was happy to vote for peru to join the convention.
in writing. ‒ the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a particularly important instrument. it has been ratified by all eu member states. this convention establishes a system enabling states parties to cooperate in finding a solution to cases of international child abduction. following the accession of peru to that convention, it was necessary for the council to adopt a decision authorising two member states austria and romania which had not yet approved peru's accession to accept that accession. this will allow the entry into force of the convention between peru and the whole of the european union. i support this council decision, which the council has already taken in advance, and therefore i voted in favour of its adoption. many citizens of peruvian origin live in the eu. children who are connected in some way to the peruvian community will thus be protected from kidnapping.
in writing. ‒ i supported peru's accession to the hague convention, as it is an important international convention protecting the rights of the child. the convention has been ratified by all eu member states and the eu now has exclusive external competence in this area, as the court of justice has ruled. it is therefore necessary for the council to adopt a decision authorising austria and romania to accept accession. this will allow the entry into force of the convention between peru and the whole union. eu countries will be able to use the system of cooperation with peru to find solutions in cases of international child abduction. such cases often occur when parents from different countries divorce. parents may seek to obtain custody of a child by abduction where there is no cooperation between the states concerned. the individual countries have strongly national legal systems in this area. thus, there are regular situations where the courts of both states concerned declare themselves competent and each of them grants custody to the parent. this is precisely what the convention seeks to prevent by requiring the competent court and the law of the state in which the child is domiciled to be determined at international level. this will better protect children of peruvian origin living in the eu from abduction.
in writing. ‒ the hague convention addresses cases where a child is abducted by one of the parents to another country in the hope that the legislation there will provide him with a better position in a custody dispute. the extension of the hague convention narrows the scope for such action and increases the international legal protection of children.
in writing. ‒ the 1980 hague convention on international child abduction is a particularly important instrument for addressing the civil law aspects of international child abduction. international child abductions are a huge negative impact on the life of the whole family and especially on the child's psyche. the objective of this convention is therefore to restore the situation by the immediate return of the child who has been wrongfully removed to the country of his or her habitual residence, through a system of cooperation between central authorities designated by the parties. the convention has so far been ratified by 93 states, including all the member states of the european union. given the objective of the convention, it is therefore very important that as many countries as possible accede to it, thereby reducing as much as possible the situations where a child is abducted abroad, but unfortunately there is no legal instrument to help the child return, as the country where the child was abducted has not ratified the convention. for these reasons, i therefore welcomed peru's decision to accede to the convention and supported the report on the acceptance of this accession by the european union.
in writing. ‒ the 1980 hague convention was created to prevent and combat the illegal removal of children. the convention has been ratified by all eu member states. under the convention, the law of the state in which the child is present is applicable and the court of that state has jurisdiction. the convention facilitates the settlement of civil disputes involving an international element, particularly where parents are living apart in different countries. similarly to peru, following the accession of kazakhstan to the convention, a council decision authorising member states to accept the accession of kazakhstan is required, thereby allowing the entry into force of the convention between kazakhstan and the eu. the commission has assessed the functioning of the judicial system in kazakhstan with civil justice experts from the member states and has concluded that the country is ready to implement the convention. the hague convention system is more effective the more countries that join it. i supported the entry into force of the agreement between kazakhstan and the eu.
in writing. ‒ the european union has a very strong position in guaranteeing fundamental rights and is committed to ensuring that citizens of the member states are not exposed to danger and that their fundamental rights are protected. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 is one of the instruments adopted by the european union to protect the rights of the child. the convention allows the parties to cooperate and seek common solutions to international child abduction cases that still occur in the 21st century. following the accession of kazakhstan to that convention, it is necessary for the council to adopt a decision authorising member states other than denmark, which is not covered by the union's civil-law policy, and the netherlands, which have already accepted the accession of kazakhstan, to accept the accession of kazakhstan. this will allow the entry into force of the convention between kazakhstan and the whole of the european union.

in writing. ‒ i was pleased to vote in favour of accepting kazakhstan's application to accede to the hague convention. protecting children's rights should be a priority for every country. they are the main victims of the increasing divorce rate, and it is true that sometimes the irrational decisions of parents, such as kidnapping their own children before a court verdict is delivered or before a trial begins, put them in situations that are very difficult to avoid. often they grow up completely cut off from the rest of their family, which puts a heavy psychological burden on them.

in writing. ‒ according to several projections, there will be more than 8.5 billion people on earth in 2030. the european union cannot ignore the fact that 795 million people already lack enough food to live a full and quality life. it is therefore crucial that we focus more on creating opportunities and increasing productivity for small farmers, who are the biggest actors in agricultural production, and in doing so ensure sustainable agriculture and food systems. it is important to avoid accepting trade agreements that could have a detrimental impact on food security and contribute to malnutrition if the leasing or selling of arable land to private investors leads to local people losing access to productive resources essential to their livelihoods or if it would result in a large proportion of food being exported and sold on international markets, making the exporting host country more dependent on and vulnerable to commodity price fluctuations on international markets.

in writing. ‒ on 2 september 2016, caterpillar announced that it would close its headquarters in gosselies, belgium, in april 2017, laying off more than 2 000 employees. on 7 september 2016, alstom announced that it would move the production of trains in france from belfort to reichsoffen, putting 400 jobs at risk. unfortunately, the closure of branches of large corporations and the gradual redundancies that affect the subcontracting network and smes have been a fact of life in europe for some time. several large industrial manufacturing companies have pursued strategies focused on short-term financial returns and where the constant pressure to increase the profitability of capital is at the expense of innovation, investment in research and development, employment, wages and skills renewal. the european union needs an ambitious, environmentally efficient and green industrial strategy to restore production capacity and create highly skilled and well-paid jobs.

in writing. ‒ the the aim of this resolution is to define the european parliament's position ahead of the upcoming cop22 conference in marrakech in november. the resolution focuses, among other things, on the need to ratify the paris agreement, the european union's climate ambitions before 2020, as well as the need to reduce co2 emissions. the resolution welcomes the paris agreement as a successful milestone in the fight against climate change. it is an ambitious, balanced, fair and legally binding agreement.
in writing. ‒ by ratifying the paris agreement, the european parliament has sent a clear signal about the importance of climate change. it aims to limit the rise in global temperature to a maximum of two degrees celsius by the end of the century compared with the pre-industrial period. the agreement will enter into force 30 days after it has been ratified by at least 55 states representing at least 55% of global emissions. to date, 62 countries have signed it, representing 52% of their emissions. the marrakesh conference should contribute to finding a way to start implementing the commitments of the paris agreement in individual countries. addressing the need for climate change affects all sectors of the economy with major implications for the quality of the environment and the protection of health and life on our planet in general.
in writing. the 22nd conference of the parties to the united nations framework convention on climate change (cop 22) will be held in marrakech, morocco, from 7 to 18 november 2016. the main points of discussion will be: the role of non-state actors, the need for a comprehensive effort across all sectors, the reduction of co2 emissions, resilience to climate change through adaptation, climate diplomacy, etc. the paris agreement on climate change is a successful milestone in the fight against climate change, and is also significant for its multilateral nature. the approval of the ratification of this agreement by the european parliament on 4 october 2016 will help to accelerate its entry into force. however, many areas remain unresolved. a global policy framework for regulating aviation and maritime transport is needed to reduce emissions from international aviation and maritime transport, which was absent from the paris agreement. the union and its member states should continue to be actively involved in the so-called 'coalition of high ambition', including by supporting the moroccan presidency in its focus on the contribution of renewable energy sources and adaptation measures in the global fight against the negative phenomena of climate change. ambitious energy efficiency targets in the eu can help to achieve an ambitious climate target while reducing the risk of carbon leakage. finally, energy efficiency and renewable sources are among the main objectives of the eu's energy union.
in writing. ‒ the according to 2014 scientific evidence, warming of the climate system is undeniable, climate change is occurring, and human activity is the main cause of the observed warming since the mid-20th century. the far-reaching and significant impacts of climate change are already evident in natural and human systems on all continents and in the oceans. the un climate change conference in marrakech should follow up on the paris agreement, in particular in the area of climate finance and capacity building. the eu has the ability, but also the obligation, to lead by example and to start working immediately to align its climate and energy objectives with the agreed international target of limiting the increase in average global temperature to below 2°c, while also aiming to limit the increase to 1,5°c. the intensification of climate change mitigation actions in the period before 2020 is a prerequisite for achieving the long-term goals of the paris agreement and a key element for assessing the success of cop 22 in marrakech.
in writing. ‒ the european union is coming to cop 22 with concrete proposals that strike a balance between the need to slow down global warming and the need not to jeopardise industrial production and jobs. modernisation and digitalisation in industry, motoring and agriculture are tools that will play a key role in the fight against pollution of the planet.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this resolution is to set out the european parliament's priorities for the forthcoming 22nd conference of the parties to the unfccc, to be held in november in morocco. like the paris conference, the 22nd will address the need to keep global warming below 2°c and ideally below 1.5°c. to this end, the resolution proposes a number of ways to achieve this ambitious target, ranging from decarbonisation to preventing forest degradation. overall, it calls on the commission and the member states to step up efforts to achieve the objectives and also to encourage partner countries to get involved in their implementation. the report also addresses the need for adaptation measures for the population in relation to climate change. however, as the report also contained several articles which i could not support, such as the introduction of a financial transaction tax, i voted against it in the final vote.
in writing. ‒ regulation (ec) no 1935/2004 covers substances that come into contact with foodstuffs in the course of their normal daily use. it is essential that these substances do not, as such, cause harm to health or react with food in a way that may be harmful to health or have an adverse effect on the composition of food. for most food contact materials there is no generally accepted regulation at union level. materials have to meet certain criteria, and there are currently four that are covered by eu standards: ceramics, plastics, regenerated cellulose and active and intelligent materials. the other substances are subject to different standards in different member states. a study on this subject was prepared by the european parliament's research service. in the light of these data, the preparation of the regulation began, identifying four main areas: risk assessment, traceability and enforcement and control of compliance. the risk assessment of harmonised substances is the responsibility of the european food safety authority (efsa), but there are no adequate financial resources for this. they therefore recommend that efsa should be funded for these activities. however, efsa does not have competence for non-harmonised substances. this is why a uniform set of rules is needed to which those involved in the field can adhere. i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ the in addition, evidence gathered in recent months indicates that there is an urgent need to address current shortcomings in the implementation and enforcement of existing legislation. this regulation lays down general safety requirements applicable to all possible materials and articles intended to come into contact with food. so far, specific measures have been adopted at eu level for only four food contact materials. these were specifically plastics, including recycled plastics, ceramics, regenerated cellulose and active and intelligent materials. this regulation should extend that number to 17 materials. action at european union level is necessary to address the absence of specific european union measures and the deficiencies in the areas of risk assessment, traceability, compliance and control.
in writing. ‒ the food security is a fundamental human right. it also covers the safety of food contact materials. the regulation in force on these materials lays down general safety requirements and also provides for the possibility of adopting specific measures for the 17 materials listed in the annex to the framework regulation. such measures have so far been adopted for only four materials: plastics (including recycled plastic), ceramics, regenerated cellulose and active and intelligent materials. the evaluation of the implementation of the regulation at eu level has identified shortcomings in the implementation of the legislation and the need for further binding harmonisation in the area of food contact materials. i support the proposal that asks the commission to intensify research and risk assessment of materials, in effective cooperation and coordination with the member states and the organisations concerned, and using new modern practices and knowledge. it is necessary to introduce a declaration of conformity and to increase the traceability of materials from third countries in order to ensure a uniform high level of health protection.
in writing. food contact materials (fcms) are used on a daily basis and are subject to legally binding rules at eu level (regulation (ec) no 1935/2004). until now, specific measures at eu level have only covered 4 fcms: plastics (including recycled plastic), ceramics, regenerated cellulose and active and intelligent materials. for other fcms, member states may adopt specific measures at national level. this leads to the development of different standards for product safety, as the specific measures taken by one member state may differ from those taken by another member state. in addition, the absence of specific eu measures for other fcms creates barriers in the internal market, the associated increased costs are often borne by the consumer, and thereby a loss of competitiveness and innovation. further harmonisation of non-harmonised materials would be a positive step. priority would be given to materials that pose a specific risk to human health and are in higher demand on the eu market (such as paper and cardboard, including recycled paper and cardboard, coatings, printing inks and adhesives). in the interest of greater efficiency, it is also necessary to address the shortcomings in the implementation of existing legislation and to strengthen the funding of the european food safety authority (efsa), which plays a key role in the risk assessment of fcms.

in writing. ‒ the food contact materials regulation (fcpm) sets out the general safety conditions for all materials that come into contact with food. i supported the resolution because it comes with proposals that should encourage business operators to develop safe, reusable and recyclable (sre) products, thereby supporting the european union's (eu) efforts to create a more efficient circular economy. as the report states, there are 13 materials that are not regulated at eu level and that could be subject to specific measures. i believe that, given the high prevalence of these materials on the eu market and the risk they pose to human health, and in order to preserve the single market for msmes and food products, the commission should start prioritising the development of specific eu measures for materials such as paper, cardboard, varnishes and paints, metals and alloys, printing inks and adhesives without delay. it regrets that the role of food contact materials in food contamination is generally underestimated and that there is a lack of information on human exposure to chemicals. i therefore expect member states to involve all relevant stakeholders in the process of designing specific safety requirements for msp and to increase the frequency and effectiveness of official controls.
in writing. ‒ the quality and safety of food is not only affected by its composition, but also by the substances, including packaging, that come into contact with it in the process of its marketing. in cooperation with efsa and echa, we want to identify these substances, assess the potential risk to consumers and take measures to eliminate any undesirable consequences of their use.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report by ms schaldemos on the implementation of the regulation on materials in contact with food. the regulation deals with materials that we come into contact with every day without being aware of their possible effects. these are mainly kitchen utensils, food packaging and cutlery. these materials may react differently and transfer their constituents to foodstuffs in contact with them. it is therefore necessary to subject such materials to strict safety requirements. however, surprisingly, the possible effects of the various combinations of these materials on human health have not yet been properly investigated. in the implementation report to the regulation, we therefore invited the commission to consider imposing specific safety requirements on all 17 material categories and member states to properly control compliance with these requirements. at the same time, the report looked at how best to assess risks and improve existing legislation in the light of results. and although this regulation will in practice mean a slight additional harmonisation of european union legislation, i think the protection of human health is an invaluable counterpart.
in writing. ‒ the european commission produces an annual report, this year for the 32nd time, on the application of eu law. the report in question covers the year 2014. several parliamentary committees, including the committee on petitions (peti), also delivered opinions on the 2014 report. in addition to infringement proceedings, eu pilot also detects and resolves a number of cases. the latter involves less formalities and provides for a quicker settlement of breaches of union law, which can benefit both the member state concerned and, above all, those affected by the legislation, union citizens and businesses. as the head of the pp in peti, i pointed out that petitions also play a role in the application of eu law in the member states, with a significant proportion of petitions helping to monitor and identify shortcomings in the transposition and application of eu law in the member states. the petition data show that there is a preponderance of alleged breaches of eu law in the following areas: fundamental rights, including the rights of persons belonging to minorities and persons with disabilities, discrimination mainly on the basis of nationality , internal market, free movement, transport, environment, education, employment and health. it is important that the commission also address fundamental rights complaints in an equal manner.
in writing. ‒ the the european commission's annual report on monitoring the application of european union law has once again produced some interesting findings and insights. as in the past, most cases of failure by member states to fulfil their obligations fall within the areas of environment, transport and internal market and services. it is also welcome that the report findings show that the number of formal infringement procedures has decreased over the last 5 years, which may indicate the progress made under the eu pilot project. however, the european parliament still has very limited access to the information processed in the context of the project in question and it is therefore very difficult to determine to what extent the reduction in the number of formal infringement procedures actually reflects better compliance with union law by member states rather than compromise solutions between the commission and the member states. despite a number of positive results that have undoubtedly been achieved in the application of european union law by member states, it remains clear that we need to continue to take further steps to achieve an even higher level of transparency.
in writing. ‒ the commission's audit of the effective application of union law has revealed shortcomings, in particular in the areas of the environment, transport, the internal market and services. in 2008, the eu launched the 'eu pilot' project as a method to improve assistance to citizens and businesses in applying eu law. it aims to reduce the number of infringement proceedings. however, the number of proceedings cannot reflect the actual respect and application of the law, for example also because of the persistent lack of awareness of the possibilities for citizens and legal persons to lodge complaints. i agree with the proposal that the ep should set up a separate process for monitoring the application of union law, which would also draw on the work and expertise of parliament's standing committees in the relevant areas.
in writing. this year's annual report on the application of eu law in the individual member states of the union highlighted shortcomings, particularly in the areas of the environment, transport and the internal market. if the european commission considers that european law is not being applied sufficiently in the territory of individual member states, an eu pilot is activated, which initiates a dialogue between the commission and the country concerned. the latter has the obligation to explain why the discrepancy occurs and to make a subsequent correction. as it is an exchange of messages between the member state concerned and the commission, it is rather problematic for the european parliament to have a sufficient overview of how many eu 'pilots' have actually been launched and what the de facto state of application of union law is. therefore, i believe that it would be appropriate for the commission to provide the european parliament with more adequate access to transparent information also in this context. i'm reporting in support.

in writing. ‒ i supported the ep motion for a resolution on monitoring the application of union law annual report 2014. the report states that the environment, transport and the internal market and services remained the policy areas with the highest number of infringement cases opened in 2014. the report therefore shows that the enforcement of union law is not sufficiently transparent. the proper implementation and application of union law is the primary responsibility of the member states, which must fully respect the fundamental values and principles enshrined in the treaties and the eu charter of fundamental rights when implementing union law. only the timely and correct transposition of union law into national law and a clear national legal framework should become a priority for member states in order to prevent infringements of union law while bringing the desired benefits to individuals and businesses through the efficient and effective application of union law. the social partners and civil society organisations have an important role to play in monitoring and reporting on shortcomings in the transposition and application of union law by the member states.

in writing. ‒ the the 2014 annual report shall cover the monitoring of the application of union law. it contains in particular statistics on breaches of union law. the report notes that the number of these infringement complaints has decreased, while also suggesting a possible solution to the persisting number of complaints relating to the environment, transport or the single market, which could be a longer implementation period. according to the report, it is precisely unrealistic deadlines for implementing legislation that can be the cause of infringements by member states. the report also looks at the benefits of the interinstitutional agreement on better law-making and condemns the practice of 'pricing out' legislation. on the other hand, the report also touched upon such areas as the calls addressed to the commission for a legislative proposal on european administrative procedural law. although i do not share these challenges, i have decided to support the report as a whole.

in writing. ‒ i agree that the european parliament is asking the commission to withdraw its draft implementing decision on the placing on the market of genetically modified maize bt11 for cultivation. i consider that the commission implementing decision is not in accordance with union law as it is incompatible with the objectives of directive 2001/18/ec of the european parliament and of the council, which is in accordance with the precautionary principle with a view to approximating the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the member states and protecting human health and the environment in the event of deliberate release into the environment of genetically modified organisms for any purpose other than placing on the market within the community and placing genetically modified organisms on the market as or in products within the community. that is why i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ i supported the objection against the commission's implementing decision to renew the authorisation for the cultivation of genetically modified maize bt11. an application for the cultivation of this maize was submitted in france as early as 1996. however, maize bt11 contains a protein that guarantees tolerance to the herbicide glufosinate-ammonium, which is classified as toxic for reproduction and whose authorisation expires in 2017. moreover, the cultivation of this maize is banned in many countries. since scientific evidence indicates that released pollen may spread across borders, the precautionary principle should be respected. if such gmos were to be cross-bred and spread, there could be a threat to biodiversity and risks for farmers. since the current methods of monitoring the planting of gmo maize cannot guarantee a sufficient level of protection of human life and health, the commission should not issue such decisions on gmos. i therefore take the view that the commission should withdraw its implementing decision and present a new legislative proposal which will better take into account the specificities of the cultivation of gmo crops.
in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament's objection to the commission's implementing decision authorising the placing on the market of products containing genetically modified maize. my opinion on genetically modified organisms remains unchanged, as there is not yet sufficient evidence regarding their safety. nor do we have sufficient information on their effects on the environment. that is why i agree with the view that, in the circumstances, where the risk assessment is not thorough and complete, the european commission has exceeded its powers in this implementing regulation, let alone acted in accordance with the precautionary principle, which is absolutely necessary in cases where human health may be at risk.

in writing. in 2009, dow agrosciences europe submitted to the competent authority of the netherlands an application to place on the market foods, food ingredients and feed containing, consisting of, or produced from 281-24-236 × 3006-210-23 × mon 88913 cotton. this genetically modified cotton provides, among other things, tolerance to glyphosate-based herbicides. however, in 2015, glyphosate was listed by the world health organisation for cancer research (a specialised agency of the who) as a substance with probable carcinogenicity in humans. under eu law, all authorised gmos must meet traceability and labelling requirements. the aim is to provide consumers with information and freedom of choice and to enable member states to take appropriate action if an unforeseen adverse reaction is detected. in this case, although the cultivation of the gmo takes place within the territory of a member state, its trade is cross-border in nature, so that a national prohibition on sale and use, as proposed by the commission, would not be enforceable without the reintroduction of border controls on imported goods. the draft commission implementing decision authorising the placing on the market of products containing genetically modified cotton under regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 of the european parliament and of the council goes beyond the implementing powers provided for in this regulation. the commission should therefore withdraw its implementing decision and submit a new proposal to amend that regulation.

the union does not need a pact on democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. all this is in the treaties to which the member states are bound. we also have a mechanism in the treaties to deal with cases where a member state does not respect its commitment. the commission is the guardian of the treaties. not the un, the oecd, the council of europe, or professional and sectoral associations. if the commission becomes convinced that a member state has infringed the treaty, it should refer the matter to the european court of justice. we can talk about whether the commission is using its powers well. whether it prefers to avoid more substantial disputes out of caution or, conversely, whether it is not overly sensitive to minor differences in views on democracy. we may ask why the commission has not so far used article 2 of the eu treaty as a legal basis in its action against a member state. alternatively, ask for its opinion on the possibility of drawing up a so-called 'joint action' to address a possible systemic problem in the area of democracy and the rule of law in a member state. that kind of debate would make sense. but let's not invent new structures, meetings, reports and committees that will only result in lots of paperwork and hours of empty talk at taxpayers' expense. i can't support that idea.

in writing. ‒ i supported the draft recommendation on the council position with a view to adopting a regulation amending the rules on rail transport statistics as regards the collection of data on goods, persons and accidents. the aim of this proposal is in particular to simplify the rules for the production of rail transport statistics and thus to reduce the burden on member states in this area. in this case, several attempts have already been made in the process of adopting new rules. i believe that the original requirements, as submitted by the commission, were not set in accordance with the principle of proportionality. they required the collection of a volume of data which would have burdened the member states without the resulting statistics demonstrating significant efficiency. of course, it is possible that they would contribute a little to better planning and a higher level of rail transport, but i do not think that the effort that member states would have to put into producing these statistics would be comparable to the result. that's why i didn't agree with the first draft of the ordinance. however, after the negotiations on the final text resulted in the current compromise that no additional data would be collected, i decided to support the report.

in writing. ‒ the single market holds enormous potential for the future of the european union. the problem is that the rules are supposed to be the same for all participants, but the penalties for breaking the rules vary considerably. without an integrated enforcement procedure including sanctions, it is not possible for the customs administrations of the member states to act in a uniform manner, in particular given the significant differences between the sanctioning systems of the member states. this is increasingly relevant in view of the growth of electronic commerce, in particular by micro-enterprises and individuals, who require greater legal certainty as regards the consistency of systems and greater transparency in the handling of infringements by the various customs authorities. in order to ensure that penalties are effective, proportionate and dissuasive, we need to leave the door open for customs authorities to assess the relevant circumstances and, on that basis, to decide on the most appropriate penalty, as this has proven to be an effective means of reducing the occurrence of non-compliance.
in writing. ‒ the customs union and trade policy are exclusive eu competence. the persisting differences in customs administration and approaches to the application and enforcement of customs rules in individual member states cause a certain amount of mistrust among member states. in the interest of legal certainty for all the actors concerned, it is therefore necessary to establish a uniform system for the application of the rules, including in the area of sanctions. the single system will help to increase compliance and respect for the applicable standards. i therefore support the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the union legal framework for customs infringements and sanctions, which provides for a uniform mechanism of sanctions for customs infringements.
in writing. ‒ although the customs union is considered one of the foundations of the european union and the cornerstone of the single market, there is still no uniform approach to customs enforcement, including sanctions. it is welcome that the rules for enforcing customs rules, including sanctions, are the same across the eu, but i consider it a serious shortcoming that there is no uniform approach to enforcing these rules. i regret that these differences are distorting conditions for many economic operators in the eu and are also felt in the area of equal conditions, which is the basis of the internal market. i think it is essential to correct and address the problems arising from the disparity of systems governing customs offences and other sanctions within the european market. although we postponed the final vote, i believe that the new provisions will enable us not only to strengthen customs rules and sanctions, but also to eliminate the distortion of the internal market by applying a uniform set of rules in all eu member states. i expect the customs administrations of the member states to act in a uniform manner in cases of customs infringement, thus achieving the same level of control results and promoting legitimate trade.
in writing. ‒ the european single market is based on a common customs policy towards third countries. to protect it, it is important to have effective and rapidly applicable common rules, including sanction mechanisms for infringements.
in writing. ‒ the i did not support the report on the draft directive on the union legal framework for customs infringements and sanctions. this directive is intended to allow the imposition of non-criminal sanctions for infringements of customs law by approximating the laws of the member states. the directive was originally designed in response to the fact that the different regimes of the member states could cause circumvention, as importers could selectively choose the country with the lowest sanctions as the country of their official activity. however, in my view, this potential circumvention is already sufficiently addressed in the current customs code and i therefore believe that the adoption of further legislation is unnecessary and contrary to the efforts to simplify european union law. that is why i do not think that the new directive would bring any innovative solution and therefore any added value. furthermore, i consider that several of its elements are contrary to european union law.

in writing. ‒ despite the highly sophisticated legal frameworks at international and european level, corruption in many european countries is becoming a critical point for their economic and democratic development. i find it particularly worrying that countries with opaque relations and high levels of corruption perform worse and their economies are more vulnerable. unfortunately, this unwanted phenomenon undermines public trust in public and democratic institutions, increases inequalities that disproportionately affect the poorest and most vulnerable, reinforces violence and insecurity, and reduces the effectiveness of development aid. i am deeply sorry that the most important international conventions and initiatives aimed at combating corruption and illicit financial flows do not produce concrete results at the implementation stage. i supported the resolution because i see organised crime as a global threat and as such it requires a joint and coordinated response from the eu and its member states. i expect member states to apply even better the legal instruments already adopted at european and international level to combat corruption in order to fight it more effectively.
in writing. ‒ the fight against corruption must be one of the priorities of the european union's internal policy. we need to control the management of european resources thoroughly and effectively, especially at national level. the identification and tracing of financial flows that may derive from such activities is also an important part of the fight against corruption.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution on the fight against corruption and organised crime, as these illegal activities pose a serious threat to the efficient functioning of the european economy. it is important that we guard against all forms of this organised crime because ultimately it is taxpayers' money that is lost. we must recognise that these crimes are in most cases of a cross-border nature and that closer cooperation between national authorities is therefore needed to combat organised crime. police and judicial cooperation at eu level must not only be self-evident and effective, but also free from lengthy bureaucratic procedures. at the same time, we must not forget prevention in schools and the formation of young people in the spirit of honesty and justice. finally, i also welcome the social dimension of this resolution, which also considers the families of the victims and their compensation.
in writing. ‒ i did not support the resolution on the fight against corruption and the follow-up to the resolution of the special committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering (crim). this special committee was set up in 2012 following a report on organised crime adopted by the european parliament. the main task of this committee is to analyse organised crime in europe and to evaluate the implementation of european policies in this area. the current report on the fight against corruption analysed in particular the harmfulness of organised crime, corruption and money laundering and suggested possible ways to combat this crime. i agree that the report encouraged member states to exchange information more efficiently, to cooperate better in law enforcement, to ensure whistleblower protection and to ensure the transparency of the european funds. on the other hand, i think the report has gone too far on some issues. it has also addressed, for example, the legalization of soft drugs as one of the solutions to drug crime or the redistribution of money from crime for social purposes. in view of these reservations, i therefore decided to vote against it.
