in writing. ‒ the the legal framework for the protection of migrants in the eu is given by national, eu and international law, by which the member states are bound. the office of the united nations high commissioner for refugees estimates that there are at least 10 million stateless persons, with more than 65 million refugees and displaced persons affected by instability linked to humanitarian crises, particularly in developing countries. given current global developments, migration poses both a high security risk and an infiltration of illegal criminal activity in the form of trafficking in human beings, smuggling, exploitation at work. at the same time, there is a population shift from eu countries, which will have a negative impact on brain drain. migration thus affects the economic and social situation of the countries from which migrants come and, at the same time, of the countries to which they go. i support the proposal which stresses the need to respect human rights and at the same time to ensure that member states follow the procedures for granting asylum in a way that protects the security, economic and financial interests of the union countries.
in writing. migration is a frequently discussed phenomenon today, influenced by a variety of factors, whether it's economic, social and political conditions, or conditions related to work, violence, security, the deteriorating environment in a country. the rights of migrants are enshrined in international conventions and recognition of these rights is essential. migrants have the right not to be returned to a country where they are at risk of ill-treatment and torture; their rights of access to justice must be respected. women and children, the elderly and the disabled are particularly vulnerable among migrants and, more frequently, among refugees. individual member states should establish comprehensive national migration policies, with a gender-sensitive approach, on migrants and refugees in the interest of their safety. the right to education, work and family life promotes the self-reliance of migrants and refugees and their faster integration. a well-organised, concrete response by states to migration can be an opportunity, both for individuals and for countries. migration is a dynamic element, and if europe can manage it effectively, it can counterbalance the demographic crisis that many countries are gradually facing. on the other hand, europe must focus on helping to address the social, economic and political crises that trigger migration, while helping to stem the flow of migrants towards the eu's borders.

in writing. ‒ the corporate human rights abuses are a significant problem, despite the fact that all companies in the world have an obligation to respect human rights and to incorporate fundamental human rights principles and values into their activities. this is why we have addressed this issue in the report on corporate responsibility for serious human rights violations in third countries. in it, we reminded corporations that in today's globalised and internationalised business environment, their role in protecting human rights is even greater and that they should be able to take responsibility for any violation of them. we also called on them to provide an effective remedy in case of damage and to guarantee that infringements would not be repeated. i believe that this is a subject which deserves due attention and that is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament's report is a response to the european commission's communication of february this year, when it presented the european union's strategy for liquefied natural gas and its storage. with global lng stocks set to increase dramatically in the future and its price set to fall significantly as a result of oversupply, it will be very important for member states that are dependent on a single supplier to look for an alternative in the future. in the future, we must focus on efficient and renewable sources of investment in liquefied gas in the european union, but we must also not forget that it has potential and uses as a fossil fuel.
in writing. the eu lng and gas storage strategy is part of the package of legislative proposals on the union's energy policy presented by the european commission in early 2016. the strategy sets out objectives to be achieved as part of building a resilient energy union that is sufficiently competitive with the american, asian and arab markets and ensures secure, affordable and environmentally friendly energy. the lng market is not yet sufficiently developed within the eu, and it is therefore necessary for the union to implement plans to complete the missing infrastructure or to use the existing infrastructure efficiently. the situation is similar with regard to gas storage making this area more efficient is the ambition of several of the projects of common interest (pci) packages that use eu strategic funds. if i understand the strategy's focus to promote the development and application of renewable energy sources correctly, since they are to account for 100% of european production by 2100, natural gas is seen as merely a transition from heavy fossil fuels to cleaner energy sources. i support the report.
in writing. ‒ the in february this year, the commission presented a strategy for liquefied natural gas and gas storage, which follows estimates that global liquefied natural gas supply is expected to double in the coming years. as many eu countries still do not have diversified their energy sources, i supported this strategy. lng gas can provide an opportunity for the eu to improve the security of gas supply and increase resilience in cases of gas shortages. on the other hand, member states should be aware that lng is only a temporary solution. in the long term, europe will need to reduce its dependence on gas consumption in order to meet the eu's climate and energy targets as committed in the paris climate agreement. the lng strategy itself envisages that the commission will support the establishment of gas storage centres, for example in the mediterranean area. investments should therefore be made in lng and gas infrastructure. lng is also considered as an alternative fuel that could replace conventional fossil fuels in road transport as well as in maritime transport. but first, europe must be ready for the increase in lng supplies. it will therefore be necessary to improve the use of existing gas infrastructure and to prepare the ground for its expansion.

in writing. ‒ the report on the european union strategy for liquefied natural gas and gas storage is largely related to the challenge we are facing more and more, namely to ensure a resilient energy union. ideally, member states should have more energy sources and should not be dependent on a single foreign supplier. that is why the report raises questions about liquefied natural gas. this can not only bring more energy diversity but also an environmentally sustainable energy source as an alternative to traditional energy sources. that is why i think we should at least make a qualified debate on this subject and carefully weigh all its pros and cons while ensuring the highest level of environmental protection.
in writing. ‒ fisheries control in europe is essential to achieve the common objectives of the cfp. unfortunately, there are very large differences in controls, procedures and strategies across member states and regions. the mandate and funding of the european fisheries control agency are insufficient, which means that it cannot carry out more ambitious projects. this report should therefore serve as the european commission's minimum for the reform of the control regulation it is preparing for 2017. the european commission should focus on simplifying legislation, and on setting clear and understandable control standards and applying modern technology, as well as better coordination and transparency.
in writing. ‒ fisheries controls affect not only the economy, economies and budgets of the member states concerned. the report clearly shows the need for unification of legislation on the control reference framework, the training of fisheries inspectors, the introduction of uniform control methodologies and procedures, including the use of modern technologies, and the establishment of uniform penalties. it is important to do so in a coordinated manner and to streamline operations from the point of view of data collection.
in writing. there are wide variations in the scope of controls, practices and strategies in fisheries across eu member states. it is necessary to identify shortcomings in the application of the rules that create a feeling of injustice among fishermen and to propose solutions to improve the harmonisation of controls in the common fisheries policy, which is one of the most integrated policies in europe. the report makes a number of observations on the obstacles to harmonisation, but also contains proposals for the future which need to be put into practice if harmonisation is to be effective. these include simplification of community legislation, the development of a single reference framework for controls, and the training of inspectors and fishermen, which varies from one member state to another. it is necessary to ensure effective consultation of the advisory committees, which currently exist only pro forma, to provide financial support for research and innovation, thus contributing to the overall modernisation of control policy. last but not least, data collection is necessary for controls, as it allows strategies to be defined, efficiency to be optimised and the fisheries, vessels and practices that pose the greatest risk to be better targeted.
in writing. ‒ this resolution underlines, among other things, the need to ensure effective control of fishing activities in order to guarantee the sustainable use of living marine resources and to maintain a level playing field between eu fleets. it also calls for a monitoring, information transfer and data analysis system that is compatible across the union. i support this resolution. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ while the current control regulation, in combination with the unreported and unregulated (un) fisheries regulation, has brought about a significant improvement, there is a real injustice, or one felt by fishermen, that even after taking into account possible regional differences, there are significant differences between member states in the application of european legislation, especially those based on the control regulation. although each member state has its own distinctive legal system and different administrative and judicial structures, these systems often give rise to different types of irregularities and injustices between member states. i supported the resolution because i think it is right that the committee on fisheries should address the shortcomings that give rise to a feeling of injustice and, on the basis of the proposals and measures adopted, improve the harmonisation of controls in the common fisheries policy, which is one of the most integrated policies in europe. i believe that simplifying and improving union legislation and reducing the administrative burden will lead to better detection and punishment of infringements of the common fisheries policy.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report by mrs thomas on fisheries controls in europe. in fact, at present, due to inconsistent legislation, there are significant differences in the way fisheries controls are carried out. in some countries these checks are carried out superficially, in others by different authorities, and in others with excessive rigor. as a result, there is discrimination against fishermen and fishing vessels and complaints about the procedures of the various authorities. this is why the report addressed the question of how these controls can be achieved at a uniform level and without such marked differences. i also supported the resolution because it is necessary to control fishing activities in order to achieve the highest possible environmental protection and sustainable fishing as such. i also welcomed the report's call for simplification of european legislation and a reduction in administrative burdens.

in writing. transport infrastructure in central and eastern europe has undergone a major modernisation since the pre-accession period. however, the projects that restored links with the countries of western europe were the focus of the improvement. the region is currently crossed by 5 transport corridors: north sea-baltic; baltic-adriatic; mediterranean; rhineland-palatinate and orient-eastern mediterranean. quality transport links have a major impact on economic activity in europe and the quality of life of its citizens. this is particularly important to highlight in the case of central and eastern european countries, where labour migration to more western countries is a frequent phenomenon. the shortcomings related to the accessibility and interconnection of transport infrastructure need to be overcome in order to preserve economic growth and job opportunities for citizens and businesses (especially in rural and border areas) to the greatest extent possible. otherwise, these regions will continue to suffer from population outflows. improving transport infrastructure is a financially demanding process, so it is crucial to intensify coordination at all stages of transport policy and project planning between the central and eastern european member states and the european commission and to make effective use of all available synergies in funding from the different funds offered by the eu (esi funds, eib and ebrd funds, fsi). those transport policy issues that cannot be tackled by member states individually could be addressed by cooperation within macro-regional strategies. i vote in favour of the motion.

in writing. ‒ member states, together with the union, adhere to the principles of the rule of law, democracy and the protection and respect of fundamental rights. these values are enshrined in a number of international conventions and treaties, which have different legal binding force. some are binding on all member states, and some, such as the eu charter of fundamental rights, apply to certain member states (the united kingdom and poland) only to the extent that they do not exceed their national standard of human rights protection. events in some member states have rightly raised the question of establishing a minimum uniform legal protection of these values, including procedures for possible breaches. i am convinced that such a regulation must not infringe the sovereignty of the member states, must comply with the law in force and must be the result of the consensus of all the member states. all the competent institutions, the commission, the council and other european and national bodies must be actively involved in tackling this fundamental problem.
in writing. the european union is founded on the principles of democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights, it is a community of values, but it remains a community of sovereign states, founded on the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality. i consider that the provisions of the proposed eu mechanism for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights infringe the first principle. the proposal leaves the member states' investigative powers to a new group of 'independent experts', which includes, among others, international organisations such as the un, the osce and the oecd, which already have a mandate to monitor the situation of human rights and democracy. implementing the mechanism would be a duplication and a waste of money. in addition, the pact can be an instrument for the eu's political dominance over the member states. it should be possible, he argued, for states to be affected on the basis of the opinion of 'independent experts' if their populations want to protect themselves from decisions of the eu institutions in particularly sensitive areas, by means of referendums or constitutional amendments. the eu must respect the national identity of the member states, which lies in their fundamental political and constitutional systems, including regional and local self-government. that is why i am voting against the report.

in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament's motion for a resolution with recommendations to the commission on the establishment of an eu mechanism for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. the european union has enshrined democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights among its fundamental principles and objectives, which are enshrined in all the treaties and are also among the criteria for eu membership. at the same time, the eu has sufficient instruments to enforce its laws and treaties. the commission may require member states to adjust their budgets, public health systems or tax rulings to comply with eu law. however, there are still major gaps and in practice these instruments are often limited in scope, inadequate and ineffective. it is therefore necessary to adopt a framework that will allow the eu to address not only breaches of specific eu legislation but also cases of serious threats to democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. the proposed interinstitutional agreement aims to lay down measures to facilitate cooperation between the eu institutions and its member states.

four years ago, youth unemployment in europe reached a record high. as socialists and democrats, we then launched a successful campaign to guarantee jobs for young people. to ensure that every young person, within four months of leaving school or losing his or her job, has either the opportunity and offer of a job, or a national or international traineeship, or the opportunity to learn a subject needed by the labour market, or to continue further education. in my country, slovakia, 86% of those who took part in it stayed in employment even after the funding was cut, and we reduced youth unemployment by more than one third! in the eu, there were millions of young people who were helped in this way. last november, at the conciliation procedure on the budget, we managed to reach an agreement in a joint statement by the ep, the council and the commission that the council would support the continuation of the project if it was evaluated and proved successful. i called my labour minister directly from the negotiations, from the conciliation procedure: "how much time do you need for evaluation?" "until christmas!" he said. europe ended up taking 10 months longer than what individual countries were actually able to do. today we have the result of the evaluation confirming the success of the project. in his speech in september, commission president juncker expressed his support for young people. i thank you, madam vice-president of the commission, for your very positive attitude and for looking for a way to make this happen. the european council last week also supported strengthening eu programmes to support young people. i therefore believe that the council will support the european parliament's proposal in the conciliation procedure and that the project to promote youth employment will continue next year. after all, employment is really our top priority.
i would like to thank the commissioner for his reply. the european central bank has already bought up more than eur 1 400 billion of public debt. this is in clear contradiction with article 123 of the eu treaty, which prohibits state funding. at the same time, the european central bank has reduced interest rates to zero, creating the ideal conditions for ever-new debt: unlimited money that costs nothing. so it is not surprising that large countries like france, italy, spain, are always taking on new debts, and you tolerate this! the commission is doing almost nothing about these new debts. this combination of a printing press, no interest and more and more debt is leading straight to disaster. it may take another five or 20 years, but one day this destructive policy will break our common currency.
several of my colleagues have expressed dissatisfaction with the last council meeting and i understand this feeling, which stems from unfulfilled expectations. as manfred weber said, the commission has proposals, this parliament is ready to approve them, but what is missing is the ability of the member states to agree. and then to act with the determination that not only we, but above all the citizens of the european union, expect of them. but at the same time, i would like to remind you of one important thing: an agreement between states rarely comes about overnight. when i listened to the reports of president tusk and president juncker, i perceived two messages. the first was that the member states were not prepared to agree on everything. that's certainly a shame. but at the same time, it was clear from these reports that the heads of government of the member states had met in a working meeting, that their negotiations reflected the current problems facing europe; they would simply have to meet again, several more times, before reaching an agreement. ladies and gentlemen, good deals take time. let's give ourselves that time and let's give the council that time. because it is these hasty compromises that have caused most of europe's current problems.
the european council's role is to steer europe. without helping africa create jobs, we cannot address the causes of migration. the united nations projects that the continent's population will grow from 1.2 billion today to 4 billion by the end of the century. it would be a development disaster, it would be a food shortage, it would be a migration disaster. the greatest favor we can do for africa, but also for europe, is to protect children from malaria, eliminate ebola, stimulate investment and job creation, and allow girls to go to secondary school. with regard to trade agreements with canada and the united states: these agreements are generally opposed by national politicians. they can't hide behind the european commission, so they leave the public space to the populists. leaders must have the courage to clearly articulate why we need free trade, what the positive aspects of free trade are.

in writing. ‒ the the main objective of this directive is to improve the accessibility and accessibility of public sector websites and their content for citizens with a certain type of disability, but also for the elderly population. these measures will help in particular visually impaired or severely visually impaired persons, as well as persons with hearing problems or certain mobility difficulties. the european union must bear in mind that the digitisation of society is proceeding at a tremendous pace and that we live in a digital world. all citizens should have equal opportunities in terms of access to information. this directive will bring positive results in building a digital society.
in writing. ‒ the in the context of digitalisation and the spread of electronic services, the accessibility requirements for websites and mobile applications of public sector bodies are increasing. by providing such services, the public sector can communicate better, more efficiently and flexibly with the public, informing them about its services and activities and thus increasing its transparency and accountability. this form of communication is particularly important for persons with disabilities, who are thus guaranteed the possibility of obtaining the necessary information and a better chance of an active civic life. at the same time, there is a wide scope for companies engaged in e-services and the development of websites and mobile applications. the need to unify and harmonise the minimum requirements for the provision and creation of these services arises, and i therefore support the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the accessibility of public sector bodies' websites and mobile applications.
in writing. ‒ the the current fast-growing market for making digital products and services more accessible encompasses a wide range of economic operators, including developers of websites or software tools for creating, managing and testing websites or mobile applications. several member states have so far adopted measures based on internationally used guidelines for the creation of accessible websites, but unfortunately technical differences at national level and divergent national rules limit the potential benefits of sharing experiences with partners at national and international level. i supported the current motion for a resolution because i believe that it is necessary to ensure that the websites and mobile applications of public sector bodies are more accessible on the basis of common accessibility requirements and to put an end to the fragmentation of the internal market. i believe that by approximating national measures at union level on the basis of agreed requirements for the accessibility of websites and mobile applications of public sector bodies, we will remove all obstacles to the functioning of the internal market and reduce the costs for public sector bodies and other entities to procure products and services related to the accessibility of websites and mobile applications.
in writing. ‒ we are interested in digitising citizens' communication with public authorities and in using all the tools that new technologies offer us to save costs and improve the quality of services. in this effort, we must not forget citizens with disabilities, who do not have the same access to and control over websites and mobile applications as the majority of the population. we are therefore introducing a rule that all forms of online communication by public institutions should also be accessible in the version for the disabled.

in writing. ‒ plant health is a key factor for the future and presentation of a sustainable and competitive agricultural and forestry industry in the european union. it is very important that we focus on protecting agriculture in europe by preventing the entry and spread of harmful organisms and pests such as insects, fungi, bacteria and viruses that can cause serious damage to plants, especially if they come from other continents and europe lacks genetic resistance to them. the new legislation should bring about a significant increase in the safety of plant health and plant products in the european union. the introduction of the plant passport is also an innovation that will bring a high level of traceability in the future.
in writing. ‒ i support the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on protective measures against plant pests, amending the existing legislation in this field. due to climate change and globalisation of trade, there is an increasing penetration of foreign pests into the union countries. these pose a potential risk to human and animal life and health and to the protection of the environment. the regulation therefore aims to address the issue of non-eu plant pests. the objective is to eliminate risks and to establish practices and measures for the protection of plant health, with a focus on plant production, forests, native and artificially planted areas, natural ecosystems and biodiversity in the union.
in writing. plant health is threatened by species which are harmful to plants and plant products. the risk of introduction of various pests into the union territory is increasing due to the globalisation of trade and climate change. the proposal aims to modernise the tools for trade in herbal medicinal products and products in order to reduce the pest risk to an acceptable level. this needs to be done within the eu (improving traceability in the internal market) but also for goods travelling from third countries to the union (using the potential plant risk approach). prevention, protection measures and early detection of pests are important for the early and effective eradication of pests. member states should further develop multiannual survey programmes to detect the presence of union quarantine pests in areas where those pests have not been known to occur. the so-called plant passport should be extended to any movement of plants intended for cultivation within the eu, including those ordered at a distance. only products supplied to end-users such as gardeners will be exempted. in the event of a suspicion or detection of union quarantine pests, the commission shall be empowered to take measures, which it shall consult in advance with the member states. i support the motion with my vote.

in writing. ‒ i supported the report by mrs mcintyre on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation on protection measures against plant pests. it is part of a package of measures to strengthen the application of health and safety standards throughout the agricultural chain. the regulation lays down rules for decision-making on phytosanitary risks caused by plant pests. it also contains measures to reduce these risks and prevent pests from third countries from entering the eu. the rapporteur's aim was, among other things, to protect trade and avoid unnecessary red tape while taking sufficient measures. the new regulation provides for the possibility of temporarily restricting plants or plant products that have not been subject to a risk assessment or of requesting compensation for farmers who have had to destroy their crops as a result of a pest attack.

in writing. ‒ the trans-fatty acids pose a major risk to the health of citizens of the european union. the majority of the population of the european union, especially the most vulnerable, does not have sufficient information on trans-fatty acids and the health consequences of their consumption, which may prevent consumers from making informed decisions. if the average intake of trans-fatty acids is to be significantly reduced, measures should not be taken exclusively at national level, but measures are needed at european union level. the european parliament therefore considers it its duty to call on the food industry to give priority to alternative solutions that are in line with health standards, such as the use of improved oils, new fat processing techniques or the combination of substitutes for trans-fatty acids.
in writing. ‒ the according to who recommendations, the daily intake of trans-fatty acids naturally occurring in plant and animal foods should not exceed 1% of the daily intake. however, there is a high level of industrially produced trans-fatty acids in food on the eu market, the consumption of which poses a health risk to humans. they are mainly found in cheaper foodstuffs bought by poorer people. evidence shows that restricting these substances can significantly contribute to improving the health of the population. the usa and some european countries (denmark, austria, latvia, hungary) have already introduced measures restricting the use of industrially produced trans-fatty acids in food. health protection and the availability of safe and healthy food are union priorities and therefore member states and the commission must urgently propose measures to limit the use of industrially produced acids in foodstuffs, while ensuring education and awareness of these substances.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of adopting the motion for a resolution on trans-fatty acids. in today's fast-paced world, people tend to pay less attention to getting the substances, minerals, and vitamins that their bodies need through a proper, healthy diet. we begin to understand the close connection between diet and health only when we experience firsthand the negative effects of poor nutrition. it can start with constant fatigue and headaches, but it can also lead to more serious problems, such as heart disease. trans fats are dangerous and often we are not even aware of how many foods contain them. fast-food chains, for example, are very fond of them because they are cheap and can be used repeatedly. in the united states, for example, food manufacturers must phase out such acids by 2018. there are many tools available to us to regulate the subject, we just have to find the most appropriate one. i am in any case grateful to the rapporteur for drawing attention to this issue.
in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament's resolution on trans-fatty acids because i agree with the widely held view that high intakes of these acids increase the risk of several diseases. our aim in this resolution is to draw attention to industrially produced fatty acids. trans-fatty acids are often used in restaurants and fast food establishments for deep frying food, as they are cheap and can be reused. according to available sources, frequent consumption of trans fatty acids leads to an increased risk of coronary heart disease, and consumption of industrially produced vegetable oils has implications for cardiovascular disease, infertility, and gallstones. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that it is essential to raise awareness at european level of the consequences of excessive consumption of these acids. some eu countries, such as austria, denmark, latvia and hungary, have already adopted laws restricting the content of trans-fatty acids in food. the commission should therefore come forward with a proposal to set a legal limit for industrially produced trans-fatty acids. nutrition that benefits human health is an investment in the development of the individual. if people ate more carefully, they would reduce their future health-care costs.
in writing. ‒ the interest is to raise consumer awareness of the negative effects of trans-fatty acids on human health. at present, european union regulations do not regulate the content of trans-fatty acids in food products. the proposal should establish a european union legal limit for industrially produced trans-fatty acids in food in order to limit their intake.
in writing. ‒ as a doctor, i must point out that trans-fatty acids have a negative impact on human health. i therefore support any initiative aimed at limiting their use in food. several expert studies in the field of healthy nutrition agree on a significant and rapid improvement in health when trans-fatty acid restriction is used. at the same time, we must not forget about prevention and the protection of the most vulnerable groups of the population, namely children. they tend to eat foods high in trans-fatty acids. at the same time, awareness of the health risks of eating such foods needs to be improved. although there is legislation on the labelling of trans-fatty acids, i consider that legislation to be insufficient, since it concerns only certain foods and does not cover, for example, meals served in restaurants. moreover, according to the world health organisation (who), a labelling policy is much more costly than a blanket ban and monitoring of its compliance. it is therefore necessary to take inspiration from the example of denmark and adopt a similar limit for the restriction of trans-fatty acids in food at eu level. the approach of all member states should be uniform. dialogue with representatives of the food industry will also be a decisive factor in the fight against trans-fatty acids.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution of the parliament's committee on the environment, public health and food safety (envi). consumption of trans fats is associated with a higher risk of cardiovascular disease, but it can also be associated with infertility problems and alzheimer's disease. despite these risks, however, only a fraction of the population is aware of the harmfulness of these acids and, given that trans-fatty acids are mainly found in cheaper food products, their consumption is higher among socially disadvantaged groups. in this resolution we therefore called on the european commission to come forward within two years at the latest with a proposal for limits on industrial trans-fatty acids for all foodstuffs. this is to prevent the population from taking in increased amounts of these harmful substances. in addition, there is a need to raise awareness of the problem so that the citizens of the european union are able to make informed decisions that will not be harmful to their health.
in writing. belarus should be seen as one of the last strong authoritarian regimes in europe. unfortunately, little has changed on this definition since the september elections. with a little optimism, we can say that the elections were held in a calm atmosphere and not quite a step back. but we should not close the door to belarus. our goal should be to intensify our relations with one another. we should have a dialogue with belarus that will help to achieve this objective. focus should be placed on increasing diplomatic contacts in areas of common interest. however, a value-based dialogue is needed to promote gradual change. we must not overlook cases of violation of human rights and restrictions of personal freedoms. we must condemn the use of the death penalty, but also raise safety issues, such as the controversial construction of a nuclear power plant near ostrovets. our policy should aim to support projects that will enable the modernisation, gradual opening-up and development of belarus such as mobility partnerships, investments in infrastructure modernisation, environmental protection, education or the development of bilateral trade.
our relations with turkey are becoming more complicated. i agree that we should make it clear that a country which wants to continue accession negotiations with the union and wants visa liberalisation cannot suppress basic civil liberties, including freedom of the press. censorship and the arrest of journalists are not what brings confidence to our common dialogue. nor are they president erdogan's sharp, unacceptable remarks to the union. regardless, i think we need to continue the dialogue with turkey. however, it is very important that we make it clear that there are limits within which this dialogue should take place. i have a very unpleasant feeling that we are moving far beyond those boundaries at the moment.
when we talk about volunteering, about altruistic care for your loved ones, for your community, for the world around you, i agree with what president obama said: "the best way to not succumb to despair is to get up and do something. don't expect good things to happen to you. if you get up and do something good, you fill the world with hope and you fill yourself with hope. but besides altruism, which is virtuous in itself, volunteering deserves recognition and support for a host of other good reasons. it is the ideal way to involve volunteers in the useful activities of people who want to do so, and thus improve their lives and the lives of those who benefit from volunteering. it's a great way for young people to gain experience and improve their skills, and as we know, youth unemployment is our big common problem. it's the ideal way to draw on the life experiences of older people, which enriches the whole society and can give older people a sense of purpose, of usefulness, of meaning in their lives. what i'm saying is that volunteering is not a matter that concerns just one specific group of people, it's a matter for everyone, regardless of age, education or wealth. volunteering is by definition a voluntary activity of the willing, and if we can find ways to promote it, we will be promoting other civic virtues besides the skills mentioned and the acquisition or transfer of experience interest in the world around us, participation in social activities, active citizenship. and these are the things that any healthy and functioning free society desperately needs. and besides, volunteering creates measurable value, and that's how we should measure and value it. volunteering should be encouraged and valued in every member state of the union and by the institutions of the union itself if it is to be a union of well-functioning states with free and active citizens.
in writing. a youth strategy must be based on a real knowledge of the needs of young people. young people themselves must be actively involved in these processes, contributing their knowledge, needs and experience. despite the existence of formal documents, there is a lack of effective cooperation and involvement of young people in public life, as reflected in the low turnout in elections. lack of interest, inadequate and not always quality education, not responding to the needs of the labour market, inadequate and dysfunctional social programme create a space for the penetration of extremist views, movements and parties that can have catastrophic effects on the future generations. it is therefore essential to allocate resources and develop activities that, also through modern technologies, will lead to a wider involvement of young people in public life, increase their interest in education and lifelong professional growth. the future of generations depends on the quality of education and work with the current generation of young people, which is reflected in the whole spectrum of social and political life. the european union must also continue its programmes to support young people, which lead to a reduction in unemployment. the youth employment initiative is a proof of this.
in writing. i felt obliged to reject the discharge for the implementation of the general budget for 2014. the main reason for this is the lack of willingness of some institutions to cooperate with the european parliament. where can one expect full transparency but in eu-level institutions? we had no answers to such basic questions as the cost of maintaining buildings. i will only agree to the grant of immunity if we receive clear answers and explanations to our questions. and i'm very glad that my colleagues share your opinion. the european parliament is elected by the people to represent their interests properly, and that is exactly what we are doing.
in writing. ‒ i have already supported the second discharge report for the 2014 budgets of the european council and the council and, like the rapporteur, i agree with the non-discharge for these institutions. although there is a longstanding dispute between the european parliament and the council over the interpretation of budgetary powers, the treaties clearly provide that parliament has the power to grant discharge, while the council only makes recommendations. the council is also unwilling to cooperate with parliament and has not yet commented on the observations made in april this year. not only does the parliament lack an explanation of the increasing rate of unused appropriations and the transfer of commitments, but it has also not received an annual report on the council's activities. nor were any proposals to separate the budgets of the european council and the council taken into account. the council is also spending a lot of money on its new europe building. its completion has been delayed, but parliament has insufficient information on the costs incurred and the progress made. the expenditure of the council should be auditable in the same way as that of the other institutions. it is also striking that the council has still not adopted its code of conduct and joined the transparency register. transparency and the citizens' right to information are the key factors in the credibility of the european institutions. this discrepancy should be finally closed and the council should submit all the necessary documents to enable its budgetary implementation to be audited responsibly.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament, as the only european institution directly elected by the citizens, has a legitimate right to scrutinise the management and operation of the european council and the european commission. citizens often ask members individually and parliament as a whole about the management of the european institutions' finances, and we cannot give them adequate answers because we do not have the information. this incomprehensible attitude of our partners must change in the future, also in order to increase citizens' confidence in the european union.
in writing. ‒ i did not support the discharge report on the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2014 for the sections relating to the budget of the european council and the council. this is the second report on discharge, the first report having been postponed by a vote in april this year. as in the case of the first report in april this year, i was convinced that the discharge should be granted only after the budget as such had been approved by the court of auditors. however, as this has not yet been achieved for the 2014 budget, i voted against the discharge.
in writing. ‒ i supported the discharge for the financial year 2014 of the executive director of the ecsel joint undertaking in respect of the implementation of the eniac budget. the eniac joint undertaking was established back in 2007 to define and implement a research plan for the development of key competences for nanoelectronics in different application areas. in april this year, parliament decided to postpone the discharge for the financial year 2014 as that year saw the merger of the eniac and artemis joint undertakings, creating the electronic components and systems for european leadership (ecsel) joint technology initiative. the rapporteur then expressed the belief that national procedures should be implemented to ensure the legality of individual transactions. since the joint undertaking has in the meantime provided all the guarantees that parliament has requested, we have finally decided to grant discharge. joint ventures are an important area of industrial and research cooperation for the eu. these enterprises are based on a public-private partnership that supports research, new technologies and the faster market introduction of specific technologies. the eu has a long track record of success in joint ventures, and i believe ecsel will be just as successful in its ten-year operation.
in writing. ‒ the management of european taxpayers' money is the focus of intense media, political and public attention. in this respect, we cannot afford to make any unjustified mistakes which cast doubt on the soundness of the management. eniac should therefore finally take note and apply the reservations of the court of auditors, which have been raised for the fourth consecutive year.
in writing. ‒ i supported the discharge for the financial year 2014 of the executive director of ecsel for the implementation of the artemis budget. the artemis joint undertaking was set up back in 2007 and was entrusted with the task of defining and implementing a research programme for the development of key technologies in the field of embedded computing systems in various fields, thus enabling the emergence of new markets and societal applications. in april this year, parliament decided to postpone the discharge for the financial year 2014 as that year saw the merger of the eniac and artemis joint undertakings, creating the electronic components and systems for european leadership (ecsel) joint technology initiative. the rapporteur then expressed the belief that national procedures should be implemented to ensure the legality of individual transactions. since the joint undertaking has in the meantime provided all the guarantees that parliament has requested, we have finally decided to grant discharge. joint ventures are an important area of industrial and research cooperation for the eu. these enterprises are based on a public-private partnership that supports research, new technologies and the faster market introduction of specific technologies. the eu has a long track record of success in joint ventures, and i believe ecsel will be just as successful in its ten-year operation.
in writing. ‒ the european union's enterprises serve to coordinate and implement projects of common interest, and their centralised management is more efficient than if individual member states acted individually. for this reason, the methodology for assessing the expenditure of funds should also be harmonised, as different approaches make a comprehensive and realistic audit difficult or even impossible.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to support the discharge to be given to the director of the european joint undertaking for iter and the development of fusion energy for the financial year 2014. this discharge was originally postponed in april this year because the long-awaited and repeatedly delayed iter action plan had still not been published. however, in the meantime, the iter joint undertaking has submitted this action plan. the new director-general of iter presented concrete measures to address the main constraints currently blocking the further development of the project itself. the audit finds that the action plan has been implemented since march 2015 and that improvements in the company's functioning are expected soon. the rental of the premises of the joint undertaking has also been a problem so far. i therefore welcome the agreement offered by the spanish government, whereby the joint undertaking will have the current premises on long-term lease and will also have its office space extended by one floor. joint ventures are an important area of industrial and research cooperation for the eu. these enterprises are based on a public-private partnership that supports research, new technologies and the faster market introduction of specific technologies. iter has also developed a working definition of what constitutes the application of nuclear fusion, which will enable it to operate in compliance with intellectual property rights. i therefore hope that iter will succeed in fulfilling its mandate.
in writing. ‒ we appreciate that the management of the european joint undertaking for iter, which is involved in the development of fusion, has responded flexibly and effectively to the technical and administrative problems that have emerged in recent times. the procedure followed by the director-general and the bodies under his authority in dealing with them can serve as a model for other undertakings and institutions.

in writing. military operations in the iraqi city of mosul must be conducted in accordance with international humanitarian law. there are one and a half million civilians in mosul who need to be provided with basic food and supplies. therefore, all actors should focus on assisting and protecting such persons. the suppression of terrorists in iraq is a priority that takes precedence over any resolution of territorial claims. at the same time, iraq must respect the rights of ethnic, religious and national minorities in its territory.
in writing. ‒ mosul is the second largest city in iraq. the media daily brings horrific images from this city, where isis/da'esh has imposed a harsh regime, where children, mothers, civilians are dying, where hunger and disease are threatening, so people living there are desperate for liberation and humanitarian aid. the unhcr operates five camps around mosul and is ready to provide shelter for 45,000 people fleeing mosul and surrounding areas, with plans to increase the number of camps to 11 with a capacity of 120,000 people in the coming weeks. for this reason, the eu is providing €134 million in humanitarian aid in iraq, including €50 million for assistance in mosul. the eu has expressed support for iraq's operation to liberate mosul from isis/da'esh and considers it a crucial part of the ongoing global effort to defeat isis/da'esh in a lasting way. at the same time, we recalled in the resolution that saving civilian lives and respecting international humanitarian law are the fundamental political preconditions for reconciliation and development and the only way to defeat hatred and division, and that it is essential to avoid further tension between communities and to lay the foundations for a stable and prosperous iraq.
in writing. ‒ in this context, it is important that the european union works with the iraqi government and the kurdish regional government to reach a consensus on mosul and other disputed territories. the iraqi government needs to take concrete actions and measures to protect civilians and new legislation to protect minorities in the first place.
in writing. ‒ the situation in the middle east is a long-standing concern from the point of view of regional and global security. i support the resolution supporting the operation in northern iraq to liberate the city of mosul from the control of the daesh terrorist organisation. a key factor in the success of the operation will be the cooperation of a broad coalition led by the iraqi army and in cooperation with the kurdish regional government (kgr). however, we must not forget that despite the state of war prevailing in the country, it is necessary to ensure respect for human rights and freedoms and to prevent civilian casualties, including the destruction of public civilian objects such as schools and hospitals. it's clear that mosul is a strategically important city, and capturing it could bring us closer to defeating daesh completely. but military victory will not be enough to defeat this terrorist organization. the establishment of a sustainable and inclusive post-military structure in the region will be essential. this requires diplomatic support from the international community as well as political representation of the autonomous provinces, including the nineveh plains, sinjar and tal afar, in the decision-making process. local churches and religious organizations also need to be involved in humanitarian aid. the guarantee of the territorial integrity of iraq and respect for its borders is a clear priority for the subsequent stabilisation of the situation in the region.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution prepared by the parliament's foreign affairs committee (afet) on the situation in mosul in northern iraq. as of early 2014, mosul has been occupied by isis/da'esh and according to recent testimonies, the residents of the area are starving and under the brutal regime of isis, executions are constantly carried out and civilians are used as human shields. a joint operation led by iraq is currently underway in the area to liberate mosul. that is why we expressed our support for this operation, for the territorial integrity of iraq, and called on all parties to the operation to respect international humanitarian law and to ensure that the civilian population, who need humanitarian assistance or the possibility of leaving the conflict zone safely, is hit as little as possible.

in writing. ‒ the situation in turkey remains grave following the failed coup attempt. despite the legitimate response of the turkish government to the attempted coup, i am concerned about the ongoing purges of press freedom. at least 130 journalists have been detained so far, not only denied the right to legal representation, but there is a reasonable suspicion that these people have been and are being detained in inhumane conditions. respect for the right to freedom of expression is also a principle of every rule of law, and i therefore fully support this resolution, which calls on the turkish authorities to respect the freedom and pluralism of the press and to release journalists and media workers who have been wrongfully imprisoned. we must not forget that freedom of the media and of speech in general is a key indicator of a functioning democratic, and above all, developed society.
in writing. ‒ the the resolution of two parliamentary committees deals with the situation of journalists in turkey. after the attempted coup in july, turkey has experienced a wave of chaos, layoffs and arrests that journalists are not immune to. the commission and parliament have already expressed concerns about the state of freedom of expression and media freedom in turkey in their previous resolutions. however, since the adoption of these resolutions, the situation has worsened, with several media outlets being closed and many journalists detained. i believe that every country, let alone a country that wants to become a member of the european union, must respect fundamental rights and protect the plurality of opinions that undoubtedly belongs to a democratic state, and i therefore agree that the situation of journalists in turkey is not being ignored, that we are dealing with it intensively in parliament. i hope that this will also be a signal to turkey to try to improve the deteriorating situation.
in writing. the treaty on the non-proliferation of nuclear weapons, which entered into force in 1970, has 191 parties, five of which are recognised as nuclear weapon states (the united states, the united kingdom, russia, france and china). together with the convention on the physical protection of nuclear material, they constitute a powerful tool to promote the peaceful uses of nuclear energy, global nuclear disarmament and the prevention and investigation of nuclear related offences. the conclusion of the nuclear agreement with iran opened the way for cooperation with that country in resolving the conflict, in particular in syria and yemen. rising tensions and regional conflicts around the world raise legitimate concerns about possible nuclear terrorism. it is therefore essential to intensify cooperation between countries on disarmament with a view to achieving an international binding instrument on disarmament and to creating the conditions for eliminating the possible misuse of nuclear energy.
in writing. currently, global security is increasingly being challenged by various terrorist groups, as well as by some states, including the dprk, which is destabilising the region by testing its nuclear systems. the non-proliferation treaty (npt) is currently the only binding commitment in a multilateral treaty that addresses the goal of disarmament by nuclear-weapon states. the five countries that have the legal right to possess nuclear weapons are also among the signatories (the united states, the united kingdom, russia, china, and france). global cooperation is essential to prevent nuclear terrorism. however, the attempt to revise the npt in 2015 ended without a clear result and the absence of russia, the country with the largest nuclear arsenal in the world, from the nuclear security summit in 2016 is not a favorable sign of functioning cooperation. i join the call for the need to strengthen cooperation between states on the security of nuclear materials in order to reduce the risk of these materials ending up in the hands of terrorist groups.
in writing. we live in a dangerous world. the european union is doing everything it can to maintain national peace and stability, but we are still facing serious challenges. it is frightening to think that the buildup of tension between individual countries could end in a nuclear catastrophe. perhaps the only weapons more dangerous than these would be nuclear weapons in the hands of terrorist groups. last but not least, as we look back on the tragic events at chernobyl, we can see that even a small accident can cost thousands of lives. the european union's objective in this area is a world free of nuclear weapons, which i can fully support. more and more countries are returning to the development of nuclear weapons, such as the democratic people's republic of korea, which this year conducted its second hydrogen bomb test. we also discussed the unfavourable situation in turkey, the syrian conflict, in addition to the attempted coup. the question arises as to how safe the nuclear weapons owned by the united states and entrusted to turkey by nato are. i could go on and on about the situation in russia. i am confident that the situation will improve, but i also see the need to develop a european union strategy.
in writing. ‒ this resolution does not encourage states enough to reach the goals set in the treaty on the non-proliferation of nuclear weapons, the treaty banning nuclear tests in the atmosphere, in outer space and under water, the convention on the physical protection of nuclear material and others as main tools for nuclear security and non-proliferation. instead, it is getting close to breaching the principle of subsidiarity and it also does not acknowledge the right of the recognised nuclear weapons states to retain their nuclear deterrents as an important element of national security. the motion does not call for nuclear security and non-proliferation as such, but takes different approaches to different states and areas.
in writing. ‒ international peace, security and stability are currently under serious threat from a variety of events, including the deteriorating relations between nuclear-weapon states. nuclear weapons tests or any other nuclear explosions are a threat to international peace and security and threaten the global nuclear disarmament and non-proliferation regime. i supported the motion for a resolution in which we express our deep concern at the deterioration of the security situation around the european union and beyond its neighbourhood, as this deterioration could lead to the re-emergence of nuclear weapons as an active deterrent and to their proliferation among states and non-state actors. we therefore called on all nuclear-weapon states to take concrete interim measures to reduce the risk of nuclear weapons explosions, including reducing the operational status of nuclear weapons and moving nuclear weapons from deployment sites to storage sites, limiting the role of nuclear weapons in military doctrines, and accelerating the reduction of all types of nuclear weapons.
in writing. nuclear security in the sense of a world without nuclear weapons is the most important objective of global arms control policy and also the objective of the treaty on the non-proliferation of nuclear weapons. in view of the worrying events of recent years, the significant deterioration of stability and security around the european union, the deterioration of relations between nuclear-weapon states and the current heightened nuclear threat posed by russia's stance, cooperation at global level is essential.
in writing. ‒ nuclear weapons are one of the most effective instruments of security policy. the deterrence and second-strike strategy guarantees the nuclear powers a degree of immunity from direct military attack. but this policy has its pitfalls, and the use of even a single nuclear warhead threatens global conflict. it is deplorable that states must guarantee their inviolability and power with weapons of mass destruction. our world is currently on the brink of another cold war, and the nuclear security situation is rather degrading. such a status is imposed on non-state actors that trade in nuclear weapons, posing a huge risk to global security. moreover, the deteriorating relations between russia and nato are not a good indicator of improvement in the nuclear security situation. the deployment of iskander missile systems in the kaliningrad region capable of carrying nuclear warheads is worrying. i fully support the resolution which has been tabled, which calls for dialogue, respect for international treaties on non-proliferation and the prohibition of nuclear weapons tests. we need more trust, and we will achieve it by all states coming together to engage in dialogue with each other to eliminate their nuclear arsenals.
i was very happy to support the motion for a resolution on volunteering, which is a concrete expression of solidarity between people. volunteers make the world a better place, and this comes back to them in the form of new experiences, valuable contacts and social skills. there are more people who could be involved in volunteer activities than there are who actually do. this is a potential that the european voluntary service should also draw more from. volunteering is a concrete expression of active citizenship. because people who care about their neighbors and are willing to lend a helping hand care about the society in which they live, the politicians who represent them, the laws that are followed, and the money that goes to taxpayers.
in writing. volunteering has a positive impact on all its actors. it is a sign of solidarity and responsibility on the part of those who carry it out, and at the same time a real help for those to whom it is provided. it is also a means of mutual learning and cooperation, addressing many of the social, societal and environmental needs and challenges of the world today. i support the motion for a resolution calling for the collection of data on volunteering from different countries in order to create comparable european indicators and methods for measuring the social impact of volunteering. the introduction of an economic value measurement system will allow a better understanding not only of the human dimension but also of the economic benefits of this activity.
in writing. the european voluntary service is a highly effective tool of the european union to encourage young people to become active. volunteering has become a real trend among young people and thanks to the eu programme, everyone can get involved. the european voluntary service provides accommodation, meals and allowances, and reimburses volunteers for their travel expenses. thus, young people can try out a new situation in which they can help others and develop their own abilities. over the past years, the importance of volunteering experience has also increased in the eyes of employers, which has further helped to place people from disadvantaged social backgrounds and raise their standard of living. i think this is a great opportunity that no one should miss!
in writing. ‒ in the case of the resolution on european voluntary service and the promotion of volunteering, i voted in favour of its adoption. volunteering not only represents an important added value in terms of solidarity and assistance in europe, but also contributes significantly to the growth of the european economy.
in writing. ‒ the the european year of volunteering 2011 was a major political opportunity to raise the profile of the contribution of volunteering in europe. people volunteer freely, of their own choice and for their own reasons, without seeking financial gain. volunteering has great value and significance and is one of the most visible expressions of solidarity. today, nearly 100 million citizens of all ages are volunteering in europe, and their work contributes to around 5% of eu gdp. it is therefore necessary to support and implement the proposal that time spent on voluntary activities may be co-financed under european grants. it is also necessary to cover volunteering with a common legal framework that defines the status of volunteering, including rights and obligations, and allows for mobility and recognition of skills and knowledge. developing a more coordinated european policy for volunteering would link the different initiatives and programmes and improve access to volunteering programmes.
in writing. ‒ the this year the european voluntary service is celebrating its 20th anniversary. over the years, over 100 000 volunteers have been supported, who have had the opportunity to learn new things and gain valuable experience through non-formal learning. such activities undoubtedly have a positive impact on the dissemination of european values, intercultural dialogue and are an important tool for social inclusion and cohesion.
in writing. ‒ i was happy to support the report of the committee on culture and education (cult). the european voluntary service helps young people to travel and participate in volunteering programmes, not only within the eu member states but also in third countries. it not only helps them to gain experience, work with people or learn foreign languages, which in turn helps them to improve their position on the labour market and thus helps to fight youth unemployment. on the other hand, it also contributes to a return to basic humanity, to unselfish help to others, and to a sense of purpose or meaning in life. i think that this concept should be encouraged because it is beneficial in many ways. in addition to supporting volunteering projects, we should make it easier for people who help in a selfless way not only during volunteering but also after it, at least by recognising the skills acquired and giving due consideration to the time spent in volunteering.

in writing. ‒ the report by ms bocskorová is aimed at evaluating the european union's youth strategy for the period 2013 to 2015. it is divided into several key areas, within which it assesses the situation over a given period, identifies shortcomings and formulates future recommendations. among the main challenges facing the youth strategy, it deals in particular with high unemployment, early school leaving, discrimination, the integration of refugees and migrants, and the problem of acquiring skills that do not correspond to labour market requirements. in the light of these problems, the report expresses concern that without a targeted and effective strategy, young people will be at risk of social exclusion, isolation or radicalisation. the report also brings many potential solutions to the main problems, with a special focus on the most disadvantaged and vulnerable groups of young people. on the other hand, it also presents views that can be described as problematic, such as the requirement of a guaranteed minimum income, gender quotas, some problematic references to the refugee crisis, or calls for support for projects that have proven to be very ineffective in practice. in view of these facts, i decided to abstain in the final vote.
in writing. the andrieu report on the link between the common agricultural policy (cap) and job creation proposes a good and adequately funded cap. although the objectives of the report are the same as those of the national farmers, the text contains proposals that could jeopardise the future financing of the cap. the report would also open the way to projects aimed at solving social and demographic problems through the agricultural policy, which is not acceptable, since cap resources must actually reach farmers. the report is not a legislative text and therefore has no legal consequences for the eu's common agricultural policy. it is unacceptable that crisis situations caused by social and demographic changes are covered by direct payments or rural development funds, whether on a voluntary or even compulsory basis. the cap's resources must be effectively channelled to farmers and food producers, without which the eu would not be able to ensure adequate food supplies for the continent.
in writing. agriculture and food account for 6% of the european union's gdp. this is 15 million businesses and 46 million jobs concentrated mainly in rural areas. support for agriculture and employment is therefore directly linked to the development and maintenance of life in rural settlements. the measures and the aid granted must take account of the specific features of agriculture, such as differences in climatic and geographical conditions and the higher employment of women in the sector. smes must be able to secure financing for their investments from eu funds. it is also necessary to increase the interest of young people in working and entrepreneurship in this field. the common agricultural policy is therefore an important tool for maintaining employment, ensuring the availability of its own high-quality and safe food and at the same time developing the countryside. the commission and the member states must direct their efforts towards this enduring objective.
in writing. rural areas cover more than 77% of the eu's territory and many jobs in these areas depend on agriculture and the food industry. within the eu's common agricultural policy, it is important to maintain its two pillars. the first pillar prevents the outflow of small and family farms from the sector and preserves jobs in the agricultural sector; funding from the second pillar ensures job creation in other areas such as tourism, food processing and others. the crisis that has hit europe has affected rural areas the most. in the interests of prevention, it is necessary to promote the diversity of farming systems. smes that are more innovative, highly flexible and often better organised in producer groups are more resilient during a crisis and able to adapt more easily to its consequences; they also benefit local communities, thus contributing to supporting the rural economy. the challenge for the future cap after 2020 must be to simplify procedures and provide sufficient financial coverage. more attention must be paid to modernisation and investment. rural development contributes directly to job creation. it is therefore essential that member states, through their local authorities, contribute to the achievement of the cap's objectives by making use of the available means it offers. rural development programmes and operational programmes can be used to create and maintain jobs and to improve services in rural areas.

in writing. ‒ the this report focused on how to improve the use of existing cap instruments to create new jobs. according to this report, the solutions were mainly aimed at making the agricultural environment attractive to attract new businesses and thus create new jobs. at the same time, the rapporteur also used the report as an opportunity to highlight shortcomings, in particular the strong support for dominant agricultural species through existing instruments. while i agreed with some elements of the report, in particular the calls for simplifying the common agricultural policy and thus making things easier for small farmers, as well as the calls for achieving better access to services in agricultural areas and focusing on research and innovation, it contained many elements with which i disagreed. for example, the report has intervened in areas of taxation, social rights or other issues that fall within the exclusive competence of the member states. this was a breach of the principle of subsidiarity, and i have therefore decided to vote against the report as a whole.

the commissioner's speech that, even after a year, we have not made any progress on this matter. we realize that we're not just talking about making people's lives easier. we're talking about health, even lives saved, property damage, as experts have already sufficiently demonstrated the link between time change and increased road accidents, as well as complications in medical operations. and that's not to mention the negative consequences for agriculture and animal husbandry. moving the hands of a watch twice a year not only saves money. on the contrary, experts estimate that the european economy will lose 1 to 2 percent of its gross domestic product each year because of this change. this represents a loss of almost 300 billion euros. i must admit that i was a little surprised that in in writing ‒ after a long negotiation since 2012, the european parliament has managed to agree with the council on a multiannual fisheries management plan. i am glad that we have finally reached a compromise that will lead to greater legal certainty for fishermen, which is why i supported the proposal at second reading. the original proposal for a regulation was submitted by the commission during the last parliamentary term. however, at that time the council decided to bypass parliament and adopt the multiannual cod fishing plan without consulting it. the commission and parliament therefore appealed to the court of justice, which finally upheld the parliament's right. the contested regulation was subsequently repealed and parliament was granted the right to directly co-decide on fishing plans. among other measures, the compromise proposal for a regulation envisages maintaining the fishing mortality rate at a level acceptable according to scientific advice, which should allow the recovery of fish stocks. similarly, member states should develop and promote measures to ensure that unwanted catches are prevented. in addition, the plan provides for exemptions for vessels that do not contribute to the death of cod, and member states should also focus on measures that would reduce the rate of cod discarding. as this agreement establishes the principles of a new common fisheries policy, it is time to take a stand on responsible fishing and respect for the need to restore fish stocks.
