in writing. the implementation of two of the four european freedoms, the free movement of persons and goods, is not possible without a functioning infrastructure and the removal of existing barriers. the railways have played their historic role in connecting europe, but their importance will not diminish in the future, but increase. as the most environmentally friendly and efficient means of long-distance transport by land, the european union wants to strengthen rail transport and prepare it for the era of automation and digitalisation. the harmonisation of different technical regulations, certificates for train staff and increased transparency in selection processes are the first steps towards creating a single rail transport system across europe, based on competition between different carriers, which will increase pressure on quality and lower prices for people and businesses.
the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it was a very challenging task for me to prepare this report on fundamental rights, and i would like to thank the shadow rapporteurs and the other collaborators for their cooperation. the two big issues of the past year have been the crisis of migration management and the unprecedented spread of terrorism. in managing migration, we have highlighted the responsibility of member states, but also that migrants have not only rights, but also obligations. in preventing terrorist acts, we are focusing on the creation of a security union. and we're not forgetting the rights of the victims and their families. let me tell you about some of the important social problems that are addressed in this report. we have a strong focus on children's rights, the most pressing of which is still the high level of child poverty and the high number of missing children. it is also important to point out the unjustified separation of children from their parents. this can only be done as a last resort, and states should give parents more opportunities to improve, to improve the situation of their children. we also focus on the rights of people with disabilities, who continue to suffer from a high degree of discrimination in the union. we negotiate constructively for the rights of minorities, who enrich europe's diversity. do we realize that their denied rights are merely insignificant concessions to the majority nations, but that their denial can become a dangerous tool for political incitement, for the incitement of nationalism in the hands of our enemies, foreign and domestic? a common minimum standard would greatly help to establish rights and to enforce them where they are politically neglected or avoided as an inconvenient matter. we also looked at women's rights in detail, because we need to create social conditions for women to be able to achieve their self-fulfillment and career development in line with their specific mission of having children. we have also not forgotten the issue of gender equality, which is a deeply frustrating issue for many of our fellow citizens. we will discuss the fight against discrimination and roma rights in a separate chapter. it is also increasingly important that new technologies do not compromise our rights. in addition to digital safety for children and the protection of personal data, drone harassment or the right to be forgotten is also very timely. the report calls on member states to promote education in human and fundamental rights, e-governance and the promotion and simplification of participatory democracy. we have not avoided the rule of law either, as it is the only guarantee that all these rights will be exercised. your honor, i'm not sure. it is very positive that the european union, as a legal entity, is joining more and more international conventions, including civil law conventions. so our accession to the istanbul convention can also serve as an example for hesitant member states. i therefore propose that we should act in a similar spirit with regard to international conventions on the protection of the rights of children and minorities. the european union must lead not only in economic and environmental policies but also in civil and fundamental rights, giving direction to its member states. in conclusion, i would ask the honourable members to comment on the report.
madam president, i welcome the report which, as in previous years, points out the shortcomings of the eu in the area of fundamental rights. one such unsolved eu problem that emerges year after year is the situation of indigenous minorities. for many years now, my colleagues from the minority community have been asking the commission to establish european minimum standards for the protection of minority rights. it's all for nothing. the commission dismisses the responsibility by saying that this is a national competence and that it cannot do anything. but while the copenhagen criteria require accession countries to ensure the protection of minorities, discrimination against national minorities is often overlooked when it is committed by an eu member state. think about it, colleagues, how can a minority expect to be defended by a national majority that is trying to discriminate against it? it is naive to expect this, and we need to find a solution at european level and put pressure on the member states. minority rights are fundamental rights and an integral part of them, they simply cannot be circumvented. article 2 of the lisbon treaty also covers this. the commission has also provided information on the implementation of the eu aid volunteers initiative in the member states. the issue of migration cannot distract attention from the problems that already exist. madam president, national minorities represent and nurture european culture and values. union citizens who make an integral contribution to the diversity of the union only in some cases regret that they are treated as second-class citizens of the union. this cannot be tolerated.
a well-known middle eastern history teacher once criticized the legal experts of his day for passing the mosquito or mosquitoes in a glass but swallowing the camel. they were mindlessly preoccupied with the details, but they were culpably missing the big picture. this report also has several such 'comrades', e.g. the push to override the dubious anti-discrimination directive or the istanbul convention, the forcible acceptance of so-called 'same-sex marriages', the making of abortion a fundamental right and immigration measures that only make the situation worse. the authors of the report have condemnably squandered an opportunity to strengthen the right to life, to draw attention to the evils of human trafficking, female genital mutilation, and discrimination against people with disabilities and ethnic groups. as a shadow reporter, i appreciate the hard work of a reporter who has tried to maintain our unity in diversity. but unfortunately, the camel in the drink is ceding more and more national sovereignty to the eu institutions and the council of europe. it's time to say goodbye to such reports and focus on the real fundamental rights in our nations. watch out for the camel in the cup, or we'll choke on it.
the rapporteur. thank you very much, madam president, madam commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, thank you for your valuable comments, and of course i would like to respond to all the speakers, but perhaps i should just say again that it is well known that the annual report on fundamental rights is intended to assess the state of fundamental rights in the european union and its member states. it's clear from the comments that we have a lot of problems, and it's very difficult to find the right balance between freedom of speech and hate speech, between security and freedom. it may seem easier to guarantee the rights of certain discriminated groups, such as the disabled, the elderly, migrants, national minorities, but also women and children. unfortunately, that is not the case. our job is to create, alongside universal fundamental rights, the framework, the legal framework, within which this can be done. and it is also the task of parliament to investigate how and to what extent these rights can be guaranteed by the public and eu institutions, and to hold them to account. let me respond to the commissioner's statement very briefly. i was very pleased to hear that the commission is already preparing the european union's accession to the convention on human rights. we also heard that the european commission has a serious intention to develop a comprehensive eu strategy on children's rights, on topics such as child-friendly justice, the right to education, the rights of children with disabilities, or online child protection, child protection. i would just like to repeat the call that i would like to make to move in a similar spirit with regard to international conventions that include the protection of minority rights. i believe that the european union must be at the forefront, not only of economic and environmental issues, but also of civil and fundamental rights, and show the way to the member states.
in the european union, we are witnessing an increasing number of tax fraud cases, which are unfortunately becoming more sophisticated and sometimes reaching the highest levels, as in the case of slovakia, even to the level of the minister of the interior or the prime minister. so it's important that we find a cure for this disease, and i think the cure is a simple, transparent tax system. i am glad that the european parliament is doing a lot in this respect it has already ensured the exchange of information between the tax authorities of the member states, but also between the tax authorities of the problem countries. it is important that we simplify the system and ensure uniform vat registration in all countries, but also that we really ensure that profits are taxed where they are generated. i think it's important to also talk about value added tax, because this system doesn't deliver what we expect it to and it has big tax evasions. that is why it is important to re-examine the whole vat system to find a way to take as little as possible from people and businesses and to encourage activity so that people end up with more.

in writing. ‒ the european union is seeking to strengthen the reform and modernisation of partner countries that have joined the programme through the european neighbourhood policy programme. one of these countries is algeria, which has expressed interest in participating in many programmes under the european neighbourhood policy. the protocol in question contains a framework agreement covering the general principles for the participation of algeria in european union programmes. these are standard provisions which are intended for all the european neighbourhood policy partner countries with which protocols are concluded.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. algeria is an important country for achieving the objective of limiting migration through the central mediterranean, which is now the main migration route. in the framework partnership agreement with third countries adopted in june this year, algeria was identified as one of the 16 'priority' countries with which the european commission wants to conclude agreements. the eu wants to work with algeria on preventing migration and taking in deportees. at the same time, the eu wants to provide algeria with various aid, such as development aid and trade, and participation in its programmes. algeria has already expressed its interest in participating in a wide range of programmes open to eu partner countries in 2013.
in writing. ‒ i supported the conclusion of the eu-algeria framework agreement, as i am pleased with algeria's interest in participating in union programmes. similar framework agreements have been concluded by the eu with several neighbouring countries. algeria is joining the european neighbourhood policy through this framework agreement. it will thus gradually open up the possibility of cooperation with the union's member states through european programmes and agencies. for the european neighbourhood countries, this policy is one of the tools that allows them to reform their societies and modernise their countries. the protocol that i have agreed with algeria contains the general principles that will govern algeria's participation in union programmes. as this is a protocol containing standard clauses already used in other similar framework agreements, its implementation should be smooth. this horizontal agreement, which provides for economic, financial and technical cooperation, should gradually open algeria to european citizens. the potential for mutual exchange thus created will certainly be beneficial to both parties.
in writing. ‒ the economic and political stability of the north african region is crucial for europe's security. with the help of the european union, morocco has been able to stabilise after the unrest. we are now offering the same assistance to algeria, which is also an important partner for us in the diversification of energy sources.
in writing. ‒ i supported the legislative proposal for the conclusion of the euro-mediterranean agreement between the eu and algeria. algeria is a major regional player, especially in energy production. it is therefore in the interest of the union and its member states to promote deeper cooperation between themselves through various programmes focusing on political and socio-economic reforms and the fight against corruption. this agreement is part of the wider european neighbourhood policy (enp). as early as 2007, the council issued a directive to the commission to negotiate a legal framework for agreements with the acp countries, including algeria. in february 2013, algeria subsequently expressed its interest in actively participating in a wide range of programmes for these countries. algeria now joins the majority of the southern partners who have already signed similar agreements with the eu. this will strengthen cooperation and the development of a democratic society, as well as promoting economic integration and education.
in writing. ‒ i supported the recommendation on the proposal for the conclusion of a protocol to the euro-mediterranean agreement establishing an association between the european community, of the one part, and the people's democratic republic of algeria, of the other part. this protocol concerns the general principles for the participation of algeria in union programmes, the principles concerned in particular the technical and financial conditions for the participation of algeria in those programmes. i believe that algeria's participation in european union programmes will help this country to implement democratic reforms and overall modernisation. and since all this is the aim of the european neighbourhood policy, i had no reservations about concluding the protocol.
in writing. ‒ the the compromise text in question represents a balanced approach to deep-sea fishing in the north-east atlantic. the text is in line with the principles of the new basic regulation and the reform, which ensures conditions to prevent adverse impacts on sensitive marine ecosystems. vessels will be required to report encounters with sensitive marine ecosystems at a depth of 400 metres and immediately cease operations and move to an area at least 5 nautical miles from the encounter point. the reform should also increase the participation of scientific observers by 20%.
in writing. - i voted against the rejection of this resolution. fisheries need to be regulated and protected in order to be managed sustainably in the long term. in the context of this regulation and protection, it was necessary to review and establish specific conditions for fishing for deep-sea fish stocks in the north-east atlantic. for example, the agreement results in the european union freezing its fishing footprint by specifying the area in which deep-sea fishing will be allowed. specific sanctions will be introduced for vessels that violate the deep sea fisheries regulation and no derogations will apply for certain provisions. a depth limit of 800 meters was also agreed.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution because i believe it is right to ensure, in accordance with the united nations general assembly resolutions, in particular resolutions 61/105 and 64/72, the protection of sensitive deep-sea ecosystems from the impact of bottom fishing gear and the sustainable exploitation of deep-sea fish stocks. although deep-sea fisheries have been regulated in the eu since 2003 through total allowable catches (tacs), i believe that only further effective measures can prevent further adverse consequences of unregulated fishing and the destruction of deep-sea fish stocks. i regret that some deep-sea fish stocks are threatened by fishing activities outside the main fishing grounds. in order to ensure that deep-sea fish stocks can recover and can be exploited sustainably in the long term, it is necessary to reduce some catches. i am convinced that it is in our interest to make further progress in this area, because it is a good investment not only in the health of our seas, but also in the future of our fishermen.
in writing. ‒ the i did not support the amendment by the efdd political group rejecting the council's position. i do not agree with this rejection, but i support the council's proposal for a regulation laying down specific conditions for fishing for deep-sea stocks in the north-east atlantic and provisions concerning fishing in international waters of the north-east atlantic. the proposal deals with the so-called high seas, where fishing takes place at depths of 600-800 m. however, such fishing, especially when using certain types of gear, causes irreversible damage to the environment and damages deep-sea ecosystems. that is why the regulation introduces stricter measures against such damage to the seabed. meanwhile, fishing will only be allowed where the so-called fishing footprint already exists, fishing will not be allowed in areas whose ecosystems are designated as vulnerable and stricter controls will be introduced. i think that the environment should be protected as much as possible and that, on the contrary, activities that lead to its, in this case irreversible, damage should be controlled. i consider the rules introduced by the proposed regulation to be appropriate and hope that they will prove their effectiveness.
in writing. as a result of years of conciliation work, parliament's rules of procedure have been amended, with effect from next year. the parliament's working procedures are reformed by changes brought about by the review, which also clarify the part concerning the handling of petitions falling within the competence of the committee on petitions (rule 216). this includes a new section on fact-finding visits to member states, giving a precise description of the substance of the fact-finding visits and the commission's work to be done thereafter, and amendments and additions to the information on the petitions portal for accepted petitions.

in writing. ‒ i supported the revision of the ep's rules of procedure, as the amendments concerned the better functioning of the european parliament, clarifying the rules, improving transparency and protecting the parliament from being disrupted by deliberate elements of sabotage of our work. the revision was the result of 18 months of working group meetings, during which a high degree of consensus was reached on many points. the rules of procedure increase transparency in the work of members by prohibiting them from engaging in paid lobbying or by requiring them to make a more detailed declaration of their financial interests. we also adopted a number of proposals for measures to improve the efficiency of the ep's work. we have adjusted the order of voting on legislation, changed the rules for question time and, in order to reduce the excessive number of questions for the commission, we have provided that each member may submit a maximum of 20 questions for a continuous period of three months. i also supported the proposal that members should be sanctioned for using defamatory, racist and xenophobic language or for interfering with parliamentary business.

in writing. cultural and creative industries (ccis) are those industries that are based on cultural values, individual creativity, skills and talents and are able to create wealth and jobs through value creation based on intellectual property. they connect art and culture with business and technology. the further development of smes requires a comprehensive industrial strategy at european level. the european parliament report calls on the commission to establish a comprehensive and long-term industrial policy framework for the cultural and creative sectors and to make the development, promotion and funding of smes one of the eu's strategic objectives. there are a lot of opportunities in the small industries. this is also a sector that is important for job creation and would benefit from a legal framework that takes account of the specificities of the sector and allows for further innovation.
in writing. ‒ a coherent policy on cultural and creative industries is a strategic step towards creating new jobs, sustainable growth and fostering innovation and cultural heritage. legislation in this area focuses on measures that will lead to the realisation of the full potential of this sector through clear and precise definitions. member states should develop or introduce a legal and institutional framework for creative artistic activity in the case of contracts, social security, health insurance, direct and indirect taxation and compliance with european standards. the european commission must respond to the reduction of the value gap and will have to ensure that authors and creators and rightholders are adequately compensated for their works.

in writing. ‒ the this report focuses on the situation of women and their rights in the eastern partnership countries, which include armenia, azerbaijan, moldova, ukraine, belarus and georgia. despite the fact that women's rights are enshrined and protected in the individual constitutions of these countries, the reality is often different and social and economic discrimination based on gender persists. gender equality is an area where enhanced cooperation between the european union and the eastern partnership countries would be very beneficial. most of the challenges are inherently common to both the european union and its eastern neighbours, and the aim of this report is to contribute to the increased importance of women's rights and gender equality in the political priorities of the eastern partnership.

in writing. ‒ i support the granting of consent to the conclusion of this agreement, which replaces the original eu-norway agreement of 1980. the agreement is in conformity with the international law of the sea currently in force. it ensures the continuation of the historically reciprocal approach to fishing between the two member states of the european union, denmark and sweden, and norway in the skagerrak and kattegat, with regard to the conservation, management and control of fisheries in these areas.
in writing. ‒ fishing has traditionally been free of national borders. the skagerrak and kattegat are typical examples of areas where fishermen have fished since the middle ages, and have followed the migration of different fish species. as early as 1966, denmark, norway and sweden concluded an agreement on reciprocal access to fisheries in these areas. it recognised the geographical specificities and historical rights of fishermen from these three countries. the agreement itself was very simple and contained only three articles. with some minor adjustments, mainly due to the accession of denmark and sweden to the european union, this agreement was valid until 2012. the accession of these countries to the eu has transferred the responsibilities for the administration of this agreement to the european commission. in 2009, norway decided to terminate the original agreement, mainly due to recent developments in international fisheries law. the norwegian authorities have become convinced that the agreement is obsolete and that its provisions will need to be brought into line with current fisheries control methods. i approved the new format of the agreement, in particular because it takes account of the union's common fisheries policy. and this not only supports the original rights of fishermen, but also modern trends in the control of the use of fish resources.
in writing. ‒ i supported the recommendation for a draft council decision on the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and the kingdom of norway on reciprocal access to fishing in the skagerrak for vessels flying the flag of denmark, norway and sweden. the skagerrak area has traditionally been a fishing area for vessels flying the flags of these three states. the original reciprocal fisheries agreement, which allowed fishing up to 4 nautical miles from the coastal waters of denmark, norway and sweden, has now expired. i therefore think that the historic right of the fishermen of denmark, norway and sweden must be supported and enshrined in the treaties. at the same time, the agreement contained measures to ensure sustainable fishing and the conservation of fish stocks in the area.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade. on 8 november 2016, the commission adopted a proposal for a decision to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund for spain to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant by bosal s.a. following its bankruptcy and closure, primarily in the region of valencia, spain. in 2015, passenger car production in the eu-27 decreased by 0,5 million units compared to 2006, while worldwide production increased by 31,1%, mainly in china and other economies in south-east asia. bosal s.a. started its activities in 1986 in the city of sagunto. its main business was the production of engines and components for road vehicles (in particular automotive catalysts, exhaust systems, etc.). the commission also found that the company had not been able to obtain a profit margin for the period from 1 january 2011 to 31 december 2012. the egf application concerns 250 workers made redundant. the european parliament has today agreed to assure the commission that the conditions laid down in the egf regulation are met and that spain is therefore entitled to a financial contribution of eur 856 800 under that regulation, covering 60% of the total expenditure of eur 1 428 000 and the reintegration into the labour market of 250 workers made redundant.
in writing. ‒ in this particular case, it is a request that came from spain, specifically for bosal s.a., a company engaged in the manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers and trailers in the region of valencia. this is an application for an allowance of eur 856 800 for 250 redundant staff. the commission also found that the average price of the product concerned in the union market was higher than the average price of the like product sold in the union. in order to adjust production capacity to demand and reduce costs, the company introduced mandatory reduction of working hours for all employees. the commission has not received any comments from interested parties.
in writing. ‒ the the bankruptcy and subsequent closure of the spanish company bosal s.a., which manufactured motor vehicles, trailers and trailers, resulted in the loss of 250 jobs. in this context, spain has requested assistance from the european globalisation adjustment fund for measures to reintegrate redundant workers into the labour market. the application complies with the conditions for the granting of the egf, and i have therefore supported the granting of aid to spain of eur 856 800 in commitment and payment appropriations.
in writing. ‒ i fully support measures aimed at setting policies that create growth and jobs. however, i do not consider the european globalisation adjustment fund to be the right and effective instrument for these policies. that's why i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to give workers made redundant as a result of structural changes in the world market a chance to be re-employed as quickly as possible. the fund shall be open to member states to draw a total of eur 150 million each year. whenever there is a mass redundancy in the domestic market for reasons related to globalisation shifts, the government of the country has the possibility to request a contribution to mitigate the impact on the redundant employees. in this case, we examined the request of the spanish authorities, where 250 workers were made redundant following the bankruptcy of bosal s.a. since the request meets the formal requirements, i have approved the release of almost eur 857 thousand in favour of spain. bosal was originally engaged in the production of parts and accessories for motor vehicles when it started its activity in sagunto in 1986. it subsequently expanded its activities and moved from the spanish market to other european markets, where it supplied other original automotive components. the commission notes that the commission did not provide any information on the sales of the like product to the sampled exporting producers. despite efforts to restructure by reducing costs or working hours, the company was not saved before it declared bankruptcy in 2015. i therefore fully support the granting of this aid to its former employees.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund is an important tool for maintaining employment and upskilling displaced workers. in the case of comunidad valenciana, the mobilisation will involve 250 employees, mainly men over 45 years of age who are at risk of falling into social deprivation. the appropriations will be used in particular for allowances and incentives to facilitate their search for new employment, including a travel allowance.
in writing. ‒ i did not support the draft decision which, in response to spain's request to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund, recommended the allocation of eur 856 000 from this fund. spain requested the financing because the changes in world trade are forcing the automotive industry in valencia to lay off 250 employees. i think that changes in world trade are really having a very negative effect on the number of employees, or even entire regions, where there is a surplus of employees due to closures or reductions in production. i also think that we need to help these laid-off employees as soon as possible. on the other hand, i do not think that the european globalisation adjustment fund is the right instrument for this. even after a comprehensive evaluation report had been drawn up, it was not known how many redundant workers were able to find new jobs thanks to the fund and whether they were able to return to work thanks to their skills and expertise. it is also a fact that re-employment varies widely from country to country and depends more on the capabilities of the country or region than on assistance from the fund. that is why i am of the opinion that, until the data relating to this fund are sufficiently identified and evaluated, we should focus on other instruments rather than helping these displaced workers.

in writing. due to the imperfection and globalisation of agricultural markets, the weather-related volatility of supply and the uncertain balance of food supply, european farmers are constantly exposed to price volatility and increasingly dependent on stable markets and prices, adequate public funding and measures to ensure the competitiveness of farms and family farms. a multifunctional and sustainable agricultural production is desirable. proposals to reduce price volatility in agricultural markets include strengthening sectoral organisations and contracting systems, better protecting farmer incomes by creating appropriate tools to manage the risk of price volatility, and strengthening market transparency by setting up price monitoring centres. the report suggests that the system of direct payments and the single area payment scheme, which are essential to ensure farmers' income and provide them with a certain level of financial stability, should be maintained.
in writing. ‒ in recent years, we have seen deepening instability and price volatility both at the level of the european and the global economy. this phenomenon was caused by a number of factors, but mainly by rapid succession and changes in supply and demand, or fluctuating prices. unfortunately, the cap in its current configuration is unable to address and adequately respond to the high price volatility on agricultural markets, which places an undue burden on producers while the rest of the food chain remains unaffected. after a thorough analysis, the report provides a number of solutions and identifies the main problems. in the future, we should focus on increasing support for individual sectors and producer organisations, improving the contract system and increasing transparency. the report also points out that risk management tools can be better used to protect farmers' incomes. we need effective measures at european level to ensure the necessary protection of farmers as well as consumers against unfair trading practices. farmers are the weakest link in the food chain, and many forget that they are the most important link. the future cap must seek new ways of combating price volatility and of trying to stabilise farmers' incomes.
in writing. ‒ the safety and stability of the agricultural sector are essential for food security and sufficiency. globalisation of trade in agricultural products, climate change, animal and plant health affect the availability, price and quality of agricultural and food products. this has implications for the health and lives of the population, in addition to economic risks. the common agricultural policy must therefore respond flexibly to all factors affecting agricultural production through risk management tools, so that agriculture is a stable economic area capable of providing affordable and quality agricultural products.

in writing. ‒ i voted today in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 539/2001 of the european parliament and of the council. that regulation has already been amended once, in 2013, introducing significant elements such as the so-called 'suspension mechanism', which has now itself been amended. visa policy is a key issue for the european union, as it is a key part of the union's external policy and also has an impact on internal security. the 2013 amendment introduced the so-called 'suspension mechanism', which allows for the temporary suspension of visa-free travel for third-country nationals as a last resort in certain emergency situations. the amendment is intended to strengthen the suspension mechanism by making it easier for member states to notify the circumstances leading to a possible suspension and by allowing the commission to activate the mechanism on its own initiative. it makes the whole system faster and more flexible. the visa waiver may be suspended if there is a significant and sudden increase in the number of third-country nationals staying irregularly in the eu, in the number of unjustified asylum applications lodged by nationals of that third country or if the third country does not cooperate in the field of readmission. however, increased flexibility must be accompanied by a robust set of guarantees and measures to protect human rights.
in writing. in the interests of the security and public order of the union and the member states, it is necessary to strengthen the visa procedures for applicants from third countries with a simultaneous guarantee of the protection of human rights. the union's visa policy instruments need to respond flexibly to security threats posed by unjustified asylum applications or increased numbers of irregular third-country nationals on union territory. the commission is required to monitor the situation in these countries and report its findings to parliament.
in writing. ‒ visa policy is undoubtedly one of the important instruments of the union's external action and also affects internal security. the recent revision of the visa policy introduced new measures, namely the so-called suspension mechanism and the reciprocity mechanism. they are two sides of the same coin and act as legislative and political counterbalances, which required that their procedures be harmonised. in particular, it was necessary to specify precisely the functionality of the suspension mechanism. given that the visa liberalisation process is currently underway and that the eu is facing a complex political and migration situation, it was necessary to make the suspension mechanism faster and more flexible. i supported this effort because i agree that we need to create tools that enable the eu to respond to exceptional circumstances. in the event that a member state is unable to cope with a sudden increase in the number of foreigners on its territory, unjustified asylum applications or other security threats on european territory, it will be able to suspend the application of the visa regime with a certain third country. however, as such a measure is one of the most stringent policy measures in the interest of third-country nationals, it is necessary that this increased flexibility goes hand in hand with human rights safeguards.
in writing. ‒ in connection with the introduction of visa-free travel with ukraine and georgia, we are also strengthening the mechanism for its suspension and temporary reintroduction in the event of massive abuse or if an unforeseeable situation arises in one of the countries that may have a negative impact on the european union's ability to control the movement of persons.
in writing. ‒ visa policy is an area of activity of the european union, which follows on from external policy as well as internal security. i voted in favour of the text because it is a revision of the suspension mechanism for visa-free travel and seeks to make this instrument more effective. it gives both the commission and the member states the power to renew the visa requirement for third-country nationals, if necessary. the eu needs effective tools to enable it to respond to exceptional circumstances resulting from a sudden and significant increase in the number of third-country nationals staying illegally in the eu or from an increase in unjustified asylum applications by third-country nationals. the visa brake should also apply in the event of a third country rejecting a readmission request from an eu member state, and also in the event of security threats on european territory. however, we must also be aware that the renewal of the visa requirement for third-country nationals is a powerful political and diplomatic act that can have different consequences. it is therefore of the utmost importance that this mechanism is applied on the basis of factual, objective and relevant evidence.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the draft regulation amending the regulation listing the third countries whose nationals must be in possession of a visa when crossing the external borders of the member states and the countries whose nationals are exempt from this requirement. the amendment of the regulation concerned the mechanism by which the visa waiver may be suspended. the european union has concluded a number of bilateral agreements on visa liberalisation, and although the situation in a given country is carefully examined before any such agreement is concluded, in terms of respect for human rights, the principles of the democratic rule of law, but also the dangers of illegal migration, the situation in these countries may also change over time. this is why it was necessary to create a more flexible instrument that would allow member states and the european commission to react more quickly to changing conditions and, for example, threats to the security of the european union. i think the mechanism approved serves that purpose. the regulation now describes in detail the different stages of a proposal for suspension of an exemption and extends the grounds on which such suspension can be applied. i believe that these changes will also help to strengthen citizens' confidence in the european union and the treaties that the european union concludes with third countries.

in writing. the administration of the drug thalidomide, which was introduced to the european market by the german pharmaceutical company chemie grünenthal for pregnant women in the 1950s and 1960s, had disastrous effects on the development of human foetuses. this chemical and drug have caused the birth of 20,000 children with severe physical and mental disabilities. there are currently 4000 victims of this medicine in the union who face increased healthcare and social and economic costs due to their health problems. these victims are in need of help, but at the same time it must be said that in the case in question the regulatory and control activities for the marketing of the medicinal product, for which specific bodies are responsible, have failed.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution in support of the victims of thalidomide because it is really high time that those affected are compensated. the case has dragged on for decades, and now is the right time for the german authorities to compensate the victims of this drug. a medicine containing the active substance thalidomide, also known by the trade name contergan, was introduced in 1957. it was considered a "safe sleeping pill". in the following five years, it was sold under various trade names in dozens of countries around the world (in the former czechoslovakia, it was not registered and no permit was issued for its legal emergency import). in november 1961, a german pediatrician openly expressed public suspicion that the use of contergan might be associated with a sudden increase in the number of newborns with congenital malformations. soon, several hundred mothers were bringing deformed babies into the world. the suspicion was confirmed that contergan, which had previously been ' an excellent sedative and sleeping medicine ' with no side effects and was therefore popularly used by pregnant women, caused severe developmental disorders in the mother' s body. we therefore want to put pressure on the german government and the commission with this resolution to finally compensate the victims in full and to have the company which placed the medicine on the market accept its responsibility.

in writing. the committee on petitions (peti) as the parliamentary committee with direct contact with the citizens of the union regularly reports on its activities during the previous year to the plenary, which is open to public debate. 2015 was the first full year of the five-year legislative period that began in 2014 and there were tangible changes in the work of peti through streamlining the handling of petitions. this has led to old, forgotten or lost petitions being put on the agenda, the committee deciding on the issues raised and the citizens of the union being answered. the processing of newly received petitions is no longer hampered by the large number of petitions that had been accumulated in the past. the development of an internet portal for the electronic submission of petitions has helped to make eu citizens more aware of the possibilities offered by the right to petition. the good functioning of peti is an important confidence factor, and the trust of eu citizens in the eu institutions depends to a large extent on its performance. the dialogue with citizens should be continued as it has been in recent years and could be further developed, for example, by means of new it applications to be introduced within the secretariat and by adhering to general principles such as equal treatment of petitions. in the light of the above, i have endorsed the report. the committee on petitions should also follow these principles when considering petitions concerning the hungarian community in slovakia, which i represent.
